title: A probable supernova remnant and a possible neutron star in the main body of 30 Doradus
abstract: We report a probable supernova remnant (SNR) within Shell 1 in the main body of the 30 Doradus giant region, using multiwavelength data from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST), Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO), Spitzer Space Telescope, Chandra X-ray Observatory, South African MeerKAT Radio Telescope, and Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). While the optical shell of Shell 1 exhibits properties consistent with a photoionized superbubble in a dense medium, its interior shows compelling evidence of SNR signatures. These include diffuse X-ray emission, nonthermal radio emission with a spectral index of approximately -0.64, localized enhancements of the H ii S ii /Hα ratio, and high-velocity features in the Hα line. From the X-ray morphology and characteristics of high-velocity features, we find it plausible that more than one supernova explosion is responsible for the observed SNR signatures. We further use the initial masses and ages of the underlying massive star population to search for clues to the supernova progenitor's properties. Several X-ray point sources are detected within Shell 1, and their nature is discussed. The bright source CX15 may be a neutron star candidate.

title: Probing long-lived particle production in muon decays at the SNS with a highly capable hydrocarbon detector
abstract: The spallation neutron source (SNS) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is a prolific muon producer, making it an ideal location for studying dark sector particles produced in muon decays at rest. In this paper, we explore sub-GeV dark particle detection possibilities in a tons-scale, highly capable hydrocarbon scintillator ( HC 2 ) detector at the SNS. We consider a search for e + e − final states produced by decays of long-lived, O ( 10 – 100 ) MeV axionlike particles and heavy neutral leptons. The HC 2 technology space, exemplified by the PROSPECT and mobile antineutrino demonstrator detectors, offers strong rejection capabilities for the cosmic ray backgrounds that would normally dominate this search. By benchmarking on-surface cosmic ray signatures with data from PROSPECT at ORNL, we generate robust predictions for a multiyear SNS deployment of a range of HC 2 detector implementations. Results indicate the potential for order-of-magnitude improvements in sensitivity to axionlike particles and heavy neutral leptons in the 10–100 MeV mass regime compared to current global limits. We also comment on the neutrino detection possibilities of a HC 2 deployment at the SNS.

title: First Measurement of the D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 μ + ν μ Decay, Study of Dynamics and Test of Lepton Universality with D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 ℓ + ν ℓ Decays
abstract: We report the first measurement of the semileptonic decay D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 μ + ν μ and an improved measurement of the decay D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 e + ν e using a sample of 7.33 fb − 1 of e + e − annihilation data collected at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 and 4.226 GeV with the BESIII detector at the Beijing Electron Positron Collider (BEPCII). We measure the branching fractions to be B ( D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 μ + ν μ ) = ( 2.07 ± 0.2 2 stat ± 0.1 0 syst ) × 10 − 3 and B ( D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 e + ν e ) = ( 2.14 ± 0.1 8 stat ± 0.1 0 syst ) × 10 − 3 . Based on a simultaneous study of the dynamics in two semileptonic decays, the hadronic form factor parameters in the D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 transition are determined to be r V = V ( 0 ) / A 1 ( 0 ) = 1.63 ± 0.1 4 stat ± 0.0 8 syst , r 2 = A 2 ( 0 ) / A 1 ( 0 ) = 0.60 ± 0.1 3 stat ± 0.0 6 syst , and A 1 ( 0 ) = 0.56 ± 0.0 2 stat ± 0.0 1 syst , where V ( 0 ) is the vector form factor and A 1 , 2 ( 0 ) are the axial-vector form factors evaluated at q 2 = 0 . The precision of r V and r 2 is improved by twofold and A 1 ( 0 ) is measured for the first time. We also report the first model-independent measurements of the differential decay rates and the lepton forward-backward asymmetries for D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 ℓ + ν ℓ decays. Based on these measurements, we perform a test of lepton flavor universality in full and separate q 2 intervals with D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 ℓ + ν ℓ decays. No violation is found within uncertainties. Our results present for the first time a complete study of the dynamics in the D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 transition, and provide stringent tests of various nonperturbative theoretical calculations.

title: Charged-current neutrino-nucleus scattering off Xe 129 and Xe 131 including the meson-exchange contributions
abstract: The scattering cross sections of (anti)neutrinos off the detector material in liquid xenon detectors is of great interest in both dark matter searches and neutrino physics. Here it is necessary to use calculated cross sections because directly observed experimental ones do not exist. In this work we provide the scattering cross sections for charged-current (anti)neutrino scattering off the even–odd xenon nuclei 129 , 131 Xe. To do this we use G-matrix-based two-nucleon interactions in large single-particle valence spaces. We model the nuclei involved using the Microscopic Quasiparticle-Phonon Model, constructing the states of the even–odd and odd–even nuclei from BCS (Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer) quasiparticles and QRPA (Quasiparticle Random Phase Approximation) phonons of the neighbouring even–even nuclei. Such calculations have been done before for 129 , 131 Xe, but here we go beyond earlier works by including the effect of the meson-exchange two-body currents (2BC) that can naturally explain a part of the quenching of the weak axial-vector coupling g A . A comparison to a phenomenologically quenched one-body-currents-only (1BC-only) model shows that the inclusion of the 2BC can account for a majority of the quenching of g A .

title: Unexpected Large Relative Strong Phase and Search for Isospin Breaking and C P Asymmetries in J / ψ → K * ( 892 ) K ¯
abstract: Using a direct scan of 26 energy points near the J / ψ resonance, we perform the first measurement of the relative phase ϕ γ , 3 g between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in J / ψ → K ¯ 0 K * ( 892 ) 0 + c . c . and J / ψ → K + K * ( 892 ) − + c . c . Unexpectedly, the phase in the neutral channel is found to be ∼ 15 0 ° , deviating from orthogonality (90°) by 4.8 σ and from a relative real amplitude (0° or 180°) by 12.6 σ or 2.8 σ , respectively. By contrast, the charged channel phase is consistent with ∼ 180 ° within 1 σ , exhibiting channel-dependent behavior. The corresponding branching fractions are consistent with the world averages but achieve better than twofold improvement in precision. The ratios between the branching fractions of J / ψ → K ¯ 0 K * ( 892 ) 0 + c . c . and J / ψ → K + K * ( 892 ) − + c . c . are also measured. After subtracting the electromagnetic contribution, the corresponding strong contribution ratios obey isospin symmetry within 1.4 σ . A search for direct C P violation yields asymmetries consistent with zero.

title: SN 2020hvp: A Normal-luminosity Type Ib Supernova Powered by 56Ni Decay and Magnetar Spin-down
abstract: Abstract This paper presents optical observations of the Type Ib supernova SN 2020hvp. Its multiband light curves decline more slowly than even some slowly declining supernovae, while early-time spectroscopy indicates more rapid spectral evolution. The photospheric velocity near peak, inferred from Fe ii 5169 Å, is approximately 8500 km s−1. The bolometric light curve peaks at Lpeak = 1.93 × 1042 erg s−1, consistent with normal-luminosity Type Ib supernovae. We fit the light curve using the 56Ni model, the magnetar model, and the 56Ni plus magnetar model. Fitting results and the Katz model suggest that SN 2020hvp is mainly magnetar-powered, contrary to the traditional view that stripped-envelope supernovae are primarily powered by 56Ni decay. Derived magnetar model parameters are Mej = 2.89 M⊙, P = 43.16 ms, B = 1.96 × 1015 G, and v = 3.51 × 109 cm s−1. The combined model yields similar parameters but gives MNi = 0.05 M⊙. AIC/BIC tests and the Katz integral method indicate that the 56Ni plus magnetar model provides a better explanation. The energy source of SN 2020hvp appears to be a combination of 56Ni decay and magnetar spin-down: early-time radiation is primarily powered by the magnetar, while the late-time light curve is dominated by 56Co decay. These results support previous studies suggesting that some normal-luminosity stripped-envelope supernovae can be powered, at least in part, by magnetar spin-down in addition to radioactive decay.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Role of neutron skin thickness in α-decay dynamics and implications for multimessenger astrophysics
abstract: Abstract We establish neutron skin thickness as a central structural descriptor of $\alpha$-decay systematics in even even heavy nuclei ($Z=74$ to $94$), revealing a highly constrained structural trajectory in neutron skin space that connects nuclear surface structure to decay dynamics. The neutron skin $\Delta_n(A,Z)$ and its evolution during $\alpha$ decay, $\zeta_{\alpha n}(A,Z)=\Delta_n(A-4,Z-2)-\Delta_n(A,Z)$, exhibit systematic correlations with decay energies and half-lives, establishing a connection between surface isospin structure and decay systematics. Ground state properties from the self consistent Skyrme Hartree--Fock--Bogoliubov framework with UNEDF1, benchmarked against FRDM, DRHBc, and AME2020 data, capture the established shell effects at $N=82$ and $126$, together with the predicted closure at $N=184$. Three principal structural and phenomenological results emerge. First, a global parameterization in $\ln Q_\alpha/Z$ organizes the calculated isotopic chains into a common linear relation with Pearson correlation coefficient $r=-0.9932$, reducing the residual sum of squares by $45.8\%$ relative to the two-coefficient generalized Geiger--Nuttall form. Second, we show analytically that the parent and daughter skin correlation follows naturally from the approximately linear dependence on isospin asymmetry and its kinematic transformation under $\alpha$ emission. The resulting trajectory identifies the regular surface evolution and resolves its structural departures. Third, the skin dependence on isospin asymmetry supplies a finite nucleus diagnostic of the isovector sector. A calibration across relativistic mean field models connects the UNEDF1 $^{208}$Pb skin to $R_{1.4}=12.58\pm1.19$ km and $\Lambda_{1.4}=518^{+385}_{-221}$, with propagated descriptive 95\% prediction bounds, and to the gravitational wave tidal response of binary neutron stars. These results provide a unified structural framework connecting microscopic nuclear structure, $\alpha$-decay systematics, and phenomenologically inferred multimessenger astrophysical observables.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
abstract: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

title: A Multiwavelength View of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5: An X-Ray Luminous and Eclipsing Dwarf Nova
abstract: Abstract We report the independent discovery of the cataclysmic variable (CV) SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 using Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey 12 band photometry, following its initial identification via ASAS-SN variability. Here, we investigate the system using optical photometry alongside optical and X-ray spectroscopy. High-cadence optical light curves from publicly available Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) data and a dedicated campaign at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in Brazil revealed a highly inclined system exhibiting pronounced eclipses with an orbital period of 1.81 hr. We found no evidence of a white dwarf (WD) spin period. Despite seasonal gaps, the long-term ASAS-SN light curve revealed several outbursts (15 with Δmag ∼ 1.5 brighter than the mean magnitude) and one superoutburst over the past decade. During Swift X-ray telescope observations, the system exhibited X-ray luminosity of 8.5 × 10 31 erg s −1 in the 0.3–10 keV band, originating from thermal plasma emission at a temperature consistent with accretion shocks. Optical spectroscopy from the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrographs on the Gemini South telescope confirms the CV nature of the system, showing strong, double-peaked H and He I emission lines alongside a weak He II 4686 line. Altogether, these features strongly support the classification of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 as a quiescent, eclipsing dwarf nova with an unusually high X-ray luminosity.

title: A Coherent Search for New Galactic Magnetars Using Fermi/GBM and Follow-up Swift/BAT: Seven Candidates and a Large Burst Catalog
abstract: Abstract Galactic magnetars are a rare class of neutron stars with extreme magnetic fields, with only about 30 known sources. Their short, hard X-ray and soft gamma-ray bursts provide an important channel for discovering magnetar activity. Wide-field instruments such as the Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) are well suited to detecting these bursts, but their broad localization uncertainties make it difficult to associate individual bursts with specific sources. Coded-aperture telescopes, in contrast, provide arcminute-scale localizations but have narrower fields of view. We search for previously unidentified magnetars and construct a magnetar burst catalog by combining a broad sample of short, soft triggers from our coherent GBM detection pipeline over 2013–2025 with targeted searches of archival Swift/BAT images. We develop a statistical association framework that uses BAT detections to localize GBM bursts to arcminute precision, together with a spatiotemporal clustering framework that associates poorly localized bursts with common sources. Together, these methods identify 1720 magnetar bursts, of which 1170 are confidently associated with 11 known magnetars. The remaining 550 bursts could not be assigned to specific sources. We identify seven candidate new magnetars through three complementary discovery channels. The catalog, composed of the associated bursts, extends to the lowest fluences observed by GBM. We also provide spectral and temporal analyses of the catalog. The new candidate sources provide targets for X-ray follow-up that could reveal previously unidentified Galactic magnetars. More broadly, this work demonstrates how combining instruments with complementary capabilities can maximize the scientific return of high-energy transient observations.

title: Hadronic and partonic composition of QCD matter across the crossover
abstract: We construct a phenomenological equation of state of strongly interacting matter at zero chemical potentials that provides a unified description of lattice QCD thermodynamics in terms of hadronic and partonic degrees of freedom in the temperature range $T=100$-$510$ MeV. The hadronic phase is described by the quantum van der Waals hadron resonance gas, extended by excluded-volume repulsion between mesons, while the quark-gluon plasma is modeled as an ideal gas of quarks and gluons supplemented with a phenomenological interaction term proportional to $T^3$. The two regimes are connected by a smooth crossover switching function. We determine the four model parameters - the meson hard-core radius, the strength of the partonic interaction term, and two parameters of the switching function - by fitting to lattice QCD results for the trace anomaly. In this model, hadronic contributions remain significant up to about $200$ MeV, well above the QCD chiral crossover. We also quantify the crossing contributions generated by the temperature dependence of the switching function. The switching temperature and the hadronic and partonic contributions depend on the chosen equations of state and switching function. The lattice thermodynamic data do not uniquely determine the microscopic composition of QCD matter.

title: Total kinetic energy of fission fragments within time-dependent density functional theory: role of particle-number projection and collective deformations
abstract: Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations of fission fragment total kinetic energy (TKE), restricted to axially symmetric trajectories and a single symmetry-violating mean-field state, underestimate TKE by 10-20 MeV away from the most probable mass split. We reexamine this for $^{240}$Pu and $^{252}$Cf within relativistic TDDFT+BCS, combining particle-number projection (PNP) with an extended collective space including hexadecapole and non-axial deformations. Varying the pairing strength leaves the TKE essentially unchanged, but PNP converts each trajectory into a resolved TKE distribution over fragment mass, and the enlarged collective space is needed to reach the correct scission configurations. Together, these reproduce the empirical TKE mass dependence substantially better than standard calculations, indicating the discrepancy reflects missing symmetry restoration and configuration space rather than a deficient energy functional.

title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
abstract: We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
abstract: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $\lambda_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $\Lambda$-deuteron and $\Lambda$-$\alpha$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.

title: Analyzing Fermionic Dark Matter Scenarios with Anomalous Compact Objects
abstract: In this paper, we consider three compact objects (HESS J1731-347, PSR J1231-1411, XTE J1814-338) with anomalous mass-radius relations to analyze the possibility of their being dark matter admixed neutron stars. We try to infer the properties of the dark matter particles, under the assumption of behaving as a free Fermi gas. The main novelty relies on the use of a baryonic equation of state obtained from first principles over the whole density range, which allows the model dependence of the baryonic part of the calculation to be eliminated. Once the possible dark matter admixed neutron star configurations are obtained, we check their stability and whether it is feasible for a neutron star to capture the necessary dark matter fraction. Our analysis shows that our dark matter model favours the dark matter admixed neutron star hypothesis over the pure baryonic neutron star one, with the most favoured dark matter mass of $m_{DM} = 1$~GeV, although the necessary dark matter content cannot be explained in a standard galactic environment.

title: Transverse Single-Spin Asymmetry Extraction, using both Binned and Unbinned Analysis, including Background Subtraction and Unfolding
abstract: The determination of transverse single-spin asymmetries in experiments involving polarized targets and/or beams may encounter challenges when (1) the magnitude of the polarization varies greatly with time, (2) the polarization magnitude is not the same for each spin state, (3) different integrated luminosities occur for different spin states or different target materials, and/or (4) some kinematic variables require unfolding; these are just a few examples. We present general methods of determining the asymmetry based on both binned analysis and unbinned maximum likelihood optimization, incorporating the unfolding of kinematic variables that are smeared by detector effects, and also including the possibility of background subtraction.

title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
abstract: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians
abstract: Many questions about interacting quantum systems ask which member of a Hamiltonian family $H(\mathbf{q})$ has the lowest ground-state energy, rather than for the ground state of one Hamiltonian. A pointwise scan answers this with one many-body solve per candidate. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) instead holds all $N_q$ candidates in a coherent register and searches them with a ground-energy threshold oracle, replacing $N_q$ solves by $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ coherent oracle calls. We identify static-field (Hubbard-Stratonovich) families as a broad class in which this minimum is a rigorous variational bound that the parent ground state does not reveal, and we make the oracle robust to imperfect ground-state preparation by fixed-point amplitude amplification. The measured search constant places the crossover against a pointwise quantum scan at $N_q \approx 220\xi^2$, where $\xi$ is the overhead of a coherent call. We test the search on realistic sd-shell (USDB) static quadrupole landscapes with up to $10^6$ grid points and on a Hubbard ring with competing orders. It pays where competing minima trap local descent, needing about four times fewer energy queries than multistart descent for oblate-prolate coexistence in $^{28}$Si, and not on smooth single-well landscapes. Circuit-level simulations validate the complete pipeline on a schematic model. The gain concerns the number of energy queries; any advantage of the quantum solver itself is separate.

title: Neural Network Potential Reconstruction from Phase Shifts in Resonant $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ Scattering
abstract: We reconstruct a local, energy-independent effective potential for the narrow $D_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ from elastic phase shifts, using a Gaussian-enveloped neural parametrization coupled to a differentiable variable-phase calculation and checked by independent radial Schr\"odinger solvers. For the first resonance (below $2.5$ MeV LAB), the reconstruction gives a $90^\circ$ crossing at $1.001$ MeV LAB and a derivative width of $85$ keV LAB. The published Dubovichenko potential gives similar values with its original kinetic coefficient. Four reconstructions with adjustable range place the crossing within $5$ keV of one another while their central potentials span $47$ MeV. This spread illustrates the radial ambiguity of the inversion for the measured $D_{3/2}$ phases. The broad $P_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+\alpha$ serves as a benchmark for the same method.

title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$\nu$DEx time projection chamber
abstract: The N$\nu$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms. With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events. With sampled CSA shaping, FFT accepted the same 855 waveforms and direct fitting accepted 866 of 873. On the four-way common sample of 855 events, the direct-fit separation RMSE was 0.180~ms with fixed shaping and 0.217~ms with sampled shaping. An accepted near-readout direct fit outside the FFT sample had a 184~ms separation error, giving an RMSE of 6.25~ms over all accepted sampled-response direct fits. With the fixed response, the full-track fit retained 1,185 of 1,810 observed pads in 100 selected Geant4 events. The median event-level depth RMSE was 0.184 cm. Subtracting each event's mean Monte Carlo residual gave a median event-centred RMS of 0.102 cm as a diagnostic of relative track shape. The absolute depth remains sensitive to the common event time. Validation with detector data is needed to assess the effects of diffusion, electronics noise, and inter-pad response.

title: Population synthesis of low-mass binaries with wind-accreting neutron stars
abstract: We perform population synthesis modeling of neutron star binary systems containing a low-mass main-sequence companion underfilling its Roche lobe. About $10^5$ such systems are expected to exist in the Milky Way. In the majority of such systems, NSs are expected to start accreting the stellar wind matter within a few Gyr, resulting in the appearance of a dim X-ray source. The exact value of this fraction mainly depends on the efficiency of the propeller spin-down, properties of the stellar wind, and common envelope efficiency. Mostly, NSs in such systems are formed in electron capture supernovae. Thus, they obtain a low natal kick. Due to this, the center-of-mass velocities of such binaries are low, too. Only in the case of high common envelope efficiency ($\alpha_\mathrm{CE}\gtrsim 3$), a few tens of long-lived high-velocity binaries can be produced in core-collapse supernovae.

title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r -modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
abstract: Abstract The r -modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes α ≲ 1. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear l = ∣ m ∣ = 2 r -modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency f spin ≈ 792 Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small- α approximations. The star is idealized as an unmagnetized, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r -mode frequency is measured to be f r-mode = 1014 Hz for initial amplitude α 0 = 0.2. The dimensionless frequency κ ≈ 0.7197 agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. The f r-mode increases quadratically with amplitude, and κ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where α 0 is varied through the range 0.2 ≤ α 0 ≤ 1.2. The gravitational-wave strain calculated from the Newman–Penrose scalar implies h r-mode ≈ 9.7 × 10 −22 at 10 kpc for α 0 = 0.2, which agrees with Einstein’s quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g., differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
abstract:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2 eta$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $\alpha$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2
u}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay.

title: The relativistic BCS-BEC crossover in closed form: the cutoff as an effective range
abstract: At zero temperature the mean-field potential of a Dirac fermion with a pairing gap contains one momentum integral, that of the sum of its two quasiparticle levels. We evaluate it in closed form from a geometric construction: the two levels are distances in a plane, and the momentum line is a finite arc of a fixed ellipse, along which the charge, the scalar density and the pair amplitude, summed over the modes, are combinations of Legendre's three elliptic integrals. As the upper limit of the momentum grows, the integral grows by a quartic term, a quadratic term and a logarithm with a known coefficient. The two powers are absorbed into a constant and into the coupling, and with all momenta integrated what remains is a finite combination of Legendre's integrals and the logarithm of one scale $\lambda$. The gap equation and the density of the relativistic BCS-BEC crossover follow in closed form. Once the coupling has been traded for the scattering length, $\lambda$ takes the place of the cutoff that the literature keeps as a third parameter. We show that it fixes the effective range of the channel of the pair: for a pair of Dirac fermions of mass $m$ with the pairing vertex $\gamma_5$, $r_e=-(4/\pi m)[\ln(2\lambda/m)-1]$. At low density and a fixed $k_Fr_e$ the crossover is that of the two-channel model of a Feshbach resonance with the same scattering length and effective range. In the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model the pion decay constant fixes $\lambda$, the effective range of the pion channel is $-8\pi f_\pi^{2}/(N_cM^{3})$, and the constituent mass $M$ of the quark is the one parameter that remains free.

title: Nuclear Excitation by Inelastic Positron Scattering in Hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ Ions
abstract: We develop a relativistic theory of nuclear excitation by inelastic positron scattering (NEIPS) with nuclear hyperfine mixing (NHM) explicitly included and apply it to hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ ions. The target ion is described by dressed hyperfine states, while the incident and outgoing positron continuum states are treated within a relativistic distorted-wave approach. We calculate hyperfine-resolved excitation cross sections for incident positron energies from $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}~\mathrm{eV}$. The cross sections increase strongly with the positron energy, with the $F_g=2\rightarrow F_e=2$ channel exhibiting the largest value. Comparison with NEIPS of the bare $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{90+}$ nucleus shows that NHM enhances the excitation cross sections by about four orders of magnitude. These results demonstrate that NHM provides an efficient mechanism for enhancing NEIPS and broaden the range of nuclear excitation processes in which NHM plays a significant role.

title: Machine learning for trigger, reconstruction and generation
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly embedded in every stage of the LHC data-processing chain, from event generation to final reconstruction. This contribution reviews the latest ML developments from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations that were made public in the year preceding LHCP2026, following the workflow of the experiments: event generation and detector simulation, real-time trigger selection, and online/offline reconstruction. Highlights include generative models that accelerate the simulation of specific ALICE detector components by up to six orders of magnitude, the CMS AXOL1TL and ATLAS GELATO unsupervised anomaly- detection triggers now operating in Run 3, a quantised Deep Sets jet tagger for the CMS Phase-2 Level-1 trigger, ML-based jet energy correction and flavour tagging at LHCb, the first empirical scaling laws for transformer-based flavour taggers in ATLAS, and several transformer and graph- based reconstruction algorithms (ATLAS GN3 flavour tagging and MaskFormer tracking, LHCb GarNet, CMS MLPF) developed for HL-LHC operation.

title: Lightest $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $-3$ and $-6$ within the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations
abstract: We investigate the binding energies and spatial properties of few-body $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $S=-3$ and $S=-6$ using the configuration-space Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations. For the first time, microscopic Faddeev--Yakubovsky calculations are performed for the four- and five-body $\Omega NNN$, $\Omega NNNN$, and $\Omega\Omega NN$ systems. We employ HAL QCD and meson-exchange $\Omega N$ interactions, together with the HAL QCD $\Omega\Omega$ potential, and examine the effects of Coulomb interactions and spin--isospin configurations. The calculations predict substantial enhancement of binding with increasing baryon number, with the most strongly bound $\Omega NNNN$ configurations reaching approximately $60$~MeV and bound $\Omega\Omega NN$ states in the $S=-6$ sector. The results reveal pronounced spin dependence and compact few-body structures, with the $\Omega$ baryon preferentially localized near the center-of-mass. These findings provide new predictions for light multistrange nuclear systems and extend microscopic few-body calculations into the four- and five-body $\Omega$-baryon sectors.

title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
abstract: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/\psi$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $\alpha_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.

title: Coulomb-Induced $K^- pp$ Molecular State
abstract: We study a new bound state in the three-body system consisting of an antikaon and two protons. The state is primarily induced by Coulomb interactions between the $K^-$ and the two protons, and is modified by strong $K^- p$ and $pp$ interactions. This spatially extended molecular state has binding energy and width that are of the order of keV, compared to the tens of MeV binding energy and width of the much-studied quasi-bound $K^- pp$ state caused primarily by strong interactions.

title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
abstract: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.

title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.

title: Probing the neutron skin with extreme collision geometries in heavy-ion collisions

Theory of correlation short pulse reflectometry
abstract: Abstract An analytical 1D model is considered for studying the short pulse reflectometry diagnostic for evaluating the feasibility of measuring the radial correlation length of the electron density fluctuations. Expressions are obtained for the cross-correlation function of pulse delays and widths corresponding to different probing frequencies. The results demonstrate the dominance of the small-scale fluctuations in both signals, contrary to conventional reflectometry. Analytical results are confirmed with 2D full-wave simulations, demonstrating the robustness of the 1D results in realistic probing geometry, but also revealing their sensitivity to nonlinear effects. Additionally, a wide correlation function of the pulse amplitude consistent with conventional correlation reflectometry is demonstrated, providing an upper bound for the radial correlation length within the same measurement.Based on these analytical results, a method for measuring the radial correlation length based on a single probing frequency is proposed and tested numerically. Although it is shown to be affected by both nonlinear effects and probing geometry, it nonetheless provides an order of magnitude estimate for the radial correlation length of the turbulence in 1D-like geometries.

title: The power exhaust constrained SPARC separatrix operational space
abstract: Abstract In this work we extrapolate the separatrix operational space (SepOS) projections to SPARC and introduce detachment access criteria, thus formulating the combined power exhaust constrained SepOS (i.e., PE-SepOS) to evaluate integrated power exhaust solutions at scale. Through the interpretation of SPARC SOLPS-ITER datasets and foundational work already demonstrated in experiments we formulate an as simple as possible description of the SOL net power and momentum losses in dissipative regimes to link the main power exhaust quantities (q ⊥ , T e,t , ⟨c Ne ⟩ sep ) with the SepOS parameters (n e,sep , T e,sep , Z eff , α t ). Through this framework, we demonstrate the utility of a normalized PE-SepOS framework in identifying accessible operational points for given exhaustible P sep requirements. In applying the PE-SepOS framework to project the SPARC operational space, we find inherent trade-offs, namely: i) accessing high impurity radiation scenarios leads to pronounced reductions in n e,sep (e.g., 50% reductions at ⟨c Ne ⟩ sep =2%) as a consequence of power limitation, and ii) given present understanding of access criteria to the quasi-continuous exhaust regime (QCE), a compromise between high radiative fraction and high density/neutral pressure is required for QCE access at sufficiently high density, high α t conditions, with the divertor dissipative regime transitioning to pronounced detachment. We further show that by establishing robust correlations between actuators Γ D,core , Γ Ne , P in , and physics parameters T e,t and ⟨c Ne ⟩ sep , the PE-SepOS framework can be used to inform experimental strategies in scaling up from low heating power to reactor-scale values of P sep /R. Taking advantage of universal trends enabling projections of density and impurity seeding scans, the PE-SepOS thus provides a framework for mapping out the edge plasma operational space in a scalable manner, subject to validation during early SPARC operations with suitable divertor and edge plasma observables.

title: Temperature- and Geometry-dependent grain boundary transport of deuterium in tungsten by hydrogenography
abstract: Abstract Tritium permeation through tungsten plasma-facing components is a key concern for fuel retention, inventory control, and safety in future fusion reactors. However, the extent to which grain boundaries contribute to hydrogen isotope transport in polycrystalline tungsten remains insufficiently resolved experimentally. In this work, deuterium permeation through tungsten is investigated with spatial resolution of 10 µm, using a patterned hydrogenography approach. Recrystallized tungsten foils were exposed to low-temperature deuterium plasma on one side, while hydrogen-sensitive indicator dots, consisting of either yttrium or tungsten oxide thin films, were deposited on the opposite side to visualize the local permeation flux. A systematic study of the temperature dependence of grain-boundary-mediated transport was conducted between 300 K and 700 K using tungsten foils with geometries favoring grain-boundary-dominated permeation. The results reveal an increasing number of permeation-active grain boundaries with increasing temperature. At temperatures of 630 K and above, distinct halos of deuterium flux density form around several grain boundaries, indicating the onset of deuterium desorption and a gradual transition toward bulk-dominated transport. The influence of microstructural geometry was further investigated at 600 K using tungsten foils with average lateral grain size to thickness aspect ratios of (0.2 ± 0.1), (1.1 ± 0.7), and (1.6 ± 0.8). For the two lower aspect ratios, deuterium transport is dominated by grain boundary permeation, whereas the highest aspect ratio promotes bulk transport accompanied by local depletion of permeation near several grain boundaries. These findings provide spatially resolved experimental evidence of grain-boundary mediated hydrogen transport in tungsten and offer constraints for models aimed at predicting tritium permeation in fusion reactor materials

title: Heat and particle loading of SPARC PFCs by lost fusion alphas
abstract: Abstract The SPARC tokamak aims to produce up to 140 MW of fusion power in a Q > 10 burning plasma. With the potential for plasma-limiter gaps of less than 1 cm at the outer midplane, heat loads induced by unconfined fusion alphas on certain plasma-facing components (PFCs) may be significant in these high-power pulses, and these loads can be increased by misalignments of the toroidal field (TF) coils, which leads to TF ripple and loss of fast ion confinement, as well as by misalignments of the PFCs. In this work, simulations of alpha losses and PFC loads in SPARC are performed with the Monte Carlo orbit-following code ASCOT5 based on actual CAD models of the TF coils and PFCs, allowing misalignments within current SPARC assembly tolerances. An asymptotic method is used to approximate peak heat loads to PFC edges on spatial scales smaller than the triangular wall mesh, and the peak alpha-induced heat loads are predicted to be between 2.5 − 22 MW/m 2 depending on TF and PFC alignment. The impact of outer gap size, plasma current, and magnetic field strength are investigated, and temperature rise, recrystallization, and sputtering of tungsten PFCs induced by the predicted alpha loads are calculated, showing that even with the worst possible alpha loads, it will be possible to run high performance pulses in SPARC for 5−10 s, with some restrictions if alignment is poor. These results will be used to inform safe operation of SPARC as it moves into the burning plasma regime.

title: First divertor exposure experiments of a renewable boron pebble aggregate in DIII-D
abstract: Abstract Boron pebble aggregate was tested for the first time as a high-heat-flux granular plasma facing material in a tokamak divertor. Exposures of up to q∥ = 80 MW/m² incident heat flux were conducted in the DIII-D tokamak. Single protruding rods of pebble aggregate composed of sintered amorphous boron pebbles bound with carbon binder were mounted in the Divertor Material Evaluation System (DiMES) sample holders and exposed to L-mode lower single null (LSN) plasmas. Under these heat loads, significant boron dust emission from the boron spheres was observed, and this dust dominates the divertor boron ionization source. Only about half of the released boron was recovered locally as mm-sized particles, with the rest presumably lost mainly as dust into the plasma and vacuum chamber. Preliminary estimates suggest that the rate of surface recession of ~1 cm/s in the pebble conglomerate within the plasma divertor is consistent with the recession rates observed in laser bench tests subjected to normal incidence heat loads. Although core performance was not adversely affected by the high boron dust emission, future work will need to improve the boron pebble aggregate design to reduce boron dust emission at high heat loads.

title: Strange two-photon exchange in timelike electromagnetic form factors
abstract: While two-photon exchange (TPE) effects in spacelike nucleon electromagnetic form factors have been extensively studied for over two decades, their manifestations in the timelike region have yet to be definitively established. We propose the isospin-violating decay J / ψ → Σ ¯ 0 Λ and its charge-conjugate process as a sensitive probe of TPE contributions to timelike hyperon electromagnetic form factors. This channel provides a clean laboratory for isolating TPE effects through sensitive and robust polarization and spin-correlation observables, which are particularly enhanced by the Λ − Σ 0 mass splitting. Combining a dispersion-relation analysis of the one-photon-exchange contribution with explicit loop calculations of the TPE amplitudes, we perform a quantitative study of TPE effects in the threshold region. Our results demonstrate that the considered observables can provide unambiguous signatures of TPE contributions and present predictions for their size together with the associated theoretical uncertainties.

versions.title: Strange Two-Photon Exchange in Time-Like Electromagnetic Form Factors
versions.abstract: While two-photon exchange (TPE) effects in space-like nucleon electromagnetic form factors have been extensively studied for over two decades, their manifestations in the time-like region have yet to be definitively established. We propose the isospin-violating decay $J/\psi \to \bar{\Sigma}^{0}\Lambda$ and its charge-conjugate process as a sensitive probe of TPE contributions to time-like hyperon electromagnetic form factors. This channel provides a clean laboratory for isolating TPE effects through sensitive and robust polarization and spin-correlation observables, which are particularly enhanced by the $\Lambda$-$\Sigma^0$ mass splitting. Combining a dispersion-relation analysis of the one-photon-exchange contribution with explicit loop calculations of the TPE amplitudes, we perform a quantitative study of TPE effects in the threshold region. Our results demonstrate that the considered observables can provide unambiguous signatures of TPE contributions and present predictions for their size together with the associated theoretical uncertainties.

versions.title: Strange two-photon exchange in timelike electromagnetic form factors
versions.abstract: While two-photon exchange (TPE) effects in spacelike nucleon electromagnetic form factors have been extensively studied for over two decades, their manifestations in the timelike region have yet to be definitively established. We propose the isospin-violating decay J / ψ → Σ ¯ 0 Λ and its charge-conjugate process as a sensitive probe of TPE contributions to timelike hyperon electromagnetic form factors. This channel provides a clean laboratory for isolating TPE effects through sensitive and robust polarization and spin-correlation observables, which are particularly enhanced by the Λ − Σ 0 mass splitting. Combining a dispersion-relation analysis of the one-photon-exchange contribution with explicit loop calculations of the TPE amplitudes, we perform a quantitative study of TPE effects in the threshold region. Our results demonstrate that the considered observables can provide unambiguous signatures of TPE contributions and present predictions for their size together with the associated theoretical uncertainties.

title: P-ONE-1: the first detector line of the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
abstract: Neutrino telescopes instrument optically transparent media with three-dimensional arrays of photosensors to detect Cherenkov radiation induced by neutrino interactions within or near the instrumented volume. The small cross-sections of the weak interaction and the low neutrino fluxes above TeV energies require vast detector volumes, which only natural media on Earth can realistically provide. Spurred by the detection of the first neutrino sources by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a new generation of neutrino telescopes is emerging to increase the global instrumented volume and detection sensitivity. The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) aims to install such a telescope in the Northeast Pacific Ocean, building on established neutrino telescope design targets in collaboration with Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). This article presents the design, integration, and testing of the first P-ONE line, P-ONE-1, in preparation for its deployment and integration into ONC's deep-sea observatory NEPTUNE. Alongside the detector design and integration methods, we detail in-air and in-water system-level validation performed at several test sites in Canada, culminating in the successful construction of P-ONE-1 and its preparation for deployment.

title: Multispectral representation of Distributed Acoustic Sensing data: a framework for physically interpretable feature extraction and visualization
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables continuous monitoring of dynamic strain along tens of kilometres of optical fibre, generating massive datasets whose interpretation and automated analysis remain challenging. DAS data can be understood as a time-distance image array. However, the absence of standardised representation methods limits both the physical interpretability and the development of automated image-based analysis pipelines. This work introduces a systematic framework for visualisation and feature extraction of DAS data based on a multispectral signal representation. The approach decomposes strain-rate measurements into predefined frequency bands and produces band-limited energy images that describe the spatial and temporal distribution of acoustic energy across distinct spectral regimes. The framework is evaluated using DAS recordings containing fin whale and blue whale vocalisations. Three experiments are conducted to assess the approach: enhanced visualisation of bioacoustic signals, unsupervised clustering of acoustic patterns, and event detection using a convolutional neural network. The visualisation experiment shows that the multispectral representation allows for the simultaneous visualisation of sets of events that cannot be visualised using the strain amplitude representation. The unsupervised clustering experiment confirms that the multispectral representation yields class-discriminative feature spaces without requiring labelled data, enabling the automatic grouping of acoustically distinct event types. Finally, the use of multispectral composites as input of a ResNet-18 achieves an accuracy of 95.9% in whale vocalisation detection, demonstrating that the proposed representation provides an effective feature space for automated analysis.

title: Design, Testing and Calibration of the GAPS Experiment Si(Li) Tracker Readout ASIC: From the First Flight Campaign Toward the Second Mission Upgrade
abstract: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) is a balloon-borne experiment designed to perform three long-duration flights from Antarctica to search for low-energy cosmic antinuclei, in particular antideuterons, as an indirect signature of dark matter. Its detection method relies on the formation and decay of exotic atoms, identified through the emission of characteristic x-rays and the subsequent annihilation into secondary particles. At the core of the instrument is the silicon tracker, composed of lithium-drifted silicon detectors operated at -40{\deg}C and read out by a custom application-specific integrated circuit, SLIDER32, implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. This thesis reports on the integration, calibration, and validation of the SLIDER32-based tracker readout electronics. Laboratory characterization of a tracker module with an Am-241 source and cosmic muons was complemented by calibration and testing of the full tracker in flight configuration, leading to the first x-ray spectrum acquisition from a Cd-109 source. These activities were part of the integration and testing phase for the first flight, culminating in the complete instrument assembly and validation during the 2024 Antarctic campaign. Building on this experience, the work presents the design and characterization of ANTARES4, a prototype integrated circuit in 65 nm CMOS technology conceived as an upgrade to SLIDER32. The chip integrates eight analog channels up to the shaping stage and implements dynamic signal compression based on dynamic-threshold MOS transistors, together with an improved detector leakage current compensation circuit at the preamplifier input. Its characterization provides a first validation of these design choices, laying the foundations for the next-generation tracker readout to be adopted in the second flight of the experiment.

title: CEDVR: A virtual reality event display for CMS
abstract: Collision event displays are widely used in high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, enabling researchers to visualize and debug raw and reconstructed event data, and to communicate aspects of individual events to broader audiences. Such event displays are typically viewed on a conventional two-dimensional computer screen. To enhance immersion and interactivity with CMS data, we have developed a virtual reality (VR) software package named CEDVR (for CMS Event Display in Virtual Reality) that uses widely-available VR headsets and hand controllers. This application provides an immersive detector-coordinate view and a novel, complementary LEGO-style view. CEDVR provides easy access to physics object properties and object filtering, and incorporates novel VR features for navigation and object selection. Compatible with consumer-grade Quest headsets, CEDVR is a useful visualization tool for CMS physicists, and contains built-in sample events that support educational and public outreach initiatives.

title: TWIN-1: A new 185 to 350 MHz Two-Element Radio Interferometer for Solar Observation at Gauribidanur
abstract: We present details of a new two-element radio interferometer, namely the TWIN, developed for routine monitoring of solar events at the Gauribidanur Observatory (77.428{\deg}E, 13.603{\deg}N) between 185 MHz and 350 MHz. This interferometer is built using custom-built antennas, an indigenous RF front-end consisting of LNAs, power combiners, and high-gain amplifiers, and RF over fiber signal transport modules. A data capture system was developed using a commercial digital storage oscilloscope and controlled with custom-designed Python-based tools. The oscilloscope digitises the RF signals with a time resolution of 0.8 ns, bursts of 9952 time samples, with a nominal duty cycle of 3 seconds, and the resultant data is collected on a remote computer. Specialised tools were developed to analyse the data and detect solar events. The interferometer has been operational since July 2023. In our analysis, we have detected several solar events from the ongoing Solar Cycle 25. This paper outlines the design philosophy, signal flow, commissioning and validation, results from a solar event, and future plans for data capture, data analysis, and archival.

title: Noncontact Chemical and Morphological Profiling in Liquid via Fiber-Based Micro-FTIR
abstract: Liquid-phase mid-infrared (MIR) imaging is challenging due to the strong MIR light absorption of most liquid media. Existing liquid-phase MIR microscopy approaches overcame the background absorption using predominantly either ultrathin liquid cells or attenuated total reflection (ATR) setups. However, these designs introduce additional challenges, such as sample confinement, limited probe volume, probe perturbation, and/or lack of quantification capabilities. In this work, a fiber-based Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) microspectroscopy method was developed to overcome the technical barriers of liquid-phase MIR characterization. By integrating a tapered fiber microprobe, a transmission-based optical setup, and a scanning stage, we achieved noncontact chemical and morphological profiling in liquid. The micro-FTIR capabilities were benchmarked by measuring a micropatterned photoresist substrate in water, obtaining quantitative spatial chemical distribution and morphological profiles with ~35 {\mu}m lateral resolution and nanometer-scale vertical detection limit. This noncontact, quantitative, liquid-phase micro-FTIR technique is promising for non-perturbative characterization of heterogeneous structures in liquids.

title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
abstract: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

title: Determining the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode via X-ray spectroscopy
abstract: This paper reports on a measurement to determine the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode. By measuring the spectra of several X-ray sources and comparing the response between the silicon-carbide diode and a commercial silicon diode, the electron-hole pair creation energy in 4H-SiC is determined to be (7.87 $\pm$ 0.09) eV. This is the first result obtained using X-ray spectra from several sources and including an estimate of the uncertainty. The result is in good agreement with studies of comparable devices.

title: A source-based decomposition of thermal noise for mechanical system design
abstract: Thermal noise limits the sensitivity of precision mechanical instruments. We present a thermal- noise formulation for lumped-element mechanical systems that writes the total displacement thermal noise at the readout as the sum of contributions from all dissipative elements. For each contribution, we separate the thermal force generated by the element from its transfer to the readout. This decomposition provides simple design rules for comparing contributions from elements in series and in parallel and identifying the dominant noise source. It applies to frequency-dependent dissipation and to elements at different steady temperatures under local thermal equilibrium. We use it to identify the frequency regimes in which parallel and series dissipation dilution reduce displacement thermal noise. We then use examples of a pendulum on a lossy support, a rotational flexure, and rigidly mounted lunar optics to show how support noise can dominate even when the support has little effect on the system dynamics. Finally, a feedback-controlled suspension illustrates how sensing and actuation noise can be included in the same displacement-noise budget.

title: Study of the fourth-order term of the symmetry energy based on the generalized liquid drop model
abstract: The fourth-order symmetry energy of nuclear matter and the corresponding $$I^4$$ term of finite nuclei are still poorly known. In the liquid drop mass formula this term competes with the Wigner term, so the extracted symmetry energy coefficients depend on the form assumed for the Wigner energy. In this work the liquid drop mass formula is extended by a fourth-order volume symmetry term and a Wigner term, and three common forms of the Wigner term are compared by fitting the AME2020 masses. With the selected form, the same formula is fitted by bootstrap resampling to the AME2020 data and to the FRDM2012, WS4, WS4+RBF, HFB24 and HFB31 mass tables. This common analysis reads out the second-order, fourth-order and Wigner isospin contributions encoded in each mass table and compares them on the same footing; the experimental table yields a negative fourth-order coefficient, opposite in sign to all theoretical tables. Fitted only in the region of measured nuclei, the theoretical tables give the same negative coefficient, so the sign difference arises from their extrapolation far from stability. The volume and surface symmetry coefficients are then converted into the slope L and curvature $$K_{\text {sym}}$$ of the nuclear matter symmetry energy, and the effect of the fourth-order term on these constraints is evaluated.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Stars on the ascending helium giant branch. II. A metal-rich luminous helium sdO gone astray
abstract: Hot subdwarf stars with masses above sim0.7 M_⊙ expand after core helium exhaustion and ascend the helium giant branch before entering the white dwarf (WD) cooling track. In the first paper of this series, we identified the luminous helium-rich hot subdwarf HE 1518-0948 (HE 1518) as the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger in this evolutionary phase. Here we present a detailed analysis of a second luminous helium-rich O-type hot subdwarf (He-sdO), Gaia DR3 5369742867090186624 (G5369). We derive an effective temperature of 55 000 K, a surface gravity of łog g = 4.85 and an upper limit on the hydrogen abundance of łognHE$>2.5$. The close similarity of its atmospheric parameters and its helium and carbon abundances to those of HE 1518 indicates that G5369 is also likely the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger. In contrast to HE 1518, G5369 is metal-rich, with an iron abundance of about twice solar. The metallicity-adjusted abundance pattern of G5369 for the elements C, N, O, and Ne is broadly consistent with the nucleosynthesis predictions of a composite He-WD merger model and is similar to the observed abundances of R CrB stars, extreme helium stars, and the O(He) star KPD 0005+5106. The kinematics of G5369 place it near the boundary between the thick disk and halo. Its orbit, with a pericentre of ∼3.5 kpc, together with its high metallicity suggests that G5369 most likely originated in the inner Galaxy.

title: Node role discovery reveals novel structural decompositions and topological shifts in complex networks
abstract: Most complex systems can be captured by graphs or networks. Networks connect nodes (e.g., airports) through edges (flights), thus summarizing the system's structure. A popular way of interrogating graphs is community detection, which uncovers sets of close and densely connected nodes. Alternatively, we may ask what a node occupies within a network, and cluster them according to topological or structural similarity, irrespective of the distance and density of connections between them. We exploit to study a series of networks that capture relevant complex systems. In our framework, each graph guides our attention to its key features, in order of salience. Thanks to this, we uncover informative network decompositions that complement community-based analyses. We illustrate this framework for the global airport network, for which we discover a nontrivial decomposition based on airport functionality. We also apply the approach to the U.S. House bill cosponsorship graph, in which we discover a drastic reorganization of cooperation patterns likely driven by polarization. Other brief analyses on more networks highlight the framework's versatility.
