title: Euclid. XI. A two-point correlation approach to diagnosing star-related systematics in the spectroscopic survey
abstract: The Euclid spectroscopic survey will measure galaxy clustering with unprecedented precision, which demands stringent control over observational and instrumental systematics. Among these, star-related effects may contaminate the spectroscopic images through photometric persistence and through imperfect masking of stellar images. We characterized the imprint of star-related effects in the spectroscopic exposures and quantified their impact on galaxy clustering analyses. If these effects produce characteristic angular features, they can be identified and characterized in the data, thereby enabling an assessment of their impact on cosmological measurements. We used angular and spatial auto- and cross-correlation statistics to quantify these effects. For the galaxies we used mock spectroscopic catalogues extracted from EuclidLargeMocks. We focused on a 330 region of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS). For the stars, we considered the real Gaia and star catalogues in the same area. To simulate photometric persistence, we implemented a simplified detector-level model calibrated on spectroscopic measurements and modulated the strength of the effect to introduce varying fractions of `interlopers' into the mock galaxy catalogues. For the stellar mask, we modelled potential inconsistencies between the mask used to remove regions around stars in the data and the mask applied to the random catalogue used to quantify the survey selection function. We measured the star--star, galaxy--galaxy, and star--galaxy angular correlation functions using the Landy--Szalay estimator and quantified deviations from the expected null star–galaxy correlation with a dedicated metric. Finally, we evaluated the impact of these systematics on large scales using the 3D two-point correlation function (2PCF). Our results show that photometric persistence produces a characteristic feature in the star--galaxy angular cross-correlation at scales of order 100 consistent with the scale set by the Euclid dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry. It also induces a spurious, positive cross-correlation signal that remains approximately constant in amplitude up to 1^̧irc. We find that star–galaxy cross-correlation analysis is a sensitive tool for detecting residual persistence and is capable of revealing spurious contamination levels as low as 10% in a Data Release 1-like spectroscopic catalogue. In contrast, mismatches in stellar masking produce strong small-scale angular signatures but do not significantly impact the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.

title: Three-body forces in the quark model
abstract: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.

title: The Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at isospin density in closed form: what a regularization can change
abstract: At zero temperature, the mean-field thermodynamic potential of the two-flavour Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model at isospin chemical potential reduces to a divergent momentum integral of two quasiparticle levels. In practice this integral is cut off at momenta not far above the chemical potentials being probed. We evaluate it exactly, at an arbitrary cutoff, using the Hermite reduction. The result is an algebraic boundary term and three incomplete elliptic integrals, one of each kind. Their modulus, parameter and amplitude at the end of the path are fixed by the triangle formed by the two levels at zero momentum. The power divergences reside in the boundary term, while the remaining divergence is logarithmic: the momentum axis is an open path on an elliptic curve, and the ultraviolet is the puncture at which it ends. The closed form makes the role of regularization explicit. As the cutoff is removed, sharp and smooth cutoffs acting on the momentum alone differ only by an additive constant and by two terms that the vacuum inputs fix. The medium separation scheme reproduces the resulting potential up to an additive constant. By contrast, a cutoff applied separately to the two levels generates an isospin density below the onset of condensation and violates the Silver Blaze property. The closed form gives the state that continues the vacuum along the isospin axis without numerical momentum integration. With the same vacuum fit, a cutoff kept finite gives a visibly different state. The two differ by explicit terms that vanish only as the cutoff is removed: they are different models, not two regularizations of one.

title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering
abstract: The hardware-based Level-1 triggers of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments select collisions with algorithms designed for one signature each, acting on a coarse, low-latency view of every event. We present a learned event embedding for several trigger tasks and evaluate its transfer to processes absent from training. Using paired offline and Level-1 views of the same simulated collisions, we train an offline transformer with a supervised metric loss and distil it, event by event, into a quantised Level-1 transformer whose bit widths are learned under a fixed resource budget. Trained on 25 Standard Model processes, the embedding places 28 held-out processes next to their physical relatives. A nearest-neighbour selection against background collisions, which never enter encoder training, rejects 99% of them. It retains a median of 90% of seen and 96% of unseen Standard Model events and 88% of a set of 52 beyond-the-Standard-Model benchmark samples, the best-performing score across the three groups among the baselines evaluated on the same events. A second gate against the seen processes isolates high-mass dilepton signals into label-free clusters, and long-lived signals too when displaced-track information is available. With 7512 parameters and an FPGA latency of 147 ns, the encoder uses one event representation, learned once, to derive several selections, opening the door to a foundation model for the LHC's hardware-based triggers.

title: Hint of universality in $\alpha$-cluster nuclei
abstract: The empirical ground-state energies of the $\alpha$-cluster nuclei are placed on the universal function that governs $N$-boson systems with a shallow state. The data fall on the finite-range-corrected universal curve, suggesting Efimov-type universality. No excited states, transition strengths, radii, or cluster geometries enter the analysis; the nuclei are treated as $N$ structureless bosons. A zero-shape $\alpha$-$\alpha$ Bargmann potential, describing the $^{8}$Be resonance, provides the pairwise interaction with no shape freedom. Simple three- and four-body forces, each a single Gaussian in the hyperradius, are fitted to $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O; microscopic calculations for $^{20}$Ne and $^{24}$Mg ($N=5,6$) follow as parameter-free predictions. A compact $0^+_2$ state near the Hoyle energy emerges in $^{12}$C without being targeted by the fit.

title: Finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions
abstract: We study finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions, regularized in the relative momentum of each pair so that they remain Galilean invariant. Pauli blocking alone then makes the trimer dispersion deviate from free center-of-mass motion, so the trimer energy can be lowest at finite total momentum. Allowing this motion expands the $abb$ region among pairs and trimers and removes the region where an odd-wave pair is lowest. The $aabb$ quartet lies below all these branches at every sampled coupling, and in a strip starting on the crossing of the two dimer-pair channels its lowest breakup channel is a moving $abb$ trimer and an atom. At weak interspecies attraction, a variational bound shows that two odd-wave Cooper pairs bind into a quartet, whose binding exceeds that of the coexisting trimer by orders of magnitude as the attraction weakens. At stronger interspecies attraction, the quartet binding relative to two unlike-species dimers disappears when the odd-wave interaction is switched off, although the even-wave interaction dominates the interaction energy. Relative to the in-vacuum case, the Fermi sea enhances the weak-coupling quartet binding, and at fixed scattering lengths the quartet binding grows with density while the coexisting trimer becomes much shallower. These results show that neither the most strongly bound pair nor the dominant interaction energy alone determines whether the quartet binds.

versions.title: Finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions
versions.abstract: We study finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions, regularized in the relative momentum of each pair so that they remain Galilean invariant. Pauli blocking alone then makes the trimer dispersion deviate from free center-of-mass motion, so the trimer energy can be lowest at finite total momentum. Allowing this motion expands the $abb$ region among pairs and trimers and removes the region where an odd-wave pair is lowest. The $aabb$ quartet lies below all these branches at every sampled coupling, and in a strip starting on the crossing of the two dimer-pair channels its lowest breakup channel is a moving $abb$ trimer and an atom. At weak interspecies attraction, a variational bound shows that two odd-wave Cooper pairs bind into a quartet, whose binding exceeds that of the coexisting trimer by orders of magnitude as the attraction weakens. At stronger interspecies attraction, the quartet binding relative to two unlike-species dimers disappears when the odd-wave interaction is switched off, although the even-wave interaction dominates the interaction energy. Relative to the in-vacuum case, the Fermi sea enhances the weak-coupling quartet binding, and at fixed scattering lengths the quartet binding grows with density while the coexisting trimer becomes much shallower. These results show that neither the most strongly bound pair nor the dominant interaction energy alone determines whether the quartet binds.

title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
abstract: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.

title: Construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor of the Skyrmion coupled to additional dynamical degrees in the large-$N_c$ expansion
abstract: We formulate an order-by-order construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in the large-$N_c$ expansion of the model where the Skyrmion is coupled to additional dynamical fields. We show that, expanding the equations of motion and the EMT in powers of $1/N_c$, the inclusion of the backreaction to the Skyrmion from the additional fields is essential for achieving the conservation law of the EMT, which is contrasted with the fixed-background approximation where the effects of backreaction are neglected. We apply the construction to the model for hyperons based on the Callan-Klebanov bound-state approach, where the antikaon is bound to the Skyrmion, to obtain the EMT up to next-to-leading order of the $1/N_c$ expansion. We explicitly show that the divergence of the EMT from the backreaction for the Skyrmion exactly cancels that of the kaon to achieve the conservation of the total EMT. We find that the conserved EMT gives a negative hyperon D-term whose magnitude is smaller than that of the nucleon D-term and radii of gravitational form factors for the hyperon smaller than those for the nucleon, which implies that the hyperon is more compact than the nucleon.

title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$\mu_5$ matching in the NJL model
abstract: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $\delta\Omega_r=c_r\mu_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$\mu_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$\mu_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $\mu_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$\mu_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.

title: Binding energy formulas for Skyrme energy density functional and two-parameter density distribution
abstract: Abstract The formulas for the binding energy of nuclei for the Skyrme energy density functional and two-parameter distribution of proton and neutron densities are obtained. The kinetic energy density functional is taken in the extended Thomas-Fermi approximation with accuracy included ℏ 2 terms, and with the effective mass equal to the nucleon mass. It is shown that the binding energy of the nucleus is presented in series on A 1/3 and Y 2 , where A is the number of nucleons in the nucleus and Y = (N -Z)/A is the asymmetry parameter dependent on the number of protons Z and neutrons N in the nucleus. Expressions for the coefficients of the binding energy formula proportional to A k Y m , where k = 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 and m = 0, 2, 4, 6, were obtained. The volume coefficients of these formulas, i.e., which are proportional to A 1 , are connected to the Skyrme force parameters and the density of the nucleus in the center. The surface (∝ A 2/3 ) and curvature (∝ A 1/3 ) terms, as well as the terms proportional to the A 0 , depend on the Skyrme force parameters, the density of the nucleus in the center, and the diffuseness of the density distributions.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Antinucleon--nucleon interaction at next-to-next-to-leading order in covariant chiral effective field theory
abstract: We construct antinucleon--nucleon ($\bar NN$) interactions at next-to-leading order (NLO) and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in covariant chiral effective field theory. The short-range interaction is represented by complex covariant contact terms, while the long-range part is obtained from the corresponding nucleon--nucleon interaction through $G$-parity transformation. The low-energy constants are determined from the Nijmegen partial-wave analysis, and phase shifts and mixing angles are calculated for all partial waves with $J\leq2$. Compared with NLO, NNLO improves the overall description of the phase shifts and mixing angles, particularly in several $J=2$ channels, although the improvement is not uniform across all partial waves or at higher energies. We estimate Bayesian truncation uncertainties and compare the results with heavy-baryon chiral interactions. We also revisit the pole candidates identified in our leading-order study and calculate the corresponding threshold parameters. The isoscalar ${}^{13}P_0$ pole remains a few MeV below the $\bar NN$ threshold with a width of about 40 MeV at both NLO and NNLO, whereas the $S$-wave candidates show stronger sensitivity to chiral orders. The NNLO covariant $\bar NN$ interaction therefore provides a useful basis for studies of antinucleon--nucleon scattering and near-threshold phenomena.

title: A response-based self-energy from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory and its reduction to GW, GW+SOSEX, and GF2
abstract: We construct a frequency-dependent one-particle correlation self-energy by coupling a reference Green's function to the neutral excitation response obtained from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory with singles and doubles (EOM-CCSD). Direct, mixed direct-antisymmetrized, and fully antisymmetrized choices of the external interaction vertices define three approximations, all admitting an explicit spectral representation without numerical frequency integration. In the bare-state limit, the mixed and fully antisymmetrized forms recover second-order Green's-function theory (GF2), whereas the direct form retains only its ring contribution. With a direct random-phase approximation (RPA) response, the direct and mixed forms reduce to $G_0W_0$ and $G_0W_0$ plus second-order screened exchange (SOSEX), respectively. For molecular ionization potentials, replacing the RPA response by EOM-CCSD generally lowers the ionization energies, whereas introducing exchange at one external vertex raises them. These substantial opposing effects partially compensate, although the mixed approximation does not systematically improve upon conventional $G_0W_0$, either against IP-EOM-CCSD or QUESTDB reference energies (aug-cc-pVDZ mean absolute errors relative to the QUESTDB theoretical best estimates: 0.45 vs 0.36~eV). A third-order perturbative analysis reveals that the three approximations retain different contributions and weights of particle-hole diagrams while omitting explicit particle-particle and hole-hole ladder contributions and the static self-energy. In particular, the fully antisymmetrized form recovers GF2 at second order but assigns incorrect weights to its retained third-order diagrams. These findings highlight the importance of a balanced treatment of screening and vertex corrections in constructing accurate self-energy approximations.

title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
abstract: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $\gamma_{\rm v}N\to\Phi_1\Phi_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $\gamma p\to\pi^0\pi^0p$ and $\gamma p\to\pi^+\pi^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.

title: Non-Equilibrium Steady States in Nucleosynthesis
abstract: Steady-state behavior underlies many nucleosynthesis processes in which the population number of nuclei can remain nearly constant despite the rapid nuclear reactions. While existing theoretical descriptions largely focus on established chemical equilibrium, as in nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE) and quasi equilibrium (QSE), non-equilibrium steady states (NESSs) can form in process-specific approximations such as classical $\beta$-flow $r$-process. We develop a general framework for describing NESSs in nuclear reaction networks by formulating the steady-state condition as a balance of reaction flows within a reduced linear description of the relevant network subset. We apply the framework to four representative nucleosynthesis scenarios spanning different steady-state regimes: disequilibrium between nucleons and $\alpha$ particles during $\alpha$-rich freeze-out, the classical $\beta$-flow steady state, the neutrino-assisted $\nu r$-process, and the fission-cycling phase of the $r$-process. In particular, the fission-cycling scenario is described by a quasi-steady-state (QSS) approximation maintaining the population ratios between two nuclei while not conserving the total number of nuclei. The framework reproduces the characteristic abundance pattern for each case while providing a unified interpretation of the underlying steady-state behavior. The eigenvalue spectrum reveals network structure and characterizes the relaxation timescales of abundance distributions. These results establish a general approach for analyzing nucleosynthesis beyond the condition of chemical equilibrium and provide a foundation for extending graph-based methods to complicated nuclear reaction networks.

title: Improved Fusion Yields at the National Ignition Facility via Ramped-Profile Capsule Doping
High-rate accumulation of ${8.9\times10^9}$ positrons using a linac-driven buffer-gas trap combined with a SiC remoderator
abstract: We report the accumulation of $(8.9 \pm 0.9)\times10^9$ positrons in less than 35 minutes in a Penning--Malmberg trap connected to the GBAR electron-linac-based positron source. To our knowledge, this exceeds the largest previously reported trapped-positron population by more than a factor of two and was achieved at an 18-fold higher average accumulation rate of $4.5\times10^6$~e$^+$/s. The accumulated positron clouds are intended for the creation of dense positronium targets to produce keV-antihydrogen beams by charge exchange with antiprotons delivered by the CERN AD/ELENA facility. The system combines a low-energy electron linac, a modified Surko-type buffer-gas trap enhanced by a silicon carbide remoderator, and a high-field Penning--Malmberg trap operated as a positron accumulator. Time-resolved annihilation measurements provide insight into the capture and cooling dynamics, while comparisons of CO$_2$ and SF$_6$ show that the trapping signal reaches saturation at lower gas pressures with SF$_6$. Measurements show that the SiC-remoderator-based trapping scheme more than doubles the trapping efficiency, contributing to a more than threefold increase in the positron accumulation rate compared with the original configuration.

title: Toward Neutrino and Dark Matter Detection with Ancient Minerals: TEM Study of Heavy-Ion Tracks in Olivine
abstract: Solar, supernova, and atmospheric neutrinos, and possibly weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, have been interacting in the Earth beneath our feet for billions of years. The ''paleo-detector'' technique seeks to detect and characterize the induced crystalline defects from these events, in particular from energetic nuclear recoils, which in some minerals can be preserved on these timescales. Such defects can manifest as nuclear recoil tracks, on the order of a few nanometers wide and extending up to hundreds of microns in length, which can be detected with nanoscale-resolution microscopy. In order to test the feasibility of the paleo-detector technique and to study the formation and morphology of track defects in promising mineral candidates like olivine, we use ion irradiation to artificially implant tracks to effectively mimic astrophysical particle interactions. We present a study of heavy-ion track width as a function of depth, which we relate to ion energy, in an olivine crystal irradiated with 15 MeV Au$^{+5}$ using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Unlike previous studies, which measure tracks at the surface of the irradiated sample, we instead take measurements at various target depths via focused ion-beam sectioning of the irradiated sample. No etching techniques are used to enhance the tracks. In addition, we provide a comparison to predictions from simulations using SRIM software and previous results with a variety of ion species and energies. Notably, we find that a significant change in track continuity across the energy range studied (0.4-12.9 MeV) is indicative of the transition between electronic and nuclear stopping power dominance, consistent with the simulations' predictions. Overall, the tracks produced in olivine indicate that this mineral is an attractive candidate for paleo-detection, with robust track creation at the MeV scale.

title: FGPA-based advanced muon trigger algorithms for long-lived particle detection at the High-Luminosity LHC
abstract: The CMS Level-1 trigger must reconstruct muons in real time under stringent latency and hardware resource constraints. Conventional algorithms lose efficiency for high-energy muons undergoing radiative energy losses and can be suboptimal for displaced trajectories, limiting sensitivity to exotic signatures such as long-lived particles (LLPs). The Phase-2 upgrade introduces advanced FPGAs that enable more sophisticated reconstruction algorithms. This work presents two complementary developments addressing these challenges. In the barrel region, a dedicated algorithm detects showers from Drift Tube hit patterns at the first processing stage. At the subsequent filtering stage, shower primitives are correlated with conventional trigger primitives, currently targeting radiatively showering high-momentum muons, with LLP signatures as a broader objective. Simulation studies yield approximately $80\%$ shower-classification accuracy and an estimated matching efficiency above $80\%$ for radiating muons. Firmware prototypes demonstrate a shower-detection latency of approximately $20\,\mathrm{ns}$ and sub-bunch-crossing latency for preliminary matching logic. In parallel, a hardware-oriented optimization methodology is investigated for future graph neural network based displaced-muon reconstruction in the barrel--endcap overlap region. Using a GraphSAGE proxy on a benchmark dataset, a workflow combining integer quantization, power-of-two scaling, and data-driven bit-width optimization achieves $(75.0 \pm 1.1)\%$ accuracy and a deterministic latency of $19$ cycles ($52.8\,\mathrm{ns}$ at $360\,\mathrm{MHz}$), with only $20\%$ digital signal processor utilization. These results establish a basis for implementation studies using CMS muon data.

title: Tritium breeding lifetime assessment of a ceramic-based blanket in a fusion tokamak device
abstract: Abstract Achieving tritium self-sufficiency is a critical requirement for the viability of future fusion power plants. Here, a comprehensive assessment of the operational lifetimes of ceramic breeder materials under neutron irradiation within a tokamak environment is presented, focusing on the evolution of the tritium breeding ratio (TBR) over reactor-relevant timescales. This is defined here as the operational timeframe at which the TBR is maintained above a critical threshold of ≈ 1.10. Using the depletion capabilities within the OpenMC neutronics code, both conventional ceramic breeders (Li 2 TiO 3 , Li 4 SiO 4 , and advanced ceramic breeder—ACB) and emerging hybrid breeder-multiplier ceramics (Li 8 PbO 6 , Li 2 Be 2 O 3 ) are assessed for operational lifetime strategies. Initial optimisation identifies breeder-to-multiplier volumetric ratios that maximise TBR at time zero, followed by time-dependent simulations to quantify TBR degradation due to lithium depletion during service. It is shown that while higher initial multiplier fractions enhance TBR, they also accelerate lithium depletion, reducing blanket lifetime. Conversely, hybrid ceramics with intrinsic neutron multiplication show reduced sensitivity to additional multipliers. A novel layer-wise optimisation approach, varying breeder and multiplier distributions radially and poloidally, is shown to extend blanket lifetimes and maintain TBR above the critical threshold for longer periods demonstrating lifetime limitations may be elsewhere within the breeder blanket. Verification against FISPACT-II confirms the accuracy of the OpenMC depletion methodology utilised. The results highlight the importance of spatially optimised material distributions and lithium inventory management in maximising breeder blanket longevity. This work provides a robust framework for the design of next-generation solid breeder blankets, offering practical strategies to minimise replacement frequency and support sustainable fusion energy.

title: Strangeness, entropy, and chemical non-equilibrium from p+p to Pb+Pb: the $K^+/\pi^+$ horn on the system-size axis
abstract: The maximum ("horn") of the $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ excitation function in central Pb+Pb collisions near $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.6$ GeV is interpreted as the competition between strangeness production and the faster rise of entropy production at the onset of deconfinement. Statistical hadronization analyses by Letessier, Rafelski, and collaborators have shown that the horn is described quantitatively only if the light-quark phase-space occupancy $\gamma_q$ is free, with $\gamma_q$ near the pion condensation limit from 30$A$ GeV upward. We carry this analysis along the system-size axis provided by NA61/SHINE (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, preliminary Xe+La) and NA49 (Pb+Pb). Our main new result is the first non-equilibrium analysis, to our knowledge, of the Be+Be and Ar+Sc $4\pi$ multiplicities, published in 2021 and 2024: in Ar+Sc, chemical equilibrium of light quarks ($\gamma_q = 1$) is disfavored, but through the $K^+/K^-$ asymmetry rather than the pion yields, while the Be+Be data do not discriminate. For central Pb+Pb, our fits to the final NA49 data confirm the earlier result, most robustly at 30$A$-80$A$ GeV; the preference rests on the excess of produced hadrons per net baryon and on the Bose-Einstein enhancement of pions. Decomposing $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ into strangeness and pion yields per wounded nucleon, we find that the step between Be+Be and Ar+Sc is carried by a doubling of strangeness per participant, whereas the horn appears only in Pb+Pb, where the pion yield per participant is suppressed at 20$A$-40$A$ GeV. Parton-hadron transport (PHSD) reproduces the Pb+Pb horn but predicts one also in Ar+Sc and Xe+La, where none is observed.

title: On nonlinear saturation of toroidal Alfvén eigenmode due to thermal plasma nonlinearities
abstract: Abstract The nonlinear saturation of toroidal Alfv{'e}n eigenmode (TAE) due to thermal plasma nonlinearities is investigated using gyrokinetic particle-in-cell simulations and theoretical analysis. Numerical simulations are performed based on the International Tokamak Physics Activity (ITPA) parameters to focus on the evolution and saturation of single-$n$ TAE, either alone or with $n=0$ zonal fields (ZFs), thereby excluding the cross coupling between TAEs with different toroidal mode numbers. Here, $n$ is the toroidal mode number. In the simulations with ZFs filtered out, we find that the saturation level of TAE is governed by thermal plasma nonlinearities for $\gamma_{\rm L}/\omega_n>0.47\%$, which has weak dependence on the linear growth rate $\gamma_{\rm L}$, i.e., ``stiffness'' in saturation level. We find that the frequency of TAE decreases as the amplitude of it increases, which is induced by the phase-space zonal structure (PSZS) of thermal plasmas universally existed in particle-in-cell simulations. The saturation of TAE can be finally reached when the mode merges into the continuum. Following this process, the separation of neighboring poloidal harmonics and mode transition to energetic particle modes can be observed. In simulations with ZFs, ZFs can essentially counteract the effects of PSZS of thermal plasmas, leading to roughly a factor of 2 enhancement of the TAE saturation level compared to the case without ZFs, implying the necessity of including ZFs in evaluating the saturation level of TAE.

title: Near scrape-off layer decay lengths in D, T and DT plasmas on JET
abstract: Abstract The near scrape-off layer (SOL) decay lengths of electron temperature (λ T ), electron density (λ n ), and electron pressure (λ p ) strongly influence the peak particle and heat fluxes to the divertor target, thereby constraining the operational space of a fusion reactor design through power-exhaust limitations. This study compares hydrogen isotopes (D, T and DT) to investigate the dependence of near-SOL decay lengths on the turbulence control parameter α t in ELMy and quasi-continuous exhaust (QCE) regimes on JET. Outboard decay lengths were measured using midplane Thomson scattering, and the separatrix position was determined self-consistently assuming Spitzer–Härm electron heat conduction. Results showed that both λ T and λ p increased with α t and did not contradict the Eich et al. scalings from ASDEX Upgrade (Eich et al. 2020 Nucl. Fusion 60 056016) within experimental uncertainty. These scalings include the dependences α t ∝1/√m i and, at constant α t , a linear scaling of the SOL width with the ion poloidal gyroradius (ρ s,pol ∝√m i ). The λ n measurements exhibited more scatter, indicating different particle and heat transport mechanisms. Trends for ELMy and QCE conditions were similar. Tritium pulses exhibited lower electron temperatures and higher electron densities at both the separatrix and pedestal top compared to their reference deuterium pulses. Divertor configuration affected decay length measurements, indicating that target recycling plays a role not captured by the α t framework. Separatrix quantities n e,sep and T e,sep were consistent with the separatrix operational space model (Eich and Manz 2021 Nucl. Fusion 61 086017).

title: Linear and nonlinear benchmark of gyrokinetic simulation of energetic particle driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes in ITPA TAE benchmark case
abstract: Abstract A new gyrokinetic code, TEK , was benchmarked in simulating energetic particle (EP) driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) in the simple tokamak configuration chosen by the ITPA-EP group for code benchmarking purposes. Linear benchmark has been well established by other codes, whereas nonlinear benchmark for this case is lacking. This paper presents, besides the linear benchmark, nonlinear results for both single- n and multiple- n simulations ( n is the toroidal mode number). The nonlinear results are in good agreement with an analytical theory on zonal field beat-driven by Alfvén eigenmodes, partially verifying the correctness of the nonlinear simulations. The saturation level and the resulting EP transport are examined. This provides data for future inter-code nonlinear benchmarking. In TEK , all species (electrons, thermal ions, EPs) are treated on the same footing using the gyrokinetic model (with electrons in the zero Larmor radius limit). The electromagnetic cancellation problem is mitigated by using the mixed-variable pullback method. Numerical details related to electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulation are discussed.

title: Cross-machine density control experiments in DIII-D and KSTAR with relevance for ITER and FPPs
abstract: Abstract Cross-machine density-control experiments on DIII-D and KSTAR have demonstrated the ability to control the plasma density using an end-to-end, model-based control strategy relevant for ITER and fusion power plants (FPPs). This cross-machine work has proved the generality of density control based on particle-balance models. In addition, the density-control design is adaptive to handle uncertainties in the global particle confinement time and actuator fueling efficiency, and combines actuators with radically different time scales (i.e., fast deuterium pellet injection and emulated slow gas puffing). Prior to \mbox{DIII-D} and KSTAR experiments, simulation testing of the adaptive density controller has been performed for a variety of machine and plasma parameters to replicate the unknown conditions that would be found in experiments. As a result, robust experimental results have been obtained in both DIII-D and KSTAR despite using different plasma scenarios, varying wall conditions, and machine-specific gas and pellet injection systems. Moreover, the density-control models have been extended to a database of ITER-baseline discharges on \mbox{ASDEX-U}, TCV, and JET, highlighting the potential applicability of the modeling approach to future devices when using high-fidelity simulated data. This collaborative work has been carried out under the International Tokamak Physics and Engineering Activity framework, within the Integrated Operating Scenarios topical group.

title: An Innovative Photon-Driven Subcritical Reactor Concept Powered by Synchrotron Radiation Source
abstract: Most reactors are fuelled with enriched uranium, whose production is proliferation-sensitive and concentrated in a few suppliers, and discharge fuel that still contains fissile material and accumulates in storage. Accelerator-driven subcritical reactors relax the requirements on the fuel, but proton beams must travel in vacuum to a spallation target inside the core. Here we show that synchrotron radiation can drive a subcritical heavy-water reactor fuelled with natural uranium or with spent fuel loaded without reprocessing. A photon beam with a critical energy of 10 MeV, from a proposed 32 GeV electron storage ring, releases neutrons in a uranium converter at the centre of the core. Coupled photon-neutron Monte Carlo simulations show that the two cores, loading different fuels but being at a multiplication factor close to 0.985, reach the same gain: one 400 kW beamline drives each of them close to 4.4 MW of fission power, about 11 times the beam power. A storage ring with 50 beamlines could drive one core from each beamline, every core controlled through its own photon beam. These results make synchrotron radiation a candidate driver for thermal subcritical reactors that need neither enrichment nor reprocessing, complementary to proton-driven fast systems for transmutation.

title: A Coupled Source Description of Pseudorapidity Distributions from RHIC to LHC: Emergent $1/\mu_B$ Scaling and Limiting Fragmentation
abstract: One of the most remarkable observations in heavy-ion collisions is the systematic regularity exhibited by pseudorapidity distributions of charged particles across collision energies. While single-source models fail at higher energies and independent multi-source approaches do not reproduce the central dip observed at LHC energies, a unified description across the full RHIC-LHC energy range remains elusive. These distributions from Au+Au collisions at RHIC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 19.6--200 GeV) and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76--5.36 TeV) are analyzed using a novel parametrization based on coupled Gaussian sources where the interaction strength is quantified by parameter $\lambda$. This coupled two-source model captures the interaction between forward and backward sources through the medium formed in the collision. Remarkably, $\lambda$ exhibits empirical scaling behavior resembling $1/\mu_B$, suggesting sensitivity to baryon stopping and the strongly-interacting medium. All fitting parameters follow systematic energy trends, with the peak-to-peak distance and chemical freeze-out temperature exhibiting identical exponential saturation patterns, indicating that geometric expansion and thermal evolution share a common underlying dynamics governed by QCD phase structure. Furthermore, the approach naturally preserves limiting fragmentation behavior across all energies, in contrast to independent source models that suggest its violation at LHC energies. Although the theoretical basis requires further investigation, these empirical correlations successfully unify charged particle production across nearly two orders of magnitude in collision energy, revealing fundamental connections to underlying collision dynamics.

title: Ultrabroadband, high-sensitivity time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy enabled by a Yb-based laser system
abstract: Ultrafast optical fields have introduced numerous novel light-induced states in quantum materials. Identifying these states and elucidating their formation mechanisms require comprehensive, quantitative access to nonequilibrium electrodynamics across relevant energy scales. Here, we develop a Yb-laser-based time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) platform combining multi-pass-cell pulse compression, spintronic terahertz generation, and air-biased coherent detection. A single time-domain waveform scan provides continuous phase-resolved spectral coverage to 25 THz ($\sim$100 meV) with a Fourier resolution of 0.1 THz ($\sim$0.4 meV). This capability enables the characterization of both low-frequency charge dynamics and higher-energy resonant excitations in quantum materials under a common temporal reference. The system achieves a single-scan time-domain signal-to-noise ratio of 72 dB with long-term waveform stability, while preserving most of the laser pulse energy for tunable excitation. Measurements on intrinsic GaAs resolve extremely weak phonon features above 23 THz and demonstrate quantitative retrieval of equilibrium and transient complex optical properties. The resulting platform can provide a more complete microscopic picture of light-induced states in quantum materials.

title: Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of shifts in experimental particle physics collaborations from ranked wishes under institutional quotas
abstract: Experimental particle physics collaborations staff the operation of their detectors with shifts, taken in the control room or remotely by members drawn from dozens of institutions. The established practice for filling them is a credit system with self sign-up: institutions owe a quota of credit, and people take the seats they want when booking opens. This paper describes a method in which seats are instead allocated from ranked wishes under institutional quotas, the result is issued as offers that each person accepts or declines, and an independent checker recomputes every rule before anything is published: the platform proposes, never assigns, and proves that it kept the rules. The credit and quota model is inherited from current practice. Around that core the paper adds a quota rule that keeps indivisible blocks fair to institutions whose share of a period is smaller than one block, and four rules that make fairness visible beyond the count: shares of owl, weekend and holiday blocks, seats shown in the laboratory's clock and the institution's own, reachable pools for institutions that cannot travel, and booking order by balance. On a synthetic collaboration of 48 institutions and 256 eligible members, the method allocates 70 to 72 of 72 seats per period in two rounds, with a mean rank satisfaction of 84 to 95% and no rule broken; after a year of running every institution of four members or more is within 13% of its cumulative share, and the smallest institutions, which one block overshoots by arithmetic, are brought within the same range by pooling in pairs. The method is stated completely enough to be reimplemented; a reference implementation exists and is available to collaborations under license. It applies as it stands to any scientific collaboration that staffs a facility in blocks of shifts under institutional quotas.

title: Probing the X ( 3700 ) through two-photon D D ¯ production in ultraperipheral collisions and at the EIC
abstract: We investigate near-threshold production of the scalar D D ¯ molecular candidate X ( 3700 ) through two-photon fusion in ultraperipheral collisions and at the EIC. The charged and neutral production amplitudes are dressed with a three-channel Bethe-Salpeter interaction in the { D + D − , D 0 D ¯ 0 , D s + D s − } basis. Including the virtual D s D ¯ s channel shifts the bound-state pole from 3.7162 to 3.7205 GeV while preserving the characteristic continuum pattern: final-state interactions enhance the charged channel and suppress the neutral one. Over 3.70 ≤ W ≤ 3.85 GeV , the central calculation gives a charged-channel enhancement of order 13 and a neutral-channel ratio of about 0.34 in both collision systems. Variations of the main model inputs produce sizeable, nonstatistical sensitivity ranges without changing this qualitative behavior. The most direct normalization-independent observable is the integrated charged-to-neutral ratio, which changes from about 0.043 at bare level to 1.70 after final-state interactions.

title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
abstract: Inverse problems for stiff parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs), such as the inverse heat conduction problem (IHCP), are severely ill-posed: the forward map rapidly damps high-frequency interior structure before it reaches the boundary. Soft-constrained physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which embed the PDE as a residual penalty, decouple the diffusivity from the surface data in their standard two-network inverse formulation, and the evaluated variants fit boundary measurements while leaving the interior field essentially untouched. We propose Neural Field Thermal Tomography (NeFTY), a hard-constrained neural field framework for label-free three-dimensional inverse heat conduction. NeFTY represents the unknown diffusivity as a continuous coordinate-based neural network, and at every optimization step passes the candidate field through a differentiable implicit-Euler heat solver with harmonic-mean interface flux, so that the simulated temperature satisfies the discretized heat equation up to the solver tolerance. Adjoint gradients propagate the surface reconstruction error back to the network weights at solver-level memory cost, making test-time inversion tractable on a single GPU. Across synthetic 3D benchmarks, NeFTY outperforms soft-constrained PINN variants, a voxel-grid baseline, and classical L-BFGS voxel inversion through the same solver on label-free volumetric recovery, and it transfers to real thermography data, surpassing classical signal-processing baselines in both defect segmentation and depth estimation. Additional details at https://cab-lab-princeton.github.io/nefty/

title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
abstract: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $\Gamma/2\pi=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $\omega_0/2\pi=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $\omega_0\Gamma$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.

title: Label-free self-calibration of a segmented HPGe $\gamma$-ray tracking array from the Compton scattering constraint
abstract: Pulse-shape analysis in segmented HPGe $\gamma$-ray tracking arrays such as AGATA relies on reference signals for known interaction positions, which are costly to measure and only approximate when calculated. In a simulation of 51 AGATA crystals, we show that the interaction positions can be learned from the pulses without position labels. For a \Co\ photon that is Compton scattered in one segment and absorbed in another, the scattering angle follows both from the deposited energies and from the positions of the source and of the two interactions. A neural network shared by all crystals predicts one position per fired segment and is trained only to make these two angles agree; the unmeasured order of the two interactions and the selection of the pairs are revised during training. The pulses, synthesised from AGATAGeFEM bases for $2.79\times10^{6}$ pairs of fired segments whose energies add up to a \Co\ line, selected from $4\times10^{7}$ simulated decays, include noise, cross-talk, trigger-time jitter and differences between crystals. For the hits of held-out pairs, the mean three-dimensional position error falls from 10.4~mm with the segment centres to 1.65~mm, with a FWHM of 1.0--1.3~mm in each coordinate, compared with 1.07~mm for the same network trained on the simulated positions. The constraint determines the positions along the crystal axes only weakly, and at small scattering angles it pulls low-energy first interactions towards the source, which is why deposits below 200~keV are excluded. Even with the simulated positions, the two angles differ, mainly because a segment with several interactions is described by a single position and energy rather than because of Doppler broadening.

title: In-pixel lock-in readout for wide-field nitrogen-vacancy radio-frequency spectrum analysis
abstract: The growing use of radio-frequency (RF) technologies requires compact, room-temperature sensors that can analyze a wide RF band in real time. Here we present a quantum RF spectrum analyzer based on the gradient-encoded electron spin resonance of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensemble in diamond and read out with a $512\times542$-pixel lock-in camera that demodulates the signal in each pixel. On/off keying the signal under test at the camera's reference frequency lets every pixel extract the spin-resonant photoluminescence modulation. Before digitization, each pixel suppresses the static background and low-frequency noise that limit conventional camera readout. Translating a single permanent magnet tunes the encoded band continuously from 10~MHz to 32~GHz. The magnet position establishes a trade-off between instantaneous bandwidth (up to 4~GHz) and frequency resolution (7--22~MHz), with a 5~ms readout time. The wide-field readout integrates all spectral channels in parallel in a room-temperature sensor head and requires no phase synchronization to the RF carrier. The SNR remains above 70 at an applied power as low as $-32.5$~dBm. The magnetic-field configuration can be adapted to different RF bands without changing the pixel-parallel readout.

title: A Novel Multi-Target Approach for simultaneous enhancement of brightness, intensity, and bi-spectral performance of cold neutron sources
abstract: Increasing the brightness of cold neutron beams is a central objective in modern cold neutron source development, since it largely governs the sample intensity for high-resolution neutron instruments. Raising accelerator beam power is constrained by the target heat-removal limit of 0.5-1 kW/cm2, and increasing the moderator length beyond about 20-30 cm becomes inefficient owing to the finite mean free path of cold neutrons. We propose reversing the conventional design logic: rather than tailoring the cryogenic moderator to a fixed target-premoderator source, we tailor the thermal-neutron source geometry to a high-performance moderator configuration. The concept is realized as a staircase moderator assembly of several shorter compressed moderators, each with its own target-premoderator unit, which distributes neutron production among multiple units and thus enables higher accelerator powers while preserving the brightness advantages of compressed moderators. This approach can provide additional brightness and intensity gains relative to a single low-dimensional or conventional voluminous moderator at the desired transverse beam size and may naturally generate bi-spectral neutron beams, thereby extending the dynamic range of neutron instruments.

title: A Multimode-Fiber Speckle Sensing Node with a Press-Robust Quantized Network for Liquid-Cooling Thermal Monitoring
abstract: Liquid-cooled AI and HPC racks concentrate heat at cold plates and manifolds, below the granularity of facility sensors. We present a self-contained edge node that turns one multimode fiber into a distributed thermal-event sensor over nine pipe segments, with a 450 nm laser, a camera and a Zynq UltraScale+ device that captures, infers, displays and reports over MQTT. The speckle decorrelates within tens of seconds at constant temperature, and a press can change it as much as a 1 degree Celsius rise. The node averages each 20 s window and feeds two planes, the mean pattern and a 19-dimensional temporal-feature map, to a 61.6k-parameter int8 convolutional neural network (CNN) that treats presses as hard negatives and runs in the programmable logic at 565 microseconds per frame. On a 59-session, 70,148-window dataset, session-held-out validation gives a pooled AUC of 0.961 against 0.876 for decorrelation, no alarm during the hold or the 45 s rebound in 23 press trials against 6 and 16, and a mean per-fold step detection of 83.8% at 0.4 false alarms per hour.

title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$\pi$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.

title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.
authors: mar.quest | Marburg Center for Quantum Materials
G. S. Matthijs Jansen (I. Physikalisches Institut
International Center for Advanced Studies of Energy Conversion)

title: lawless: Normalization, Scaling, and Merging of Laue Data in the AIMLESS Framework
abstract: lawless, a new program for wavelength normalization, scaling, and merging of Laue data from both X-rays and neutrons, is presented. Based on the AIMLESS program, lawless provides two methods of wavelength normalization via Chebyshev polynomials and Gaussian process regression, the latter of which is a more general method for various sources. Coupled with AIMLESS gentler outlier rejection methodology and superior error modelling, lawless provides better quality neutron maps than previous methods by focusing on completeness over better-looking merging statistics. Even as R-factors increase and CC1/2 numbers decrease, dataset completeness is the biggest limiting factor in neutron map quality and should be a primary focus in data reduction.

title: XTCP: an open-source FPGA TCP endpoint for readout over 10 and 25 Gigabit Ethernet
abstract: XTCP is an open-source implementation of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for high-rate detector readout. It targets sustained single-connection throughput near the TCP payload limit. In separate 10 Gigabit Ethernet transfers on the same Kintex UltraScale+ KU5P card and Linux host, XTCP and SiTCP-XG each delivered a median application-level throughput of 9.49 Gbit/s towards the host. Towards the FPGA, the medians were 9.49 Gbit/s for XTCP and 5.76 Gbit/s for the tested SiTCP-XG configuration. The XTCP prototype used more lookup tables and on-chip memory. In a 96 GiB echo test spanning repeated sequence-number wraps, recording when an acknowledgement first crossed the recovery boundary allowed four fast recoveries that the earlier signed comparison would have blocked. On one 25 Gigabit Ethernet bitstream, increasing the IP maximum transmission unit from 1500 to 9000 bytes raised median one-way throughput from 23.30 to 24.70 Gbit/s towards the host and from 22.09 to 24.08 Gbit/s towards the FPGA. At 9000 bytes these rates reached 99.7% and 97.1% of the TCP payload limit, respectively. In a separate echo test, the host verified all 8.77 TB returned by a jumbo-frame prototype over one connection in 3595 s, averaging 19.51 Gbit/s per direction.

title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.

title: Rotating Capacitive System for Measurement of a Third Order Gravity Gradient Based on a Single-Axis Mechanical Oscillator. Part I, Theory
abstract: This paper is a feasibility study on a single-axis mechanical oscillator, mounted on a miniature circular rotating platform, that is proposed to be used for measuring a quantity proportional to the second vertical derivative of gravitational acceleration projected onto the oscillator's sensitivity axis. The latter is aligned with the axis of rotation. Part I establishes theoretical feasibility only. Design constraints, quantitative sensitivity, error budgets, and mobile platform performance will be addressed in Part II.

title: Quark and gluon gravitational form factors of the nucleon at next-to-leading order
abstract: We compute the quark and gluon gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the nucleon in three-point QCD sum rules at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$ for the quark and gluon energy-momentum tensors (EMT), treating both at the same order in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme. The nucleon EMT also tests the method, showing where the sum rules are reliable and why. Protected estimators of $D$ and of the trace form factor $\bar c$ require antisymmetric Borel moments, since none with equal Borel masses alone is protected. The $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections reduce $A_{\rm tot}$ by $32$--$40\%$, $J_{\rm tot}$ by $22$--$27\%$ and $|D_{\rm tot}|$ by $21$--$27\%$, since the perturbative share of the two-point function is much larger. The total form factors agree with lattice QCD for $1\le Q^2\le2.5$~GeV$^2$. At $Q^2=1.5$~GeV$^2$, $A_{\rm tot}=0.337\pm0.113$, $J_{\rm tot}=0.206\pm0.100$ and $D_{\rm tot}=-0.206\pm0.121$. $D$ is the most reliable result: its correlator is mostly perturbative, and its quark and gluon parts agree with the lattice. In $A$ and $J$, a local gluon-condensate term that does not fall with $Q^2$ is the largest, and their gluon shares are well below the lattice, possibly because the gluon EMT couples at this order only through gluon exchange and the condensate. A working region exists only near $\beta=1$, and the constant part of transitions cannot be separated within the Borel windows. The individual conservation identities deviate at one point by two standard deviations, consistent with a missing finite term in the $g_{\mu\nu}$ structure, and $\bar c$ is therefore given at leading order with condensates.

title: Neutral and Charged Pion Modes in Magnetized Quark Matter with Chiral Imbalance
abstract: We investigate neutral and charged pion correlations in a two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model at finite temperature in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and a prescribed chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$, using the mean-field approximation and the single-channel random phase approximation (RPA). The pion masses are defined by the selected positive-energy zeros of the real parts of the corresponding inverse propagators. We demonstrate that, at zero external spatial momentum, the complete Dirac trace in the neutral channel eliminates mixed-branch contributions, thereby precluding a finite-energy Landau cut. In contrast, the charged channel allows non-diagonal Landau-level transitions and exhibits both pair-production and thermal-scattering contributions. With increasing $\mu_5$, the neutral-pion mass exhibits only a weak variation at low temperature, while the rapid decrease of the mass shifts toward higher temperatures. The charged-pion mass decreases with increasing $\mu_5$ over the selected solution segments. This behavior may help account for the lattice QCD results. At zero temperature and fixed $\mu_5$, increasing the magnetic field lowers the neutral-pion mass but raises the charged-pion mass.

title: Machine-learning-assisted photon pairing for neutral-pion reconstruction at future Higgs factories
abstract: Neutral-pion ($\pi^0$) reconstruction is important for precision measurements at high-energy colliders, particularly in flavor, $\tau$, and Higgs physics. We study $\pi^0$ candidate selection in four benchmark physics processes at electron--positron colliders, comparing an optimized diphoton mass-window (MW) baseline with four machine-learning methods: a boosted decision tree (BDT), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), ParticleNet (PN), and Particle Transformer (ParT). Performance is evaluated using the product of selection efficiency and purity. At the reference ECAL energy resolution, all four machine-learning methods outperform MW. PN and ParT achieve relative improvements of 53%--95% and 60%--128%, respectively, primarily through better rejection of incorrectly matched photon pairs. Their performance advantage is maintained across the investigated ECAL energy resolutions. Training-sample-size scans reveal two periods of rapid performance improvement separated by slower growth in most PN and ParT learning curves. The improved candidate selection provides a starting point for further studies of $\rho$ and hadronic $\tau$ reconstruction.

title: Ion Backflow Suppression and Absorption Dynamics in Cascaded GEM Structures
abstract: Ion backflow (IBF) is a persistent challenge in Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors: positive ions drifting back into the sensitive volume distort the drift field and degrade both spatial and energy resolution. We investigate the ion-absorption characteristics of single- to quintuple-GEM detectors using ANSYS and Garfield$^{++}$ for an Ar/CO$_2$ (70:30) gas mixture. A layer-resolved formalism is developed that distinguishes conditional foil-level absorption from a detector-level absorption metric that correctly weights ion production at every amplification stage. For the conventional biconical geometry, cascading foils improves the overall ion-absorption fraction only moderately, from 47.83\% for a single GEM to 59.06\% for a quintuple GEM. Replacing the biconical holes with a single-conical profile raises the absorption fraction to 75\%-87\% across the same range of multiplicities and reduces the IBF/Gain ratio by a factor of two to three an improvement that exceeds what is gained by adding four additional biconical foils. As a secondary test under more realistic conditions, the second transfer-gap length of a triple-GEM detector is varied from 1.2 to 3.5~mm. The gain shows a non-monotonic dependence with a maximum near 2.0-2.5~mm, while the IBF/Gain ratio decreases monotonically with increasing gap length; the single-conical geometry retains its factor-of-two advantage throughout. These findings establish that ion suppression in cascaded GEM structures is governed not only by the number of foils but primarily by the local ion-collection properties of each foil, and that single-conical holes represent a promising route to improved performance in high-rate detector applications.

title: Impact of Gain Layer Doping Concentration on the Performance of 4H-SiC LGADs
abstract: Gain layer doping concentration determines the electric field profile in a low gain avalanche detector (LGAD) and is therefore the primary design parameter. This work reports its influence on the charge collection and timing behavior of 4H-SiC LGADs. Two mesa-isolated devices with cold He ion implanted termination differ only in gain layer doping, $4\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$ and $5\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$, and are characterized together with a PIN diode from the same wafer using the ultraviolet transient current technique (UV-TCT). The 25\% doping difference produces a gain difference of about two orders of magnitude at the same applied bias, representing a gain range of 3.7 to 216. Under UV-TCT excitation, the higher-doped device exhibits time-resolution minima within a gain range of about 20--80 across the investigated laser intensities, consistent with the transition from electronic-noise-dominated jitter to multiplication shot noise. The non-monotonic timing response is also observed under a $^{90}Sr$ beta source with a Si LGAD reference: the higher-doped device reaches 51.7 ps at 280 V and then degrades, while the lower-doped device requires more than 450 V. This measured gain window provides an experimental reference for further optimization of the gain-layer design.

title: HEP-like 1550 nm wide-field pixelated optical receiver for inter-satellite laser links: a simulation-based proof of concept for Earth, lunar and Earth-Moon scenarios
abstract: I propose and evaluate by simulation a wide-field dome optical receiver (a field of view larger than a hemisphere) at 1550 nm for the acquisition of inter-satellite laser links. The detector is an InGaAs pixel hybrid of about 1 Mpixel with event-driven, time-stamped readout, inspired by the pixel detectors of high-energy physics. A pulsed beacon is detected by the coincidence of m hits in a sliding block of pixels, and the angle of arrival (AoA) is estimated by clustering and centroiding and handed to a narrow-field data channel. In a 550 km Earth constellation, with a 5 mrad beacon and a 10 mm aperture, detection takes 12 $\mu$s to 2 ms (up to 116 ms with the 6-9 mm that the optics allow), with a whole-frame false-alarm rate below 0.01/s, and the AoA error is 0.13-0.23 mrad. Cooling to about 233 K gives a service life above 5 years for fluences up to about $2\times10^{9}$ p/cm$^2$ per year. The receiver is also studied around the Moon and on the Earth-Moon link, where it works only between high orbits. Compared phase by phase with published scan-based acquisition, the search phase (3-18 ms with 10 mm) is shorter by a factor of about $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}$; end to end, with assumed pointing and loop-closure times, it takes 0.16-1.5 s, comparable to a terminal with calibrated open-loop pointing but without requiring that pointing at the receiver; the partner's beacon must still be pointed at it to about 1.25 mrad (5 mrad beacon). All values are simulation results, obtained with idealised optics and a 1 Mpixel detector that does not exist today; none is a measurement.

title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
abstract: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.
