title: D 0 − D s + elliptic-flow splitting under event-shape engineering: A probe of sequential charm hadronization
abstract: Recent work has proposed sequential hadronization of open-charm hadrons in the quark-gluon plasma, wherein more tightly bound species such as D s + form earlier near 1.2 T c and D 0 forms later at T c . That work showed that this mechanism naturally reverses the sign of the D 0 − D s + elliptic-flow splitting Δ v 2 ≡ v 2 ( D 0 ) − v 2 ( D s + ) relative to the conventional simultaneous baseline. In this work, we demonstrate that event-shape engineering (ESE) provides a sharper discrimination between the two pictures than inclusive measurements alone. By selecting large- q 2 and small- q 2 events in 0–10% and 30–50% centrality classes in Pb–Pb collisions at s NN = 5.02 TeV , we show that the geometry-driven enhancement of charm-meson v 2 can be separated from the hadronization-time response: the positive Δ v 2 ( D 0 − D s + ) at intermediate p T in the sequential scenario grows systematically with q 2 , while the corresponding response slope χ reveals a species-dependent hierarchy χ ( D 0 ) > χ ( D s + ) that is robust against the overall flow normalization and absent in the simultaneous baseline. In the simultaneous case, the splitting is near zero or negative and does not follow the same geometry scaling. Notably, the semicentral 30–50% class emerges as the optimal window, because the nonmonotonic interplay between quark-gluon plasma lifetime and initial eccentricity maximizes the late-stage flow conversion. The q 2 ratios of the D s + / D 0 yield ratio remain close to unity, supporting that the splitting is a dynamical flow effect rather than a chemical yield modification. These results suggest Δ v 2 ( D 0 − D s + ) and the response slope χ under ESE as complementary differential probes of the space-time structure of charm hadronization near the QCD transition temperature.

title: Landau-Zener formula and resonant axion conversion in neutron star magnetospheres
abstract: We investigate the Landau-Zener description of resonant axion-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres. We find that this picture often fails for axion conversions to millimeter-to-optical band photons due to the characteristic resonance width exceeding the size of the conversion region. This comparison of scales yields a simple criterion for evaluating the validity of the Landau-Zener formula. We verify this criterion numerically, and show that when invalid, the Landau-Zener conversion probability may significantly deviate from the numerical result. In light of these findings, we revise constraints on axions from neutron star optical-band polarization searches.

title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
abstract: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 exhibited persistent X-ray activity for more than 26 years after its discovery, prior to entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest that this low X-ray state results from the emergence of a complex layer of absorbing material, whose exact nature remains unknown. Since the X-ray emission is obscured, radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes associated with this phase. Recently published Very Large Array (VLA) and East Asian VLBI Network (EAVN) observations have revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). Here, we present higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) and European VLBI Network (EVN) during the early X-ray obscuration phase across four epochs spanning 2019--2021, sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. In this paper, we focus on the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes across the four epochs and contextualize these in relation to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many of the PAs measured post-2018 are significantly offset from GRS 1915+105's pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of 142^ ̧irc ± 7^ ̧irc on milliarcsecond scales. We find a maximum offset of 57^ ̧irc ± 8^ ̧irc from this axis, the largest such offset reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our four epochs reveal a broad variety of jet behaviours, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similarly large offset, to an extended jet with a PA that is closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and finally to a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual eight-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, given the timescales involved, coupled with the system's geometry and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration event, favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, in a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

title: Information content of the Gamow Teller resonance: Bayesian inference with self-consistent Skyrme models
abstract: Many important charge-exchange weak processes, such as beta decays, double beta decays, and neutrino-nucleus and neutrino-nucleon reactions, are closely related to the spin- and isospin-dependent nuclear force, yet few of them can be precisely measured, or even observed, in terrestrial experiments. The Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR) in finite nuclei is one of the few experimental probes of this spin-isospin force. In a companion letter, we obtained the probability distribution of the Landau-Migdal parameter $G'_0$, which characterizes the main part of the spin-isospin force, from GTR measurements using Bayesian inference. In this follow-up work, we quantitatively study the correlations emerging from this Bayesian analysis. From the posterior, we identify two standard Skyrme parameterizations (nuSky*) that reproduce, in a unified manner, ground-state observables of finite nuclei, the salient features of the GTR, and the bulk properties of neutron-star matter. Since collective excitations in finite nuclei and in neutron-star matter are related, we use the Skyrme interactions sampled from the posterior to constrain the axial-current, charged-current neutrino-nucleon reaction rates in hot and dense compact-star matter, as the first astrophysical application of this study. The GTR-informed calculations substantially reduce the spread of the neutrino opacity; nevertheless, significant uncertainties remain due to the poorly constrained symmetry energy at sub-saturation densities. Constraining this quantity on top of a well-constrained spin-isospin interaction would pave the way towards a systematic determination of neutrino interactions in dense matter.

Parameter scan of multi-fluid equilibria in rotating p-11B plasmas: Effects on fusion power and Bremsstrahlung losses
abstract: Abstract We investigate how temperature, reference density, fuel-ion ratio and rotation affect the fusion power and bremsstrahlung losses of prescribed-profile p-¹¹B equilibria. The multi-fluid equilibrium solver VEQ-MF (Veloce Equilibrium–Multi-Fluid) couples generalized Boltzmann density responses and quasineutral electrostatic polarization to a spectral Grad–Shafranov solver, and evaluates the resulting fields with a drift-Maxwellian fusion reactivity and a relativistic bremsstrahlung model. For four cases with the same prescribed inputs, the finite-difference and VEQ-MF results agree to within 0.49% in total stored energy and both powers. Parameter scans in the EHL-2 and EHL-3B geometries show that the ion and electron temperatures affect the reaction-rate and radiation responses differently, while both modify the equilibrium density distribution. Increasing the reference density raises both powers almost quadratically and changes their ratio much less. At fixed reference electron density, varying the fuel-ion ratio f = N_B0/N_p0 produces a broad maximum in the fusion-to-bremsstrahlung ratio near f = 0.08 in the equal-rotation case examined here. When protons and boron ions rotate toroidally at the same angular velocity, faster rotation promotes outboard boron accumulation and increases bremsstrahlung. Reducing the boron angular velocity while holding the proton rotation fixed weakens the electrostatic polarization and lowers the radiation. Relative toroidal flow raises the effective reaction-rate coefficient over the range examined here, and the competition between this coefficient and the proton–boron overlap determines the total fusion-power response.

title: Hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation for disruption prediction in EAST
abstract: Abstract Plasma disruption is a critical threat to tokamak safety. Existing data-driven predictors mainly rely on time-series diagnostic signals, while visible images provide complementary spatial cues including plasma deformation, local brightening, and radiation-structure evolution. Although the image modality improves the model's discriminative capability, it also substantially increases the computational cost during inference. To address this issue, we propose a hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation framework for disruption prediction on a synchronized EAST multimodal dataset. During training, visible images and time-series signals are used to train a multimodal teacher, which learns plasma representations through Transformer-based encoders and a prototype-guided spatiotemporal hypergraph module. During inference, only the time-series student is retained, with multimodal knowledge transferred through graph-structure-level, representation-level, and decision-level distillation. On the 1307-discharge EAST dataset, at FPRs of 10% and 5% under a 10 ms valid-warning constraint, the multimodal teacher achieves strong performance, attaining TPRs of 98.77% and 97.53%, respectively, and an AUC of 99.15%. The distilled unimodal student, which relies on time-series inputs during inference, still achieves TPRs of 92.59% and 81.48% at FPRs of 10% and 5%, respectively, and an AUC of 95.77%. Meanwhile, it requires only 3.13 ms for inference, 26.50 G FLOPs, and 23.18M parameters. Compared with the multimodal teacher, the distilled student achieves a 2.59× inference speedup and reduces the FLOPs and parameter count by approximately 66.06% and 47.15%, respectively. The similarity analysis confirms that the distilled student inherits the teacher's discriminative capability in latent representation, decision boundary, and structural preference. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can preserve the discriminative advantages of multimodal learning while substantially reducing inference cost, and provide an effective route for efficient disruption prediction in EAST.

title: Erosion profiles in strongly magnetised plasmas
abstract: Abstract Ion-induced erosion of an electrode in strongly magnetised Capacitively Coupled Plasmas (CCP) is governed by anisotropic transport along magnetic field lines, leading to spatially non-uniform and often poorly characterised erosion patterns. In particular, the coupled influence of ion energy and angular distributions, plasma geometry, and magnetic-field orientation on erosion remains insufficiently understood.In this work, spatially resolved erosion profiles of semi-circular molybdenum-coated copper electrodes are experimentally investigated in an argon CCP operated at a magnetic field of 3 T. The experimental configuration enables independent variation of key parameters, including the angle between the electrode surface and the magnetic field defined as θ, the plasma column connection length to the nearest grounded surface, set via a counter-electrode, the plasma column shape through electrode rotation, and the sheath thickness through controlled self-bias. Plasma parameters were not measured directly, as their determination was beyond the scope of this erosion-focused study and remains experimentally challenging under strong magnetic field conditions. Coating erosion was quantified using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy combined with a multi-energy, standard-based analysis.The results reveal a non-monotonic dependence of erosion on θ, reflecting the interplay between ion energy and angular distributions shaped by the magnetic pre-sheath. In addition, the erosion profiles are shown to depend strongly on the plasma geometry: electrode geometry imprints the plasma column topology, while variations in connection length lead to local ion-flux asymmetries along magnetic field lines. Finally, increasing sheath thickness expands the effective ion collection region, resulting in a redistribution of ion flux and a localised enhancement of erosion at low angles. These findings demonstrate that erosion in magnetised CCPs is governed by the coupled effects of anisotropic transport, sheath dynamics, and plasma-column geometry, and cannot be captured by ion-flux variations alone, providing new insight into plasma-surface interaction and material erosion under strong magnetic fields.

title: Bayesian optimization of stellarator alpha-particle confinement using data-informed parameter spaces and dimensionality reduction
abstract: Abstract Modern stellarators are typically designed by optimizing the shape of the plasma boundary surface, with the parameters taken to be Fourier amplitudes. Many promising optimization algorithms such as Bayesian methods require bound constraints on the parameters and are most efficient when each parameter is scaled similarly to the others. With the typical Fourier parameterization, it is unclear how to set these bounds: wide constraints lead to self-intersecting boundaries and frequent failures of the MHD equilibrium calculation, while tight bound constraints limit expressiveness. To address these issues, here we propose two new parameter spaces for stellarator optimization. Both begin with a dataset of existing stellarator boundaries. In the first approach, a quantile transformation is applied to each Fourier degree of freedom, mapping the data distribution to a uniform distribution on the unit interval. In the second approach, principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to points on the boundaries, followed by a quantile transformation. For both approaches, the transformed variables become the degrees of freedom, naturally bounded to [0, 1]. The PCA method has the additional benefit of dimensionality reduction, with high expressiveness for a small number of parameters. The methods are demonstrated via Bayesian optimization for good alpha-particle confinement with guiding-center tracing inside the optimization loop, using asynchronous parallelization. These optimizations yield stellarator configurations with excellent collisionless fast-particle confinement in fields that can be far from quasisymmetric or quasi-isodynamic.

title: Asymptotic normalization coefficient of the 14O→13O+n configuration from the peripheral 14O(d,t)13O reaction
abstract: The neutron transfer reaction [Formula: see text]O[Formula: see text]O at a deuteron energy of 34.6[Formula: see text]MeV has been analyzed within the Modified Distorted Wave Born Approximation (MDWBA) framework. The angular distribution of the reaction was calculated and compared with the available experimental data to investigate the reaction mechanism and determine the degree of peripheral character at the main angular-distribution maxima. The analysis demonstrates that the reaction is predominantly peripheral in the angular region corresponding to the principal maxima, indicating that the measured cross section is sensitive to the asymptotic part of the [Formula: see text] overlap function. Exploiting this peripheral behavior, an experimental Asymptotic Normalization Coefficient (ANC) for the [Formula: see text] configuration was extracted for the first time. The resulting ANC value is [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]fm[Formula: see text]. This result provides an important experimental constraint on the asymptotic properties of the [Formula: see text]O ground state overlap and demonstrates the applicability of the MDWBA method for extracting a reliable ANC value from a peripheral neutron transfer reaction.

title: Theoretical investigation of neutron shell gap at N=100
abstract: Experimental pairing gap values deduced from binding energy and energy of the first [Formula: see text] state show certain discontinuities in rare-earth nuclei around [Formula: see text]. The neutron single-particle levels in even–even [Formula: see text] nuclei around [Formula: see text] have been studied using Skyrme–Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov method with the Skyrme energy density functional SLy6 as well as with Gogny interaction D1N. We find that both interactions show a deformed shell gap at [Formula: see text]. This gap plays an important role in determining r-process abundances.

title: A Surrogate Detector Model for the MINERvA Open Dataset
abstract: The growing availability of open neutrino data promises broader scrutiny of interaction models, but a critical barrier remains: mapping theoretical predictions into reconstructed observables, which previously required computationally intensive methods inaccessible outside the original experimental collaborations. In this work, we present a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset to map generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables, without relying on generator-specific interaction labels. We assess its fidelity through conditional response distributions, reconstructed observables, and classifier-based closure tests. We further demonstrate generalization beyond the limitations of conventional phase-space-dependent reweighting by withholding two-particle-two-hole interactions entirely from training and showing that the surrogate reproduces their reconstructed response within the estimated uncertainties. In an end-to-end application to MINERvA charged-current inclusive muon-neutrino data, we reproduce selection efficiencies and purities and forward-fold predictions from GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU for direct comparison with measurements. By moving theoretical predictions into reconstructed space rather than unfolding the data, this work establishes a reusable interface between neutrino interaction models and experimental observations, expanding the scope of physics accessible through open datasets.

title: Measurements of inclusive $J/\psi$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
abstract: Inclusive $J/\psi$ production at mid-rapidity ($|y| < 1.0$) in Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon-nucleon pair ($\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$) of 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV is measured with the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The nuclear modification factor $R_{{\rm AA}}$ is used to quantify modifications of $J/\psi$ production relative to an interpolated $p$+$p$ reference. The measured $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows a hint of a decreasing trend from peripheral to central collisions, reaching a value of approximately 0.5 in the 0-20% centrality class across all collision energies. Unlike similar measurements in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 200 GeV, where $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows little dependence on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm {T}}$), the corresponding $R_{{\rm AA}}$ at the lower collision energies of 14.6-27 GeV shows a tendency to increase with $p_{\rm {T}}$. Additionally, the inclusive $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$, integrated over $J/\psi$ $p_{\rm {T}}$, in central collisions exhibits no significant variation within uncertainties over the energy range of 14.6 to 200 GeV. These results can be qualitatively described by transport models that incorporate hot and cold nuclear matter effects.

title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
abstract: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

title: Testable leptogenesis and 0 ν β β decay in extended seesaw model
abstract: We investigate the possibility of observable neutrinoless double beta decay ( 0 ν β β ) and viable leptogenesis within a low-scale extended inverse seesaw mechanism with additional sterile neutrinos. General effective field theory considerations suggest that if there are experimentally observable signatures in 0 ν β β decay and a lepton asymmetry generated by heavy right-handed neutrino decays, thermal leptogenesis is likely to be unviable. However, in this work, we show that, in the context of low-scale leptogenesis, one can obtain the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe and observable signatures of 0 ν β β decay in the presence of additional sterile neutrinos. In this framework, the light neutrino masses are suppressed by the extended seesaw parameter μ , thereby allowing for O ( 10 TeV ) right-handed neutrinos while avoiding small Yukawa couplings as in other neutrino mass models and near degeneracies in the right-handed neutrino spectrum as required by the low-scale leptogenesis paradigm. Contributions to the 0 ν β β -decay rate from additional sterile neutrinos can be appreciable, while the corresponding contributions to the early Universe lepton asymmetry washout rate are suppressed by other parameters not entering the 0 ν β β -decay amplitudes. We show that, for keV–MeV scale, sterile neutrinos future ton-scale 0 ν β β -decay experiments offer potential signals while maintaining viable leptogenesis.

title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks
abstract: Abstract Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO 2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four ‘AI-dreamt’ MOFs.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Light-particle emission in nucleon-induced fission of $^{235,238}$U at energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV
abstract: Background: In nucleon-induced fission up to GeV energies, early nonequilibrium emission alters the residual nuclei before statistical evaporation and scission. The emitted light particles therefore probe each reaction stage while supplying needed nuclear data. Purpose: We study neutron and light charged-particle emission in $^{235,238}$U$(n,f)$ and $^{235,238}$U$(p,f)$ reactions at incident energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV. Methods: The reactions are simulated event by event by coupling the isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics model with the GEMINI++ statistical decay code. Results: The calculations follow the measured rise in average neutron multiplicity with incident energy, while yielding higher values above 100 MeV and in the proton-induced prescission component. Within the coupled calculations, the neutron multiplicity growth comes mainly from statistical evaporation before scission, whereas emission from the fission fragments changes weakly. Although the average preequilibrium neutron yield remains small, early emission spreads the residual nuclei across multiple elements and wide excitation energies. At high energies, protons are emitted predominantly before equilibration, directly reducing the charge retained by the residual nuclei. Conclusions: In the coupled calculations, statistical evaporation before scission governs the neutron multiplicity growth, whereas early nonequilibrium emission shapes the residual nuclei and dominates high-energy proton emission. These results provide a reference for modeling intermediate-energy fission, in which prescission emission changes the charge, mass, and excitation energy of the fissioning system.

title: Systematic Parameter Optimization of Quantum Molecular Dynamics Models Using Multi-Ion Fragmentation Data: Implications for Hadron Therapy
abstract: Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) models are widely used to simulate nuclear fragmentation in hadron therapy, but their predictive accuracy depends strongly on parameters that are often selected empirically. We developed an optimized QMD framework by systematically calibrating three parameters for a relativistic mean-field model with the NS2 parameter set and Skyrme models with the SLy4 and SkM* parameter sets: the wave-packet width L, maximum evolution time Tm, and impact-parameter envelope factor benv. The wave-packet width was determined from experimental charge radii, whereas Tm and benv were parameterized as functions of incident kinetic energy and reaction-system mass and optimized using proton- and heavy-ion-induced fragmentation data over 30-400 MeV/u. Performance was compared with the original LiQMD, Binary Cascade, and Liege Intranuclear Cascade models. The optimized Tm depended strongly on incident energy but only weakly on system mass, indicating that the transition from the dynamical QMD stage to statistical de-excitation is governed mainly by collision energy. In contrast, benv showed model-dependent behavior: NS2 favored larger peripheral-collision contributions for lighter systems at low energies, whereas the Skyrme models showed relatively weak energy and mass dependence. The optimized parameterizations improved agreement with experimental fragment production cross sections, angular distributions, and energy distributions. The optimized Skyrme models achieved the best overall performance and outperformed the cascade models for most datasets. This framework provides a physically consistent description of nuclear fragmentation across multiple observables and may improve calculations of secondary-particle transport, dose deposition, and linear energy transfer in hadron therapy.

title: Probing the structure of the two proton Borromean nucleus $^{17}\rm{Ne}$ through inclusive breakup data
abstract: The proton-rich nucleus $^{17}$Ne exhibits a Borromean structure, $^{15}$O+p+p, since both $^{16}$F and diproton systems are unbound. The low-energy spectrum of this nucleus consists of a series of resonances that remain poorly identified. In this work, a three-body model is used to describe the structure of $^{17}$Ne, with special attention to the emergence of resonant states. The four-body continuum-discretized coupled-channel (CDCC) formalism is used to study the reaction of $^{17}$Ne on a $^{208}$Pb target near the Coulomb barrier. Comparing the calculated elastic and breakup cross sections with the recently available experimental data~\cite{OVEJAS2023138007} provides an excellent framework for probing the resonant structure of this nucleus.

title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
abstract: Abstract Upon infection, arteriviruses, coronaviruses, and other nidoviruses transform endoplasmic reticulum membranes into viral replication organelles. These include large numbers of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) whose interior is considered the primary site of viral RNA synthesis. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. The discovery of DMV-spanning pore complexes in coronavirus-infected cells provided a plausible solution for this topological challenge. However, their structural organization, functional features, and evolutionary conservation across the nidovirus order, have remained unclear. Here, we investigate the macromolecular architecture of DMVs induced by two prototypic arteriviruses using cellular cryo-electron tomography. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

title: A study of neutrinoless double electron capture in $^{40}$Ca from the AMoRE experiment
abstract:
The search for neutrinoless double electron capture ($0
u\mathrm{2EC}$) provides a sensitive probe of lepton-number violation and the Majorana nature of neutrinos. We investigate the $0
u\mathrm{2EC}$ decay of $^{40}$Ca using cryogenic detectors equipped with metallic magnetic calorimeters in the AMoRE-I experiment. The analysis is based on a physics dataset corresponding to a total exposure of 7.32 kg$\cdot$yr from thirteen $^{40}$Ca$^{100}$MoO$_4$ crystals. No significant excess is observed, and a lower limit on the half-life is obtained as $T^{0
u}_{1/2} > 2.0 	imes 10^{22}$ yr at 90$\%$ confidence level. An improved sensitivity is expected for the upcoming AMoRE-II experiment. These results demonstrate the potential of CaMoO$_4$ detectors to explore rare decay processes beyond the primary $^{100}$Mo $0
u eta eta$ search program.

title: u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
abstract: u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.

title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
abstract: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^\pi=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.

title: Electron-capture rates in medium-mass nuclei, $$^{48}$$Ti, $$^{56}$$Ni, $$^{60}$$Zn, and $$^{64}$$Ge, within deformed quasiparticle random-phase approximation
abstract: Electron-capture (EC) rates in medium-mass nuclei are governed by Gamow–Teller (GT) strength distributions and provide important input for stellar weak-interaction processes. In this work, we investigate the deformation dependence of the GT strengths and stellar EC rates in selected medium-mass nuclei in and near the pf shell, namely $$^{48}$$ Ti, $$^{56}$$ Ni, $$^{60}$$ Zn, and $$^{64}$$ Ge. The $$\hbox {GT}^{(+/-)}$$ strength distributions are calculated in the deformed quasiparticle random-phase approximation (DQRPA) on a single-particle basis obtained by the Skyrme SGII interaction, while the stellar EC rates are evaluated from the resulting $$B(\textrm{GT}^+)$$ strengths using the standard phase-space formalism. The potential-energy curves are used to characterize shallow and competing intrinsic minima that may suggest shape softness or possible shape coexistence. We find that deformation strongly modifies the GT strength distributions by changing the centroid energies, resonance splitting, and fragmentation patterns. In particular, a pronounced shape dependence of the $$\hbox {GT}^{(+/-)}$$ strengths is found for $$^{56}$$ Ni and $$^{64}$$ Ge, whereas $$^{60}$$ Zn is characterized by a favoured prolate minimum and $$^{48}$$ Ti exhibits a soft near-spherical/prolate landscape. By contrast, the corresponding EC rates are generally much less sensitive to deformation than the differential GT response itself, except in the low-temperature and low-density regime, particularly for $$^{48}$$ Ti with $$Q_{\textrm{EC}}<0$$ , where the low-lying $$\hbox {GT}^+$$ strength becomes decisive. Available charge-exchange data for $$^{48}$$ Ti and $$^{56}$$ Ni are used as benchmarks of the model predictions. The present results provide microscopic constraints on the sensitivity of stellar weak rates to deformation and competing intrinsic configurations in selected medium-mass nuclei, including proton-rich isotopes near the $$N=Z$$ line.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Structure and Binding of the \texorpdfstring{$pn\Omega^-$}{pnOmega} System with a Near-Unitary \texorpdfstring{$N\Omega$}{NOmega} Interaction from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
abstract: The binding and spatial structure of the \(pn\Omega^-\) system are investigated in the \(I(J^P)=0(5/2^+)\) channel using the physical-point HAL QCD \(N\Omega({}^{5}S_2)\) interaction. The pairwise Hamiltonian includes the spin-triplet \(pn\) interaction and the finite-size Coulomb attraction in the \(p\Omega^-\) pair. The three-body Schr\"odinger equation is solved with the Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM), including all three Jacobi rearrangement configurations. For the central HAL QCD potential at \(t/a=14\), the calculated three-body binding energy is \(18.63\) MeV, corresponding to a separation energy of \(16.39\) MeV relative to the \(d+\Omega^-\) threshold. The spatial structure is examined through interparticle root-mean-square distances, pair and spectator radial distributions, and the correlation between the two Jacobi coordinates. Relative to a frozen-deuteron folded reference, the full three-body solution exhibits a substantially more compact spectator distribution and a contracted \(pn\) pair. The dependence on the Euclidean-time choice of the HAL QCD potential is also assessed. The results characterize the three-body rearrangement induced by the attractive \(N\Omega\) interaction within the adopted pairwise model.

title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
abstract: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

title: Particle-vibration coupling model with explicit doorway states based on the Skyrme density functional
abstract: Modern $\gamma$-ray detectors can achieve energy resolutions of a few keV, motivating microscopic studies of strength fragmentation in nuclear excitation spectra. Particle-vibration coupling (PVC) describes the spreading of giant resonances, but conventional formulations based on an energy-dependent effective Hamiltonian in the 1 particle-1 hole (1p1h) space do not explicitly provide individual excited states and their wave functions. We develop a PVC model with explicit doorway states by directly diagonalising the PVC matrix in the space of 1p1h and 1p1h coupled to a phonon (1p1h$\otimes\nu$) configurations. Using the Skyrme energy density functional SkM*, we study the isovector giant dipole resonance (GDR) in $^{208}$Pb. The one-body transition densities show that the neutron and proton components of the dominant GDR states remain out of phase after including PVC, preserving their isovector character. Wave-function analysis reveals that the $2^+$ and $3^-$ phonons play a key role in GDR fragmentation. The fragmented states are dominated by 1p1h$\otimes\nu$ configurations, accounting for more than 80\% of the wave-function norm. Nevertheless, coherent contributions of 1p1h configurations preserve the collective character of the $E1$ transitions. Thus, PVC strongly modifies the microscopic structure and fragmentation of the GDR without changing its essential isovector collective character.

title: Elastic scattering cross-section of 10B projectile on light, medium and heavy targets using different effective interactions
abstract: This work is a comprehensive and systematic investigation of the elastic scattering of the weakly bound projectile [Formula: see text] from a broad range of light, medium and heavy target nuclei over several incident energies within the double-folding framework. The real and imaginary components of the nuclear optical potential are constructed using the M3Y, R3Y and B3Y-Fetal effective nucleon–nucleon (NN) interactions combined with nuclear density distributions obtained from the two-parameter Fermi (2pF) and relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. The calculated elastic-scattering angular distributions are compared with available experimental data to assess the predictive capabilities of the different interactions and density parametrizations. The calculated angular distributions generally reproduce the main features of the measured elastic-scattering cross-sections, although the quality of agreement varies among the investigated systems and incident energies. Among the interactions considered, the B3Y-Fetal interaction generally provides the best overall agreement with the experimental data with calculations employing RMF densities using the NL2 parameter set, while the phenomenological 2pF densities show comparatively weaker performance in several cases. Based on these findings, empirical relations are proposed to predict suitable [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] values for elastic-scattering analyses involving [Formula: see text]B projectiles. Beyond the description of individual systems, this study establishes global trends in the optical-model parameters and their dependence on target mass and incident energy, thereby providing a unified framework for understanding the reaction dynamics of the weakly bound nucleus [Formula: see text].

publisher: World Scientific Pub Co Pte Ltd

title: A Study of Renyi Entropy in pp Collisions by ALICE Data- A Comparison with UrQMD Simulation and AI-Assisted Modeling
abstract: In the present investigation a systematic study of order dependence and energy dependence of Renyi entropy calculated from the ALICE experimental data of charged-particle multiplicity distributions in pp collisions at the centre-of-mass energies \root s= 2.76, 7 and 13 TeV within the pseudo-rapidity interval and transverse momentum range as selected by ALICE collaborationc has been carried out. ALICE collaboration compared the experimental multiplicity distribution of charged particles in pp collisions by PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model and hence Renyi entropy has also been evaluated from the corresponding PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model results reported by the ALICE Collaboration. An independent comparison has been carried out using UrQMD simulation generated for the same collision energies and kinematic acceptance by the author himself. In addition, an AI-assisted multiplicity distribution is considered as an auxiliary statistical reference for Renyi entropy estimation. In all the cases, the Renyi entropy exhibits a decreasing trend with increasing order q, indicating the presence of multifractality in pp collisions. The values of Renyi entropy for a particular order increases systematically with the increase of collision energy from \root s = 2.76TeV to 13 TeV, reflecting the increasing disorder and dynamical fluctuations of the particle-production process.

title: Probing the G ( 3900 ) state in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: We investigate the interactions of the recently confirmed exotic hadron G ( 3900 ) —with quantum numbers J P C = 1 − − —with the hadronic medium composed of light mesons produced in heavy-ion collisions. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we compute both vacuum and thermally averaged cross sections for processes such as G ( 3900 ) + π → D ( * ) + D ¯ ( * ) and their inverse reactions. Following recent proposals, the G ( 3900 ) is interpreted as a P -wave D D ¯ * / D * D ¯ molecular state. The resulting thermally averaged cross sections are employed in a rate equation to determine the time evolution of the G ( 3900 ) multiplicity, with initial conditions provided by statistical and coalescence hadronization models. We find that the large decay width of the G ( 3900 ) leads to a strong suppression of its abundance during the hadronic phase. Although decay is the dominant depletion mechanism, the full kinetic evolution shows that regeneration through inverse reactions becomes relevant at intermediate and late times, making the final yield different from that obtained from a decay-only treatment. The final G ( 3900 ) multiplicity is considerably smaller than that of the Z c ( 3900 ) , under the assumptions adopted here.

title: The Explosion Time of the Jittering Jet Explosion Mechanism (JJEM)
abstract: Abstract We compare the expected explosion time of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to that in the neutrino-driven (the delayed neutrino) mechanism, and conclude that for most, but not all, stellar models, even when the neutrino-driven mechanism might have led to an explosion, the JJEM starts to operate before the neutrino mechanism fully revives the stalled shock. To achieve this goal, we conduct comprehensive one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations using the code mesa to determine the expected explosion time according to the JJEM, which corresponds to the time when the inner convective layer of the core is accreted onto the newly born neutron star (NS). We present results for many hydrogen-rich, hydrogen-stripped, and helium+hydrogen-stripped envelope CCSN progenitor models. We find that most, but not all, of our models in the initial mass range of M ZAMS = 12 M ⊙ to M ZAMS = 40 M ⊙ , have at least one strong convective zone inside the mass coordinate that is the maximum baryonic mass of an NS, m ≃ 2.65 M ⊙ , which can facilitate the JJEM. This study contributes to establishing the JJEM as a viable explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

title: Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
abstract: We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $\gamma$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $\gamma$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.

title: Hadron masses and pseudoscalar meson form factors in a Poincar\'e-invariant constituent quark model
abstract: We study a Poincar\'e-invariant constituent quark model with pair, fine-structure, and finite-range three-quark interactions treated in the diagonalization. A fit of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses gives an rms deviation of $6.85\,\mathrm{MeV}$, with the common offset fixed by a spectral condition. The same mass-fit wave functions give the elastic form factors of ten pseudoscalar mesons in the light-front impulse approximation with the Melosh rotation. The pion and charged-kaon radii are $0.407$ and $0.411\,\mathrm{fm}$, below the measured values. Unlike experiment, the kaon radius slightly exceeds the pion radius. Replacing the pion radial function by the normalized $S$-wave component of the $\rho$ raises its radius to $0.604\,\mathrm{fm}$, showing that hyperfine compression accounts for most of the deficit in the mean-square charge radius. With the light-quark size fixed by the pion, the $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes that differ by $2.2$ standard deviations.

title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
abstract: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

title: Diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter using a chiral SU(3) model
abstract: We study the diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter. The effects due to the baryon density, isospin, strangeness, and temperature on the nucleons and hyperons are studied within a chiral SU(3) model. The medium modifications of the baryons arise due to interactions with the mean scalar and vector fields within the model. The thermodynamic and transport properties are studied in the hot strange hadronic matter. The diffusion matrix associated with the multiple charges (baryon number, isospin, and strangeness), as well as the coefficient of shear viscosity, are computed from the Boltzmann equation using first-order Chapman--Enskog expansion within the relaxation time approximation. The diffusion coefficient, $\kappa_{QQ}$ corresponding to the conserved electric charge has also been studied in the present work. There are observed to be significant effects from the isospin asymmetry as well as the strangeness of the medium on the diffusion coefficients. The coefficient of shear viscosity, $\eta$ is observed to have a large enhancement in the presence of finite strangeness in the medium due to additional contributions from the hyperons. The effects due to isospin asymmetry on the shear viscosity coefficient is however observed to be marginal both in nuclear and hyperonic matter. The present study can be relevant for the experimental observables of asymmetric relativistic heavy-ion collisions, e.g., in the compressed baryonic matter (CBM) experiment at the FAIR facility at GSI as well as in the future J-PARC-HI program.

title: Charged pion production in the annihilation reactions $e^+ + e^- \to p + \bar{n} +\pi^-$ and $e^+ + e^- \to n + \bar{p} +\pi^+.$ Contribution of the nonresonant mechanism
abstract: The nonresonant mechanism in the reactions $e^+\,e^-\to \pi^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ and $e^+\,e^-\to \pi^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ is investigated in frame of the one-photon exchange approximation. The description of the hadronic phase space and the invariant amplitude formalism, earlier developed for the neutral pion channel, are applied here. Some modification is required to fulfill the conservation of the hadron electromagnetic current and to account for an additional contribution due to diagram with the pion pole. The double and single distributions over the invariant variables as well the total cross section, are obtained. The results are plotted for $s=$5,\,10,\,16\, GeV$^2$. The calculations are performed for the $\pi^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ channel and the rules to proceed to the $\pi^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ channel are formulated for every distribution.

title: The Last Gasps of a Dying Star: ALMA Observations of the Preplanetary Nebula IRAS 06530–0213
abstract: Abstract We present high-angular-resolution ( ∼ 0 . ″ 1 − 0 . ″ 5 ) Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of millimeter-wave line and continuum emission (at ∼0.44 and 0.88 mm) in the preplanetary nebula IRAS 06530–0213 (IRAS 06530). These data show the presence of an extended circular ring—first evidence of the last thermal pulse preceding the post-asymptotic giant branch (AGB) phase in a carbon star—and a central bipolar nebula (CBN) and torus. The mass-loss rate of IRAS 06530’s AGB progenitor decreased immediately after the thermal pulse, then rose again just before the post-AGB phase, as evidenced by the presence of filamentary arc structures around the CBN. The arc stuctures are likely part of a 3D Archimedean spiral structure generally attributed to the presence of a binary companion. However, we do not find a compact continuum source at the location of IRAS 06530’s central star, such as that associated with the compact dusty disks typically found in disk-prominent post-AGB objects known to have binary companions. The expansion ages derived for the torus and CBN imply that IRAS 06530’s progenitor transitioned to a post-AGB star ≲700 yr ago. The molecular mass of the ejecta in IRAS 06530 is dominated by the filamentary arc region, with a mass M H 2 = ( 0.12 − 0.25 ) M ⊙ . Compared with solar values, the torus of IRAS 06530 appears to be significantly (modestly) enriched in 13 C and 17 O ( 15 N), as well—a pattern of rare-isotope enrichment inconsistent with standard nucleosynthesis models. From the luminosity of IRAS 06530 and the age of its detached shell, while it was still on the AGB, we infer that the mass of IRAS 06530’s progenitor was 1.6–3.4 M ⊙ .

title: Probing forward-backward multiplicity correlations and fluctuations with UrQMD using the strongly intensive observable Σ in Pb-Pb collisions at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron
One- and two-nucleon transfer in Sn 116 + Ni 60 : A coupled reaction channels analysis
abstract: Background: Recent studies of multinucleon transfer in heavy-ion collisions have employed both macroscopic and microscopic models. Although macroscopic approaches offer useful insights, microscopic analyses of high-precision experimental data provide a more reliable framework for understanding the nucleon transfer mechanisms.Purpose: The present study aims to carry out a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the $^{116}\mathrm{Sn}+^{60}\mathrm{Ni}$ system using microscopic coupled reaction channels (CRC) calculations, which include quasielastic scattering and one- and two-nucleon transfer channels.Method: The calculations employ microscopic double-folding S\~ao Paulo potentials, incorporating all relevant inelastic and transfer couplings guided by observed $\ensuremath{\gamma}$-ray transitions, if available, to better constrain the model. For the one-nucleon transfer channels, spectroscopic amplitudes are obtained either from large-scale shell-model calculations using different effective interactions or from the literature. In the case of two-nucleon transfer, sequential, microscopic cluster, and extreme cluster mechanisms are considered to reproduce the data.Results: Results for quasielastic scattering and one-neutron ($1n$) transfer show excellent agreement with experimental data, validating the chosen optical potentials and structural inputs. Spectroscopic amplitudes computed by different shell-model interactions produce consistent $1n$ transfer probabilities. In contrast, measured one-proton ($1p$) transfer probabilities are best described by incorporating experimental spectroscopic amplitudes in the CRC calculations. For transfer of two nucleons, the extreme cluster mechanism is found to best reproduce the data. CRC results of all transfer channels underpredict the data at higher energies, pointing to the probable role of absorption effects.Conclusions: This study highlights the significant influence of inelastic excitations, multistep processes and absorption effects in shaping transfer dynamics, thereby offering deeper insights into multinucleon transfer mechanisms in heavy-ion collisions. Feasibility of microscopic description of one- and two-nucleon transfer between two heavy ions in the CRC framework, without taking recourse to arbitrary normalization of the cross sections, is quite encouraging. Nonetheless, the lack of experimental corroboration for all the transitions included in the calculations and practical limits of computational resources, affecting the accuracy of shell-model results and causing a cap on the number of states, leave room for further refinement of the results.

title: Disaccharide production in marine cold seeps links dissolved organic carbon to anaerobic oxidation of methane
abstract: Abstract Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) has been proposed as a source of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) at marine cold seeps, but the underlying molecular mechanism for its production remains unknown. Here we demonstrate a previously unrecognized link between AOM and porewater DOC by analyzing disaccharides in sediment and porewaters from a methane-charged cold seep in Astoria Canyon (Oregon, USA). In the AOM zone, sediments contain up to 17.7 mg L −1 trehalose with δ 13 C values as low as −78‰, and porewaters contain up to 1 mg L −1 sucrose with δ 13 C values as low as −66‰, representing 4.6% of DOC. Stable isotope probing experiments reveal AOM-dependent biosynthesis of trehalose and sucrose, and both disaccharides turn over faster than diagnostic lipids, suggesting that these compounds serve as biomarkers for active AOM. Accordingly, disaccharides mediate a relationship that may sustain microbial food webs and influence carbon cycling in methane-rich marine sediments.

title: An Evolutionary Channel to the Peculiar Millisecond Pulsar PSR J0435+3233: The Irradiation Effect of X-Rays
abstract: Abstract PSR J0435+3233 (J0435) is a peculiar millisecond pulsar (MSP) with a spin period of 3.2 ms and an anomalously high spin-down rate of P ̇ s = 4.88 × 1 0 − 17 s s − 1 , in which the spin-down rate is 2 orders of magnitude higher than those of other known MSPs. Therefore, J0435 provides an opportunity for testing the classical recycling model and binary evolution theory. In this work, we propose that the irradiation effect of X-ray of an accreting neutron star (NS) plays a vital role in evolving toward J0435 from a low-mass X-ray binary. Our detailed stellar evolution models indicate that a binary system consisting of a 1.4 M ⊙ NS and a 1.2 M ⊙ main-sequence companion star in an initial orbit of 4.18 days can evolve into J0435-like systems in a detached episode when the irradiation effect and radio evaporation process are included. Our results are in good agreement with the observed parameters of J0435, such as spin period, spin-down rate, and the mass and effective temperature of the companion star. Therefore, the irradiation effect could be a potential evolutionary channel to the peculiar MSP J0435.

title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass–Radius–Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
abstract: Abstract We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass–radius space instead of pressure–energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass–radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass–radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass–radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

title: The antibaryon-baryon interaction based on chiral EFT with a focus on $\bar pp$ and $\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ reactions
abstract: The antibaryon-baryon ($\bar BB$) interaction is reviewed in the context of the hyperon(Y)-production reactions $\bar NN\to\bar YY$ with special emphasis on the $\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ system. The experimental situation for $\bar BB\to\bar YY$ from threshold up to antiproton lab momenta of $2$ GeV/c is discussed and likewise past theoretical approaches and results. The formalism for a description of the $\bar BB$ interaction in terms of potentials derived within SU(3) chiral effective field theory (EFT) is outlined. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry on the $\bar BB$ interaction in the various reaction channels are discussed. As concrete application a new analysis of the reaction $\bar pp\to\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ is performed utilizing potentials for the $\bar NN$ and $\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ channels, and for the $\bar NN\to\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ transition, up to next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion, supplemented by a phenomenological part to account for annihilation processes. An excellent reproduction of data from the PS185 experiment at CERN up to momenta of $1.55$ GeV/c is achieved. When including higher-order contact terms in the analysis the range of agreement can be extended up to momenta around $1.65$ GeV/c, where a complete set of scattering observables is available. Predictions for $\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ scattering are provided and compared to results from the literature.

title: Naturalness scale inference in chiral perturbation theory and chiral logarithms
abstract: We infer naturalness scales of chiral perturbation theory in the mesonic sector using Bayesian techniques that are extended to explicitly take into account chiral logarithms. To demonstrate our approach, we consider the chiral expansion of the pion decay constant $F_\pi$ and the threshold and subthreshold parameters of $\pi\pi$ scattering. We find a strong observable dependence of the inferred naturalness scales, and show that they need not coincide with the pion mass at which the order-by-order hierarchy of the chiral expansion breaks down. As an application, we discuss the requirements for lattice-QCD constraints on the two combinations of $O(p^6)$ low-energy constants that in the current matching of Roy-equation analyses to chiral perturbation theory need to be estimated from resonance saturation, but could be extracted from the pion-mass dependence of $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters.

title: Mass and decay angles in the $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
abstract: We compare three definitions of $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ mixing within a constituent-quark model: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the two operator-based definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The operator-based angles are closer to the lattice determinations $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$, but remain larger. We then couple conventional $qsQ$ states to virtual $qsQg$ configurations, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. An orbital-$S$-wave chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability stays below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. Eliminating the hybrid sector gives a rank-one mass correction precisely when all weighted transitions select the same retained-state combination. The mode-resolved calculation separates the flavor-breaking response that changes the mixing angle from the response that generates a second transition direction. The accompanying effective-current relation connects this mass analysis to radiative and semileptonic amplitudes through their current matrix elements.

title: Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
abstract: We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

versions.abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. From Lead to Helium: Potential for a Measurement of Jet Quenching in the Smallest Collision Systems
abstract: We present perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) predictions for the modification to the yield of high-momentum particles in very light ion collisions - ${}^{10}\mathrm{B} + {}^{10}\mathrm{B}$, ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li} + {}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$, ${}^{4}\mathrm{He} + {}^{4}\mathrm{He}$, and ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ - both with and without medium-induced energy loss. We show that there is non-trivial suppression expected from our partonic energy loss model in symmetric systems from ${}^{208}\mathrm{Pb} + {}^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ to ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and in asymmetric systems $A + B$, and that the energy loss scales approximately with $(\sqrt{A B})^{1 / 3}$. Further, we find that deep inelastic scattering measurements in ${}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$ tightly constrain the nPDF baseline, making these isotopes a particularly clean environment for searching for final-state partonic energy loss induced by the formation of a quark-gluon plasma in these very small systems.

title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
abstract: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $\Delta m^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $\Delta m^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $\nu_\mu$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$, and the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $\theta_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy range, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|\Delta m^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $\delta_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.
