title: The science of compressional heating on the LM26 magnetized target fusion experiment
abstract: Abstract The Lawson Machine 26 (LM26) operating at General Fusion has demonstrated compressional heating of a spherical tokamak deuterium plasma as it was compressed by an imploding solid lithium liner. Results from the first 11 compression experiments on LM26 are presented, the highest-performing of which show more than a three-fold increase in electron temperature, a ten-fold increase in density, and a ten-fold increase in poloidal field in the plasma driven by three-fold radial compression. The experimental device and its instrumentation are reviewed in detail, followed by direct observations from each of the key diagnostics for liner trajectory and plasma properties, measuring increases in magnetic field, electron density, as well as emission of neutrons, X-rays, and visible radiation. Observations from fast-camera images during compression provide detailed context for interpreting the spatial structure of plasma-wall interaction. Overviews of the various models developed and used in the analysis are presented. Diagnostic data are used to reconstruct the experimental equilibrium state in computational modeling as a function of time. The results indicate the reconstructions are sufficiently accurate to match the essential observations from the experiment, validating the models and building confidence in the stability and transport analyses that support the key conclusions. Trends across the full set of 11 compression shots are presented, and a more detailed examination of the high-performance shots are given individually. The key conclusions of the integrated physics model specifically indicate that compressional heating was achieved in this set of experiments, as evidenced by the balance of heating power from compression, Ohmic heating from plasma current, and losses to the boundary necessary to match the experimental data. A majority of the increase in temperature is attributable to compressional heating. An increase in neutron flux is also observed during compression. The results provide a basis for planned improvements to the LM26 facility that will enable the compression of magnetized plasma to increasingly higher densities and temperatures.

title: Nonlinear modeling of Edge Localized Modes control using Resonant Magnetic Perturbation on HL-3
abstract: Abstract Utilizing the three-dimensional nonlinear code JOREK, the dynamics of edge localized modes (ELMs) evolution with the application of resonant magnetic perturbation (RMP) have been modeled for the HL-3 tokamak. Scanning of the RMP coil current shows that, with increasing of the RMP coil current, ELMs are first mitigated followed by total suppression. Calculation of the time correlation function, as well as the Poisson bracket quantity, indicates a significant energy transfer between toroidal modes, implying that application of the RMP field acts as a constant external drive which greatly facilitates the energy redistribution between toroidal modes through nonlinear mode coupling. For the ELM mitigation case, a single most unstable mode is replaced with several unstable modes at similar amplitudes due to energy redistribution, and large ELMs are replaced with more frequent but small-sized bursts. When the RMP field is sufficiently strong, a substantial edge transport is induced to reduce the height of the edge pedestal and bring the pressure gradient to a value below the stability boundary of the peeling-ballooning modes, thus fully suppresses the onset of ELM bursts. Mode braking of the edge instability has been found with application of the RMP field. The static RMP mode dominates at the high field side of the torus, while slowly rotating toroidal modes still exist at the low field side.

title: Nonlinear evolution of perturbatively driven kinetic instabilities far from marginal stability
abstract: Abstract Kinetic instabilities develop when a system's distribution function deviates from thermal equilibrium in such a way that allows free energy from that distribution to drive resonant modes. Motivated by the case of Alfv'enic instabilities driven by minority populations of energetic particles in tokamak plasmas, we consider a kinetic instability with perturbative drive far from its instability threshold, where a theoretical description of the time evolution has not yet been established. In cases with steady-state saturation levels, we find that the mode first evolves linearly, driven by the positive distribution gradient, then undergoes a fast, strongly nonlinear transition where the distribution function slope is completely flattened around the resonance. The system then evolves in a nonlinear regime driven by the balance of the wave drive and dissipation until reaching saturation. The strongly nonlinear transition is sufficiently fast that it can be treated as occurring instantaneously, and by considering a time-local approximation for the distribution after the flattening has occurred, we find a closed-form analytical solution for the mode amplitude in the nonlinear phase. A compact continuous solution for the entire time evolution of the mode amplitude is therefore constructed, and this result is shown to agree closely with nonlinear kinetic simulations.

title: Design and modeling of a Runaway Electron Mitigation Coil for the TCV Tokamak
abstract: Abstract A novel Runaway Electron Mitigation Coil (REMC) has been designed for the Tokamak à Configuration Variable (TCV) to enable the passive deconfinement of relativistic runaway electrons (REs). This non-axisymmetric coil is designed to couple passively to the disruption-induced loop voltage during the current quench phase, generating strong non-axisymmetric fields to destroy magnetic flux surfaces and drive beneficial MHD. The TCV REMC is designed to drive an $n=1$ perturbation while maximizing inductive coupling to the plasma, thereby inducing significant current in the coil. It represents the first passively driven coil of its kind to be implemented in a plasma with an RE plateau, thereby enabling a direct test of its ability to prevent RE beam formation. The ThinCurr electromagnetic modeling code was used to explore various coil configurations under realistic machine constraints. This model incorporates a detailed representation of the vacuum vessel, including material thicknesses and resistivities, and enables the evaluation of both induced coil currents and the resulting 3D magnetic field structures. The results highlight the importance of capturing the physics of the currents induced in the wall and therefore support the use of ThinCurr as the primary development tool. Based on these vacuum criteria, the three most promising coil configurations were selected. At the expected coil resistance of $200~\mu\Omega$, the configuration selected for initial installation is predicted to produce a maximum coil current of $13.3$ kA and an $n=1$ poloidal field exceeding $0.5\%$ of the background toroidal field by the end of the current quench. The REMC will be validated by assessing its ability to couple to the plasma current, influence the current quench rate, and prevent RE plateau formation. Beyond TCV, the results of this study provide valuable insights for future tokamaks considering similar passive coils, such as SPARC and STEP, and contribute to evaluating the potential role of passive mitigation systems in reactor-scale devices.

title: Damping and accumulation characteristics of flow driven by fishbone instability
abstract: Abstract The persistence of fishbone-driven flows across successive bursts is critical to their potential role in regulating turbulence and improving core confinement, yet the damping characteristics of such flows have not been experimentally characterized. Here we report the first direct measurement of the damping rate of fishbone-driven flows using Doppler reflectometry on the EAST tokamak. The experimentally obtained damping rate exceeds prior theoretical predictions, and this discrepancy can be reconciled by incorporating the effective charge number Z eff into the calculation of the damping rate. Furthermore, we observe that flow accumulation occurs when the time interval between successive fishbone bursts is sufficiently short, and we estimate the critical inter-burst interval threshold for accumulation to be approximately 1 ms under the present discharge conditions. These results establish an essential experimental foundation for understanding the temporal persistence of fishbone-driven flows and their implications for transport barrier dynamics.

title: Core-edge integration of negative triangularity plasmas in TCV
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates the core-edge integration of negative triangularity (NT) plasmas with reactor-relevant operation on TCV. Neutral beam injection (NBI)-heated scenarios are developed, achieving stationary, high-performance plasmas, with β N up to 1.7 and H 98 , y 2 above 1, at a relatively high density (Greenwald fraction of approximately 0.4). Featuring a hybrid shape that combines a negative upper-triangularity and a positive lower-triangularity, the NT L-mode achieves central ion and electron temperatures that are higher than those of its positive triangularity counterpart. Before any extrinsic impurity seeding, the divertor is already cold. This is evidenced by the retreat of the C III front from the outer target, which corresponds to a low outer-target electron temperature ( T e ≈ 6 eV ), as well as by a significant fraction of radiated power, partly attributable to the high operational density. With divertor N 2 seeding, an X -point Radiator is formed, further cooling the divertor, with only a slight reduction in plasma performance.

title: A fully electromagnetic hybrid PIC-fluid model for predictive fusion neutron yield in dense plasma focus
abstract: Abstract A fully electromagnetic hybrid ion-PIC/electron-fluid framework is developed for the implosion-to-pinch phase of dense plasma focus (DPF) discharges. Ions are advanced kinetically, electrons form a charge-neutralizing fluid under the quasi-neutral approximation, and the full Maxwell equations are solved in both plasma and vacuum. The generalized Ohm law includes resistive, electron pressure-gradient, and Hall terms. Applied to a non-hollow 180 kA geometry initialized from a pre-ionized end-of-rundown state, the framework reproduces the axial rundown, radial compression, and pinch stages. The sheath front trajectory agrees with fully kinetic benchmarks within 10%, and a pinch-radius comparison captures the radial collapse. A beam-target neutron diagnostic applied to the simulated ion distribution gives a yield of 0.296 × 10 7 , at the same scale as the fully kinetic reference. The ion spectrum develops a non-Maxwellian suprathermal tail to about 0.25 MeV. The yield remains sensitive to the electron-temperature closure and anode geometry. The framework captures relevant macroscopic observables and ion-kinetic diagnostics at a computational cost roughly 10 5 – 10 6 times lower than comparable fully kinetic electromagnetic PIC simulations.

title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
abstract: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.

title: Generalized parton distributions of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model: Sum over all quark states at nonzero skewness and momentum transfer
abstract: We compute the combinations E M = H u + d + E u + d and H E = H u − d + t E u − d / ( 4 M N 2 ) of unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model at nonzero skewness ξ and nonzero momentum transfer t . The combinations contain the GPDs H u − d and E u + d , which are subleading in the expansion in the inverse number of colors. Both combinations are double sums over the quark states. A multipole expansion of the light-cone operators makes the sums computable at every ξ and every t ≤ 0 . The contribution of the Dirac continuum is summed over the quark states, without an interpolation formula and without a gradient expansion. The first moments satisfy the form-factor sum rules, and the second moments satisfy polynomiality.

title: Design of an electrostatic violin mode damper for gravitational wave detector enhancement
abstract: The test mass suspension fiber resonances and their harmonics pollute the sensitivity of the detectors of the advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Observatory (aLIGO) and cause operational issues. The current method of damping these violin modes requires the GW detector be locked; identifying modes after a test mass replacement takes valuable commissioning time, and modes which are close together in frequency are hard to distinguish and damp independently. We present the design, prototyping, and initial lab testing of an electrostatic violin mode damper: a compact sensor and actuator set next to the fiber to monitor and damp resonances. The design uses a split photodiode and LED integrated into a shadow sensor, and an electrostatic actuator. The device is vacuum compatible and its mechanical design is compatible with the suspension and surrounding cage of the advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Observatory test masses. The shadow sensor has a shot noise limited displacement noise floor of 5e-11 {\meter\per\sqrt\hertz}, sufficient to measure the test mass violin modes when highly excited. The modeled actuator strength is 0.3 nN, meeting the requirements to damp the modes for the aLIGO suspensions.

title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe the millihertz gravitational-wave sky, including millions of long-lived Galactic binaries (GBs), tens of thousands of which are expected to be individually resolvable throughout the mission's lifetime. Extracting these sources requires jointly determining their number and physical parameters from strongly overlapping signals, posing a computationally demanding trans-dimensional inference problem. We introduce SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that constructs a learned approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior, producing a probability distribution over source multiplicity and parameter densities for individual binaries in a single evaluation, without requiring their number to be specified in advance. We demonstrate this framework using year-long LISA simulations containing up to ten binaries within a 2 $\mu$Hz frequency interval, focusing on a high-SNR regime in which source overlap, rather than individual-source detectability, is the primary challenge. The inferred source count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases, while the model identifies individual binaries even when their signals overlap strongly in frequency. A complete evaluation, including parameter sampling, takes just 41 ms per band on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU, or 530 ms on eight laptop CPU threads. We further demonstrate that these distributions can be used to initialize subsequent likelihood-based inference, connecting fast amortized predictions with joint parameter estimation.

title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
abstract: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $\mu$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
abstract: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

title: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
abstract: Hercules X-1 ( is one of the most well-studied X-ray binaries that exhibits super-orbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of the super-orbital periodicity in is still under debate between counter-precessing, twisted--tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star, with no clear consensus. The fluctuations in the super-orbital periodicity in with data obtained during the 1970--1990 period have been reported to be stochastic in nature with no long-term trend. We aim to investigate the long-term trend of the super-orbital modulations in with more recent and uninterrupted data from 1995--2025 to examine the presence of features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. The main aim of this study is to test the stability of the super-orbital period using data available from sensitive all-sky instruments. We probed the variation in the super-orbital period in using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely ̊xte, and along with data available in the literature, together spanning ∼50 yr. We employed multiple timing-analysis tools to trace the long-term evolution of the super-orbital period. In the uninterrupted data of super-orbital modulation for the last 30 years, the super-orbital period in s s is decreasing at the rate of ∼ -5 10^ -5 -1 . The analysis of the diagram showed that the super-orbital period in also has variabilities at shorter time scales on top of an overall decay. Hence, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the variabilities observed in the curve. A positive correlation was found between the mean count rate and super-orbital period obtained at different linear segments of the curve. The modulation of the super-orbital period in from a few to a few tens of super-orbital cycles suggests that there is a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss the possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variabilities.

versions.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
versions.abstract: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of this periodicity remains debated between a counter-precessing twisted-tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star. Earlier observations (1970-1990) reported stochastic fluctuations in the superorbital period, with no long-term trend. Aims. We investigated the long-term trend of the superorbital modulation using more recent, uninterrupted data from 1995-2025 to identify features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. Methods. We probed the superorbital period using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, and MAXI/GSC, together with literature data spanning $\sim$50 yr. We employed multiple timing analysis tools to trace its evolution. Results. The uninterrupted data from the last 30 years show that the superorbital period is decreasing at a rate of $\sim -5 \times 10^{-5}$ s s$^{-1}$. The $O-C$ analysis reveals shorter-timescale variability superimposed on the overall decay; thus, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the observed $O-C$ variations. We also find a positive correlation between the mean count rate and superorbital period across different linear segments of the $O-C$ curve. Conclusions. Period variations over a few to a few tens of superorbital cycles suggest a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variability. (Abbreviated.)

title: Dependencies of characteristics of negatively charged pions on transverse momentum of the leading protons in p+12C collisions at 9.9 GeV/ c
abstract: The experimental dependencies of the average values of the multiplicity, transverse and total momenta, longitudinal rapidity, cosine of emission angle of the negative pions on the average transverse momentum of leading protons in [Formula: see text]C collisions at incident momentum of 9.9[Formula: see text]GeV/c have been investigated. Average fraction ([Formula: see text]) of the incident proton energy, transferred to the target [Formula: see text]C nucleus, has been studied as a function of the transverse momentum of the leading proton in events containing a leading proton in [Formula: see text]C collisions at 9.9[Formula: see text]GeV/c. The experimental data have been compared systematically with numerical calculations performed using the modified FRITIOF model. The FRITIOF model has reproduced satisfactorily the experimental dependencies of the transverse and total momenta, and longitudinal rapidities of the negative pions on the average transverse momentum of leading protons. The model has underestimated significantly the average multiplicity of the negative pions and ([Formula: see text]) in [Formula: see text]C collision events with leading protons. The experimental values of ([Formula: see text]) have demonstrated significant dependence on the average transverse momentum of leading protons in contrast to the very weak dependence obtained for this parameter in the model.

title: Outflow Properties from a Broad Range of GR$\nu$RMHD Stellar-Mass Black Hole Accretion Disks
abstract: The majority of the mass ejected by neutron star mergers comes from accretion disk outflows. Over timescales of seconds, the thermodynamic evolution of the disk and its resultant outflows set the stage for the ejecta properties which manifest in kilonova observations at later times (hours/days). Kilonova observables depend sensitively on key properties of these outflows -- mass ejection, the ejecta velocity distribution, late-time ejecta morphology and nucleosynthetic yields -- which can only be modeled with a detailed treatment of microphysical interactions including neutrino and general relativistic effects. In this work, we present a library of 25 general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic accretion disks with neutrino transport, to our knowledge the largest to date, spanning a broad range of black hole and accretion disk combinations. From fits to our simulations, we derive analytic estimates of the average ejecta velocity distribution and mass ejection both at simulation end and extrapolated out to the end of the disk's lifetime. We also report ejecta morphology at timescales relevant to kilonova modeling, present spatially-dependent nucleosynthetic yields, and discuss the latter's dependence on initial disk conditions. While our disk library primarily includes initial conditions expected after neutron star mergers, a subset of our disks are applicable to other kilonova-adjacent scenarios.

title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

title: Anisotropic hybrid stars: Interplay of superconductivity and magnetic field leading to gravitational waves
abstract: Neutron stars, at their cores, are highly dense and, thus, are expected to have a number of exotic processes. This includes a possible phase transition to deconfined quark matter at the core, leading to a hybrid star. The quark matter is expected to additionally be color superconducting. The physics of superconductivity plays an important role in understanding the high density matter in the interiors of neutron/hybrid stars. At their high densities, additionally, both proton superconductivity and neutron superfluidity are expected. We study the effect of superconducting (quark/proton) matter, along with the internal magnetic field, leading to pressure anisotropy within hybrid stars. We aim to probe the effect of superconductivity, especially from color superconducting quarks, on hybrid star structure. We propose new phenomenological model anisotropy profiles within a one-dimensional framework. We model quark matter using the vector interaction enhanced Bag model, and hadron matter with the DD2 equation of state. A Maxwell construction joins both phases. We further investigate the possible observational signatures of these hybrid stars. These include mass enhancement and the possibility of continuous gravitational waves arising from the anisotropy induced deformation, giving us a way to further constrain our model and its physical parameters.

title: Resonant filling for long-pulse operation of EuXFEL using iterative learning based feed forward
abstract: A future operation scenario of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) is long-pulse (LP) mode, where the 800 superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities of the linac are energized with RF pulse lengths of up to 500ms. Compared to the current, short-pulse (SP) mode with less than 2ms, the dominant mechanical eigenmodes of the cavities at a few hundred Hertz pose a significant control challenge, as the RF pulse extends beyond a multiple of their periods. To improve energy efficiency of LP operation, cavities are operated at bandwidths in the range of tens of Hertz, a factor of 10 narrower than in SP. Due to peak power limitation of the proposed high power amplifiers, even the fill time surpasses mechanical mode periods. This paper presents experimental evaluation of two feed forward adaptation approaches to facilitate resonant-filling despite mechanical mode transients: In a single-cavity regulation setup, the RF drive phase is adjusted to match the Lorentz force detuning induced cavity phase shift. In vector-sum RF regulation systems, the incident phase cannot be adjusted to each cavity individually, so the concept is inverted by adapting mechanical cavity tuner drives to match each individual cavity resonance trajectory with a fixed common RF drive phase.

title: Probing the nonstrange quark star equation of state with compact stars and gravitational waves
abstract: A recent study shows that incorporating a new term into the thermodynamic potential density, as required by the thermodynamic consistency criterion, can effectively resolve the thermodynamic inconsistency problems of the conventional perturbative QCD model. This additional term plays a crucial role in resolving inconsistencies at relatively low densities and becomes negligible at extremely high densities. Within this revised perturbative QCD model, we find that if we require only that the energy per baryon of up-down ($ud$) quark matter exceeds 930 MeV so as not to contradict the standard nuclear physics, the maximum mass of an $ud$ quark star allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model can reach up to 2.17 $M_{\odot}$. From this perspective, the observed 2.14 $M_{\odot}$ pulsar PSR J0740+6620 may be an $ud$ quark star. However, if we further impose the constraint that the tidal deformability of a 1.4 $M_{\odot}$ $ud$ quark star must be consistent with the GW170817 event, the maximum mass allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model would decrease to no more than 2.08 $M_{\odot}$. Consequently, our results suggest that the compact object with a mass of 2.50-2.67 $M_{\odot}$, as observed in the GW190814 event, cannot be an $ud$ quark star, according to the revised perturbative QCD model.

title: Nucleon Short-Range Correlations and Supersoft Nuclear Symmetry Energy: Compatibility with Massive Neutron Stars and GW170817
abstract: Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. Given the importance of the nuclear symmetry energy in neutron-rich matter, an intriguing question arises: Can the symmetry energy become supersoft at high densities while remaining compatible with these seemingly competing constraints? Within the nonlinear Walecka framework, we demonstrate that nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs), manifested as a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the nucleon momentum distribution, can accommodate such behavior without introducing additional interaction parameters. We derive for the first time analytical expressions for the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ for both free Fermi gas (FFG) and HMT momentum distributions. Using model parameter sets that reproduce empirical nuclear matter properties around saturation density, we find that SRC-HMT yields substantially more negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$ than the FFG case, allowing the symmetry energy to reach a maximum at low supra-saturation densities and subsequently decrease while the total pressure remains sufficient to support massive NSs. The resulting EOSs also predict smaller NS radii and tidal deformabilities consistent with GW170817. These results connect the microscopic nucleon momentum distribution with the density dependence of the symmetry energy and macroscopic NS properties.

title: Hydrodynamic modeling of liquid metal field emitter deformation under combined RF and DC magnetic fields
abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) breakdowns, also known as vacuum (or electrical) arcs and breakdowns, or electrical discharges, have been studied for over decades, but the mechanisms of the RF breakdown are still questionable. This phenomenon reduces the stability of the beam, damages the RF cavities, and thus limits the achievable accelerating field in the particle accelerator. In the case of Muon Collider, the RF cavities have to withstand an electric field of the order of multi tens of MV/m and a DC magnetic field of a few tens of teslas, with a minimum rate of RF breakdown. Different models have been proposed, and some important factors that could lead to the RF breakdown have been identified, such as the field emission current, irregularity of the surface , presence of hot particles on the surface and the role of the DC magnetic field. In this paper, we give insights to the mechanism of RF breakdowns using a hydrodynamic and a magnetohydrodynamic approach, focusing on understanding the forces that deform the liquid copper emitter. We found that if the local RF electric field is sufficiently high, it could provoke the emission of hot copper droplets into the cavity. Our simulations use the computational fluid dynamics module, the magnetic and electric field module, and the level set method in the COMSOL software to simulate the behavior of a copper liquid emitter with the Navier-Stokes equation under the influence of the pressure radiation, and the surface tension force.

title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
abstract: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $\mu$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

title: New unintegrated gluon density in proton and nuclei tested with small $x$ processes at modern colliders
abstract: We present a new unintegrated, or transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density in proton and nuclei. Parameters of the new function have been obtained from a fit on inclusive soft charged hadron production and structure functions at low scales, and from comparison with data on a number of processes at higher scales results taken at LHC and HERA, such as heavy quarks production, prompt photon photoproduction and Higgs boson production. A modification employing the geometric scaling approach has been made to extend the obtained parton density to the case of light and heavy nuclei. As a test of the nuclear TMD distribution we perform a calculation of the charged hadrons multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at the LHC energies.

title: Neutron stars in $f(Q) = Q +\xi Q^2$ gravity
abstract: Modified theories of gravity based on the symmetric teleparallel framework have recently attracted considerable attention as viable alternatives to General Relativity. In this context, f(Q) gravity, in which the gravitational interaction is encoded in the nonmetricity scalar Q, provides a consistent geometrical formulation that differs from the standard curvature-based description. In this work, we investigate the structure of neutron stars within a family of f(Q) gravity models by employing realistic equations of state, namely FPS, SLy, ENG and MPA1. Using the covariant formulation of f(Q) gravity, we derive the corresponding Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and apply them to model compact stellar configurations. Numerical integration of the field equations provides the mass-radius relations and the maximum masses supported by each equation of state, enabling a direct comparison with current observational constraints. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the nonmetricity scalar both inside and outside the stellar object, providing additional insight into the gravitational structure of compact stars in this framework.

title: Thresholdless ion Bernstein wave emission and alpha-to-thermal-ion energy channeling via pole resonance of fusion-product ions
Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural laboratory for superfluid matter under extreme conditions. Its nonlinear dynamics is central to pulsar glitches, their possible links to fast radio bursts, and tidal interactions in inspiralling binaries. We develop a general-relativistic superfluid hydrodynamics framework incorporating entrainment, vortex forces, and line energy, and derive, for the first time, necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity. We also show that commonly used dissipative, force-balanced formulations without line tension are generically ill-posed at short wavelengths because of the Donnelly-Glaberson instability. Exploiting the analogy between vortex arrays with tension and force-free electrodynamics, we recast vortex dynamics in terms of effective electric and magnetic fields and drift velocities. This motivates a new finite-volume scheme combining constrained transport of superfluid vorticity with implicit electric-field evolution, enabling stable numerical evolution of the full system. We validate the scheme using an exact solution to the relativistic superfluid Riemann problem and Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, among other tests. Finally, we simulate dynamical, global general-relativistic two-fluid neutron-star equilibria, validate their oscillation modes, and present the first simplified calculation of superfluid interior spin-down with prescribed vortex release and repinning. The resulting stationary state retains both a net twist in the vortex array and residual differential rotation of the superfluid. Our framework thus enables nonlinear numerical studies of general-relativistic superfluid dynamics in neutron-star interiors.

title: Nucleon light-front transverse densities from three-body and quark + diquark Faddeev equations
abstract: Nucleon elastic electromagnetic form factors obtained from two complementary continuum Schwinger function approaches -- a Poincar\'e-covariant three-body Faddeev equation formulated in rainbow-ladder truncation and a quark + fully-interacting-diquark, $q(qq)$, Faddeev equation -- are used to chart light-front transverse charge and magnetisation densities of the proton, the neutron, and their dressed valence quarks. Going beyond a comparison of observables, the bound-state amplitudes that underlie them are also compared. Both amplitudes are dominated by $s$-wave structures; and in the three-body solution, the mixed-antisymmetric (mixed-symmetric) flavour component is dominated by structures with the Dirac character of scalar (axialvector) diquark correlations, so that the association between these flavour components and diquark correlations is realised explicitly. The $q(qq)$ amplitude falls more slowly with the quark-diquark relative momentum than the three-body amplitude does with the corresponding Jacobi momentum. The two descriptions deliver mutually compatible densities, which match expectations based on modern parametrisations of data. Transverse-plane valence $u$- and $d$-quark Dirac radii are practically indistinguishable, whereas the $d$-quark Pauli radius is roughly 10% larger; and the valence $d$ quark is magnetically far more active than the valence $u$ quark, a feature tied to the mixed-symmetric (axialvector-diquark) components of the nucleon amplitude. For a $+\hat{x}$ polarised nucleon, positive charge is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction, with the opposite effect for negative charge.

title: New Candidate Activity Periods from FRB 20240209A and Repeating Fast Radio Burst Sources in the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
abstract: Repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources with periodic activity provide important constraints on FRB models invoking neutron-star precession, rotation, or orbital modulation in binary systems. Although a few FRB sources exhibit evidence of periodic behavior, it remains unclear whether periodic activity is a common underlying feature of repeating FRBs. Using a new FRB periodicity search pipeline introduced by A. B. Pearlman et al. (2026), which is optimized for sparse event-arrival-time data from FRB surveys, we search for activity periods in the burst arrival times from FRB 20240209A and repeating FRBs in the Second Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME)/FRB Catalog. For FRB 20240209A, we identify a new candidate activity period of 170.4 $\pm$ 4.7 days, with a trials-corrected statistical significance of 5.3$\sigma$. Our larger burst sample shows no evidence of the 128.5-day activity period previously reported for this source by A. Pal (2025). We also report candidate activity periods of 28.46 $\pm$ 0.08 days, 86.7 $\pm$ 0.5 days, and 36.4 $\pm$ 0.5 days for FRB 20190208A, FRB 20200926A, and FRB 20220529A, with trials-corrected statistical significances of 3.1$\sigma$, 4.0$\sigma$, and 3.5$\sigma$, respectively. All statistical significances are evaluated against a homogeneous (constant-rate) Poisson null hypothesis, and we caution that they may decrease under null models that incorporate burst clustering. Collectively, our results constitute the most comprehensive search for periodic activity in the repeating FRB population to date.

title: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients with high brightness temperatures, but their physical origin remains uncertain. The association of FRB 200428 with a Galactic magnetar provides compelling evidence that at least some FRBs originate from magnetar-like systems. Nevertheless, periodic modulation associated with neutron-star rotation has not been robustly detected in extragalactic FRBs. Motivated by the reported 1.7 s periodicity in the active repeater FRB 20201124A, we conduct a systematic search for short-timescale periodicity in four highly active repeating FRB sources. We employ a sliding-window method that analyzes temporally adjacent bursts within restricted time intervals, allowing transient or intermittent periodic signals to be identified. The search yields apparent period candidates with nominal Poisson-calibrated significances comparable to that reported for the 1.7 s signal, although the inferred periods vary substantially among sources and observing windows. We then perform a nonparametric waiting-time randomization test, in which the observed waiting-time distribution is preserved while the temporal ordering is destroyed. The randomized sequences reproduce the main candidate-period structures seen in the data, demonstrating that these apparent periodicities can arise from the non-Poissonian waiting-time statistics rather than from a coherent periodic process. Rotation-modulated epidemic-type aftershock sequence simulations provide a complementary parametric illustration of the same effect. We therefore find no robust evidence for a short intrinsic periodicity in these data, and the reported 1.7 s signal is not uniquely distinguished from clustering-induced candidates. Robust periodicity searches must evaluate significance against null models that account for the observed waiting-time statistics and the full search procedure.

title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Hyperaccreting magnetized neutron stars inside rotating massive envelopes: Low-power jets and precursor flares
abstract: The engulfment of a neutron star (NS) by a massive companion initiates a highly dynamic common-envelope (CE) evolution phase. As the NS spirals into the dense stellar core, it is subjected to hypercritical accretion rates that threaten to rapidly collapse the NS into a black hole (BH). However, if the infalling envelope possesses sufficient angular momentum and magnetic fields, the NS might survive longer and launch feedback-driving jets. To investigate this, we perform fully coupled, axisymmetric General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of hyperaccreting NSs, featuring energy-integrated two-moment neutrino transport and a 13-isotope nuclear reaction network. We systematically vary the envelope rotation profile and the magnetic field strength of the NS surface ($B_{\rm surf} \sim 5 \times 10^{10} - 5 \times 10^{13}$~G). In non-magnetised models, we find that envelope rotation naturally forms a centrifugal barrier and a geometrically thick accretion disk, which suppresses the mass accretion rate and lowers the neutrino luminosity; conversely, the intrinsic spin of the NS has a negligible global impact. In magnetised models, the differential rotation of the accretion flow vigorously amplifies the toroidal magnetic field via the $Ω$-effect, driving the expansion of magnetic towers. Crucially, for strong initial surface magnetic fields ($B_{\rm surf} \gtrsim 2.3 \times 10^{13}$~G), the intense magnetic pressure could completely halt the accretion flow at the NS surface and evacuates a low-density polar funnel. We conclude that while this highly magnetised NS engine successfully delays prompt BH formation and may launch low-power precursor jets (with powers up to ${\sim} 10^{46}~{\rm erg/s}$) capable of generating observable X-ray flares, it lacks the energy budget to unbind the massive envelope, potentially setting the stage for a subsequent BH-driven explosion.

title: Stability of parton distributions at high x : Impact of nuclear and power corrections
abstract: We present a comprehensive new global QCD analysis of unpolarized parton distribution functions (PDFs) based upon proton, deuteron, and A = 3 data, including the latest inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) measurements from Jefferson Lab at high Bjorken- x . Using the JAM Bayesian Monte Carlo framework, we systematically explore the stability of the PDFs with respect to variations in the cuts on the invariant mass W of the DIS final state, the implementation of target mass and higher twist corrections, as well as on the nuclear wave functions for the A = 2 and 3 data. We find the u and d quark PDFs (and the d / u ratio) are relatively stable up to x ≈ 0.8 and able to describe DIS data down to W 2 = 3.5 GeV 2 and Q 2 = m c 2 . Within the collinear factorization framework, the fitted higher twist corrections to DIS are found to be positive and largely isospin independent. The description of the nuclear data also requires nonzero isoscalar and isovector nucleon off-shell PDF contributions, which gives specific predictions for the ratio R D of deuteron to isoscalar nucleon structure functions.

title: Microscopic spin-parity distributions of fission fragments
abstract: Recent microscopic studies have investigated various features of the spin distributions of fission fragments, but their parity distributions remain largely unexplored. In this Letter, we provide a complete characterization of the spin--parity content of fission fragments within a time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov framework, performing for the first time simultaneous projections on angular momentum, particle number, and parity. Calculations are carried out for the thermal neutron-induced fission of $^{239}$Pu using both the Gogny and Skyrme energy density functionals. We find that dynamical pair breaking during fission populates a significant fraction of unnatural-parity states and generates components with non-zero spin projections $K$. The parity content is found to depend on the number parity of the fragments, with odd-mass nuclei exhibiting pronounced parity staggering and odd-odd nuclei favoring negative parity. These results show that the parity distribution of fragments can depart significantly from the equiprobable partition commonly assumed in statistical de-excitation models, with potential implications for the modeling of fragment decay.

title: Improving the accuracy of the Lorentz integral transform method using complex kernels
abstract: The Lorentz integral transform (LIT) method is a powerful tool for calculating quantum response functions; however, it requires an ill-posed inversion. Here we show that solutions of the LIT equation can also determine two additional integral transforms: a complex Stieltjes transform and a double-pole transform, at little additional computational cost. A Fourier analysis of the associated deconvolution problem shows that both alternative kernels are better conditioned than the Lorentzian kernel at the same width parameter $\Gamma $. We benchmark the resulting inversions for deuteron photodisintegration by adding controlled noise to the LIT solutions. Relative to the standard LIT, the alternative kernels yield response functions with reduced noise-induced scatter: by a factor of 2-3 for the complex Stieltjes kernel and 3-4 for the double-pole kernel.

versions.abstract: The Lorentz integral transform (LIT) method is a powerful tool for calculating quantum response functions; however, it requires an ill-posed inversion. Here we show that solutions of the LIT equation can also determine two additional integral transforms: a complex Stieltjes transform and a double-pole transform, at little additional computational cost. A Fourier analysis of the associated deconvolution problem shows that both alternative kernels are better conditioned than the Lorentzian kernel at the same width parameter $\Gamma $. We benchmark the resulting inversions for deuteron photodisintegration by adding controlled noise to the LIT solutions. Relative to the standard LIT, the alternative kernels yield response functions with reduced noise-induced scatter: by a factor of 2-3 for the complex Stieltjes kernel and 3-4 for the double-pole kernel.

title: From vacuum-like fragmentation to overlap-influenced evolution in SMASH: Identified hadron spectra in proton-proton collisions at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron
Comparison of several model averaging methods in nuclear charge radius predictions
abstract: The performance of five model averaging methods, including the arithmetic mean (AM), weighted mean (WM), naive Bayesian model averaging (NBMA), principal component analysis (PCA), and power-moderated mean (PMM) methods, in nuclear charge radius predictions is investigated. Five commonly used nuclear charge radius models are adopted as inputs for the averaging procedures. The charge radius differences between the experimental data and the original nuclear models are analyzed and the results after considering the model averaging methods are also discussed. The calculations show that the NBMA method can provide the best root-mean-square (rms) deviation among these five model averaging methods. The PCA method can extract useful physical information and not only helps to interpret the model differences but also offers a feasible way to construct improved empirical models by recombining the principal components. In contrast to the other methods, whose results worsen upon including a new model with a larger rms deviation, the rms deviation of the PCA method remains almost unaffected. The PMM method is capable of integrating the strengths of various nuclear models and delivering reasonable uncertainty estimates not only in known regions but also in unknown ones. This method can automatically adjust data uncertainties to achieve consistency, and it can provide a tool for a smooth transition of the nuclear charge radius prediction from the WM to the AM. The extrapolation ability of these model averaging methods is checked by 66 newly observed data after year 2021. The calculations show that model averaging offers a reliable strategy for nuclear charge radius predictions, combining high accuracy on known data with robust extrapolation to new measurements. The charge radii and the odd-even staggering in calcium isotopes are also discussed.

Isospin effects and symmetry energy in nuclear reactions
abstract: Isospin and the symmetry energy are linked within the symmetry term of the liquid-drop mass formula and within the corresponding term of the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter. The Pauli exclusion principle leads to a leading quadratic dependence of the kinetic part of the symmetry term of the nuclear binding-energy formula on the neutron-proton asymmetry (N-Z)/A. Charge symmetry ensures the same leading quadratic dependence for the potential part. Charge invariance further generalizes this dependence, to lowest order, from T$_3^2$ to T(T+1). The strength of the symmetry term, in contrast, is determined by the symmetry energy. At sub-saturation densities the symmetry energy can be constrained by nuclear-structure observables, such as neutron skin thicknesses, isovector collective modes and the related electric dipole polarizability, and excitation energies of isobaric analog states. It can also be constrained by reaction observables, such as charge exchange and elastic scattering cross sections, isoscaling and isospin diffusion. At supra-saturation densities, by contrast, the only means of studying asymmetric nuclear matter under laboratory conditions are relativistic heavy-ion collisions. These studies use differential observables such as neutron/proton flows and light isobar or $\pi^{-}/\pi^{+}$ ratios. Complementary information can be obtained from neutron star observations including gravitational waves. The latest measurements and analyses of the stiffness of the symmetry energy will be presented, together with the recent NA61/SHINE observation of an unexpectedly large isospin-symmetry violation in kaon production. Attention will also be paid to the challenges of measuring charged and neutral products of relativistic heavy-ion collisions in the context of the recent ASY-EOS II experiment at GSI and to the new detectors used in the setup.

title: GRB 181201A: Spectropolarimetric Constraints on Prompt Emission and Magnetic Field Structure
abstract: Abstract Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have served as testbeds for high-energy astrophysical phenomena since their discovery over 50 yr ago. GRB detections reveal diverse properties across events, complicating efforts to constrain their emission mechanisms, magnetic fields, jet structures, and compositions. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool utilized to disentangle these properties. INTEGRAL/IBIS has previously detected three polarized GRBs 041219A (65% ± 26%), 061122 (>33%), and 140206A (>28%). We present the time-integrated and time-resolved analyses of the fourth-polarized GRB 181201A. This GRB exhibits high polarization ( 81 . 5 − 15.7 + 17.2 % ) over three time bins with the highest signal-to-noise ratio, and the polarization angle (PA) shows a modest temporal evolution. The photon index does not cross the synchrotron line-of-death and shows a hard-to-soft evolution. A high degree of polarization (PD) tends to disfavor a photospheric emission model, as previous studies indicate that this model yields PD < 20%. A modest evolution in the PA points towards a nonaxisymmetric jet with a multipatch emission. Our results indicate that under standard synchrotron conditions, the magnetic field is coherent but lacks global structure. Moreover, the field has multiple patches, but only one or a few dominate due to high PDs, which overlap with the intrinsic maximum of synchrotron emission within 3 σ errors. The high PD is also indicative of the Compton drag scenario, but only under certain conditions, such as viewing the relativistic jet near its edge. However, given our error bars and the scope for improvement in our pipeline, we cannot strongly favor either scenario; both may remain viable.

High-order perturbative calculations of nuclear ground states: Automated evaluation of many-body diagrams
abstract: We advance the many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) calculations of the ground-state energy and radius of closed-shell nuclei beyond third order. Using automated diagram generation and evaluation up to fifth order, we present ground-state properties of selected closed-shell nuclei up to $^{78}$Ni with two- and three-nucleon interactions derived from chiral effective field theory. A clear convergence trend is observed for the ground-state energy enabling calculations at improved accuracy. We further investigate in detail the decomposition of the fourth-order contributions. For the ground-state energy, the magnitude of the fourth-order contribution is typically less than half of the third order, and a typical cancellation among different classes of diagrams is observed. Finally, we perform a comprehensive comparison between MBPT and non-perturbative in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) calculations, with the goal to provide insight into many-body uncertainties associated with the IMSRG(2) truncation.

title: The location of the upper edge of the pair-instability supernovae black hole mass gap
abstract: Abstract Gravitational wave observations are beginning to probe the upper edge of the pair-instability supernova (PISN) black hole mass gap, a key prediction of stellar evolution. In this work, we quantify the sensitivity of this boundary to stellar-evolution inputs and modeling choices using a suite of simulations that vary inputs including nuclear reaction rates, mixing processes, and stellar winds. We find that variations of the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction rate produce the largest shift in the upper edge, ΔM ∼ 34 M⊙, with the triple-α rate producing a comparable shift of ∼24 M⊙. Notably, 16O + 16O reactions shift the upper edge by ∼15 M⊙ while leaving the lower edge unchanged, implying they can widen or narrow the mass gap. Other processes affect the location at the ≲ 10 M⊙ level. In contrast to the lower edge, we find that the upper edge is robust to variations in spatial and temporal resolution, indicating that it is reliably resolved in current simulations. Our results demonstrate that the upper edge is most sensitive to nuclear reaction rates and, while comparatively less affected by astrophysical contamination than the lower edge, provides a direct probe of the nuclear processes governing pair instability. We discuss the implications for interpreting high-mass black hole detections in gravitational wave data.

title: The Price of Discovery: Cost-Optimized Detectors for the GUT-Scale QCD Axion
abstract: Grand unification and string theory point to a quantum chromodynamics (QCD) axion with mass between $10^{-11}$ and $10^{-8}$ eV, while heterotic string theory suggests a mass of $0.5-0.8$ neV. We study which laboratory experiment could discover or exclude DFSZ-strength QCD axion dark matter at and above 0.5 neV at the lowest cost, which we estimate from scaling laws calibrated to historical data. We find that a lumped-element detector, building on the ABRACADABRA concept, can do so with demonstrated readout technology; an example is a shielded toroid about 14 m across with a 6 T NbTi magnet, whose magnet and cryostat we estimate at around 120 million Swiss francs (MCHF). If projected readout targets are met, a 5 m toroid at 25 MCHF suffices. We find these designs by optimizing the toroid, solenoid, and core lumped-element topologies under a common cost metric. The toroid emerges as the most promising and cost-effective topology. The optimal field of the toroid detector is far below the 16 T of the proposed DMRadio-GUT design, which would cost nearly twice as much as our optimum. Heterodyne searches with superconducting radio-frequency cavities, with cavity shapes that we optimize for price, cost between about the same as and twice as much as the lumped-element detectors, but require cavities of volumes $\sim50-2000$ m$^3$. We find that nuclear-magnetic-resonance searches (CASPEr) need orders-of-magnitude gains in spin polarization and coherence. We release axionMultiPhysics, an open-source finite-element and multiphysics package for, e.g., magnetoquasistatic and full-wave electromagnetics, superconductors, readout circuits, and mechanics, from which most of our numerical results were obtained.

Density functional theory of renormalization group in nuclear matter
abstract: We present the density functional renormalization group (density-fRG), in which density fluctuations are separated from the quantum fluctuations in the vacuum and are integrated out successively within the functional renormalization group approach. This allows us to quantify medium effects and to study the physics of high baryon densities. The method is applied to the nucleon-meson effective field theory, also known as the Walecka model, where the density dependence of the nucleon-meson Yukawa couplings is generated self-consistently by their flow equations. It is found that both the attractive and the repulsive nucleon-meson interactions are screened by the dense medium. This results in an equation of state of symmetric nuclear matter that is stiffer than in the relativistic mean-field approximation for $\rho_0\lesssim\rho\lesssim 2.5\,\rho_0$, and becomes softer for $\rho\gtrsim 2.5\,\rho_0$, where $\rho_0$ is the saturation density. Furthermore, a new phenomenon called the locking of the Fermi surface is found: the effective energy of the quasi-nucleon stays close to the Fermi surface, while both are running with the renormalization group scale.

title: Beyond-point-Coulomb electromagnetic corrections in ab initio nuclear-structure calculations
Neutron stars with an agnostic dark sector: Core and halo configurations from a two-fluid approach
abstract: The study of dark matter admixed neutron stars has the potential to advance our understanding of dark matter particle candidates. However, the large parameter space of dark matter particle masses restricts a systematic, model-independent study. In this analysis, we employ agnostic hadronic and dark matter equations of state to construct dark-matter-admixed neutron stars within a two-fluid formalism. Dark matter is characterised solely by its low-density equation of state and mass, and is modelled as a Fermi gas, while hadronic matter is anchored at low and high densities by chiral effective field theory and perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations. A speed-of-sound parametrisation covers the intermediate density region for hadronic matter and the high-density region for dark matter, so the dark matter equation of state is constrained only by thermodynamic consistency, free from bias toward a softer or stiffer equation of state. Within this agnostic framework, we find that dark matter does not generically compactify the star: light dark matter forms extended halos that raise the tidal deformability, while heavy dark matter forms compact cores that lower it. Consequently, the dominant observational constraint shifts from gravitational-wave tidal deformability for light, halo-dominated models to NICER mass--radius data for heavy, core-dominated models. Using current data at $1\sigma$, we constrain the dark matter fraction to $f_{\mathrm{DM}} \lesssim 0.11$ for light dark matter. Being almost independent of any assumed dark-sector microphysics, our framework yields conservative, broadly applicable bounds on the dark-matter content of neutron stars. Neutron stars with similar masses but very different tidal deformabilities could be a smoking-gun signature of dark matter in Neutron stars.

title: Evaluation of tracking plane pitch and xenon-helium gas mixtures for the NEXT experiment
abstract: NEXT is an experimental program to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay ($\beta\beta 0\nu$) in high-pressure xenon gas using electroluminescent time projection chambers. A key feature of the NEXT technology is the reconstruction of MeV-scale electron tracks, which plays a key role in identifying $\beta\beta 0\nu$ events. This work presents a Monte Carlo study aimed at determining the optimal configuration for NEXT detectors employing SiPM-based tracking planes. The simulations are carried out in the NEXT-100 detector geometry, and to classify the events as signal or background, we use a Sparse Convolutional Neural Network. We find that topological rejection power improves by approximately a factor of two at the lower pressure studied (5 bar) compared to the baseline design (13.5 bar). A finer pitch also offers consistent improvement, where reducing pitch from 15 mm to 5 mm decreased the accepted background fraction by a factor of approximately 1.4 at 13.5 bar for a fixed signal efficiency in the different configurations studied. The addition of helium to reduce electron diffusion provides a comparable enhancement, reducing the accepted background fraction by up to a factor of 1.5 at 13.5 bar. We highlight two key practical configurations at 13.5 bar pressure: the present NEXT-100 (pure Xe with a 15 mm tracking plane pitch) and an upgraded NEXT-100 (a Xe-He gas mixture and a 10 mm tracking plane pitch). These results provide quantitative guidance for the design and optimisation of future NEXT detectors, balancing physics performance with technical and financial constraints.

title: Core-edge integrated scenario with a high-performance hybrid core, naturally small ELMs, and a dissipative divertor on DIII-D
abstract: Abstract Operating at higher gas fueling and lower injected torque has improved the core-edge integration and reactor relevance of the hybrid scenario. Progress was made in the core, pedestal and edge of the plasma. In the core, higher density ($>50\%$ increase compared to past hybrid plasmas) lowered the heat diffusivity and turbulent energy flux. In particular, electron cyclotron heating (ECH) had less of a deleterious effect on confinement at higher density. High fueling rates led to an increase in separatrix density, which destabilizes a higher n ($n>50$) resistive-ballooning mode at the foot of the pedestal. This higher n mode is associated with smaller, higher frequency edge localized modes (ELMs) ($f_{ELM} \geq 500$ Hz) that limit pedestal growth below the peeling-ballooning stability limit associated with type-I ELMs. Access to this small-ELM regime requires both a wide density pedestal (from higher gas puffing) and sufficiently high plasma squareness. These higher frequency ELMs have oscillations in the stored energy of $<1\%$ with each ELM and lower peak heat flux to the divertor compared to type-I ELMs. The higher edge density with a wider density pedestal also helps to maintain core performance through partial divertor detachment. Puffing N$_2$ gas from the private flux region of the divertor led to partial detachment without a decrease in $\beta_N$, while maintaining pedestal temperatures of $\sim1$~keV. Under the assumption of a hybrid-like pedestal, FASTRAN projections of the high-density hybrid scenario to a compact fusion pilot plant produce positive net electric power.

title: Fluctuations and Correlations of Conserved Charges in Isobar Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 200 GeV with the STAR Detector
abstract: We report measurements of second-order cumulants and correlations of experimentally accessible baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness proxies in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$~GeV with the STAR experiment. The results exhibit similar centrality dependences in the two isobar systems within uncertainties. The baryon-strangeness correlation $C_{BS}$ is compared with lattice-QCD and UrQMD calculations. Motivated by recent lattice-QCD predictions for QCD matter in an external magnetic field, several ratios of conserved-charge correlations are studied as functions of centrality. In peripheral collisions, the measured ratios exhibit the same ordering as the lattice-QCD prediction. A qualitatively similar hierarchy is also found in UrQMD, although the model underpredicts the observed peripheral-to-central enhancement. These results motivate further quantitative studies of possible magnetic-field contributions and other sources of the observed centrality dependence.

title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $\delta_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $\beta$ decays
abstract: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $\alpha$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $\epsilon_\chi$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $\delta_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $\beta$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals. The relative size of three-nucleon corrections to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$ in medium mass nuclei, where two-body contributions tend to be smaller, remains to be investigated. We then use these results to determine $V_{ud}$ from the superallowed transition ${}^{10}\mathrm{C}\rightarrow{}^{10}\mathrm{B}$.

title: Semi-regularised three-body pseudopotential for mean-field and beyond-mean-field calculations
abstract: Abstract We derive the most general form of a local leading-order semi-regularised three-bodypseudopotential. This particular form of pseudopotential is developed with the aim ofgenerating contributions to the nuclear energy density functional (EDF) in both theparticle-hole and particle-particle channels and, hence, to be usable in mean-field andbeyond-mean-field calculations without ambiguities or mathematical difficulties. Once theEDF is obtained, analytical expressions of commonly considered properties of infinitenuclear matter are provided. Finally, the structure of the EDF and the associated meanfields are given for spherically-symmetric systems.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Predicted Exotic Doubly Heavy-Strange Pentaquarks
abstract: We predict exotic doubly heavy--strange pentaquarks with minimal quark content $u\bar d sQQ'$ ($QQ'=cc,bc,bb$) within a coupled-channel unitary framework where the interaction is derived from an extension of the local hidden gauge approach to the heavy-quark sector. We obtain a robust spectrum of manifestly exotic states; two states appear in the $u\bar d scc$ sector, three in $u\bar d scb$, and two in $u\bar d sbb$. These emerge either as bound states or resonances, along with seven additional virtual states manifested as threshold cusps. The binding mechanism is dominated by off-diagonal transitions among heavy-baryon--light-meson channels, while diagonal interactions are strongly suppressed. These results extend exotic hadron spectroscopy into the doubly heavy--strange sector and provide concrete targets for future experimental searches.

title: Novel approach to short baseline oscillation searches using neutrino tagging with nuSCOPE
Effects of charm-strange resonances on charmed meson production by recombination in relativistic heavy ion collisions
abstract: We discuss charmed mesons in heavy-ion collisions by focusing on their production from the quark-gluon plasma by quark recombination. We consider the production of not only the $D$, $D^*$, $D_s$, and $D_s^*$, but also the $D_{s0}^*(2317)$, $D_{s1}(2460)$, $D_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_{s2}^*(2573)$, thereby investigating the important role of heavier charm-strange resonances in understanding the measurements of the $D$ and $D_s$ mesons at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We calculate their yields and transverse momentum distributions, and also evaluate ratios of the transverse momentum distribution between various charmed mesons, i.e., the $D_s$ and $D^0$, the $D_s$ and $D^+$, $D_s^*$ and $D^{*0}$, and $D_s^*$ and $D^{*+}$. Through this analysis, we attempt to understand in more detail the effects of strangeness enhancement on charmed meson production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV.

title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium
abstract: Abstract Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF -MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.
authors: Huub J. M. Op den Camp
citation_authors: Op den Camp, Huub J. M.

title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

title: Spin-dependent fermion potentials from mixed tensor couplings of massive spin-1 and spin-2 bosons
abstract: Searches for weak spin-dependent forces are commonly interpreted in terms of a basis of sixteen rotationally invariant two-fermion potentials. We derive finite-range coordinate-space potentials generated by a massive spin-1 boson with vector, axial-vector, tensor, and pseudotensor couplings to Dirac fermions. In addition to the familiar vector--vector, vector--axial-vector, and axial-vector--axial-vector interactions, we obtain the mixed vector--tensor, vector--pseudotensor, axial-vector--tensor, and axial-vector--pseudotensor potentials, together with tensor--tensor, tensor--pseudotensor, and pseudotensor--pseudotensor terms. We retain the contact terms needed in atomic-scale applications and give compact expressions that include both orderings of inequivalent fermion vertices. We then extend the analysis to a massive spin-2 mediator described by a symmetric Fierz--Pauli field. Besides the conventional coupling to the conserved fermion energy--momentum tensor, we consider a symmetric axial-tensor current. Its nonconservation for massive fermions makes the longitudinal spin-2 helicities contribute to axial-tensor--axial-tensor exchange. The leading minimal spin-2 interactions are either P,T even or P odd and T evenl. Heavy-mediator contact limits and the distinction between the M-->0 massive-spin-2 limit and a genuine massless graviton are also discussed. We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.
