title: Multi-Gaussian Model for Intrabeam Scattering
abstract: Conventional analytical models of intrabeam scattering (IBS), such as the Piwinski model and Bjorken-Mtingwa model, generally rely on the assumption of a Gaussian beam distribution, limiting their applicability to non-Gaussian cases. In this work, we develop a multi-Gaussian model to extend analytical IBS calculations to a broader class of non-Gaussian phase-space distributions. The proposed approach represents a non-Gaussian distribution as a superposition of Gaussian components sharing a common covariance matrix but having different mean values. We derived a generalized model for evaluating the momentum second-moment evolution rate and the IBS growth rate. Furthermore, for equally spaced Gaussian components, we developed an infinite bunch train model and introduce a practical truncation rule to reduce computational costs. The model is applied to a representative steady-state microbunching (SSMB) storage ring, where longitudinal overlap between neighboring microbunches is shown to enhance IBS growth rates in all three directions. The proposed framework provides a practical approach to evaluating IBS in non-Gaussian beam distributions and offers a basis for further development toward a more general non-Gaussian IBS theory.

title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

title: A Diagnostic Method for Proto-Neutron Star Magnetic Fields by Supernova Fallback Neutrinos
abstract: Young isolated neutron stars exhibit a wide range of magnetic field strengths. To understand the origin of this diversity, it is important to observationally constrain magnetic fields during the proto-neutron star (PNS) phase. We propose a novel diagnostic of PNS magnetic fields using neutrinos associated with supernova fallback. By performing one-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the supernova fallback onto a magnetized PNS, we investigate how the energy spectra of the fallback neutrinos depend on the PNS magnetic field strength and the fallback accretion rate. We find that stronger magnetic fields and lower accretion rates produce softer spectra because the fallback neutrinos are emitted mainly near the magnetospheric radius, which becomes larger under these conditions. To quantify this spectral softening, we define a hardness ratio based on event rates above and below 30 MeV and introduce a hardness-event-rate diagram. Using this diagram, we identify the parameter region in which our diagnostic is applicable. Its applicability depends on the PNS magnetic field strength, fallback accretion rate, onset time of the fallback phase, and neutrino mass ordering. We also investigate the dependence on the PNS radius and find that a larger radius produces softer spectra, indicating a degeneracy between the magnetic field and PNS compactness. An independent constraint on the PNS compactness would therefore enable us to better constrain the magnetic field. These results suggest that future multimessenger observations of galactic supernovae can provide a new window into the NS diversity.

title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
abstract: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $\Lambda_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $\epsilon_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $\Delta=1/3-P/\epsilon$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

title: Robust feedback control of collisional plasma dynamics in presence of uncertainties
abstract: Magnetic fusion aims to confine high-temperature plasma within a device, enabling the fusion of deuterium and tritium nuclei to release energy. Due to the very large temperatures involved, it is essential to isolate the plasma from the device walls to prevent structural damage and the external magnetic fields play a fundamental role in achieving this confinement. In realistic settings, the physical mechanisms governing plasma behavior are highly complex, involving numerous uncertain parameters and intricate particle interactions, such as collisions, that significantly affect both confinement efficiency and overall stability. In this work, we address particularly these challenges by proposing a robust feedback control strategy designed to steer the plasma towards a desired spatial region, despite the presence of uncertainties. From a modeling perspective, we consider a collisional plasma described by a Vlasov-Poisson-BGK system, which accounts for a self-consistent electric field and a strong external magnetic field, while incorporating uncertainty in the model. A key feature of the proposed control strategy is its independence from the random parameter, making it particularly suitable for practical applications. A series of numerical simulations confirms the effectiveness of our approach and demonstrates the ability of external magnetic fields to successfully confine plasma away from the device boundaries, even in the presence of uncertain conditions.

title: Gravitational Wave Modeling of White-Dwarf--Compact-Object Binaries and Observational Outlook
abstract: Binaries consisting of a white dwarf and a compact object (neutron stars, black holes, or sub-solar-mass compact objects) display unique orbital evolution and gravitational wave signals. We investigate the end stages of these systems by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker "outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz--incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.

title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=\alpha\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $\alpha$ by construction, whereas increasing $\alpha$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$\alpha_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $\alpha$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-\kappa$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
abstract: The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers. We then discuss measurements of the angular differences between three different axis definitions inside the jets. The three definitions offer different sensitivity to wide-angle soft radiation and systematically probe the radiation pattern from charm quarks. The final measurement regards jet angularities, which characterize the weighted angular distribution of the jet constituents. These powerful observables probe the parton shower, with sensitivity to parton-mass and Casimir-factor related effects that can be tuned by adjusting the importance of wide-angle radiation.
authors: Emma Yeats (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)

title: Recent Advances and Precision Measurements with the JYFLTRAP Double Penning Trap Mass Spectrometer
abstract: High-precision atomic-mass measurements with the JYFLTRAP double Penning-trap mass spectrometer at the IGISOL facility provide direct information on decay energies, nuclear binding and shell evolution, isomer excitation energies, and masses relevant to nuclear astrophysics. Recent work has combined the phase-imaging ion-cyclotron-resonance (PI-ICR) method with established ion-purification and selective ion-production techniques to study low-yield nuclei and resolve isomeric states. At JYFLTRAP/IGISOL, mass-selective buffer-gas cooling, Ramsey cleaning, resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS), phase-dependent cleaning, and species-resolved PI-ICR analysis are used in complementary combinations according to the ion yield and the required separation. Laser-frequency tagging correlates individual ion events with the corresponding laser frequency and enables state-resolved resonance-ionization spectra. Selected ion bunches are used for direct mass measurements with PI-ICR or time-of-flight ion-cyclotron resonance (TOF-ICR), for ion counting, or for post-trap decay spectroscopy. When multiple species or states are present, resolved PI-ICR phase spots allow the mass-measurement data to be assigned to the corresponding component. Examples from the recent program include high-precision $Q$-value measurements, neutron-deficient nuclei below $^{100}$Sn, neutron-rich fission fragments, rapid structural evolution around $N\approx60$, and rare-earth nuclei relevant to the astrophysical $r$ process.

title: Fast computation of microscopic optical potentials: beyond existing capabilities
abstract: A microscopic approach to optical potential calculations, based on the leading term in the spectator expansion of the optical potential operator and carried out in momentum space, has been successful in describing nucleon elastic scattering above 100 MeV. However, high computational cost precludes the inclusion of all physics relevant to scattering, such as the tensor part of the nucleon-nucleon (NN) amplitude, three-nucleon forces, multiple scattering and medium effects. Also, this approach does not provide any nucleon-nucleus scattering wave functions needed for reaction calculations. In this Letter, we develop a harmonic oscillator expansion version of this approach, which provides the same representation of optical potential both in momentum and coordinate spaces, accelerates calculations by two orders of magnitude, includes the missing tensor component of the NN scattering amplitude and is applicable to nuclei with any spin. Test calculations have been performed for several light nuclei whose densities were obtained in the No-Core Shell Model using a chiral Hamiltonian. We demonstrate convergence of this expansion and clarify the role of the tensor force, which manifests itself mainly in coupling between channels with different spin. Comparison to experimental data is presented for selected cases. The methodology could be extended for scattering of other projectiles (hadronic and pionic), small complex nuclei and hypernuclei. It also suggests a pathway for including more complicated physics into the scheme and extending it to lower energies. It could be also helpful in assessing the accuracy of upcoming scattering emulators.

title: Open Heavy Flavor in Nuclear Collisions: From Lattice QCD to Observables
abstract: Heavy quarks serve as excellent probes of the Quark-Gluon-Plasma (QGP) produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Here, we report on a comprehensive framework that transports charm quarks from their initial production through the QGP medium, hadronization, and the hadronic phase to final observables in experiments. For the transport through the QGP fireball, which is described by 2+1D relativistic viscous fluid dynamics, we employ an extended Langevin equation that combines elastic diffusion processes with medium-induced radiation, including interference effects. The charm-quark transport coefficients are derived from nonperturbative $T$-matrix interactions, which are constrained by lattice QCD and also produce an equation of state for the thermal medium which is consistent with the one employed in the hydrodynamic simulations. Pre-hadronic resonant states which emerge in the $T$-matrix near the QGP transition temperature naturally lead to a transition to hadronic degrees of freedom. This transition is realized in two different approaches: a coalescence model augmented with 4-momentum conservation and the resonance recombination model, both supplemented with fragmentation functions constrained by charm-hadron spectra in proton-proton collisions at the LHC and RHIC. The late-stage rescattering of charm hadrons is assessed with schematic heavy-light cross sections implemented into a hadronic transport model. We report results for the nuclear modification factors and elliptic flows of $D^0$ and $D_s^+$ mesons and $\Lambda_c^+$ baryons, together with the $D_s^+/D^0$ and $\Lambda_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios. The calculations are compared with measurements from the ALICE and CMS collaborations in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=5$\,TeV and with STAR data in Au-Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=200$\,GeV.

title: $\alpha$--$\alpha$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
abstract: We investigate the structural evolution of $\alpha$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $\alpha$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $\alpha$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation survives. The one-body density $\rho(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $\alpha$--$\alpha$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $\alpha$-cluster centroids to isolate the $\alpha$ clusters. In all four systems the $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $\alpha$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.

title: Pairing connections between localized nuclear regions: Orbital reweighting and thermal quenching
abstract: The nucleon localization function (NLF) characterizes nuclear spatial structure; the nonlocal anomalous density (pairing tensor) describes coherent pair amplitude between two points. Global pairing measures leave connections between distinct spatial regions unresolved. We determine how selective orbital participation strengthens pairing connections between localized regions during overall pairing loss, and why heating attenuates the connection while preserving its pattern. Axial Hartree-Fock plus BCS calculations combine NLF with the pairing tensor in shape-constrained 20Ne (distinct localization lobes) and octupole-deformed 144Ba (reflection-asymmetric background). Complete signed orbital sums separate anomalous-weight and spatial-kernel changes at fixed pairing strength and cutoff. Contraction along a constrained 20Ne branch preserves identifiable end lobes while reducing total anomalous norm and increasing the absolute opposite-end integral. Coupled spectrum and gap changes favor a mixed 1d5/2/2s1/2 component and deplete anomalous participation of a predominantly 1p1/2 component. Increased positive strength and weaker destructive interference overcome the net opposing spatial-kernel response; this balance survives mesh refinement. Heating at the reference quadrupole constraint yields compensating thermal and quasiparticle-energy factors, so similar gap reductions produce nearly common attenuation. In 144Ba, octupole deformation and normal-localization modulation persist after anomalous sources vanish. Regional enhancement depends on how selective anomalous participation changes the complete signed orbital sum, including spatial feedback. Nearly proportional participation changes preserve the pattern when kernels remain stable, distinguishing stronger absolute connections from larger normalized fractions on an identifiable localization background.

title: Isospin-breaking effects on the threshold cusp structures in $\Lambda N$-$\Sigma N$ scattering
abstract: We discuss the isospin-breaking effects on threshold cusp structures in multichannel scattering near two-body thresholds. In hadronic systems with isospin symmetry, two or more nearly degenerate thresholds can appear, and their small splitting due to isospin breaking can generate multiple cusp structures in a narrow energy region. In this paper, using the $K$-matrix representation, we derive a general expression for the scattering amplitude near the thresholds and show that the cusp structures can be classified by the signs of the slopes of the cross section above and below threshold. We also show that additional restrictions appear in two- or three-channel systems and in the Flatt\'e amplitude. For three-channel scattering with two nearby thresholds, we clarify how the two cusp structures are related when the threshold splitting is small and how they merge into a single cusp in the degenerate limit. Finally, we discuss the cusp structures in the $\Lambda p$ elastic cross section in the coupled $\Lambda N$-$\Sigma N$ system with charge $Q=+1$. We show that, when isospin breaking is small, the two cusp structures are constrained by isospin symmetry. We also perform quantitative calculations using both simplified examples and realistic input based on N$^2$LO chiral effective field theory, and find that isospin breaking can significantly modify the relative sharpness of the cusps and may even change the cusp type itself.

title: Nuclear Mott transition with neural quantum states
abstract: Bound clusters can dissolve in nuclear matter due to Pauli blocking, a phenomenon known as the Mott transition that is a key determinant of the nuclear abundances in heavy-ion collisions. Microscopic descriptions of this behavior require solving the in-medium Schr\"odinger equation. However, this remains a major computational challenge because the nuclear medium breaks Galilean invariance and couples angular-momentum channels at finite center-of-mass momentum. The emergence of weakly bound states near dissociation further places stringent demands on conventional methods. Here, we address these challenges by introducing MottNet, a momentum-space neural quantum state framework based on self-attention that directly solves the $A$-body in-medium Schr\"{o}dinger equation. Benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the in-medium deuteron, MottNet reveals substantially weaker Mott suppression for $\alpha$ particles in hot and dense nuclear matter than do conventional calculations based on combined approximations. At high baryon densities, the predicted $\alpha$-particle abundance is enhanced by orders of magnitude, even after continuum-edge subtraction. This finding offers a microscopic explanation for the unexpectedly large $\alpha$-particle fraction inferred from a combined analysis of FOPI heavy-ion collision data and transport model calculations.

title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $\gamma$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $\Delta E = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

title: Ripple-induced fast-ion losses modeling in the WEST tokamak
abstract: Abstract The confinement of fast ions is of crucial importance in present and future tokamaks. In typical ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH)-heated scenarios in WEST, fast-ion losses can represent more than 20% of the total injected power. To investigate the origin and underlying mechanisms of these losses, we perform simulations of fast hydrogen ion trajectories in a realistic three-dimensional magnetic field. A weighting method is proposed as a post-process to study a particle distribution function with anisotropic temperatures, while preserving uniform statistics in terms of energy. The influence of the initial and final particle position in phase space is studied in details. The simulation results show that ripple losses fall into two categories: deeply trapped particles moving vertically towards the baffle, and drifting bananas striking the antenna along the direction of the magnetic field. If fast particle losses to the baffle can be directly compared with infrared (IR) measurements, diagnosing particles striking the antennas is more challenging, as IR cameras detect a combination of fast-ion losses, plasma heat convection, and radiation. A net reduction of baffle strikes is observed for particles accelerated on the high field side, whereas antenna strikes, in contrast, may be enhanced. Hence, this study suggests that optimizing the ICRH absorption layer position involves a trade-off: reducing deeply trapped losses at the cost of increasing drifting banana losses.

title: Implementation and first application of EMC3-EIRENE on DTT for assessing the heat load on the ICRH antenna
abstract: Abstract This paper reports on the implementation process of the three-dimensional (3D) edge plasma transport code EMC3-EIRENE on the Divertor Tokamak Test (DTT) facility and the results of its first application, with a focus on assessing the heat load on the Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ICRH) antenna surfaces. The full 3D ICRH antenna structure is incorporated in the 3D simulations. Assuming different toroidal symmetry for the antenna to determine whether the heat load assessment can be carried out with reduced computational effort, and to what extent a 3D assessment deviates. The predictions of the 3D antenna heat load distribution are obtained and the peak values on the top plate and the two side plates reach 0.9, 2.1 and 3.8 MW/m², respectively. The scan of transport coefficients reveals that the heat load was mainly influenced by the plasma density. Increasing the transport coefficients could lead to a corresponding increase in the heat load up to 1-2 order of magnitude. 3D gas puffing is included to evaluate its impact on the antenna heat load. It can increase the local plasma density near the antenna, potentially raising the heat load on the antenna surfaces by a factor of 2–3. The corresponding 3D edge plasma behavior is presented under the coupled effects of gas puffing and the antenna geometrical structure.

title: Hypernucleus production in p+Au reactions at the FAIR facility
abstract: We explore the production of hypernuclei in p+Au reactions using the UrQMD model accompanied by a standard phase-space coalescence model. We focus on the proton beam energy range of $$E_\textrm{lab}= 5 {-} 30$$ GeV as this energy range will be investigated by the CBM-experiment at the upcoming FAIR facility. Starting from proton, $$\Lambda $$ , $$\Sigma $$ , $$\Xi $$ and $$\Omega $$ production, we predict the yields, rapidity and transverse momentum distributions of $$^{3}_{\Lambda }H$$ , $$^{4}_{\Lambda }H$$ , $$\Xi $$ N and $$\Xi $$ NN hypernuclei. We conclude that the production rates of novel multi-strange hypernuclei are well within the reach of the CBM-experiment.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
abstract: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover published energy-loss measurements and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with published screened-ion calculations to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

title: Beyond the Onsager matrix: All-order resummation of relativistic particle and energy diffusion
abstract: We study the coupled diffusion of particle number and energy carried by ultrarelativistic probe particles propagating through a material medium. The probes undergo elastic scattering, which randomizes their direction, and inelastic scattering, which exchanges energy with the medium while preserving particle number. We compute exactly the full $2\times2$ frequency- and wave-number-dependent diffusivity matrix, resumming the constitutive gradient expansion to all orders. In a particularly natural Onsager-normalized basis of conserved densities, the resummed matrix is found to be diagonal at arbitrary frequency and wave number, even though particle and energy transport remain coupled and the conventional Onsager matrix has nonzero thermoelectric cross coefficients. Beyond the hydrodynamic limit, the resummed diffusivities resolve microscopic relaxation timescales and the ballistic kinetic continuum that are invisible to the ordinary Onsager coefficients.

title: Bayesian inference of the dense matter equation of state built upon extended Skyrme interactions: A generalization
abstract: The nonrelativistic theory of nuclear matter (NM) based on Brussels-Skyrme interactions is employed to develop models for dense and neutron-rich matter within a Bayesian framework. We employ the following set of constraints: the four best-known nuclear empirical parameters, the density dependence of the energy per particle in pure neutron matter (PNM), the density dependence of the Landau effective mass ($m_\mathrm{eff}$) of neutrons in PNM and symmetric NM, and a lower limit on the maximum gravitational mass that neutron stars (NSs) can support. In addition, a number of ``sanity checks'' are added: the values of the speed of sound, neutron and proton Landau effective masses, and Fermi velocities are constrained up to the central density of the most massive NS configuration and for isospin asymmetries $\delta=(n_n-n_p)/(n_n+n_p)$ ranging from 0 to 1. Our ensemble of models \emph{fully} explores the capacity of nonrelativistic Brussels-Skyrme effective interactions to describe NM at densities exceeding several times the nuclear saturation density. This is a necessary step toward a better understanding of the properties of dense matter and possible correlations between the parameters of NSs and the parameters of NM. Due to the pronounced U-shaped density dependencies of $m_\mathrm{eff}$, which qualitatively agree with the predictions of ab initio calculations featuring three-body forces, all our models exhibit a non-monotonic ``rise-and-fall'' behavior of the thermal pressure ($p_\mathrm{th}$) as a function of density, which in extreme cases leads to $p_\mathrm{th} < 0$. This work is a generalization of [Beznogov and Raduta, Phys. Rev. C 110, 035805 (2024)].

title: Sensitivity of jet quenching to the initial state in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: In heavy-ion collisions, nuclear matter is subjected to extreme conditions in a highly dynamical, rapidly evolving environment. This poses a tremendous challenge for calculating jet quenching observables. Current approaches rely on analytical results for static cases, introducing theoretical uncertainties and biases in our understanding of the preequilibrated medium. To address this issue, we employ resummation schemes to derive analytical rates for radiative energy loss in generic, evolving backgrounds. We investigate regimes where rare scattering and multiple scattering with the dynamical medium occurs, and extract relevant scales governing the in-medium emission rate of soft gluons. Our analysis indicates that strong jet quenching is only possible when the equilibration time of the medium is longer than its mean free path, highlighting the importance of medium modifications of jets in the earliest stages of heavy-ion collisions. We also demonstrate analytically that a medium evolution, which initially has a small coupling to jets, typically leads to a stronger jet azimuthal asymmetry at the same jet suppression factor.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Improved Scalability of Metallic Magnetic Calorimeters
abstract: Metallic Magnetic Calorimeters are a promising tool for high-precision X-ray spectroscopy. However the signal processing and calibration pipeline required to exploit their full potential is complex and difficult to scale for large, highly pixelated detector arrays. In this work, we investigate Machine Learning methods for maXs-series detectors, focusing on pulse classification and artifact rejection as well as pulse-shape analysis and feature extraction. By combining unsupervised label auto-discovery with supervised classification and regression, we obtain robust and scalable artifact rejection for high-confidence template building. For ML-based feature extraction, our results constitute a promising proof of principle: in simulation, the ML estimator remains competitive across realistic pulse-shape and noise variation. On real detector data, the method reaches performance comparable to the hand-optimized FIR baseline before gain-drift correction, while further domain adaptation is required to match the established manual analysis pipeline. Both results represent important steps toward a fully automated and scalable data processing procedure.
journal_ref: M. O. Herdrich, T. Mattis, G. Weber, D. A. Schnauß-Müller, J. H. Walch, Th. Stöhlker; Machine learning approaches for improved scalability of metallic magnetic calorimeters. J. Appl. Phys. 7 November 2026; 140 (17): 174501

title: Fluctuation modes in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions: from 2D to 3D hybrid simulations
abstract: This dissertation investigates how the initial stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions shape the evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the observables measured experimentally. Particular attention is given to the initial state and pre-equilibrium dynamics, which constitute the main sources of uncertainty in hybrid simulations. The first part of the dissertation reviews the framework underlying state-of-the-art hybrid simulations and the numerical tools used in phenomenological analyses. The second part studies the matching between pre-equilibrium evolution and viscous hydrodynamics. Since commonly used conformal kinetic-theory descriptions are inconsistent with the non-conformal hydrodynamic equation of state, an entropy-density matching prescription is proposed. This prescription reduces the artificial bulk pressure generated at the switching time and improves the consistency of the hybrid framework. The third part develops a mode-by-mode decomposition of initial energy-density profiles to isolate fluctuation modes and quantify their contributions to final observables. Applied to Pb-Pb collisions across centrality classes and extended to a fully three-dimensional O-O collision system, the method shows that initial fluctuations survive hydrodynamic evolution and leave measurable imprints on final observables. In O-O collisions, fluctuations can dominate over geometric effects from the impact parameter, demonstrating that intermediate-sized systems are not simply scaled-down versions of large systems. Overall, these results provide tools for constraining the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and for understanding how fluctuations propagate through the QGP evolution.

title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
abstract: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rza\.{z}ewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
abstract: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($\Delta N_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

title: Measurement of Sn 119 ( p , γ ) Sb 120 and Sn 116 ( p , γ ) Sb 117 reaction cross sections at energies of astrophysical relevance
abstract: The cross sections of the $^{119}\mathrm{Sn}{(p,\ensuremath{\gamma})}^{120}\text{Sb}$ and $^{116}\mathrm{Sn}{(p,\ensuremath{\gamma})}^{117}\text{Sb}$ reactions have been measured using the activation technique over the center-of-mass energy ranges of 2.43--7.06 and 2.43--4.92 MeV, respectively. The measured energy range substantially covers the Gamow window of 1.85--4.53 MeV corresponding to stellar temperatures of 2--3 GK. The present measurements extend the measured energy range of the cross section for the $^{119}\mathrm{Sn}(p\text{,}\ensuremath{\gamma})^{120}\mathrm{Sb}$ reaction and help to clarify the existing experimental discrepancies for $^{116}\mathrm{Sn}(p,\ensuremath{\gamma})^{117}\mathrm{Sb}$ reaction when compared with previous measurements. The extracted cross sections and the resulting astrophysical S factors, corrected for electron screening effects, were compared with predictions from the talys and non-smoker statistical models. The $^{116}\mathrm{Sn}(p,\ensuremath{\gamma})^{117}\mathrm{Sb}$ cross sections agree well with the talys predictions. For $^{119}\mathrm{Sn}(p,\ensuremath{\gamma})^{120}\mathrm{Sb}$, however, standard model combinations proved inadequate, necessitating a tailored parameter set to reproduce the data reasonably well. Utilizing these validated models, stellar reaction rates for both proton-capture reactions were calculated using talys and compared with the rates from the JINA REACLIB database.

title: Bayesian Inference of Stellar r -process Abundances
abstract: Abstract The abundances of heavy elements observed in metal-poor, r -process-enhanced stars provide unique information about the astrophysical conditions in which the rapid neutron-capture process ( r -process) occurs. We present a Bayesian framework to infer these conditions from stellar abundance patterns. Building on a large site-independent r -process survey, we use a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampler to fit observed abundances with weighted superpositions of r -process patterns from nucleosynthesis calculations, each parameterized by an initial electron fraction, entropy, and expansion timescale. Applying this framework to the nearly complete r -process template star HD 222925, we find that two components are required: a heavier H-component producing elements from the second to the third peak and a lighter L-component producing elements from the first to the second peak. Increasing the number of components does not significantly improve the agreement with observations. Extending the analysis to the limited- r stars HD 128279 and HD 122563, and to the solar r -process residuals, we find that their abundances can be reproduced by almost the same two components, albeit with different relative weights. Moreover, the lightest neutron-capture elements ( Z ≲ 35) in the Sun require additional contributions absent in HD 222925. Residual discrepancies are concentrated in elements sensitive to observational systematics (e.g., Ag and Cd) or nuclear-physics inputs (around the third peak). Our study highlights the power of combining stellar abundances with nucleosynthesis calculations to constrain the astrophysical conditions of the r -process, and motivates further improvements in both observational data and nuclear-physics inputs.

title: An improved statistical treatment for radioassay-based background projection incorporating part-to-part variation
abstract: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. This part-to-part variation can have an impact on the total activity and is not presently captured by the averaging methods used to evaluate radioassays. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
abstract: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_\sigma$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{\sigma,{\rm eff}} = 2m_\pi$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

title: Effect of a single- Λ impurity on the magnetic response of finite nuclei
abstract: Background: Ultrastrong magnetic fields, which can be generated transiently in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, can significantly modify the structure of finite nuclei. However, how a single-$\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ impurity embedded in a nuclear core alters the magnetic response of finite nuclei remains unclear.Purpose: To investigate the effect of a single-$\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ impurity on the magnetic response of finite nuclei, focusing on separation energies, single-particle levels, deformation, radii, and density distributions.Method: A nonrelativistic three-dimensional Skyrme-Hartree-Fock approach was employed with self-consistent coupling to an external magnetic field. The $\mathrm{SLy}4+\mathrm{SLL}4$ interaction combination was used for the main calculations, and additional $\mathrm{SLy}5+\mathrm{SLL}4$ and $\mathrm{SLy}4+\mathrm{LY}1$ results were included to assess the interaction dependence.Results: The calculations were performed for $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{17}\mathrm{O}$, $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{29}\mathrm{Si}$, and $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{41}\mathrm{Ca}$, together with their cores, under ultrastrong magnetic fields. We analyze the effects of the $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ impurity on the core radii, deformation, single-particle spectra, and density distributions, as well as the magnetic field dependence of the $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ separation energy, root-mean-square (rms) radius, and density distribution. Under strong magnetic fields, the $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ impurity shrinks the nucleonic density distribution, reduces the core radii, weakens the deformation response, and modifies the level-rearrangement pattern of the nuclear core.Conclusions: The single-$\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ impurity modifies the core magnetic response via the attractive $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}N$ interaction and nucleonic rearrangement, while its direct magnetic coupling mainly affects the $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ single-particle energy.

title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays using effective field theory
abstract: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

title: Calculating extremely high energy bremsstrahlung in matter
abstract: Ultra-relativistic electrons initiate electromagnetic showers in ordinary matter that evolve through bremsstrahlung and pair production. At very high energy, the quantum mechanical duration of bremsstrahlung becomes longer than the mean free time to elastically scatter from the medium, leading to a significant suppression known at the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. For some ranges of bremsstrahlung photon and initial electron energies $(k_\gamma,E)$, the duration becomes so long that it will also overlap with subsequent pair production by the bremsstrahlung photon, disrupting LPM suppression and drastically changing LPM predictions. We have previously calculated this change for extremely high energies ($k_\gamma \gg 2$ TeV or more, depending on the medium), for which the electron mass and medium-induced photon mass could be ignored. In this paper, we extend that analysis to lower (but still ultra-relativistic) energy by accounting for those masses, leading to a rich map of behavior in different regions of $(k_\gamma,E)$.

title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
abstract: Meson screening masses trace the evolution of hadronic correlations toward quasi-free quark--antiquark screening in hot QCD. Combining lattice QCD (LQCD) benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset, $x^\ast_{fg}=T^\ast_{fg}/T_c$: an operational matching scale based on the proximity of the axial-vector screening mass to its free-field reference, where $T_c$ is the pseudocritical temperature. On the finite interval $1\le T/T_c\lesssim x^\ast_{fg}$, independent light/strange and charm-containing lattice benchmarks are organized by a common medium-response function with one flavor-sector parameter. One axial-vector point fixes this parameter; the remaining axial-vector data test the temperature dependence of the response, and vector screening masses validate it without vector input. A reduced-mass interpolation then yields lattice-testable predictions for quasi-free onset scales and vector and axial-vector screening spectra in light--charm and open-bottom sectors.

title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
abstract: Gluon saturation limits the growth of parton densities at small Bjorken-$x$ and is expected to be most pronounced in heavy nuclei. Yet quantitative extractions of the nuclear gluon dipole amplitude have long relied on parametrized initial conditions, introducing uncontrolled model dependence that obscures genuine nuclear effects. We introduce a physics-informed neural-network framework that embeds the collinearly improved Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution equation directly into the training objective, allowing the impact-parameter-averaged dipole amplitude to be determined from data without assuming a functional form for its initial condition. Applying this framework to forward-hadron nuclear-modification-factor and coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction data, we extract the $^{208}$Pb dipole amplitude at $x_0=0.01$ with QCD evolution and momentum-space positivity enforced throughout training. The evolved amplitude reproduces the measured cross sections across the available kinematic range and yields a saturation-scale ratio $Q_{s0,\mathrm{Pb}}^2/Q_{s0,p}^2 = 3.17^{+0.17}_{-0.10}$, consistent with simple geometric scaling. The extracted Pb initial condition is well described by a McLerran-Venugopalan-type form, in contrast to the proton, reflecting the higher color-charge density of a large nucleus. Using the same amplitude, we predict the rapidity dependence of the transverse-momentum ratio in $pp$, $p$Pb, and Pb$p$ collisions, finding agreement with recent LHCb measurements at low multiplicity without any system-dependent parameters. This work provides the first unbiased, data-driven determination of nuclear structure in the saturation regime and establishes a general strategy for embedding nonlinear evolution equations into machine-learning extractions of dynamically constrained observables.

title: Prospects of an electromagnetic follow-up of neutron star-black hole mergers in the LIGO-India era
From mergers to collapse: Scalarization dynamics in neutron star binaries
abstract: We present the first fully nonlinear evolutions of binary neutron star mergers in a moving-punctures approach in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. We study both linear- and quadratic-type couplings between the scalar and the Gauss-Bonnet invariant and uncover new postmerger phenomena. These include an enhancement of the prompt collapse of a long-lived hypermassive neutron star remnant and cases where the remnant develops a scalar configuration due to different scalarization instabilities. This study initiates the exploration of beyond-general-relativistic effects enhanced by the nonlinear dynamics of the neutron star’s fluid.

title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
abstract: Abstract Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). Here we present high-resolution neodymium isotope (ε Nd ) records from a depth transect in the equatorial Atlantic over the iNHG. We find a persistent latitudinal and depth gradient in neodymium isotope values in the deep Atlantic during the Late Pliocene, absent in the Early Pleistocene, indicating an expansion of NADW extent over the iNHG. In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

title: Wobbling Motion in the Many-Nucleon System
abstract: The purpose of this Perspective is not to present a new progress but to shed light on another stream of the study of the nuclear wobbling motion from a viewpoint of the many-body theory under an external field. Special attention is paid to the moments of inertia, which are microscopically calculated as a response of the full $A$-body system to rapid rotations described by the cranked RPA formalism. They depend on the rotation frequency, and it is shown that approach of two moments of inertia leads to the instability of rotating triaxial mean fields.
journal_ref: Matsuzaki M (2026) Wobbling motion in the many-nucleon system. Front. Phys. 14:1965157

title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
abstract: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $\sigma/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $\sigma$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $\sigma$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_\pi$, the overall scale of the model.

title: Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
abstract: We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

title: Particle Identification Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal Electromagnetic Calorimeter
abstract: A proposal for the Circular Electron Positron Collider electromagnetic calorimeter is a highly granular scintillating crystal design that uses silicon photomultipliers to measure physics signals from photons. The potential to develop particle identification methods using deep and traditional machine learning is explored. A contrastive machine learning technique was found to enable the separation of showering and 'punch-through' pions without explicit labels. A supervised particle identification method was then trained using the results, using both a graph neural network and a boosted decision tree to distinguish electron, showering hadron, and minimum-ionizing-particle-like events. The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 for both cases. A Shapley additive explanations analysis showed the boosted decision tree classifier matched expectations for each event type. The particle identification capability is then demonstrated on experimental data taken from the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline.

title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
abstract: We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

title: Charm quark energy loss fluctuations in clumpy color string medium
abstract: We simulate charm quark propagation through an ensemble of color flux tubes formed between receding color charges in proton-proton collisions. Under the assumption of sharp string boundaries and a localized nature of the overlap regions, high flux tube densities lead to the formation of string clusters. We convert the local energy density of the superposed color field into an effective temperature of an ideal gluon gas and study the dependence of charm energy loss on its spatial inhomogeneities. By comparing different energy-density extraction prescriptions, we show that both elastic and inelastic momentum damping mechanisms are sensitive to the medium properties. However, the collisional channel is an order of magnitude smaller in absolute terms (up to $\sim0.15$~GeV) compared to the radiative loss (up to $\sim1.5$~GeV). Overall, the results demonstrate that the spatial overlap of individual strings generates a complex local energy density pattern, which predominantly governs the medium-induced quenching of charm quarks.

title: nEXO radioassay program
Reaction dynamics and production of new neutron-rich isotopes near N = 126 in multinucleon transfer reactions
Outcomes of activation measurements and analyses of ITER materials during JET DTE3 operations
abstract: Abstract The 2023 JET deuterium-tritium (D--T) experimental campaign (DTE3) achieved record fusion energy output (69 MJ), providing a unique 14.1~MeV neutron environment for irradiation studies. A range of ITER material samples were exposed in a Long-Term Irradiation Station (LTIS) within the JET nuclear environment to neutron fluxes up to $2 \times 10^{13}$~n/cm$^{2}$/s, reaching a total neutron fluence of $7 \times 10^{15}$~n/cm$^{2}$, the highest achieved in a tokamak. Post-irradiation analysis using high-resolution gamma spectrometry across five laboratories identified a range of neutron-induced activation products present in these samples, which were quantitatively compared with neutronics simulation predictions. Complementary neutron fluence measurements with metallic dosimetry foils located in the LTIS enabled validation of the simulation approach via MCNP and FISPACT-II codes. The DTE3 campaign results, combined with those obtained from prior D--T campaigns, provide a highly valuable dataset for ITER and other D--T machines, supporting the validation of predictive nuclear modelling tools towards sustained high power D--T operations.

title: Odd-even response of microscopic nuclear level densities to pairing-strength variations
Machine learning for classification, dimension reduction, clustering, and feature importance analysis of QH-mode plasma regimes
abstract: Abstract Edge-localized modes (ELMs) release bursts of energy and particles that threaten plasma-facing components in future tokamak reactors, making ELM-free operating regimes a priority for fusion research. Quiescent H-mode (QH), wide-pedestal QH-mode (WPQH), and broadband QH-mode (BBQH) form a family of ELM-free regimes at DIII-D whose boundaries and controlling parameters remain incompletely understood. This work aims to identify, from data, which measured quantities distinguish the three regimes, using a physics-labeled database of 482 high-confidence segments drawn from 323 DIII-D discharges, whose manual labeling was accelerated by the Data Fusion Labeler (dFL). An XGBoost classifier trained on 1 ms-resolution diagnostic data establishes that the manual labels are learnable: under leave-one-shot-out cross-validation it reproduces them for 87.3% of 1 ms samples (macro-F1 0.82). The same classifier underpins dFL's autolabeler for extending the database across the archive, at an estimated ~50× speedup over fully manual analysis. A supervised feature-importance analysis (classifiers evaluated on held-out discharges, with SHAP attribution), trained only on physics signals not used as labeling criteria, shows that the regimes are also distinguishable from independent physics quantities, and unsupervised dimension-reduction and clustering methods examine the same data without labels. The analysis recovers injected torque as the dominant actuator distinguishing the regimes. Within the rotation and E_r quantities considered, edge E×B shear carries the most information distinguishing the three regimes, while toroidal rotation also contributes strongly; this is a statistical association for this model and dataset, consistent with the critical-shear picture of edge harmonic oscillation onset. Where the supervised and unsupervised rankings appear to disagree, the disagreement reflects the correlation structure among related features rather than a substantive physics dispute. Together, these results identify key physical quantities associated with QH-mode regime boundaries and provide a reusable, interpretable workflow for machine-learning-based analysis of labeled databases in fusion research.

title: Low-energy nuclear recoil calibration of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a photoneutron source
abstract: The LZ experiment is a liquid xenon time-projection chamber (TPC) searching for evidence of particle dark matter interactions. In the simplest assumption of elastic scattering, many dark matter models predict an energy spectrum which rises quasi-exponentially with decreasing energy transfer to a target atom. LZ has recently reported evidence for coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) of $^{8}$B solar neutrinos, a signal nearly identical to that expected from a dark matter particle with a mass of about 5.5 GeV/$c^{2}$, which similarly produces nuclear recoil energies $<5$ keV$_{\text{nr}}$. This analysis details the first in situ photoneutron calibration of the LZ detector, using a custom yttrium-beryllium source that produces quasi-monoenergetic neutrons. Elastic nuclear recoils from both the dominant 152 keV and the rare 950 keV photoneutron modes are observed at rates consistent with expectation. We report the ionization yield, and the corresponding scintillation yield inferred from it, at a mean detected recoil energy of 3.1 keV$_{\text{nr}}$ and a drift field of 193 V/cm. The measurement demonstrates the ability of LZ to detect nuclear recoils near threshold and provides an independent check on the detector-response framework underlying few-GeV dark-matter and $^{8}$B CE$\nu$NS searches.

title: Flavour decomposition of the chiral-odd form factors of the nucleon
abstract: We compute the chiral-odd form factors $H_T$, $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ of the nucleon within light-cone QCD sum rules, separately for the $u$ and $d$ quarks, over $1\le Q^2\le 10$ GeV$^2$, and organise their values at $Q^2=0$ into the tensor monopole, dipole and quadrupole moments $g_T$, $\kappa_T$ and $Q_T$. The flavour components of the quadrupole moment and the isoscalar channel have not previously been obtained in this framework. The form factors are read from a basis of Lorentz structures that becomes independent only after a canonical ordering of the Dirac strings, and three of the eight surviving structures give the three form factors separately. Two statements follow from the analytic expressions. The $d$-quark contributions to $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ are equal and opposite in the chiral limit, the breaking being proportional to the quark mass and to the twist-six amplitude $\mathcal{V}_6$. At the level of the least suppressed momentum-fraction integral, the isoscalar tensor charge receives no leading-twist contribution, the twist-three terms of the two flavours cancelling. Neither statement is visible without resolving the flavours. At $\mu^2=1$ GeV$^2$ we obtain, for the two distribution-amplitude sets, $g_T^{u-d}=1.27(7)$ and $1.08(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u-d}=1.35(62)$ and $1.58(59)$, $Q_T^{u-d}=-4.40(83)$ and $-4.20(73)$, $g_T^{u+d}=0.39(7)$ and $0.38(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u+d}=4.47(62)$ and $4.32(59)$, and $Q_T^{u+d}=2.41(53)$ and $1.56(30)$. The mean-field relation $2\tilde{H}_T^{u-d}=-E_T^{u-d}$ holds in sign and in order of magnitude, the ratio being $0.64(16)$ and $0.67(15)$. In the impact-parameter plane the two flavour distributions are displaced in opposite transverse directions by nearly equal amounts, $\langle b_y\rangle=0.37$ and $-0.37$ fm, and both are elongated across the polarisation axis, the $d$ quark some five to six times more strongly than the $u$ quark.

title: Exploring the influence of microscopic nuclear densities and collective excitations on O 16 -induced fusion cross sections
Augmenting the extrapolation capability of disruption prediction to extended parameter regimes by predict-first neural network
abstract: Abstract The prediction, mitigation, and avoidance of disruptions are critical prerequisites for ensuring the safe operation of future fusion reactors. While machine learning-based disruption prediction techniques have achieved high accuracy in recent years, their application to a new device demands strong extrapolation capability across parameter regimes. This capability is essential to maintain robust algorithm performance as the operational space of the device expands, while it is also a main shortcoming for most machine learning techniques. This study evaluates the extrapolation capability of a disruption prediction algorithm using multiple subsets of experimental data from HL-3 tokamak, divided by key plasma parameters, yielding three key findings. Firstly, the area under the receiver-operator characteristic curve (AUC) of a standard deep learning algorithm trained on the subset with low parameters degrades to around 0.750, 0.666, and 0.540 when extrapolated to three progressively distant extrapolation regimes. However, the Predict-First Neural Network (PFNN) maintains an AUC of about 0.873, 0.823 and 0.701. Secondly, the algorithm's accuracy shows a clear contrast in degradation behavior: when extrapolating along electromagnetic parameters like plasma current, performance declines slowly and continuously; when extrapolating along energy-related parameters like stored energy, performance remains initially stable but deteriorates abruptly beyond a certain threshold. Finally, after rigorously accounting for the impact of parameter regime extrapolation and adjusting the algorithm deployment strategy, deep learning proved effective in protecting the device during HL-3's high-current and high-beta commissioning phases. This study provides valuable experience for implementing disruption prediction algorithms on new devices and is expected to offer practical reference for the initial operation of future fusion facilities like ITER.

title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
abstract: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.
authors: J. P. A. M. de Andr\'e

title: A Differentiable Surrogate for Loss-Dominated Ion Beam Transport
abstract: Radioactive nuclei with extreme proton-to-neutron ratios provide unique probes of nuclear structure, fundamental symmetries, astrophysical processes, and applications such as medicine. However, their short half-lives and low production rates mean that experiments must work with few desired ions, often amid contaminant backgrounds exceeding the signal by six orders of magnitude. Efficiently isolating, transporting, and delivering these ions through multi-stage apparatus is therefore a central challenge. We introduce a differentiable probabilistic surrogate for ion-beam transport in regimes dominated by particle loss. The model jointly captures the survival probability of ions along the beamline and the evolving phase-space distribution of the surviving particles by combining discrete-time survival analysis with conditional normalizing flows. Applied to a high-dimensional electrostatic beamline, the resulting likelihood enables gradient-based optimization of operating voltages and inference of beam properties from sparse detector observations. Once trained, the surrogate provides millisecond-scale differentiable predictions, transforming particle-tracking simulations with hard losses into an inference-ready model for experimental design, beamline optimization, and future digital twins of experiments with rare nuclei.

title: Ultralow-Energy Measurements using the Startpoint of $\beta$ Decays
abstract: We propose a novel measurement of $\beta$ decays using low-temperature solid-state detector technologies. The $\beta$ startpoint, where the $\beta$ kinetic energy is zero, offers a unique probe of weak nuclear physics that has not yet been exploited experimentally. We describe how this technique enables searches for heavy sterile neutrinos in the keV--MeV energy range and show that, with current technologies, sensitivities to sterile neutrino coupling to electrons can be achieved that exceed the current best constraints. The spectrum produced by the recoiling daughter ion also offers a calibration of the nuclear recoil response, critical for both sub-GeV dark matter searches and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) measurements. We outline a potential experimental scheme using neutron activation to produce $^{32}$P in situ in a silicon substrate, discuss projected sensitivities to sterile neutrinos, and evaluate the prospects for nuclear recoil calibrations.

title: Xenon energy-deposition widths in silicon: measurements and Geant4 comparisons
abstract: Energy-deposition fluctuations determine the isotope-separation capability of multilayer silicon detectors. We measure the central peak widths of $^{124}$Xe signals in 300- and 675-micrometre silicon layers at incident energies of approximately 152-274 MeV per nucleon and compare them with Geant4 11.4.0 electromagnetic option 4 (emopt4) and a calculation with explicit charge exchange. In the 300-micrometre detector, the emopt4 relative width of 1.844% exceeds the unselected experimental width of 1.407% by 31% and the selected width of 1.060% by 74%. For the 675-micrometre detector, selection windows around the downstream-signal peak, each approximately ten fitted first-plane standard deviations wide, give experimental upper estimates of 0.66-0.74%, compared with emopt4 predictions of 1.01-1.24%. Explicit charge-state transport gives widths of 0.889-0.932% for the thinner layer, depending on the incident charge distribution, and 0.59-0.63% for the thicker layer. These predictions are consistent with the experimental upper estimates, while emopt4 overestimates the widths for both thicknesses throughout the studied energy interval.
