title: Transport due to density gradient driven TEM & UM in advanced tokamak plasma configurations: Role of negative triangularity and magnetic shear reversal
abstract: Abstract Advanced tokamak configurations can modify microturbulence through changes in magnetic equilibrium, trapped-particle dynamics, resonance conditions. In this work, global gyrokinetic simulations are used to study density-gradient-driven trapped-electron turbulence in tight-aspect-ratio shaped plasmas, focusing on the role of negative triangularity and reversed magnetic shear. In the positive versus negative triangularity comparison, negative triangularity is found to stabilize high-n modes and reduce saturated particle diffusivity by approximately 40%. Energy-exchange diagnostics show that this reduction is associated with a weaker participation of weakly trapped electrons, while zonal-flow shearing remains comparable between the two configurations. In the reversed-shear case for positive triangularity, despite larger linear growth rates, the saturated electron diffusivity is reduced by approximately 36% as compared to positive magnetic shear case. This reduction is linked to the diminished radial support of the perturbation in the negative magnetic-shear region. The combined effect of reversed magnetic shear and negative triangularity is further investigated, revealing that although both independently reduce saturated transport levels, their combination leads to enhanced nonlinear transport.

title: Scintillator-Based Event-Mode Neutron Imaging with Timepix4 Readout
abstract: Scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging is emerging as a powerful approach to neutron radiography. Unlike conventional integrating-mode neutron imaging, which accumulates scintillation light during an exposure, event reconstruction estimates neutron-event positions and arrival times from time-stamped optical responses. We investigated this approach using a self-developed Timepix4-based optical readout system, image-formation analysis, and beam experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source under different scintillator and optical configurations. The analysis explains how event localization can reduce image blur associated with the spatial extent of individual scintillation responses. Under the same 0.35$\times$ optical configuration, event reconstruction improved the spatial resolution from 164.2 to 91.9 $\mu$m at 10% modulation transfer function (MTF), while a 2.1$\times$ configuration with a $\mathrm{Gd_2O_2S:Tb}$ scintillator achieved 26.1 $\mu$m at the same MTF threshold. Following event reconstruction and rejection of single-photon reconstructed events, the mean peak-normalized spectral response in the 6-8 angstrom out-of-band interval decreased by 85.4% relative to the raw-pixel wavelength-count spectrum, indicating reduced afterglow-related spectral background. Under the tested pulsed-beam conditions, the maximum instantaneous pixel-hit rate per pixel was approximately four times its time-averaged value, providing an experimental basis for assessing readout requirements at higher neutron flux. Conventional radiography resolved structural details, while energy-selective imaging enhanced the contrast between materials with similar broadband transmission and Bragg-edge imaging revealed crystallographic features in steel. These results demonstrate the imaging-quality benefits and capabilities of scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging.

title: Optimized finite-β tokamak-stellarator hybrid configurations achieved by planar dipole-field coils
abstract: Abstract Tokamak--stellarator hybrids seek to combine tokamak-like compactness and confinement with stellarator-like externally generated rotational transform and steady-state operation. In this work, we build on the recent tokamak--stellarator hybrid study using planar dipole-field coils (PDCs) [Yu et al., arXiv:2605.03599], in which the fixed-position, programmable coils on an axisymmetric winding surface generate flexible three-dimensional shaping fields. Using single-stage free-boundary optimization of coil currents and plasma-equilibrium parameters, we construct vacuum and finite-β configurations. The vacuum cases show controllable external transform and magnetic well.The finite-β cases accommodate various density, temperature, and pressure profiles, producing quasi-axisymmetric (QA) equilibria with self-consistent bootstrap current, favorable Mercier stability, and reduced demand for external current drive. Re-optimization enables β ramp-up and access to different field-period QA branches with moderate coil-current changes. At large rotational transform, a toroidally omnigenous (TO)-like configuration exhibits more favorable infinite-n ideal-ballooning behavior than a QA reference with matched profiles, even though ballooning stability is not directly optimized for. These results demonstrate that PDCs provide a flexible platform for achieving optimized finite-β hybrid configurations.

title: Nitrogen-seeded X-point radiator regime with good core-edge compatibility and reduced divertor in-out asymmetry in WEST L-mode plasmas
abstract: Abstract The X-point radiator (XPR) regime is considered a promising approach for mitigating divertor heat flux during long-pulse operation. In this work, nitrogen-seeded XPR discharges are investigated in WEST L-mode plasmas with a full-tungsten environment and an ITER-grade divertor. The XPR transition is characterized by an increase followed by a rapid decrease in the line-integrated density near the X-point, together with an abrupt collapse of the electron temperature at the outer strike point. During the XPR phase, both divertor targets remain detached with electron temperatures of about 3 eV and strongly reduced heat fluxes. Analysis of multiple XPR discharges shows that the plasma stored energy increases after nitrogen seeding and remains elevated throughout the XPR phase, accompanied by higher core temperature and/or density, indicating good core-edge compatibility. During the XPR phase, the total radiated power increases, with a larger fraction of the radiation originating from the X-point region, while tungsten sputtering at the divertor targets and the tungsten content in the core plasma are reduced. The pronounced in-out asymmetry of divertor plasma parameters observed in conventional discharges is also reduced. SOLEDGE3X simulations reproduce the experimental observations and suggest that the reduced in-out asymmetry is associated with reduced ionization and more similar poloidal deuterium ion transport on the inner and outer divertor legs.

title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
abstract: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, where the maps of both codes agree in every coefficient through ninth order, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores is 1.5 to 1.6 times faster than COSY at orders 3 to 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

title: Impacts of energetic ion on the unstable spectra of kinetic ballooning modes and zonal flow generation
abstract: Abstract Global gyrokinetic particle simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between energetic ions (EIs) and kinetic ballooning modes (KBMs) across different toroidal mode number ($n$) regimes, encompassing linear dispersion relations, nonlinear wave-particle interactions, and wave-wave interactions. The results demonstrate that EIs exert non-perturbative destabilizing effects on low-$n$ KBMs, while stabilizing high-$n$ KBMs through thermal ion dilution. These opposing EI effects arise from the different strengths of finite Larmor radius (FLR) and finite orbit width (FOW) effects in low- and high-$n$ regimes. Single-$n$ and multi-$n$ nonlinear simulations reveal strong wave-particle interactions between EIs and low-$n$ KBMs, resulting in higher KBM saturation levels and enhanced EI transport. Additionally, although low-density EIs have little direct influence on zonal flow (ZF), they can indirectly increase the spatial scale of ZF in multi-$n$ simulations. Since ZF is generated via the beat‑driven process and its structure is determined by the pump wave, the EI effects lead to the dominance of low‑$n$ KBM components, thereby increasing the spatial scale of the ZF.

title: Impact of helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts on magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection in a liquid metal blanket.
abstract: Abstract On the pathway toward full simulations for a liquid metal blanket, this study extends the work of Chen et al (2022 Nucl. Fusion 62 026042) on mixed convection in a full-scale dual coolant lead lithium blanket by considering a more realistic case. In this study, the model incorporates the complex geometry of characteristic sub-components, including helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts (FCIs), to investigate their impacts in several key metrics ：(1) Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) pressure drop, (2) electromagnetic coupling, (3) velocity distribution in both the bulk and gap regions, (4) flow behavior in blanket components, and (5) heat transfer. Based on the MHD-UCAS platform, these multi-region, multiphysics direct numerical simulations are performed on a highly refined mesh of 5.46 × 10 8 cells under conditions relevant to the fusion reactor: the applied magnetic field of 5 T ( Ha ∼10 4 ), the PbLi velocity of 0.1 ms -1 in poloidal ducts ( Re ∼10 5 ), and maximum volumetric heating of 30 MW m -3 ( Gr ∼10 12 ). The computational results incorporate the influence of the helium cooling channels and the FCIs on electromagnetic coupling, thereby altering the MHD pressure and flow distribution. Simultaneously, the FCIs divide the flow into bulk and gap regions, where high-speed reverse flows are identified exclusively within the gap regions of the rear poloidal ducts. The anisotropic conductivity introduced by helium channels alters the velocity and temperature distributions, further complicating the MHD flow. In addition, localized hot spots exceeding the design temperature limit are found near the top of the U-turn and in the outlet reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel walls, suggesting that enhanced cooling is required in these locations.

title: Hybrid simulations of nonlinear zonal flow generation by multi-n toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes driven by energetic particles
abstract: Abstract In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement. In this work, strong self-generated ZFs are analyzed in a multi-n TAE system through nonlinear hybrid simulations using the CLT-K code, where the ZFs are driven by self-beat interactions of TAEs. The results show that the strong ZFs dominate the nonlinear stage and significantly suppress the TAE activity. The ZF mode structures consist of the m=0 and m=1 harmonics, and are directly correlated with the spatial structures of TAEs. Further analysis of the ZF kinetic energy evolution demonstrates that a finite residual between the Reynolds and Maxwell stresses, arising from toroidal geometry, enables net energy transfer from TAEs to ZFs, with an additional contribution from the EP pressure response. In addition, the linear Lorentz force contributes either to ZF pumping or damping depending on the stage of the evolution. Strong ZF generation is favored in regimes with high EP pressure and low viscosity. A self-regulating process is identified: stronger TAEs drive stronger ZFs, which in turn regulates the TAE activity. These findings provide both numerical and physical insights into the role of ZFs in regulating EP-driven instabilities in tokamak plasmas.

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: Coarse-grained vs. Nano-grained microstructures
abstract: Abstract Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ~600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.

title: Colours and Flavours: ropes and colour reconnection as string multiplets
abstract: The increase of strange-hadron yields with event activity and the enhanced charm-baryon fractions in hadronic collisions motivate a microscopic examination of how the colour environment affects hadronization. We review and develop the string description of these effects, starting from the Lund fragmentation baseline in electron--positron annihilation and following colour correlations beyond the leading-colour approximation. Few-parton examples show how junction formation and rope hadronization arise from the same SU(3) colour structure, connecting baryon formation and the screening forces that govern strange-quark production. For nuclear collisions, we introduce a local escape criterion and a phenomenological saturation of the breakup force, motivated by a three-string example of screening through background colour correlations. With common settings, the combined prescription gives a satisfactory description of light-flavour ratios in pp and p--Pb and provides O--O predictions. Charm ratios reveal a substantial remaining deficit in $\Xi_c$ production, motivating separate tests of the fragmentation baseline and its extrapolation with activity.

title: Systematic study of baryon-baryon interactions in singly bottomed systems
abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the baryon-baryon interactions in singly bottomed dibaryon systems within the chiral quark model and search for possible bound states. By exploring the baryon-baryon interaction, we find that low-isospin channels tend to generate deeper attractive interactions and are prone to form bound states. We also find that decuplet-decuplet systems tend to show stronger attraction and support a larger number of bound states, whereas octet-octet systems generally exhibit weaker attraction and fewer bound solutions. The binding behavior of octet-decuplet systems generally lies between these two cases. Several bound states are obtained, which are Δ Σ b * with I J = 1 2 0 , 1 2 1 , 1 2 2 , 1 2 3 , and 3 2 3 ; the Δ Σ b with I J = 1 2 1 , 1 2 2 , 3 2 1 , and 3 2 2 ; the N Σ b * with I J = 1 2 2 ; the Σ Σ b with I J = 00 , 01, and 11; the Σ Σ b * with I J = 01 and 02; the Σ * Σ b with I J = 01 and 02; and the Σ * Σ b * with I J = 00 , 01, 02, 03, and 13. Further investigations of the corresponding scattering processes are still required to determine whether these bound-state candidates can be identified. These states deserve further experimental investigation.

title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

title: Oscillations of dissipative neutron stars: The impact of hyperonic reaction rates
abstract: Tidal excitations of stellar oscillation modes during binary neutron-star inspirals offer a powerful probe of the composition of dense matter at supranuclear densities. Chemical equilibration plays a crucial, but often neglected, role in stellar perturbation calculations. If the chemical equilibration timescale is comparable to the oscillation timescale, then viscous effects can damp the modes. If the reactions are fast, some modes can completely disappear since their restoring force vanishes. Typically, these calculations, however, assume either instantaneous chemical equilibrium or no equilibration (frozen composition). Motivated by this, we investigate the effects of finite reaction rates on the oscillation spectrum of neutron stars containing hyperonic matter. We calculate the dominant non-leptonic weak interaction rates and incorporate them into the relativistic perturbation equations through a complex, frequency-dependent dynamical sound speed. We show that finite-rate effects naturally manifest as bulk-viscous dissipation, modifying the properties of both the fundamental ($f$) and gravity ($g$) modes. We further examine the impact on the tidal response by matching stellar perturbations to near-zone boundary conditions, demonstrating how viscous dissipation gives rise to a tidal lag. These results provide a consistent framework connecting microscopic reaction rates and the resulting bulk viscosity to the tidal dynamics of compact binaries, and represent a step towards incorporating viscous dissipation into gravitational-wave models of binary neutron-star inspirals.

versions.abstract: Tidal excitations of stellar oscillation modes during binary neutron-star inspirals offer a powerful probe of the composition of dense matter at supranuclear densities. Chemical equilibration plays a crucial, but often neglected, role in stellar perturbation calculations. If the chemical equilibration timescale is comparable to the oscillation timescale, then viscous effects can damp the modes. If the reactions are fast, some modes can completely disappear since their restoring force vanishes. title: Optimization Framework for Full-Skyrmionic Polarimetry
abstract: Optical skyrmionic beams hold considerable potential for applications in quantum information and weak-intensity detection. These applications require accurate measurements of full topological observables using imaging Stokes polarimetry, with measurement states optimized in advance to limit the effect of stochastic error sources. However, the optimization framework for general Stokes polarimetries is based on a linear reconstruction chain for Stokes vectors and cannot quantitatively evaluate the nonlinear reconstruction of topological observables. Here, we define full-skyrmionic polarimetry (FSP) and construct its optimization framework from the reconstruction chain for full topological observables. Based on existing polarization evaluating functions (PEF), we introduce topological evaluating functions (TEF) and develop a multi-stage FSP optimization methodology. Numerical results confirm that topological optimization can further improve the reconstruction of topological observables, even when the measurement states are already optimal for polarization. Increasing the redundant projection number also effectively suppresses the effects of all stochastic error sources, providing a low-cost methodology to improve the reconstruction of both polarization and topological observables. The FSP optimization framework can identify topologically optimal configurations for arbitrary FSP structures, providing a guideline for high-precision full-skyrmionic measurements at weak-intensity levels and potential skyrmion ellipsometry.

title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.

title: Cosmic ray muon seasonal variations with the ProtoDUNE-SP Detector
abstract: We present the measurement of the cosmic ray muon seasonal variation using single-muon events with the ProtoDUNE single-phase detector located at the CERN Neutrino Platform, using data collected from December 2018 to July 2020. Cosmic ray muon runs recorded during this period are analyzed to determine the muon rate as a function of time. The results show a seasonal modulation of the muon rate, with a significance of 4 {\sigma} relative to the null hypothesis of no seasonal variation. The observed muon rate reaches a maximum during the winter, consistent with measurements from other surface experiments with a low muon-energy threshold. This measurement is possible due to the overall excellent performance of this detector technology and serves as a clear demonstration that such a detector can stably measure small, time-dependent physical signals such as seasonal variations in cosmic muon rates over long timescales.

title: Commissioning of GEM Detectors for the Super Bigbite Spectrometer
abstract: We report on the commissioning and cosmic characterization of the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) trackers for the recently completed first round of the Super Bigbite Spectrometer (SBS) experimental program conducted in Hall A of the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility. The SBS GEM trackers rank as one of the largest deployments of triple GEM detectors in operation and were critical to the success of the SBS program. Categorized by their readout strip orientation, the 56 individual SBS GEM modules range in active areas from 60cmx50cm (XY) to 150cmx40cm (UV, XW) and were fabricated at the University of Virginia. Large area layers were assembled from four XY GEM modules or a single UV or XW GEM module. The front-end electronics were based on APV25 chips with output sent to custom developed 40 MHz Multi-purpose Digitizers (MPDs). Prior to the installation of the GEM-based tracking systems for SBS experiments, the GEM modules underwent extensive cosmic-ray testing to characterize the performance of each module, including detector stability, efficiency, uniformity, timing performance, and spatial resolution.

title: Characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber prototype with Ar:CF$_4$ at atmospheric pressure
abstract: We report on the characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber (OTPC) developed as a prototype for neutron-induced reaction studies at Soreq Applied Research Accelerator Facility (SARAF). The prototype was operated with Ar:CF$_4$ (95:5) at 1 bar, using parallel mesh electrodes for charge multiplication and electroluminescence, and alpha particles from a $^{241}$Am source. Both induced charge and light signals were recorded. A systematic characterization was carried out to study charge multiplication and scintillation yield. We present the results of these measurements in single-gap amplification configurations, along with two-gap operation and a demonstration of synchronized optical readout.

title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I-type-II boundary: The low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field B sh of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on niobium (Nb). Ginzburg–Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large- κ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low- κ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with κ GL = 0.7 , we obtain B sh ≃ 290 mT at T / T c = 0.2 , using B c 0 ≃ 200 mT . For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner stability limit of about 67 MV / m .

versions.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
versions.abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$\kappa$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$\kappa$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

title: Probing the origin of the LHAASO Peanut with a hidden central accelerator
abstract: A highly asymmetric, giant peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultrahigh-energy gamma rays at a high Galactic latitude, b≈-17.5^̧irc, suggesting anisotropic particle transport around a Galactic accelerator. We investigate whether its spectrum and morphology can arise from a hidden central accelerator embedded in a projected anisotropic halo. The baseline model accounts for the diffuse strip and central excess, while a phenomenological prescription for a localized magnetic field reorientation toward the line of sight (LOS), together with a particle-conserved remapping of the electrons downstream of the far excess into an emitting column of prescribed transverse extent, enhances the emission at the far excess position. We explore various source ages, along with different combinations of ambient magnetic field strength and parallel diffusion coefficient, while accounting for radiative cooling when estimating the viewing geometry. The exploration reveals that relatively rapid parallel transport enhances the far component, while preserving a dominant diffuse strip. Representative configurations remain compatible with the observed spectral energy distribution, although the fit far component remains weaker than the central component above 100 TeV, even in cases where their component fluxes are comparable at 25-100 TeV. These results illustrate the plausibility of a hidden central accelerator as the origin of the LHAASO Peanut, while identifying the remaining difficulty in reproducing the relative brightness of its compact components within the adopted phenomenological framework.

title: Interaction of degenerate higher-order modes in periodic superconducting rf accelerating structures
abstract: Some higher-order mode (HOM) passbands in multicell superconducting rf accelerating structures may become “flat,” meaning that they have an extremely narrow bandwidth due to weak coupling between cells. In the presence of random perturbations caused by mechanical imperfections of the cell shapes, such passbands can split into individual cell resonances that are weakly coupled or completely uncoupled from the beam pipes. As a result, these modes can exhibit high-quality factors and large R / Q values, potentially leading to beam instabilities, emittance growth, and excessive cryogenic losses. This effect was observed in a high-beta five-cell 650 MHz (HB650) prototype cavity developed for the PIP-II project. An analytical theory explaining the origin of this phenomenon, along with methods to mitigate it, is presented in this paper. The HB650 cavity was successfully redesigned to eliminate the flat HOM passband and prevent the associated detrimental effects.

title: Electron beam size monitoring at the SLS 2.0 using Fresnel zone plates
abstract: The Swiss Light Source (SLS) storage ring has been rebuilt as SLS 2.0, providing an electron beam with significantly reduced horizontal emittance. This upgrade enables an x-ray beam with brightness increased by nearly 2 orders of magnitude and extends the accessible photon-energy range by approximately 50%. Precise characterization of the electron source is crucial for optimizing and fully exploiting the performance of new fourth-generation light sources. However, conventional methods for determining the electron beam source size, such as pinhole-based imaging, lack the resolution needed to characterize sub − 10 μ m beam sizes, thus motivating the development of advanced diagnostic approaches. Here, we employ a Fresnel zone plate-based system to measure the electron source size at the SLS 2.0 storage ring. We demonstrate the measurement of sub − 10 μ m electron beam sizes and discuss challenges and potential future improvements of the proposed monitor.

title: Adaptive proposals for nonparametric equation-of-state inference with RIFT: iterative Gaussian-process refinement in a compressed sequence representation
abstract: Nonparametric equation-of-state (EOS) models have two practical problems for Bayesian inference: too many parameters, introducing observationally inaccessible degrees of freedom; and no painless route to adaptive refinement, necessary to forecast future observing scenarios. In this work we address both problems, providing a framework for adaptive nonparametric EOS sampling which simultaneously provides insight into the observationally-accessible effective dimensions. Applied to a published Gaussian-process ensemble, this analysis reveals substantial sound-speed freedom beyond what observations demand. Conversely, by concrete example, we demonstrate that often-used schemes to use many EOS realizations will invariably break down when challenged by new physics, as the observationally-accessible dimension increases substantially. These functional adaptive sampling tools provide a path forward to efficient computation, interpretation, and discovery for future analyses of cold, beta-equilibrium nuclear matter.

title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
abstract: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics. Extraction is a bounded least-squares search: a bank of NGSpice simulations supplies initial candidates, finite differences of the surrogate supply the local Jacobian, and NGSpice re-simulates the resulting cards before selection. On 18 measured geometries, we compare a search over seven card parameters with a search over 43 parameters selected by NGSpice sensitivity. Relative to NGSpice re-simulations of the previously released cards, the two searches reduce the in-sample mean relative root-mean-square error (RRMS) by 17% and 26%, respectively. The 43-parameter search has the lower overall error, but the seven-parameter search has the lower mean on high-bias curves, and some individual curves have higher error than with the released cards under both searches.

title: Radiation Effects on Breakdown Voltage and Quenching Resistance in SiPMs
abstract: This study investigates the suitability of the Hamamatsu S13360 series as replacement photodetectors for the RICH upgrade II detector. I-V curves enabled a statistical analysis of breakdown voltage and quenching resistance before and after irradiation, quantifying the dependance of damage on neutron fluence and the mitigation effect of cooling. The results show that breakdown voltage degradation increases with fluence and becomes statistically significant only at high irradiation levels. Quenching resistance, by contrast, shows only a limited increase except at 6 x 10^13 neq/cm2, where substantial degradation appears. Both parameters exhibit a clear reduction in radiation-damage impact when operated at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Optimisation of gas mixture for charge and light readout with Micromegas detectors
abstract: Optical readout of Micromegas detectors is a promising technique for neutron and charged-particle imaging, offering high spatial resolution while reducing the complexity of electronic readout. Within the framework of the development of optical-readout Micromegas detectors, different noble-gas-based mixtures have been investigated to optimize charge amplification and scintillation yield. Argon-, neon-, and helium-based mixtures with various quenchers were characterized using X-ray irradiation. The detector gain, energy resolution, and optical light intensity were measured simultaneously over a wide range of amplification fields. Unprecedented energy resolutions were achieved over a large detection area (several cm$^2$) with He/\CF and Ne/\CF (90/10) mixtures, reaching 10.5\% and 13.3\% (FWHM), respectively, with the He-based mixture delivering particularly remarkable performance. Simultaneous charge and optical measurements further reveal that high charge gain does not necessarily translate into a strong optical response: while He- and Ne-based mixtures achieve effective charge gains of the order of 10$^5$, Ar/\CF mixtures produce the strongest detected light signals. Among the investigated mixtures, the ternary Ar/\CF/Isobutane (95/3/2) mixture stands out as particularly promising, combining high effective charge gain, a comparatively strong optical response, and more stable detector operation.

title: Magnetized bottom-up thermalization in heavy-ion collisions
Femtosecond Free-Space Time-Frequency Transfer at km/s Relative Motion with Doppler Compensation
abstract: A global optical clock network holds great promise for a wide range of applications, including international metrology--particularly the redefinition of the ``second''--as well as navigation, geoscience, and fundamental physics. Satellite-based high-precision time-frequency dissemination is essential for realizing such a network. Despite remarkable progress in ground-based free-space simulations over high-loss channels, the Doppler effect arising from satellite motion has remained an unsolved barrier. Here we demonstrate femtosecond two-way time-frequency transfer over a 113-km free-space link under simulated Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s. To overcome the Doppler barrier, we first reproduce satellite-like Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s on the ground by locking a frequency comb to a broadly tunable laser. We then correct the resulting disturbances with two complementary techniques: a dual-channel sampling architecture that compensates for optical dispersion and radio frequency (RF) nonlinearity while eliminating Nyquist dead zones, and an iterative interferogram reconstruction algorithm that removes Doppler-induced distortion. After correction, residual systematic errors are within $\pm10$ fs over the full 1.55 km/s range. Using simulated medium earth orbit (MEO) and geosynchronous orbit (GSO) satellite trajectories, we achieve fractional frequency instability of $3.9\times10^{-19}$ at 4,600 s and $3.6\times10^{-19}$ at 23,600 s, respectively. This extends the operational velocity range by nearly two orders of magnitude beyond previous free-space demonstrations, removing the last major technical barrier to a global femtosecond-precision satellite-based time-frequency link.

title: Detection of minimum ionising particles with internal gain in the first Silicon Electron Multiplier demonstrators
abstract: The Silicon Electron Multiplier (SiEM) is a novel sensor concept for minimum ionising particle (MIP) detection that uses internal gain achieved through a composite electrode structure embedded within the silicon bulk. Unlike conventional gain sensors (LGADs, APDs), the SiEM achieves amplification through applied electric potentials rather than doped gain layers, potentially offering superior radiation hardness above $10^{16}\,n_{\mathrm{eq}}/\mathrm{cm}^2$. Following initial conceptual studies and simulation work, several fabrication approaches were explored, including Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) at Centro Nacional de Microelectr\'onica (CNM) and Metal Assisted Chemical Etching (MACEtch) at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). This paper reports the first experimental results from functional SiEM demonstrators produced by Hamamatsu Photonics K. K. (HPK) using a single-electrode configuration with modified geometry. Electrical characterisation through I-V measurements and test beam studies with minimum ionising particles demonstrate clear evidence of charge multiplication, with gains comparable to simulation predictions.

title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
abstract: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. Like other similar detectors, it relies on a moderator (polyethylene) and $^{3}$He tubes. A novel feature of our design is the use of the weighting technique to achieve an efficiency that is virtually independent of the energy spectrum of the neutrons being measured; a property known as \textit{flat efficiency}. This approach offers two primary advantages: it yields a flatter efficiency response than conventional analysis methods, and it provides greater flexibility regarding the geometry of the long counter. The latter has enabled us to design the detector with almost every $^{3}$He tube positioned at a different distance from the neutron source, which allows us to perform not only neutron counting but also neutron spectroscopy.

title: Ab initio calculations of ${\bar\delta_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $\beta$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

title: Transient beam loading effects on energy loss during beam abort in high-current storage ring
Thorium and europium production in the early Galaxy. Implications for nucleocosmochronology
abstract: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology. Among the available chronometers, the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio provides a promising age indicator. We investigated the reliability of the log( Th / Eu ) ratio as a chronometer for old stellar populations by testing whether thorium and europium are produced in a consistent ratio in metal-poor stars. We also assessed the precision with which this abundance ratio can be measured and the resulting uncertainties in stellar ages, adopting the best available theoretical estimate of the initial production ratio to establish the absolute age scale. We present new thorium and europium abundance measurements for a sample of eight / reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. We combined these measurements with homogeneous samples from the literature and analysed the evolution of log( Th Eu ) as a function of metallicity. Adopting a theoretical r-process production ratio, we derived stellar ages and investigated the impact of observational uncertainties and sample statistics on the resulting age constraints. At low metallicities, the observed log( Th / Eu ) ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity once stars with anomalous actinide abundances are excluded, supporting the assumption that thorium and europium were typically co-produced in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are broadly consistent with those expected for metal-poor halo stars, although uncertainties in individual ages remain large. We show that higher spectral resolution is required to improve the precision of Th measurements, while combining measurements from several stars in coeval populations could provide an additional statistical improvement. Nucleocosmochronology is a valuable independent method for dating the oldest stellar populations. Although individual stellar ages are currently limited by observational and theoretical uncertainties, the analysis of homogeneous samples of coeval stars, such as members of globular clusters, could provide significantly stronger constraints. Future high-resolution multi-object spectroscopic facilities will facilitate this approach and provide independent constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

title: Thermal and electromechanical response of ultrathin carbon-strip polarimeter targets in relativistic bunched beams
Search for and identification of ejected stellar candidates from the Corona Australis chain star formation complex
abstract: Star formation predominantly occurs in the Galactic plane within molecular clouds. Recent astrometric data from Data Release 3 (DR3) have revealed a chain-like arrangement of young stellar clusters in the Corona Australis (CrA) star formation complex that exhibit accelerated motion away from the Galactic plane. The CrA chain star formation complex represents sequential generations of relatively rapidly moving clusters formed from gas previously accelerated by expulsion, massive stellar winds, and one or more supernovae (SNe). Gaia We searched for runaway and neutron stars ejected from the CrA chain to assess their origin from dynamical ejection or SNe. A traceback motion analysis and trajectory study was conducted on 459 known runaway stars and candidates as well as 476 pulsars, taking the gravitational potential of the Galaxy into account. The analysis identified five runaway stars and two neutron stars that most probably originated in two stellar groups from the CrA star formation complex, ejected in either dynamical processes or SNe. Reconstructing the origins of these ejected stars not only provides insight into the dynamical evolution of the CrA region, but also contributes to constraining the present-day mass function and estimating the lower limit of the high-mass end of the initial mass function, refining and enhancing our understanding of the distribution of stellar masses at birth.

title: Prospects for Detecting Post-merger Signals from Binary Neutron Stars with Future Gravitational-Wave Detectors
abstract: Abstract The post-merger (PM) phase of binary neutron star (BNS) mergers carries information about the merger remnant and dense-matter equation of state, but its observational prospects remain uncertain. We compare two ways of accessing this emission: the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from the BNS population and direct PM-band detections from individually resolved mergers. Using a unified inspiral–merger–post-merger (IPM) waveform prescription and the same astrophysical population model for both calculations, we evaluate representative third-generation detector configurations involving ET, CE, and a dedicated kilohertz detector. In the baseline IPM calculation, the all-source broadband BNS SGWB exceeds the adopted stochastic threshold for the representative detector-network configurations considered across the local-rate interval. By contrast, the kilohertz PM-band SGWB remains below the adopted detection threshold. For individual events, over $R_0=7.6-250~{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, the baseline IPM model predicts approximately $5-174$ PM-band candidates per year for the dedicated kilohertz detector, while the numerical-relativity cases considered here give approximately $0.07-7~{\rm yr}^{-1}$.

title: Design and modeling of liquid-lead dump concepts for beamstrahlung radiation absorption in the CERN Future Circular e + e − Collider
The HSX stellarator: History, Design, Construction and Operation
abstract: Abstract The Helically Symmetric Experiment (HSX) is a modular stellarator optimized for reduced neoclassical transport. It has a major radius of 1.2 m and an on-axis magnetic field of typically 1 T, and has been operating since 2001. The device distinguishes itself by producing plasmas with fusion relevant electron temperatures well above 1 keV, as well as by providing a comprehensive suite of plasma diagnostics ranging from profile measurements to fluctuation diagnostics. Moreover, as the world's only quasi-helically symmetric device, HSX serves as an important platform for both experimental and numerical studies. In this work, we present an overview of the history, design, construction, and ongoing operation of HSX, with the goal of establishing a reference and informing the design of future stellarator experiments.

title: Re4: scientific computing agent with rewriting, resolution, review and revision
abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are a promising class of generative artificial intelligence models and have demonstrated abilities to perform complex tasks in multiple domains, including mathematical and scientific reasoning. In this work, we construct a novel agent framework for solving representative problems in scientific computing. The proposed agent, incorporating a ‘rewriting-resolution-review-revision’ logical chain via three reasoning LLMs (functioning as the Consultant, Reviewer, and Programmer, respectively), is integrated in a collaborative and interactive manner. The Consultant module endows the agent with knowledge transfer capabilities to link problems to professional domain insights, thereby rewriting problem descriptions through text augmentation. The Programmer module is responsible for generating and executing well-structured code to deliver the problem resolution. The Reviewer module equips the agent with the capacity for self-debugging and self-refinement through interactive feedback with code runtime outputs. By leveraging the end-to-end review mechanism, the executable code provided by the Programmer undergoes iterative revision. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted on the performance of the proposed agent framework in solving typical partial differential equations, engineering-oriented flow past a cylinder, ill-conditioned linear systems, and data-driven physical analysis problems. Compared with a single-model approach, this collaborative framework significantly improves the bug-free code generation rate and reduces the occurrence of non-physical solutions, thereby establishing a highly reliable framework for autonomous code generation based on natural language descriptions. The review mechanism improved the average execution success (bug-free code and non-NaN solutions) rate of the modern reasoning model DeepSeek R1 from 59 % to 82 % , while ChatGPT 4.1-mini improved from 66 % to 87 % and Gemini-2.5 improved from 60 % to 84 % . Automatic code generation and review provide a promising workflow for scientific computing; analysis of solver-development trajectories further reveals recurring implementation difficulties in boundary treatment, array indexing, and the preservation of numerical constraints.

title: Quantum Startup, Recoil Statistics and Collective Gain in Free-Electron Lasers
abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum signatures can be distinguished from classical dynamics and statistical fluctuations in a free-electron laser. Starting from minimal coupling and the Bambini--Renieri frame, we derive the momentum-photon exchange Hamiltonian and its Raman-Nath ladder. An interaction-picture expansion retains detuning exactly and organizes recoil corrections through the mismatch between neighboring orders. Its validity depends on the accumulated recoil phase over the populated ladder, rather than on elementary recoil alone. Numerical checks and Gaussian entrance packets illustrate the effects of preparation and resonance averaging. We distinguish number-state exchange amplitudes from predictions for a coherent optical seed, and joint electron-field coherence from reduced radiation coherence. The Wigner representation connects finite recoil translations with classical transport and identifies the information required for bunching. A cavity channel then provides the basis for comparison with the recoil-resolved oscillator proposed by Kling and Giese, including the optical-undulator preparation, stimulated back-action and narrow resonance acceptance. Space charge, spontaneous diffusion and FEL-induced energy spread are compared with recoil and high-gain bandwidth scales. The coherent undulator pump is essential to exclude artificial zero-recoil antibunching from a number-state preparation. Startup and excess photon variance alone do not establish a quantum signature: the specified observable must remain distinguishable from a classical stochastic baseline under compatible preparation, propagation and detection conditions.

title: A provenance-aware zirconia conductivity database and Arrhenius-constrained screening of doped electrolyte candidates
abstract: Abstract Zirconia solid electrolytes are key oxygen-ion conductors, but reported conductivity values depend strongly on dopant chemistry, processing history and measurement temperature. Here we curate a provenance-aware zirconia conductivity database of 1351 records and use it to compare an Arrhenius-constrained physics-informed machine-learning model (PIML) with an unconstrained deep neural network (DNN). In a reserved grouped-material confirmation split, the DNN achieves the lower pooled root-mean-square error (RMSE, in log 10 ⁡ σ units) for withheld composition–processing groups. The Arrhenius-constrained model remains on a comparable error scale and provides bounded effective activation-energy estimates. Its clearest benefit appears in matched-material temperature extrapolation: when trained at ⩽ 800 ∘ C and tested at ⩾ 900 ∘ C ( n = 47 ), PIML reduces RMSE from 0.4187 to 0.3609 and raises R 2 from 0.8562 to 0.8932. Bootstrap resampling of individual records and material groups quantifies uncertainty in the observed RMSE reduction. Genetic-algorithm screening at a fixed measurement temperature identifies a Sc-rich/Mg-containing zirconia region for further study. CHGNet molecular dynamics examines oxygen transport in four selected compositions. DFT calculations use one atomic configuration per composition to compare energies relative to the constituent oxides. This work provides a curated conductivity resource and a conservative screening route for doped zirconia electrolytes.

title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
abstract: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{\pi^-}-R_{\pi^+})/R_{\pi^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

title: SPH methods in the modelling of compact objects
abstract: We review the current status of compact object simulations that are based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method. The first section of this review is dedicated to SPH as a numerical method for Newtonian, ideal gas dynamics and it should be fairly self-contained. It begins with the basics of the method, but also describes recent advances including various meshless derivatives or methods for treating shocks. A separate chapter summarizes general relativistic SPH, including its special relativistic limit, and it explains in some detail the recent development of full numerical relativity in SPH where matter is evolved together with a dynamical spacetime. The remainder of the review has an astrophysical focus, here we discuss the status of the simulations of white dwarf--white dwarf, neutron star--neutron star and neutron star--black hole systems. For each type of system the emphasis is on gravitational-wave-driven mergers, but we also briefly summarize dynamical collisions that can occur in locations with large stellar densities.

title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
abstract: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

title: Powering the Space Elevator
abstract: Powering the Space Elevator is a report on the work of an International Space Elevator Consortium study group tasked with determining the technology options for delivering power to the climbers on the space elevator at any altitude above Earth. The book covers options such as laser power beaming, microwave beaming, a solar-powered climber, and delivering power through the electrical conductivity of the tether. This report starts with the reference conceptual design of a climber from the 2023 study report, "The Climber/Tether Interface of the Space Elevator," and adds features to the climber that allow it to ascend or descend the elevator tether. The strengths and limitations of current technologies are identified, along with areas for future research.

title: Narrowband active noise control for continuous wave operation of TESLA cavities
abstract: TESLA 9-cell elliptical cavities are used in the accelerators of the European XFEL and LCLS-II. The high duty cycle upgrade study for EuXFEL and the LCLS-II-HE program target loaded quality factors of 6.10^7 and beyond, leading to RF cavity half bandwidths below 11 Hz. Stable operation in these conditions heavily relies on active RF resonance control, since the RF drive power required to maintain amplitude and phase lock would surpass amplifier max ratings if detuning is not compensated. To counteract mechanical vibrations, e.g. introduced by rotational machines in the proximity of the accelerating modules, a dedicated narrowband active noise control algorithm was introduced in previous work. This proceeding presents CPU based implementations and latest test results obtained at the Cryomodule Test Bench (CMTB) at DESY and LCLS-II at SLAC, where the stable operation gradient of a cavity could be increased from 9 to 15 MV/m without violating RF control limits.

title: Extreme PeV accelerator associated with GRS 1915+105
abstract: Microquasars, binary systems featuring relativistic jets, have emerged as sources for particle acceleration beyond PeV energies. We present a study of the broadband $\gamma$-ray emission from one of the most prominent Galactic microquasars GRS 1915+105 based on data accumulated by LHAASO and Fermi-LAT over 4 and 17 years, respectively. A joint analysis of LHAASO-WCDA and LHAASO-KM2A data reveals extended $\gamma$-ray emission whose centroid appears significantly shifted, by ~ 0.13{\deg}, from the binary system and its jets. The spectral energy distribution is well described by a curved spectrum with progressive steepening that can be described by a log-parabola function with no evidence for a sharp cutoff, consistent with parent particles reaching multi-PeV energies and an extreme acceleration efficiency approaching the limit set by the available potential drop across the source. Several features, most notably the shift of the emission and single-power-law spectrum down to GeV band, favor radiation by cosmic rays accelerated in the source interacting with the dense ambient medium. Our spectral modeling implies that at least a few percent of the jet mechanical power is transferred to protons, whose maximum energy reaches beyond 5 PeV. These results strengthen the case for microquasars as exceptionally efficient accelerators in our Galaxy.

title: Equivalent-circuit analysis of the transverse resonant beam coupling impedance due to ceramic-chamber RF shields in the J-PARC Main Ring spill-feedback quadrupoles
abstract: Ceramic vacuum chambers in fast-ramping or fast-response magnets are equipped with RF shields of conducting strips closed through lumped capacitors, which form a resonant circuit coupled to the transverse dipole moment of the beam. We evaluate the transverse beam coupling impedance due to the RF shields of the ceramic chambers in the spill-feedback quadrupole magnets of the J-PARC Main Ring. The RF shield is modelled by a magneto-quasi-static partial element equivalent circuit, and the laminated yoke of the magnet by a two-dimensional field solution with a complex permeability. The analysis shows a low-$Q$ resonant coupling impedance. The yoke lowers the resonance frequency and raises the shunt impedance per quality factor, and its effect cannot be neglected. The quality factor is determined mainly by the losses in the capacitors and in the laminations. The predicted peak impedance of the three chambers exceeds the resistive-wall impedance of the whole ring. The model can be applied to other machines and to the design of future rapid-cycling synchrotrons.

title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
abstract: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: Direct photons escape heavy-ion collisions with little rescattering, carrying information from the full emission history. Yet describing the measured direct-photon yield and the sizable elliptic flow $v_2$ together remains a long-standing challenge. Here we explore how correlations between emitting partons may affect both observables. The local $2\to2$ photon rate depends on the joint distribution of incoming partons, so a connected correlation between them can change photon emission without changing the one-particle distribution of medium particles. Once folded over the evolving medium in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, the correlation raises the photon yield toward the fitted PHENIX and ALICE data and increases $v_2$ mainly at intermediate $p_T$. The fitted temperature dependence accounts for most of the net flow increase in this region, suggesting that the correlation changes the relative contributions between hotter and cooler regions.

title: Unexpected Plateau: The Constant $ \rm \log \epsilon (Th/Eu)$ Ratio of Actinide-Boost Stars
abstract: The astrophysical site of the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) is still one of the major open questions in astronomy. A key mystery is the origin of the peculiar actinide-to-lanthanide ratio found in the so called actinide-boost stars, with $ \rm \log \epsilon (Th/Eu)>-0.35$. Here we present the largest sample of Th measurements in stars formed in an external galaxy, Gaia Sausage Enceladus. From this sample, we present the three most metal-rich actinide-boost stars discovered to date, $\rm -1.6<[Fe/H]<-1.1$. In addition, we measured Th in a comparison sample of Milky Way stars formed in situ, and compiled Th measurements from the literature which do not account for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) effects. After applying NLTE corrections to the combined sample, a bimodality in the $\rm\log\epsilon (Th/Eu)$ ratio is revealed. Unexpectedly, actinide-boost stars lie on a very narrow $(\sigma=0.02)$ plateau of $\rm \log\epsilon(Th/Eu)=-0.2$, clearly separated from actinide-normal stars. Most (if not all) of the actinide-boost stars in our sample originate from outside the Milky Way. Chemical evolution models show that such a plateau can arise, even at [Fe/H] = $-$1, when a single actinide-rich event dominates the r-process content of a small or gas-depleted system. Combined with other evidence, our results suggest that mergers with neutron stars are the most promising astrophysical site for actinide-boost stars.

title: PANTERA. I. Hunting for the Most Metal-Rich Stars in the Solar Neighborhood with High-Resolution Spectroscopy
abstract: We present PANTERA (Project for Astrophysical Nucleosynthesis and Targeted Exploration of metal-Rich Abundances), a high-resolution spectroscopic survey of the most metal-rich stars in the solar neighborhood. In this first paper, we report iron abundances for 56 metal-rich stars, selected from Gaia DR3 XP spectrophotometric metallicities. These targets were observed with the PEPSI spectrograph on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the Levy spectrograph on the Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope, and the HIRES spectrograph on the Keck telescope. We derive [Fe/H] from an equivalent-width analysis of iron lines, with the effective temperature taken from photometry and the surface gravity from the Gaia parallax. We verify our measurement using Gaia benchmark stars, observing some sources with more than one spectrograph, using a second synthesis code, and an independent equivalent-width measurement. We find that the Gaia-XP metallicities over-predict [Fe/H] for part of our sample: they agree with our values for the dwarfs, though a selection bias limits what this agreement can show, and exceed our [Fe/H] by $0.15\pm0.02$ dex on average for the cool giants. We attribute the over-prediction in part to the strong blue line blanketing of the cool metal-rich giants and to the survey labels on which the XP metallicities were trained. We find that 25 of the 56 stars have [Fe/H] $> +0.4$, with the most iron-rich stars reaching [Fe/H]$=+0.58$. We discuss the implications of our result on studying metal-rich populations.
journal_ref: The Open Journal of Astrophysics, Vol. 9, 2026

title: Constraining neutron-star properties with ensembles of thermonuclear bursts: application to SRGA J144459.2-604207
abstract: Deducing the properties of the host neutron stars from thermonuclear (type-I) X-ray bursts remains a challenge, due to incomplete data, multidimensional parameter space, and dearth of suitable models and analysis tools. Here we describe further development of the BEANSP package, with a new "ensemble" analysis mode utilising the consistent and regular "clocked" bursting exhibited by some sources. This mode requires only one model evaluation per epoch, and so is much more efficient than the previous "train" mode. We apply the code to the best-known source exhibiting "clocked" bursting, GS 1826-24, utilising a grid of KEPLER models pre-calculated for this purpose, and find good agreement with a previous study. We performed experiments on simulated data, and recovered input parameters related to the burst ignition with reasonable accuracy, but less so for the system distance, emission anisotropy and neutron star mass and radius. Finally, we assembled a set of 14 daily burst epochs covering the 2024 outburst of the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar SRGA J144459.2-604207, and attempted to constrain the system properties of this object by comparing to SETTLE model predictions. We find reasonably good agreement between the observations and model predictions for a mildly sub-solar fuel composition, with H-fraction $X\approx0.54$ and CNO metallicity $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx0.01$. However, we note that the inferred H-fraction is in excess of the limit of 0.4 established separately, and the adopted model may not provide sufficiently accurate predictions for this burst ignition regime. The inferred distance depends on assumptions about the system inclination and corresponding anisotropy of the persistent emission, and is likely in the range 6-11 kpc. Future applications with more physically realistic models are a promising avenue for this and other sources with H-rich bursts.

title: The imprint of neutron escape on non-thermal protons in AGN coronae
abstract: The coronae of active galactic nuclei (AGN) are promising sites of proton acceleration to hundreds of TeV, potentially accounting for the neutrino excess from NGC 1068 reported by IceCube. We show that photohadronic proton-to-neutron conversion provides an important proton escape channel, as neutrons can leave the corona well before decaying. In magnetized turbulent coronae, neutron escape can reduce the characteristic neutrino energy by up to a factor of four and the integrated neutrino luminosity by approximately 30% at a fixed non-thermal proton energy density. More strikingly, proton-to-neutron conversion offers an escape route roughly two orders of magnitude faster than proton diffusion, requiring a correspondingly larger proton injection rate to sustain the non-thermal population. The effect is considerably weaker when proton escape is already ballistic, as expected in magnetic-reconnection scenarios. Therefore, neutron escape is essential for quantitatively connecting neutrino emission from AGN coronae to the efficiency of proton injection into the acceleration process.

title: Inferring the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section from IceCube data
abstract: Neutrinos interact only via the weak force, through the exchange of $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$ bosons in charged-current and neutral-current interactions, respectively. Recent experiments have measured the charged-current cross section at high energies, whereas neutral-current interactions remain largely unexplored experimentally. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section using 12 years of data. We consider two strategies to constrain this quantity: $(i)$ leveraging neutrino absorption and regeneration as neutrinos traverse the Earth; and $(ii)$ using the track-to-cascade event ratio. We find that current IceCube data can set only an upper limit on the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section. We further show that IceCube-Gen2 should be able to constrain the neutral-current cross section with both methods considered here.

title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $\chi+Xe\to\chi+Xe^{*}$, as a complementary test of dark matter (DM) interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including accelerated DM populations and inelastic dark matter. Their signal patterns in the S1--S2 plane are reconstructed. The nuclear de-excitation shifts these signals toward the electronic-recoil band, where they may overlap with clustered isotope backgrounds. We then propose a schematic, physics-motivated background model to estimate their detectability. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rates are $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rates or below, and the projected sensitivity remains weak even at $200~{\rm tonne\,yr}$ for the scenarios investigated. versions.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
versions.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $\chi+Xe\to\chi+Xe^{*}$, as a complementary test of dark matter (DM) interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including accelerated DM populations and inelastic dark matter. Their signal patterns in the S1--S2 plane are reconstructed. The nuclear de-excitation shifts these signals toward the electronic-recoil band, where they may overlap with clustered isotope backgrounds. We then propose a schematic, physics-motivated background model to estimate their detectability. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rates are $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rates or below, and the projected sensitivity remains weak even at $200~{\rm tonne\,yr}$ for the scenarios investigated. Our results provide additional inelastic-xenon signal predictions for various DM scenarios and motivate improved high-energy background modeling and detector calibration for future searches.

title: Symmetry-based resolution of pseudogauge ambiguities in local equilibrium
abstract: The total angular momentum current can be decomposed into orbital and spin contributions in different ways, known as pseudogauges. This freedom leads to ambiguities in the definition of local-equilibrium density operators, which in turn affect estimates of spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the pseudogauge ambiguity, together with other ambiguities associated with improvements of conserved currents, is reformulated in terms of spurious symmetries corresponding to conserved currents with vanishing total charge. A prescription for the unambiguous definition of a local-equilibrium density operator, defined as deviating from global equilibrium only by small gradients, is introduced using the currents associated with genuine symmetries. The resulting density operator is invariant under transformations that add improvement terms to local currents, including the energy-momentum tensor.
