title: Energy resolving optical transition-edge sensor approaching fundamental limits
abstract: Transition-edge sensors (TES) have long held promise for exhibiting single-photon spectral resolution with near-unity detection efficiency, no read noise, and negligible dark counts. A TES detector capable of simultaneously achieving these traits could be revolutionary in fields including quantum computing, quantum sensing, biological imaging, and the detection of life on alien worlds by spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres. The applicability of optical TES detectors in these fields has been limited by energy resolution results that differ significantly from the theoretical expectations. We report significant enhancement of the single-photon energy resolution of tungsten (W) TESs by mitigation of athermal phonon loss during the photon-absorption energy down-conversion cascade. Implementing barriers to phonon loss dramatically increased the TES energy resolution (delta E). We achieve delta E of 34 meV - 61 meV, with resolving power (R = E/delta E) of 24 - 43, in a band spanning 1550 nm - 471 nm. All relevant electrical/thermal device parameters are explored in order to model theoretical limits to delta E imposed by noise, and provide an estimate of the athermal phonon trapping factor. Based on a simple model of electrical, thermal, and phonon escape noise sources, we estimate a phonon trapping factor approaching 90% for our best performing TES architecture. These results bring optical TES technology closer to theoretical predictions and to achieving the ambitious goals of photon-starved optical spectroscopy and fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.

title: Demonstrating CBM Capabilities through $\Lambda$ Reconstruction with mCBM
abstract: The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment at the upcoming Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR) is a high-rate fixed-target experiment designed to investigate nuclear matter at extreme baryon densities in relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions. To enable high-statistics measurements of rare probes, CBM is designed to operate at event rates up to 10 MHz. This necessitates the development of fast and radiation-tolerant detectors, self-triggered front-end electronics, a free-streaming data acquisition architecture, and real-time event reconstruction capabilities. Prototype versions and pre-series productions of the CBM detector systems have been deployed in the mini-CBM demonstrator setup mCBM - an experimental precursor comprising sub-components of all major CBM systems, installed at the SIS18 facility of GSI/FAIR within the FAIR Phase-0 program. In 2024, Ni+Ni collisions at a kinetic beam energy of 1.93 AGeV and an average interaction rate of about 500 kHz were successfully recorded. This dataset enables a detailed evaluation of the operational performance of the detector systems as well as the complete CBM data chain, while the reconstruction of $\Lambda$ baryons, which constitute a relatively rare signal within the limited geometrical acceptance of mCBM, serves as a natural benchmark. This paper presents the first results on $\Lambda$ baryon reconstruction with the mCBM experiment, demonstrating the functionality of the detector technologies and the data chain for the upcoming full-scale CBM experiment.
authors: Yue Hang Leung (for the CBM Collaboration)

title: Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC
abstract: Particle track reconstruction in high-energy collider experiments is a computationally demanding combinatorial problem, traditionally solved by Kalman filters that scale poorly with increasing detector occupancy. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative. In this work, we introduce the Manifold Helical-IN, a novel Interaction Network architecture that explicitly embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold chart using curvature-aware features. This geometric projection mathematically unrolls the tightly curling trajectories of low-momentum particles. Consequently, the network can distinguish true physical tracks from combinatorial noise with good precision. Evaluated on the TrackML challenge dataset, the proposed Manifold Helical-IN achieves a reconstruction efficiency of 0.9675 in the experimentally critical $p_T > 0.5$ GeV regime, approaching recently reported Transformer-based approaches. Crucially, the manifold embedding yields a fake track rate of 0.0037. This represents a 13-fold improvement over the baseline Helical-IN (0.0508). Furthermore, the model maintains good track coherence, as quantified by our proposed Mean Hit Recovery Fraction (MHRF) of 0.858, and achieves a highly efficient inference latency of approximately 150 ms per event on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. These results represent a critical step toward real-time soft particle tracking for the High-Level Trigger (HLT). By operating within practical HLT latency budgets, this geometry-aware approach provides a pathway to recover soft, anomalous Beyond Standard Model signatures such as unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs), that routinely evade standard hardware filters.

title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform
abstract: Active-target gas time projection chambers (TPCs) could provide the ultimate measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future neutrino oscillation measurements. Their development requires optimisation of the gas mixture, pressure, electric fields, and readout configuration. Warwick TPC (WarTPC) is an R\&D platform for investigating in these directions for neutrino physics and beyond. It can operate at pressures up to approximately 10 bar and features a combination of thick gas electron multipliers and a Timepix3 camera for optical readout. In this paper, we present the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform, describing the design and integration of its subsystems, and report the first measurements of its optical response under different operating conditions, demonstrating a stable and functioning R&D platform.

title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

title: Superradiant terahertz free-electron laser driven by wakefield-modulated electron bunches
abstract: Superradiant free-electron lasers (FELs) can significantly reduce the saturation length and produce high peak-power radiation pulses. However, this mechanism places stringent demands on the precise longitudinal microbunching of the electron beam. In this paper, we propose a compact, high-power terahertz (THz) superradiant scheme based on electron bunch trains induced by dielectric wakefield modulation. The electron beam acquires a THz-frequency periodic energy modulation in a dielectric-lined waveguide, which is converted into density modulation by the linac and chicane. In the nonultrarelativistic regime, longitudinal space-charge oscillations (LSCO) introduce coupling between the longitudinal and transverse beam dynamics, increasing the complexity of beamline optimization. Therefore, a multiobjective optimization approach based on Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II is used to determine the beamline configuration. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme generates bunch trains with tunable spacings ranging from 1 to 2 ps, with a maximum bunching factor of 0.4 at the fundamental frequency. Further analysis indicates that, after microbunch formation, LSCO contribute to a reduction in energy spread, improving beam quality. In addition, a one-dimensional FEL code is developed to investigate the radiation performance of the prebunched electron beam within the undulator. Simulation results show that the radiation frequency is tunable over the range of 0.5 – 2 THz , with a maximum radiation energy of 47.7 μ J for an electron beam with an energy of 10 MeV and a charge of 150 pC.

title: Statistical properties of attosecond SASE free-electron lasers
abstract: Modern free-electron laser (FEL) facilities produce x-ray pulses as short as hundreds of attoseconds for use in ultrafast science experiments. These experiments ideally require accurate characterization of the attosecond pulse duration; however, direct time-resolved diagnostic techniques are far from being a routine procedure. In the meantime, the most experimentally accessible information about the x-ray pulses is their spectra and pulse energies. We show that the statistics of these quantities from a large dataset are sufficient to determine the average “lasing” length of the electron bunches, after which FEL theory determines the statistics of the x-ray pulses. These predicted statistics can be compared to those obtained from direct time-resolved measurements. A strategy is proposed to systematically reconstruct the average FEL parameter and electron bunch length from the measured pulse spectra and energies. On the way, we extend the analytical frameworks put in place by Bonifacio and Saldin, generalizing to finite-length, nonuniform bunches with startup from shot noise.

title: Harmonic modulation for ultrawide tuning range terahertz free-electron laser via frequency-beating laser modulation
abstract: Broadband tunability is a key pursuit for terahertz (THz) free-electron lasers, yet it is often constrained by the narrow energy acceptance of laser modulators in prebunched schemes. Here, we propose a harmonic modulation scheme to decouple this constraint. Taking the Electron Source Test Facility at Dalian as a specific case study, our simulations demonstrate that by matching the laser field to higher-order harmonic resonances of the undulator, we can obtain efficient energy modulation across a significantly wider electron energy range (40–130 MeV), surpassing the limit of 71–130 MeV imposed by the fundamental resonance. This technique facilitates continuous frequency tuning from 0.5 to 30 THz using a single modulator-radiator chain, establishing a versatile method for ultrabroadband THz generation.

title: Generation of isolated attosecond soft x-ray pulses using a nondispersive inverse Cherenkov dielectric laser modulator
abstract: We propose and numerically demonstrate a scheme for generating isolated attosecond soft x-ray pulses based on an enhanced self-amplified spontaneous emission configuration that employs a nondispersive inverse Cherenkov radiation dielectric laser accelerator (ICR-DLA) as the energy modulator. Unlike conventional modulators, whose dispersive resonance conditions distort few-cycle laser pulses, the ICR-DLA operates with a phase-matching condition strictly independent of the driving laser wavelength, thereby faithfully mapping the temporal waveform of the few-cycle pulse onto the longitudinal phase space of the electron beam. Start-to-end simulations show that a 2.5 GeV electron beam with a current of 3 kA and a normalized emittance of 0.43 mm · mrad , modulated by a 4 μ m few-cycle laser pulse and subsequently compressed, generates a localized density profile comprising a few discrete microbunches. The dominant central spike attains a peak current of 12.1 kA and a duration of 1.5 fs and drives a nearly isolated soft x-ray pulse with a peak power of 10 GW and an full width at half maximum duration of 530 as, while the adjacent satellite pulses are suppressed to below 2 GW. By overcoming the fundamental bandwidth limitations of traditional modulators, this ICR-DLA-driven scheme provides a compact path toward next-generation attosecond x-ray free-electron lasers.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Measured Neutron Flux Profiles of the SAFARI-1 Research Reactor
abstract: Knowledge of the neutron flux distribution is essential for safe and effective reactor utilisation. In the SAFARI-1 research reactor, a set of axial flux profiles are periodically measured by activating natural copper wires inserted along the height of the fuel or control assemblies and subsequently measuring their activity using a sodium iodide detector. Improper wire insertion can, however, result in profiles that do not accurately represent the actual neutron flux distribution. Building on previously identified potential indicators of improper wire insertion, an automated approach based on unsupervised learning was developed to detect anomalous axial flux measurements. The measured data were preprocessed using missing-value imputation, decay correction, and normalisation. High-order polynomial fitting was then applied to characterise the axial flux profiles and derive features describing their shape. The Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm was employed to group flux profiles into regular and abnormal clusters based on these features with results matching the known groups. In addition, Convolutional Autoencoders were developed and trained on flux profiles from central and peripheral core positions to identify deviations from the regular profiles through reconstruction error, achieving better performance in central assemblies than in peripheral assemblies. The developed framework is intended to provide feedback to reactor operation by identifying potential wire-insertion problems in the manual technique used for axial flux monitoring at SAFARI-1.

title: Uncertainty evaluation of length measurement by spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing
abstract: In this study, we evaluate the measurement uncertainty of spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing, which has significant potential for interferometer-based dimensional calibration services owing to its simple configuration and nanometer-level precision. A super-luminescent diode (SLD) with a broadband spectrum was used as the light source for high-precision length measurement, and a frequency-calibrated spectrometer captured the spectral interference signal. The length measurement results were compared with a laser displacement interferometer. To evaluate the measurement uncertainty, numerical simulations were performed by considering the intensity-noise level of the CCD in the spectrometer and the frequency-axis uncertainty of the spectrometer. Through a comprehensive uncertainty analysis supported by numerical simulations, the combined standard uncertainty of the measured length was evaluated as sqrt((10 nm)^2 + (9.7x10^(-6)xL)^2). The resulting uncertainty budget provides a metrological basis for extending SLD-based SDI with super-Gaussian windowing toward interferometric dimensional calibration tasks over the millimeter-scale range.

title: Performance and Stability Studies of GEM Detectors for High Energy Physics Applications
abstract: R\&D on different gas-filled detectors such as Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs), Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) and straw tubes has been carried out in the detector laboratory of Bose Institute for more than a decade, keeping in mind present and future high-energy physics experiments. In this article, performance studies of a single-mask triple-GEM detector using a $^{55}$Fe X-ray source with an Ar/CO$_2$ (70/30) gas mixture are described. The study focuses mainly on the gain, energy resolution, count rate, and stability of the chamber under long-term irradiation. The experimental setup, methodology, and analysis results are presented.

title: Oversampled Filter Bank Channelizer for Cryogenic Detectors
abstract: We present the field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of an oversampled gener- alized DFT (GDFT) filter bank, optimized for its usage in the readout of cryogenic detectors, such as the microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID). A polyphase structure is derived underlin- ing the efficiency of complex valued subband processing, raised by a GDFT modulation. For the latter, a fast Fourier algorithm realization may be used, yielding a highly efficient polyphase imple- mentation for arbitrary integer decimation ratios. The filter bank is tested through a 16-channel GDFT channelizer. The implementation is based on the Xilinx Zynq family of FPGAs and aims to show the data reuse and flexibility offered by the GDFT channelizer structure. General design criteria are summarized for the 16-channel polyphase filter bank channelizer. The performance in hardware resource usage is also presented, taking into account one of the main objetives of the current physics experiments, aiming to have extremely large readout format.

title: High-Transmission Cryogenic Fiber-Optic U-Bench Filter for Ultra-Low-Background Single-Photon Detection in Superconducting Devices
abstract: We report on our progress in implementing a cryogenic fiber-optic U-bench hosting an ultra-narrow bandpass filter, designed to mitigate the dominant fiber-coupled 300 K black-body background observed for superconducting single-photon detectors. While U-benches can be routinely aligned at room temperature to achieve minor optical losses, cooling them down results in substantial misalignment due to thermal contraction of their components. To mitigate the resulting losses, we have integrated cryo-compatible piezo stepper motors to the U-bench, enabling its in situ realignment while cold. In particular, this allows us to shift the temperature dependent transmission window of the used filter by rotating it with respect to the beam axis. First results show that our U-bench filter reaches a transmission coefficient of 38% (4.2 dB loss) at 40 K temperature. We project that the U-bench filter can reduce the black-body background down to $10^{-8}$ Hz and $10^{-3}$ Hz ranges for 1064 nm and 1550 nm wavelengths, respectively. With the expected background rates and the herein reported transmission coefficient, applying the U-bench filter in series with a transition edge sensor shows great potential in increasing the sensitivity of dedicated rare-event searches. We project that the noise-equivalent power for 1550 nm wavelength could be reduced down to $10^{-20}$ W Hz$^{-1/2}$ range if intrinsic background sources can be sufficiently mitigated.

title: Extending the Love-Q relation to rapidly rotating neutron stars for gravitational-waveform modeling
Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Cost Immersion Cooling System
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, open-source, single-phase immersion cooling testbed for studying liquid cooling of data center hardware. A 500 W titanium heater, standing in for server load, is submerged in a glass tank of mineral oil, a dielectric fluid. The heated oil is circulated by a magnetic drive pump through an air-cooled radiator. An ESP32 microcontroller logs three DS18B20 temperature sensors (heater surface, bulk fluid and ambient) and switches the pump, fan and heater through a relay module. The complete system costs INR 35,318 (about USD 380), built entirely from components available in India. At quasi-steady state under the full 500 W load, the heater surface reached 118.3 {\deg}C while the bulk oil stayed at 29.3 {\deg}C, only 8.0 {\deg}C above ambient. Thermal-resistance analysis shows that the heater-to-oil interface, limited by natural convection, accounts for about 92% of the total resistance (178.0 vs 16.0 m{\deg}C/W). The external loop therefore has spare capacity. CAD files, firmware and data are openly available, so the setup can be reproduced and used to compare dielectric fluids, loads and flow arrangements.

title: Axis-selective AC magnetic-field imaging in the tens-of-megahertz regime using RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry
abstract: Spatially resolved magnetic-field imaging reveals material properties and local currents in microelectronic devices. Conventional pulsed scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry (SNVM) faces increasingly stringent microwave (MW) pulse-control requirements for detecting radio-frequency (RF) magnetic fields at frequencies ranging from tens to hundreds of megahertz. To address this challenge, we implement an RF-dressed continuous-wave (CW) sensing scheme for SNVM and demonstrate AC magnetic-field imaging at 33.5 MHz. The method exploits electron-spin double resonance in the NV spin-1 three-level system: the target RF magnetic field coherently couples two spin eigenstates, forming RF-dressed states whose splittings are detected in continuous-wave electron-spin double resonance (CW-ESDR) spectra under continuous laser, MW, and RF excitation. This approach avoids short, high-power MW pulses and synchronization between the RF field and a pulsed sensing sequence. Using an NV-ensemble diamond probe integrated with an atomic force microscope (AFM), we image the Oersted field of an RF-driven L-shaped microcircuit. Successively selecting three crystallographic NV axes by static bias-field control yields maps of RF magnetic-field projection magnitudes, with distinct distributions qualitatively reproduced by Biot-Savart calculations. Transverse bias-field control also tunes the RF-coupled spin-state transition frequency from 14.4 to 89.3 MHz, as characterized by spectroscopy and Hamiltonian analysis, with RF-dressed resonances directly observed in CW-ESDR spectra at 89.3 MHz. Together with previous RF magnetic-field detection up to 632 MHz using the same RF-dressed CW sensing principle in a confocal NV setup, these results support extending AC magnetic-field imaging with SNVM toward the hundreds-of-megahertz regime and, with additional phase information, vector magnetic-field reconstruction.

title: Accessible 3D Printed Archimedes System for Accurate and Precise Density Measurements and Uncertainty Analysis
abstract: Accurate and precise density measurements are important for characterizing solid materials and for evaluating physical properties that are strongly affected by porosity. While several methods are available for determining density, measurements of small or irregularly shaped samples can be limited by sample geometry, balance precision, liquid density, and other experimental sources of uncertainty. In this study, an accessible Archimedes density measurement system was developed using 3D printed components and an analytical balance for the measurement of solid and liquid densities. The measurement of solid densities requires knowing the exact density of the liquid. Therefore, copper, vanadium, and indium standards were used to measure the densities of ethanol (0.8116 +/- 0.0005 g/cm3), distilled water (0.9982 +/- 0.0013 g/cm3), and hexanes (0.6748 +/- 0.0016 g/cm3), all of them showing strong agreement with literature values. Uncertainty analysis indicates that the relative uncertainty in the measured solid density decreases with increasing sample mass and balance precision, while higher density liquids can further reduce the required sample mass. The uncertainty of the immersed mass measurement was found to have a greater influence on the calculated density than the uncertainty of the air mass measurement. An open-source Archimedes LS software was developed to analyse liquid and solid densities including the corresponding uncertainties. These findings demonstrate that an accessible 3D printed Archimedes system combined with an open-source software provides a practical approach for improving the consistency and comparability of density measurements between laboratories.

title: A Double Sided LGAD-Based Detector Providing Timing, Position, and Track Angle Information
abstract: We describe a detector concept which combines small pixels enabled by 3D sensor-electronics integration with gain produced by a Low Gain Avalanche Diode (LGAD) layer. The detector is double-sided, with electrons collected by the cathode, which provides timing information, and an anode with small pixels to provide position and angle information. The cathode can be coarse grained, providing timing with fewer fast amplifiers to limit power consumption. The anode layer benefits from the gain of the LGAD, with larger signals that also limit the power needed. Position can be reconstructed by measuring the pattern of total charge deposited on the anode. Angle and depth of charge deposit can be measured by the shapes of the anode pulses. We describe a possible assembly technology based on 3D integration.

title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

title: A hierarchical adaptive Fourier-feature physics-informed neural network for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma discharges
abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are difficult to train for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma fluid-Poisson systems because missing initial conditions, steep sheath gradients, and strongly imbalanced residuals can lead to unstable or nonunique reconstructions. We propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Fourier-feature PINN (HA-FPINN) for such coupled plasma models. The method combines Fourier feature mapping to improve the representation of small-scale sheath structures, sparse physical anchors to provide interior constraints, and a two-level adaptive weighting scheme to balance the PDE, boundary, and anchor losses as well as individual equation residuals. The framework is tested on an 8-equation helium discharge model and a 23-equation electronegative Ar / O 2 model. In the helium case, HA-FPINN reconstructs the space-time evolution of the main physical variables with 1 % anchors and converges for all tested network architectures, with convergence times of 110 – 246 s. In the Ar / O 2 case, HA-FPINN achieves stable reconstruction with 5 % anchors, whereas the non-adaptive FPINN and standard PINN fail to converge under the same setting. The best performance in both systems is obtained at the tested Fourier frequency parameter σ = 2.20 . Noise-injection tests show that HA-FPINN maintains the lowest reconstruction error in the helium case and preserves the main space-time structures in the Ar / O 2 case at anchor noise levels of up to 15 % . These results show that HA-FPINN provides a robust PINN formulation for strongly coupled plasma fluid models with missing initial conditions.

title: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
abstract: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. The reduced longitudinal focusing, combined with high total $R/Q$ of these cavities, can make the beam susceptible to the periodic transient beam loading (PTBL) effect, a multibunch instability characterized by slow oscillations in bunch centroids and lengths and by its resistance to conventional feedback damping. In this work, building on a recent proposal of applying reactive feedback to control the PTBL effect, we developed a frequency-domain theoretical model, including the feedback voltage in the linearized Vlasov equation to derive a Lebedev equation modified by the feedback transfer function. The reactive feedback was also implemented in the time domain in the macroparticle tracking code \texttt{STABLE}. The methods were applied to the parameters of the double-rf system of the MAX IV storage ring. Both approaches show that, above a threshold gain, an idealized pure reactive feedback is able to suppress the PTBL effect, with good agreement between theory and simulations across beam currents and $R/Q$ values. Realistic hardware limitations were included in the analysis, determining the limits for feedback gain, latency, and bandwidth, which are compatible with existing bunch-by-bunch feedback systems. Using the HALF storage ring parameters, the semi-analytical results indicate that the reactive feedback can be extended to suppress the PTBL effect in triple-rf systems, albeit at higher threshold gains than for double-rf systems.

title: Few-Ion Schottky Power Scaling and Automated Reconstruction of Single-Ion Events
abstract: Non-destructive Schottky diagnostics at heavy-ion storage rings is broadly exploited to measure revolution frequencies and intensities of stored ions. The mean Schottky power of incoherent stored ions is expected to be proportional to their number. An empirical examination of this response in few-ion populations is important for interpreting individual occupancy changes. We present an automated staircase reconstruction of the power in a selected frequency band of time-resolved Schottky spectra. The procedure was applied to 7008 selected injections recorded with a resonant cavity pickup at the Experimental Storage Ring at GSI during an experiment on the nuclear two-photon decay of the first excited $0^+$ state in bare $^{98}\mathrm{Mo}^{42+}$. The distribution of freely fitted level heights exhibits maxima close to integer multiples of a single-ion power scale up to approximately five ions. This is consistent with an approximately additive mean power response under the present measurement conditions. The reconstructed occupancy histories also retain population dwell intervals and resolved disappearance times for subsequent lifetime analyses.

title: Booster-based beam recycling for swap-out injection at the High Energy Photon Source
abstract: Fourth-generation synchrotron light sources employ ultralow-emittance storage rings with stringent injection requirements. On-axis swap-out injection alleviates the dependence on storage-ring dynamic aperture, but high-charge operation requires an efficient injector architecture capable of producing high-charge replacement bunches. This paper presents the accelerator physics design and performance analysis of a booster-based beam-recycling swap-out injection scheme implemented at the High Energy Photon Source (HEPS). In this approach, the full-energy booster serves as both an injector and a high-energy accumulator. An extracted storage-ring bunch is returned to the booster, merged with a low-charge bunch previously injected from the linac and accelerated to full energy. Following high-energy damping, the merged bunch is reinjected into the original storage-ring bucket. The scheme avoids the need for a dedicated accumulator ring while enabling high-charge bunch replacement. The recycling scheme was commissioned through staged machine studies. Full recycling-chain simulations, commissioning studies, and measured performance analysis are presented. The measured results characterize the recycling operation and quantify the transmission efficiency and performance limitations of the complete recycling loop. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the booster-based beam-recycling architecture and establish its operational basis for high-charge swap-out injection in future fourth-generation synchrotron light sources.

title: Novel observables for exploring jet quenching effects in individual jets
abstract: We introduce event-shape observables in the jet frame to characterize intra-jet shapes and study medium modifications in heavy-ion collisions. Using the JEWEL model, we investigate jet constituent angular and transverse momentum distributions, together with two representative event-shape observables, transverse thrust $\tau_\perp$ and transverse sphericity $S_\perp$, in $p$+$p$ and 0--10% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}$. These observables are evaluated after transforming the jet constituent momenta into the jet frame. The intra-jet shape distributions in Pb+Pb collisions shift toward larger values relative to those in $p$+$p$ collisions, indicating more isotropic distributions of constituent transverse momenta. Comparisons between calculations with and without recoil, along with the dependence on the constituent transverse momentum threshold, indicate that medium response plays an important role in these modifications. These results suggest that jet-frame event-shape observables provide sensitive probes of medium response in jet quenching, complementary to single-particle angular and transverse momentum distributions.

title: Holographic Butterfly Velocity and Heavy-Quark Drag in a Doubly Anisotropic Magnetized QGP
abstract: We investigate butterfly velocity and heavy-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma with two distinct sources of anisotropy, generated by collision geometry and an external magnetic field, within a five-dimensional holographic model exhibiting magnetic catalysis. In contrast to studies restricted to isotropic or singly anisotropic media, we analyze the butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag force along all three orthogonal spatial directions at finite temperature and chemical potential in the deconfined phase. We find that the collision-induced anisotropy plays a dominant role in the directional dependence of both butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag. It governs the directional splitting of the butterfly velocity, and significantly enhances the parallel drag force while suppressing the transverse components. For butterfly velocity, a strong magnetic field primarily suppresses the longitudinal butterfly velocity while leaving the transverse components nearly unchanged. For the drag force, the magnetic field breaks the transverse symmetry, yet it does not alter the overall monotonic increase of the drag force with heavy-quark velocity, temperature, and chemical potential. Most importantly, by bridging the Einstein and string frames via the Weyl transformation, we extract the frame-dependent drag-chaos relation. Generalizing it to the doubly anisotropic plasma, we demonstrate that despite the underlying frame-dependent chaos, the normalized directional drag exhibits a direction-dependent geometric correction at order $\mathcal{O}(v^{3})$. These results establish a direction-resolved connection between heavy-quark dissipation, information scrambling, and the underlying anisotropic geometry of magnetized QGP.

title: Connecting High-Twist Expansion and Color Glass Condensate Dynamics
abstract: The high-twist (HT) expansion and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) describe nuclear multiple scattering in complementary kinematic regimes. For direct-photon production in proton-nucleus collisions, we formulate an arbitrary-order multiple-scattering master expression that includes photon emission before, between, or after the ordered quark scatterings in the amplitude and its conjugate. In the high-energy limit, resumming multiple scatterings to all orders recovers the CGC Wilson-line dipole result. However, the naive power expansion of the eikonal CGC result reproduces the leading twist but only part of the twist-four contribution obtained in the HT expansion. Including longitudinal sub-eikonal phases and Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference restores the CGC-HT correspondence through twist-4.

title: Complementary Approach to Anisotropic Flows in Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: We present a complementary count of directed flow \(v_1\) and elliptic flow \(v_2\). It does not replace known methods. A fixed laboratory plane defines up--down and left--right asymmetries. A scan of the test angle is written down as a theoretical proposal. Each event is given one angle \(\alpha\) drawn uniformly on \([0,2\pi)\), the fixed plane is rotated by \(\alpha\), and the asymmetries are averaged over events. With \(\theta=\alpha\) known, the linear fit recovers \(v_n^{\mathrm{true}}\). The quadratic mean, Eq.~(5), agrees with the pair form, Eq.~(21), in which the \(1/N\) self term cancels, and both sit above \(v_n^{\mathrm{true}}\) because the event noise in \(A\) is squared. The time for one count grows linearly with the number of particles. The pair sum, and the usual two-particle correlation, grow as the square of that number. The sample is PHSD Au+Au at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2\,\mathrm{GeV}\), \(b=4.0\)--\(5.2\,\mathrm{fm}\).

title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
abstract: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $\mu_{\Delta}$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.

title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

title: Evidence for a Fast, Long-Period, Hot Population of Accreting Neutron Stars
abstract: Context. Accreting neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries allow us to probe the accretion histories that produce recycled millisecond pulsars. Aims. We expand the analysis of the spin distribution with an enlarged sample of 39 accreting neutron stars and investigate whether the high-frequency objects preferentially occur in binaries with longer orbital periods and have higher quiescent surface temperatures. Methods. We compare several empirical models for the spin distribution. We use stochastic drift-diffusion estimates and simple braking models to determine whether short-timescale torque fluctuations or secular spin-down can account for the observed population widths. Results. The best statistical description of the spin distribution consists of a broad low-frequency component and a narrow high-frequency concentration centred at ~566 Hz with a width of ~32 Hz. Fast rotators preferentially occupy longer orbital-period binaries, with possibly higher neutron star temperatures. Short-timescale stochastic accretion torque fluctuations cannot produce the observed spin-frequency dispersion in either the fast or the slow component, even under generous assumptions. We show that a non-linear deterministic braking mechanism can instead shift and compress a spin distribution, but the spin data alone do not identify the braking mechanism. Conclusions. The population widths appear to reflect differences in long-term torque conditions and/or evolutionary histories rather than short-timescale torque noise. If the fast systems are close to spin equilibrium, their narrow distribution requires the combination of physical parameters setting the equilibrium frequency to vary relatively little from source to source.Any model that explains the spin distribution should therefore also explain why the fast systems tend to have longer orbital periods and, possibly, higher temperatures.

title: A helium-rich mass-donor in a 3.5-hr low mass X-ray binary
abstract: Binary systems in which a neutron star accretes material from a low-mass stellar companion arise from evolutionary processes that depend sensitively on the progenitor properties. It is usually assumed that the accreted material has approximately solar composition, unless the orbital period is $\lesssim80$ min, indicating an "ultracompact" system with a hydrogen deficient donor. However, few constraints on the donor composition are available. Here we apply a Bayesian model-comparison framework, BEANSP, to a sample of 21 thermonuclear bursts from the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar, IGR J17511-3057, to constrain the fuel composition as well as the system parameters. Our analysis strongly indicates an extremely hydrogen- and CNO-deficient fuel composition, with $X \approx 0.03$ and $Z_\rm{CNO}\approx 4 \times 10^{-4}$, unexpected for this system with its relatively long 3.5 hr orbital period. We explore the possible circumstances under which such an object can evolve, and discuss the implications for its history also in light of the three transient outbursts that have been observed to date. Such analyses are finding an unexpectedly wide range in donor compositions, that may help to explain the remarkable diversity in the burst properties of the known burst sources

title: Revealing the Nonlinear Amplification of Radiation Reaction Effects via Vortex Radiation
abstract: Radiation reaction (RR), the back-action of emitted radiation on an accelerated charge, dominates the dynamics of ultrarelativistic electrons in an intense electromagnetic field. We derive an analytical formula for the RR-inclusive harmonic spectrum of vortex $\gamma$-ray emission in monochromatic-wave nonlinear inverse Thomson scattering (NITS), extend it to finite pulses under the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA), and take the Landau-Lifshitz (LL) solution as the starting point. We find that once cumulative RR on the oscillation radius over hundreds of cycles becomes non-negligible, the laser intensity nonlinearly amplifies RR through the modified longitudinal drift velocity, reshaping the vortex emission. For monochromatic approximation of long pulse flat-top laser, harmonic band acquire MeV-scale red shifts and spectral compression, producing overlap; higher harmonics show anomalous polarization transitions, so the superposed ellipticity departs from the RR-free case. For a $\sin^2$ envelope, the lower edge red-shifts while the upper cutoff stays fixed, broadening the band, and individual polarization transitions remain analogous to RR-free case. These harmonic-resolved spectral and polarization fingerprints constitute a self-referenced multidimensional diagnostic of RR effects that complements energy-spectrum measurements and, through the RR-inclusive scaling law between the polarization and laser amplitude, provide an independent route to measuring the laser intensity. These results have direct implications for bright high-energy $\gamma$-ray sources and the modeling of extreme astrophysical environments such as neutron-star magnetospheres.

title: Holographic SU(3) color superconductivity from color-octet condensation in AdS$_4$
abstract: We present a holographic model of $SU(3)$ color superconductivity in asymptotically AdS$_4$ in which scalar and vector color-octet condensates form at finite baryon chemical potential. At $\mu_b=0$, a channel scan within consistent truncations shows that the favored sector reproduces the known $SU(2)$ s+p competition. At finite $\mu_b$, the s-wave order generalizes to an $S_1+iS_2$ structure. In the probe limit, the $S_+$ critical temperature grows linearly with $\mu_b/\mu_3$, while the p-wave critical temperature is independent of $\mu_b$. Once backreaction is included, the p-wave critical temperature decreases with $\mu_b$ and the p-wave phase disappears beyond a critical value of $\mu_b$. At high $\mu_b$, the balanced $S_+$ phase (with $S_1=S_2$) is the dominant color-superconducting phase, while the $S_-$ condensate, which signals the imbalance between $S_1$ and $S_2$, appears only at low temperature and low baryon density. Our results provide a holographic laboratory for color-octet condensation and non-Abelian color dynamics in dense matter such as neutron-star interiors.

title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
abstract: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

title: Accretion onto a moving black hole for stiff equations of state
abstract: We revisit accretion of an asymptotically uniform fluid onto a moving Schwarzschild black hole, the relativistic analog of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion. Expanding on previous treatments, we focus on relativistic accretion of stiff fluids with adiabatic indices $\Gamma \geq 5/3$, which is particularly relevant for the treatment of primordial black holes captured by neutron stars. We perform numerical simulations to systematically explore the dependence of the steady-state accretion and drag rates on the asymptotic sound speed $a_\infty$ and relative speed $v_\infty$, and identify different regimes, both subsonic and supersonic, in which these rates either increase or decrease with respect to the spherical accretion rate for $v_\infty = 0$. We propose simple analytical approximations that capture the qualitative features observed in the dependence of the accretion and drag rates on $a_\infty$ and $v_\infty$.

We perform numerical simulations to systematically explore the dependence of the steady-state accretion and drag rates on the asymptotic sound speed $a_\infty$ and relative speed $v_\infty$, and identify different regimes, both subsonic and supersonic, in which these rates either increase or decrease with respect to the spherical accretion rate for $v_\infty = 0$. We propose simple analytical approximations that capture the qualitative features observed in the dependence of the accretion and drag rates on $a_\infty$ and $v_\infty$.

versions.title: Correlation between nuclear isospin asymmetry and $\alpha$-particle preformation probability for superheavy nuclei from a Bayesian inference
versions.abstract: In the study of $\alpha$ decay within the superheavy nuclear region ($Z \geq 90$ and $N \geq 140$), the $\alpha$-particle preformation probability $P_{\alpha}$ serves as a crucial physical quantity linking nuclear structure to decay observables. We introduce a phenomenological model incorporating the decay energy $Q_{\alpha}$, mass number $A$, orbital angular momentum $l$, isospin asymmetry $I$, and unpaired nucleon effect. For the first time, a Bayesian inference method combined with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling has been employed to impose global constraints on the model parameters, enabling the systematic and high-precision calculation of $P_{\alpha}$. The results reveal a significant suppressing effect of isospin asymmetry on $P_{\alpha}$, a finding independently corroborated by random forest-based feature importance analysis, which identified $I$ as a dominant factor. Furthermore, calculations using the maximum a posteriori (MAP) parameters not only reproduce the shell effect at $N=152$ but also yield $\alpha$ decay half-life predictions in excellent agreement with experimental ones, thereby validating this model universality. This work provides the first global analysis tool for probing the $\alpha$ preformation mechanism in superheavy nuclei, underscores the potential of the Bayesian framework for inverting complex nuclear physics problems, and establishes a reliable theoretical benchmark for guiding future experimental exploration of superheavy nuclei.

title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
abstract: Abstract We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3 hr. Our observations span 0.65–233 GHz from 6–356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium (ne∝R−k; k = 1.5 − 2). We detect significant variability in the low frequency (≤3 GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of 1.2 × 1016 ≲ R⊥ ≲ 5 × 1017 cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle θj ≳ 15 deg, low Lorentz factor (Γ ≲ 10) jet, or a narrow θj ≲ 2 deg (Γ0 > 50) highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs (EK ~ 1051 erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs (EK ~ 1050 erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

title: Precise description of spontaneous fission half-lives of Rutherfordium isotopes within the relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory
abstract: I investigate the spontaneous-fission (SF) half-lives of $^{254,256}$Rf within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov (MDC-RHB) model combined with the local quasiparticle random-phase approximation (LQRPA) method. The collective inertia is evaluated using the finite-amplitude method (FAM), which enables a fully self-consistent treatment of dynamical residual effects beyond the conventional cranking approximation. The effective collective potential is constructed by subtracting both the vibrational zero-point energy and rotational energy correction from the deformation energy surface. The SF half-lives are evaluated within the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation. Compared with the nonperturbative and perturbative cranking approximation, the FAM-LQRPA collective inertia is significantly enhanced, especially around the ground-state minimum, due to the dynamical residual interaction included in the QRPA. As a consequence, the predicted SF half-lives increase by several orders of magnitude and become consistent with experimental data. The calculated SF half-lives are 5.65 $\mu$s for $^{254}$Rf and 0.95 ms for $^{256}$Rf, both within approximately two orders of magnitude of the corresponding experimental values. These results indicate that a self-consistent treatment of dynamical residual effects and beyond mean-field correlations is crucial for quantitative microscopic descriptions of SF within covariant density functional theory.

title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

title: Investigating three-body resonances in α α Ω / Ω c c c clusters within the Ω / Ω c c c 9 Be nucleus
abstract: We investigate the bound and resonant states of the α + α + Ω and α + α + Ω c c c three-body systems, corresponding to Be Ω 9 and Be Ω c c c 9 , within the Gaussian expansion method combined with the complex scaling method. The α Ω and α Ω c c c interactions are constructed by folding the N Ω and N Ω c c c potentials obtained from lattice QCD calculations by the HAL QCD Collaboration with the nucleon density distribution of the α particle. The uncertainty associated with the α -particle matter radius is also examined. For the Ω sector, the strong N Ω attraction generates deeply bound 0 1 + , 2 1 + , and 4 1 + states in Be Ω 9 , accompanied by a pronounced contraction of the α α core, demonstrating a strong gluelike effect of the Ω baryon. An unconventional inversion between the 0 1 + and 4 1 + levels is also predicted. In contrast, the Ω c c c baryon produces considerably weaker attraction: the 0 1 + state of Be Ω c c c 9 is weakly bound, whereas the 2 1 + and 4 1 + states remain resonances. Their resonance energies and widths exhibit a clear dependence on the strength of the α Ω c c c interaction. These results reveal qualitatively different gluelike behaviors of the Ω and Ω c c c baryons and provide predictions for the spectroscopy of exotic multistrange and triply charmed hypernuclei.

title: Forward hadron production in p p collisions at LHC energies from an event generator based on the color glass condensate framework
abstract: We investigate inclusive forward single-hadron production in high-energy proton-proton collisions using a color glass condensate-inspired Monte Carlo event generator, MC-CGC. We carried out a systematic study of the sensitivity of the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution equation to its initial conditions by comparing three parametrizations: the McLerran-Venugopalan (MV) model and its two HERA deep inelastic scattering-constrained variants, MV γ and MV e . Our results indicate that the current LHCb data favor the MV γ and MV e models, while the differences from the original MV model become more pronounced at higher transverse momentum and at midrapidity. As a complementary analysis, we also compared the dilute-dense [Dumitru–Hayashigaki–Jalilian-Marian (DHJ) factorization] and dense-dense ( k T -factorization) frameworks. We found that the k T -factorization framework provides a better description of the particle production spectra at midrapidity than the DHJ framework, where both the projectile and target are in the dense regime at LHC energies. Predictions for the forward calorimeter measurements at ALICE, including the production of identified neutral mesons and jets, are also presented.

title: Highly hindered B ( E 1 ) transition strength in Ag 107
abstract: The excited states of $^{107}\mathrm{Ag}$ were populated via $^{100}\mathrm{Mo}(^{11}\mathrm{B},\phantom{\rule{0.28em}{0ex}}4n)$ reaction at the BARC-TIFR Pelletron Linac Facility located at TIFR Mumbai. The mean-life of $15/{2}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ state at 2299-keV energy level was measured using the fast timing method. The $B(E1)$ transition strengths of 1307- and 498-keV $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ rays using the measured mean-life were found to be $4.8(9)\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{\ensuremath{-}7}$ and $1.7(4)\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{\ensuremath{-}7}\phantom{\rule{0.28em}{0ex}}\mathrm{W}.\mathrm{u}.$, respectively, indicating highly hindered transitions. The shell-model analysis was performed to understand the microscopic origin of this extremely slow $E1$ transition using both proton and neutron core excitations. This study highlights the complicated structure of $15/{2}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ state, having small wave-function admixtures from the proton $0{f}_{7/2}$ and the neutron $1{p}_{3/2}, 0{f}_{5/2}$, and $0{f}_{7/2}$ orbitals.

title: Sizeable mixing between the coexisting normal and intruder structures of Zr 96 revealed through lifetime measurements
abstract: Lifetimes of excited states of the nucleus Zr 96 were studied with the Doppler-shift attenuation method following the Zr 94 ( O 18 , O 16 ) Zr 96 two-neutron transfer reaction. The obtained B ( E 2 ; 2 2 + → 0 2 + ) and B ( E 2 ; 4 1 + → 2 2 + ) transition strengths, amounting to 26 ( 2 ) and 39 ( 7 ) W . u . , respectively, firmly attribute the 2 2 + and 4 1 + states to the collective intruder band built on top of the 0 2 + state. The nature of this structure is discussed against predictions of the collective model using the Bohr Hamiltonian, the interacting boson model with configuration mixing, and the quasiparticle vacua shell model. The collective, interband B ( E 2 ; 4 1 + → 2 1 + ) = 11.2 ( 8 ) W . u . transition strength, refuting the previously assumed purity of both structures, is reproduced in the calculations. The quasiparticle vacua shell model predicts, in agreement with a simple two-state model based on experimental E 2 transition strengths, considerable mixing between the normal and intruder 2 + states.

title: Observation of the $\Lambda(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
abstract: A suppression of the baryonic $\Lambda(1520)$ resonance yield relative to the $\Lambda$ ground state by $0.589 \pm 0.015^{\rm stat} \pm 0.086^{\rm syst}$ is observed in central relative to peripheral Pb-Pb collisions, with a significance of $6.8\sigma$. The $\Lambda(1520)$ production at midrapidity is measured in six centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions for the first time at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV with ALICE. The $\Lambda(1520)$ is a sensitive probe of late-stage hadronic interactions since its lifetime is comparable to that of the hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC. Statistical hadronization model calculations, predicting yields at chemical freeze-out, overestimate the measured ratio. The transverse-momentum spectra and the centrality dependence of the suppression are reproduced by the MUSIC hydrodynamic model only when coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner, which implements rescattering and regeneration in the late hadronic stage. The measurement, which represents the first observation of resonance suppression within a single collision system, provides a stringent test of the late-stage dynamics and evidence that hadronic interactions substantially modify reconstructible resonance yield.

title: Systematic comparison of driving potentials: Benchmarking and prediction for Ca 48 + Es 254
abstract: The synthesis of the superheavy element with atomic number $Z=119$ via the $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}+^{254}\mathrm{Es}$ reaction represents one of the most promising near-term experimental goals, although theoretical predictions of its evaporation residue cross section (ERCS) are consistently low. Within the dinuclear system (DNS) model, the driving potential $U(\ensuremath{\eta})$ provides the microscopic landscape governing nucleon transfer and compound-nucleus formation. We therefore examine how different microscopic inputs modify the fusion path and ERCS predictions for $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$-induced reactions on $^{248}\mathrm{Cm}, ^{249}\mathrm{Cf}$, and $^{254}\mathrm{Es}$. Calculations based on finite-range droplet model (FRDM) and Weizs\"acker-Skyrme (WS) microscopic-macroscopic models are compared, with the former two benchmark reactions evaluated against available experimental data. Within the WS model, explicitly introducing deformation parameters $({\ensuremath{\beta}}_{1},{\ensuremath{\beta}}_{2})$ as independent degrees of freedom reduces the Coulomb potential at the entrance channel, thereby lowering the inner fusion barrier by approximately 1 MeV. The inclusion of shell-correction damping at finite excitation energy further modifies the driving potential and fusion probability ${P}_{\mathrm{CN}}$ within the optimized deformation scheme. For the $3n$ evaporation channel of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}+^{254}\mathrm{Es}$, predicted ERCS lies in the range of [0.016,0.167] pb around the favorable excitation-energy region of ${E}^{*}=32--34$ MeV. The comparison with previous theoretical studies indicates that the energy region is relatively robust, whereas the absolute cross section exhibits substantial model dependence. These results provide a quantitative assessment of microscopic uncertainties in driving potential calculations for future $Z=119$ synthesis studies.

title: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
abstract: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $\alpha$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $\alpha$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $\alpha$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.

title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes. Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: A Search for Rotation Measure Flare Candidates in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts
abstract: Abstract Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration extragalactic radio transients of unknown origin. Rotation measures (RMs) probe their local magnetoionic environments and provide important clues to their nature. While RM variability has been observed in several repeating FRBs, it is typically gradual or stochastic. Recently, observations of FRB 20220529A revealed an abrupt RM excursion followed by rapid recovery on weeklong timescales, termed an “RM flare,” suggesting a potentially distinct form of RM variability associated with localized magnetized plasma. In this work, we perform a systematic search for RM flare candidates in repeating FRBs with multi-epoch RM measurements. Using an iterative Gaussian smoothing method to estimate the baseline and a 3 σ significance threshold for candidate selection, we identify one tentative RM flare candidate in FRB 20121102A and one marginal signal in FRB 20240114A, in addition to the event in FRB 20220529A. Our results suggest that RM flares, if confirmed, may not be rare among repeating FRBs and point to highly dynamic magnetized environments local to the sources. Future high-cadence polarimetric observations, particularly following the discovery of RM excursions, will be essential for further evaluating these candidates and constraining their physical origin.

title: Jet-like di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions
abstract: Heavy-ion collisions are primarily studied to investigate the properties of hot and dense nuclear matter, known as the quark--gluon plasma (QGP). However, recent observations of hydrodynamic flow-like behaviour in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC suggest the possible formation of QGP droplets even in small collision systems. To bridge the multiplicity gap between small and large systems and to examine the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions, light-ion collisions were performed for the first time at the LHC in 2025. This contribution presents measurements of the near-side peak width of di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions with ALICE, used to search for medium effects. The width of the near-side correlation peak is studied as a function of the average charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity. At low transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$), the near-side peak is broader in OO and Ne--Ne collisions than in pp and pO collisions, and in central collisions its width approaches that measured in Pb--Pb collisions. At higher $p_{\rm T}$ the peak narrows modestly with increasing multiplicity. The results are compared with PYTHIA, AMPT, and JETSCAPE calculations, none of which reproduces the measured widths over the full kinematic range.
authors: Suraj Prasad for the ALICE Collaboration

title: Cross-shell excitations and the evolution of high spin states in $^{89}\mathrm{Y}$: A shell-model revisit
abstract: Nuclei in the vicinity of $Z=38$--40 and $N=50$ provide an important testing ground for studying the evolution of nuclear structure across the proton subshell and neutron shell closure. In particular, $^{89}$Y offers an opportunity to investigate the inert core behaviour and effect of particle-hole excitations in generating the observed high spin states. In this work, we perform a systematic large-scale shell-model study of $^{89}$Y using different model spaces and well accepted effective interactions. Excitation energies, electromagnetic transition probabilities, and nucleon occupation probabilities are calculated and compared with available experimental data to explain the microscopic structure of the observed high spin states. The role of neutron excitations across the $N=50$ shell gap is examined in detail. A comparative analysis of the employed effective interactions is performed to assess their applicability in describing the spectroscopic properties of $^{89}$Y.

title: Quasi-doublets in the 3 α spectrum of 12 C
abstract: Abstract Within the three- α cluster model of 12 C, we perform configuration-space Faddeev calculations of the low-lying 0 + and 2 + states. Resonance states are treated using a variant of the analytic continuation in the coupling constant (ACCC) method. The phenomenological Hamiltonian includes both two-body and three-body interactions. The recently proposed effective-field-theory-motivated leading-order (LO) α α interaction is approximated by a Gaussian-type (LO-simulating) potential to reproduce the experimental α – α scattering phase shifts. The parameters ( V , β ) of the three-body force (3BF), V 3 bf ( ρ ) = V exp [ − 1 2 ( ρ β ) 2 ] , are determined by fitting the experimental spectrum of 12 C. We investigate the possibility of a universal set of two- and three-body interactions capable of simultaneously reproducing the energies of lowest 0 + or 2 + states. For the 2 + levels, we find that the condition β > 3 fm must be satisfied for such universality. The ACCC method, combined with the effective-mass approach, reveals level anticrossing and demonstrates coupling between the 0 1 + and 0 2 + states, as well as between the 2 1 + and 2 2 + states, which can be interpreted as quasidoublet structures in the 3 α spectrum. The calculated results are compared with those obtained using the Ali–Bodmer potentials and the next-to-next-to-LO interaction. We find that the LO-simulating potential reduces the strength of the 3BF required to reproduce the low-lying spectrum.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Construction, commissioning, and performance of the ENUBET demonstrator
abstract: Abstract A final full-size prototype of the instrumented decay tunnel of ENUBET, referred to as the Demonstrator, was constructed and its performance was tested during the 2022, 2023 and 2024 beam test campaigns at the CERN East Area facility. We demonstrate the full scalability of this specialized longitudinal sampling calorimeter technology, based on iron absorbers and scintillator tiles readout by wavelength-shifting fibers and SiPMs. In addition, we evaluate the channel-by-channel response and the performance in terms of electron energy resolution, linearity, and particle identification capabilities, using charged particle beams with energies up to 5 GeV. A comparison with the predictions of a GEANT4 simulation of the prototype is also presented. The achieved energy resolution (∼ 17% at 1 GeV and 10% at 3 GeV) fully satisfies the requirements for positron identification. The results meet the requirements for neutrino monitoring through lepton identification in the decay tunnel and validate the ENUBET full simulation. Although some limitations have been identified, they can be readily addressed in future developments.
