title: Three-dimensional spatial modeling of nuclear de-excitation lines
abstract: Context . Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are commonly thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants. Observations of ionization rates in the interstellar medium (ISM) have indicated an excess of low-energy CRs (LECRs) beyond that expected from standard propagation models. The LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV γ -ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can provide direct constraints on the LECR flux, its morphology, and its acceleration mechanisms. Aims . We aim to construct all-sky maps of de-excitation γ -ray emission from the Milky Way based on 3D CR distribution models. By comparing the predicted de-excitation line emission with the Galactic diffuse continuum, we assess the detectability of these lines. Methods . We calculated the de-excitation emission by combining 3D CR distributions obtained with the CR propagation code GALPROP and γ -ray production cross sections calculated with the state-of-the-art nuclear reaction code TALYS. Beyond the standard Galactic CR component, we constructed models including an additional LECR component motivated by the high ionization rates measured in the ISM. Results . The predicted de-excitation emission is relatively weak when integrated over the broad regions commonly adopted in MeV γ -ray analyses (| l | ≤ 30° and | b | ≤ 15°), contributing only ≲1% above the leptonic continuum, even when considering the additional LECR component. The all-sky maps revealed that in the standard scenario, the de-excitation-to-leptonic flux ratio remains low over the entire sky, reaching at most ∼20% toward the Galactic anticenter. In contrast, models including an additional LECR component exhibited a pronounced enhancement toward the GC, where the ratio exceeds 100%, indicating favorable prospects for detection through spatially resolved analyses. We also find that the 6.1–4.4 MeV intensity ratio is particularly sensitive to the maximum energy of the injected LECR spectrum, varying by up to ∼30%. Conclusions . Our results demonstrate that the next generation of MeV observatories can already establish the presence of a distinct LECR component and constrain its origin, acceleration mechanism, and transport in the Galaxy.

title: Study of the shape coexistence in the 96 Zr, 96 Mo, 96 Ru isobars
abstract: Abstract Three stable isobars, 40 96 Zr 56 , 42 96 Mo 54 and 44 96 Ru 52 , which are in the vicinity of the harmonic oscillator proton shell closure Z = 40 and the spin–orbit neutron shell closure N = 50 , are investigated for the presence of the shape coexistence and mixing phenomena. The ground state deformation of these isobars is extracted from the potential energy surface determined within the relativistic Hartree–Bogoliubov approach using a density-dependent point-coupling interaction, while the excited states are described involving the Bohr–Mottelson Hamiltonian with octic potential for both axially symmetric and γ -unstable quadrupole deformations. Within the broader view of the two approaches, the obtained results clearly highlight the significant contribution of these phenomena to the structure of the states of these nuclei.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Space-time Areas and Hadronization Studies
abstract: Space-time area laws play a fundamental role in modeling strongly interacting phenomena, such as in relativistic string models, QCD on the lattice, and in hadronization modeling. For the latter, an exact expression for relevant space-time areas related to the final state hadronic events for hadrons of any mass is calculated. Usage of this expression in the UCLA hadronization model helps validate its space-time area law (STAL) principle and unifies the treatment of heavy and light hadrons via a single fragmentation function.

title: Relativistic Second Random-Phase Approximation: Formalism and Applications to Giant Resonances
abstract: We develop a self-consistent relativistic second random-phase approximation (RSRPA) based on covariant energy density functional with density dependent point-coupling interaction. The formalism extends the conventional simple configuration space composed of particle-hole ($p$-$h$) transitions by including two-particle-two-hole ($2p$-$2h$) configurations through a generalized Thouless ansatz and a time-dependent variational principle. To ensure consistency with the underlying mean-field ground state and avoid the double counting of correlations, we implement the subtraction method, in which the static contribution is removed from the residual interaction. The first applications of the RSRPA include studies of isoscalar and isovector giant monopole (ISGMR and IVGMR) and quadrupole resonances (ISGQR and IVGQR) in $^{16}$O, which demonstrate the importance of $2p$-$2h$ couplings to describe the fragmentation of the transition strength and the stabilizing role of the subtraction method.

title: Relating Short Range Correlated Pair Abundances to Electron-Scattering Cross Section Ratios
abstract: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from SRC pairs and includes final-state interactions through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange. We show that the inclusive $(e,e')$, proton-knockout $(e,e'p)$, and neutron-knockout $(e,e'n)$ ratios are not independent: for any two nuclei where one is isospin symmetric ($N=Z$), two of these three observables determine the third within the model. For $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}$, for example, the measured inclusive $(e,e')$ and proton-tagged $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}(e,e'n)=1.35\pm0.07\,(\mathrm{exp})\pm0.15\,(\mathrm{model})$. A measurement of the $(e,e'n)$ ratio therefore provides a direct consistency test of the factorized pair-counting description. It also constrains the single-charge-exchange probabilities. Combining all three ratios with the two double-coincidence ratios determines the relative np-, pp-, and nn- SRC pair populations of any two nuclei. If one nucleus is isospin symmetric, any two of the three ratios suffice for the same result.

title: GEX1-mediated semigamy induces both maternal and paternal haploids in cotton
abstract: How semigamy generates haploids during double fertilization has remained elusive for more than six decades. Here, we identify Gamete Expressed 1 ( GEX1 ) as the gene underlying semigamy and show that it mediates dual-origin haploid induction in cotton. A naturally occurring mutation in GEX1 disrupts normal nuclear membrane fusion during fertilization, resulting in delayed or incomplete karyogamy. Cytological analyses reveal that delayed karyogamy allows the closely apposed but unfused gametic nuclei to undergo independent mitotic divisions, giving rise to maternal haploids, paternal haploids, and chimeric progeny. CRISPR-Cas9–mediated disruption of GEX1 reproduced the characteristic defects in nuclear fusion and enabled both maternal and paternal haploid induction within a single generation. Together, our findings uncover a genetically tractable mechanism underlying semigamy that links nuclear membrane fusion dynamics to haploid formation and establish a versatile strategy for rapidly generating doubled haploids from both parental genomes to accelerate crop breeding.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

title: Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge
abstract: We study quantum simulation of SU(3) non-Abelian gauge theory dynamically coupled with fundamental fermions in $3+1$ dimensions by employing the lattice Hamiltonian in axial gauge under fixed boundary conditions, which avoids Gauss's law constraints. The temporal component of the gauge field is analytically solved in terms of independent field degrees of freedom and a lattice regulated Green's function. The axial gauge condition is trivially maintained in time evolution, even under Trotterization. The gauge field degrees of freedom are expressed in the local field basis and can be efficiently transformed into the canonical conjugate momentum basis by local quantum Fourier transforms. We prove the number of qubits needed for describing all states up to an energy $E$ with an accuracy $\epsilon$ on a lattice of volume $V$ at bare coupling $g$ is bounded as $16n_A V + 12n_f V$, where $n_A \approx \log_2 (\frac{64 E' V^{4/3}}{\pi^2\epsilon} + \frac{32\sqrt{2}g n_f E'^{1/2} V^{7/6}}{\sqrt{3}\pi^3\epsilon^{1/2}} ) $ is the number of qubits needed for each independent gauge field per site with a shifted energy $E'$, and $n_f$ denotes the number of fermion flavors. We then analyze a quantum algorithm for time evolution that is based on Trotterization, quantum Fourier transform, and Jordan-Wigner transformation, for which quantum circuits can be explicitly constructed under arbitrary gauge field truncation and digitization. We find the numbers of CNOT and single-qubit rotation gates scale as $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3}) + O(V^{5/3})$ and $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3})$, respectively, per Trotter step for fixed $n_f\leq 6$. Together with the bounded Trotterization error, we conclude that quantum resources needed for simulating real-time dynamics of lattice QCD scale polynomially with volume, energy, time, accuracy, and bare Hamiltonian parameters.

title: Beyond leading-logarithm photon production from two-loop diagrams in a hot QCD medium
abstract: We investigate high-energy photon production from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes in a quark-gluon plasma by evaluating the imaginary part of the two-loop photon self-energies in thermal QCD. Working in the imaginary-time formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the leading-logarithmic and beyond-leading-logarithmic contributions to the photon production rate from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. We retain the full Fermi--Dirac and Bose--Einstein statistical factors and compare the resulting Compton and annihilation rates with those obtained from kinetic theory and the closed-time-path formalism. The summed rates agree with the corresponding established results, providing a nontrivial consistency check of the calculation. Furthermore, when we consider the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution for incoming particles, we find that quantum corrections are absent in the individual $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. However, the total rate agrees with that of full statistics.

title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $\chi$EFT and lattice QCD
abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.
authors: Md. Emanuel Hoque (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Arunava Mukherjee (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Sayantan Sharma (The Institute of Mathematical Sciences/HBNI)

title: New scaling of neutron star tidal deformability for directly probing the central equation of state parameter
abstract: The dimensionless tidal deformability, $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$, of neutron stars (NSs), inferred from gravitational wave (GW) observations, has thus far been used primarily to constrain the pressure of dense matter near twice nuclear saturation density, leaving the core equation of state (EOS) largely inaccessible to inspiral-phase GW observations. We show that a fundamental central EOS parameter can be probed directly through $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ using a perturbative analysis of the dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations formulated in terms of scaled intrinsic variables, without invoking any specific EOS model. We uncover a remarkable EOS-insensitive scaling relation between $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ and the central EOS parameter $\mathrm{X}\ensuremath{\equiv}{P}_{\mathrm{c}}/{ϵ}_{\mathrm{c}}$, where ${P}_{\mathrm{c}}$ and ${ϵ}_{\mathrm{c}}$ denote the central pressure and energy density, respectively. The relation is validated against a broad ensemble of physically viable EOSs. Applying it to tidal deformabilities inferred from events such as GW170817 enables a direct determination of $\mathrm{X}$. By adopting the previously established effective upper bound $\mathrm{X}\ensuremath{\lesssim}0.381$, we infer a tight lower bound, ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}_{\mathrm{TOV}}\ensuremath{\gtrsim}{9.1}_{\ensuremath{-}0.5}^{+0.5}$, for maximum-mass NSs along stable mass-radius sequences, quantitatively demonstrating that even the most compact stable NSs remain distinctly separated from black holes, for which ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}_{\mathrm{BH}}=0$. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized connection between inspiral-phase tidal deformability and the central EOS parameter $\mathrm{X}$, establishing a direct link between GW observables and the microphysics of ultradense matter in the strong-gravity regime. The resulting scaling establishes inspiral-phase tidal deformability as a direct and largely model-insensitive probe of the central EOS parameter $\mathrm{X}$, and hence of key properties of NS cores.

title: Viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges to benchmark fluid simulations
abstract: We present semi-analytical solutions for the evolution of both the temperature and chemical potentials for viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges. Such a solution can be especially useful in testing numerical codes intended to simulate relativistic fluids with large chemical potentials. The freeze-out hypersurface profiles for constant energy density are calculated, along with the corresponding normal vectors and presented as a new unit test for numerical codes. We also compare the influence of the equation of state on the semi-analytical solutions. We benchmark the newly developed Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code CCAKE that includes both shear viscosity and three conserved charges. The numerical solutions are in excellent agreement with the semi-analytical solution and also are able to accurately reproduce the hypersurface at freeze-out.

title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
abstract: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

title: Probing the internal structure of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
abstract: The weak decay properties of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$, $\Omega \Xi \pi$, and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $\Omega \Xi \pi$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $\Omega \Xi \pi$ and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $\Lambda \bar{K} \Lambda \bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.

title: Particle diffusion in magnetized QCD matter with a realistic equation of state
abstract: In this study, we investigate particle number diffusion in an interacting hot QCD medium in the presence of an external magnetic field. Starting from an effective covariant description of the medium in terms of quasiparticle degrees of freedom, we employ a Chapman Enskog-like iterative expansion of the distribution function to derive the second-order relativistic magnetohydrodynamic evolution equation for the number diffusion current. The magnetic field introduces additional tensorial structures into the diffusion dynamics, thereby modifying the transport properties of the medium. We further obtain the corresponding Navier-Stokes limit and examine the influence of medium interactions and the magnetic field on the diffusion current and its associated transport coefficients. Our results show that medium interactions suppress the magnetic field-induced anisotropy in particle diffusion. This study provides a consistent framework for investigating dissipative particle transport in magnetized, interacting QCD matter and may serve as an important ingredient in developing realistic hydrodynamic descriptions of heavy-ion collisions.

title: Higher Mellin Moments of the Unpolarized PDF of the Pion and the Kaon from Lattice QCD
abstract: We present results on the Mellin moments of the unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) of the pion and kaon up to the fourth order. The computation is done using one $N_f=2+1+1$ gauge ensemble of twisted mass fermions with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical values. We reconstruct the valence pion and kaon PDFs using the connected contributions to the three Mellin moments. We compare our results on the Mellin moments and the reconstructed PDFs with other lattice QCD and phenomenological determinations.
authors: Luis Alberto Rodriguez Chacon (The Cyprus Inst.

title: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei
abstract: Entanglement governs both the classical cost of simulating correlated many-body systems and the quantum resources needed to treat them. In this work, we use nuclear symmetries to investigate the entanglement and correlations in nuclei using \textit{ab initio} symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model nuclear wavefunctions, illustrated here for $^{4,6,8}$He, $^8$Be, $^{12}\mathrm{C}$, $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, and $^{48}$Ca. In this many-body approach, deformation and collectivity naturally emerge from the underlying chiral potential, and we show that the Sp(3,$\mathbb{R}$) basis concentrates the ground state in far fewer basis states than the SU(3) basis. We compute single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examine the organization of like-particle two-nucleon correlations into symmetry channels. Single-mode entropies are largest in the valence shells, while two-mode mutual information reveals substantial correlations both within and between shells. In all cases considered, the dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, which reduces the number of variational parameters. Since the number of operator components within the channels is comparable in the two schemes for the heavier nuclei, this gives the SU(3)-coupling scheme a clear advantage. Fiedler ordering of the correlation graph with local refinement reduces the register ordering cost by a factor of 2 to 3 relative to the original shell ordering, and by 10 when two more shells are included in the register. Together, these measures link nuclear correlations to the selection of active modes and candidate excitation operators and to the design of quantum register layouts, offering guidance for the development of hybrid quantum-classical calculations of nuclei.

title: Critical excited states in quantum metrology
abstract: We investigate criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, we design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to enhance signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation using experimentally relevant generators. We show that the excited-state criticality provides a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that circumvent the 'death of adiabaticity', limiting conventional critical quantum metrology with ground-state criticality.

title: A Non-Relativistic Model of Heavy Quarkonium
abstract: We develop a non-relativistic, spin-dependent, phenomenological model of heavy quarkonium. The model is based on a hydrogen-like Schr\"odinger equation derived from a spin-dependent Hamiltonian that includes a hyperfine spin--spin interaction term. The resulting system is solved using matrix mechanics by diagonalizing the Hamiltonian to obtain the energy spectrum. The energies are further optimized using variational methods. Spin--orbit corrections are included at first order in perturbation theory. The resulting spectrum shows good agreement with experimental data for conventional heavy quarkonium states. The framework combines matrix mechanics, variational methods, and perturbation theory, and is therefore suitable for students familiar with quantum mechanics.

title: Properties of the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) ± in hot and dense nuclear matter
abstract: We investigate the properties of the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) ± in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) + stem from changes to the D K channel within the coupled D K − D s η system. As nuclear density increases, the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) + quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the D -meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of Σ c N − 1 excitations in the D -meson spectral function shifting the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) + peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) − is governed by the D ¯ K ¯ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the K ¯ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) − also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the D s 0 * ( 2317 ) + mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for D s 0 * ( 2317 ) − , its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.

versions.title: Properties of the $D_{s0}^*(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter
versions.abstract: We investigate the properties of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ stem from changes to the $DK$ channel within the coupled $DK$-$D_s \eta$ system. As nuclear density increases, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the $D$-meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of $\Sigma_c N^{-1}$ excitations in the $D$-meson spectral function shifting the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ is governed by the $\bar D \bar K$ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the $\bar K$ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$, its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.

title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Impact of errors in the shape function of rotating neutron stars in the oblate Schwarzschild approximation
abstract: Measurements of thermal x-ray flux emitted by neutron stars can constrain their radii and the equation of state of cold dense matter. Accurate flux modeling of rapidly rotating neutron stars requires an approximation for their oblate surface shape, usually given by a shape function. We examine the accuracy of five shape functions by comparing them against numerical relativistic stellar surfaces for seven representative equations of state over a broad range of compactness and spin. We characterize their errors in the surface radius and their derivative with respect to colatitude, test the extent of quasiuniversality, and propagate these errors into the differential solid angle $d\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Omega}}$, a geometric factor underlying the observed flux, under the oblate Schwarzschild approximation. We find that the shape functions produce distinct error patterns associated with their forms and parameter ranges. These errors remain structured in compactness, spin, and colatitude. Simple polynomial corrections substantially reduce the radius errors of several shape functions, with most corrected errors within approximately 0.5%. We show that errors in $d\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Omega}}$ may be understood as coming from an area contribution, which scales with twice the relative radius error, and a projection contribution controlled primarily by the error in the surface derivative. The projection contribution grows toward the limb, where small surface errors can produce much larger local errors in $d\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Omega}}$. We provide a set of guidelines for the construction of improved quasiuniversal shape functions that can be used in future radius estimation efforts. Our recommendations include that both the shape and its derivative be modeled accurately, that more accurate predictions of the polar radius be developed, and that the shape function be calibrated over the same compactness-spin range that is to be tested.

title: High-precision 81 Kr dating overcomes radiocarbon limits in Late Pleistocene groundwater
abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81 Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. Here, we extended the 81 Kr dating lower limit to ∼10 ka using high-precision atom trap trace analysis, thus covering the entire Late Pleistocene. We conducted a direct 14 C- 81 Kr comparison in the North China Plain. Within the 10- to 30-ka range, 81 Kr independently validates 14 C ages; beyond this range, it provides reliable ages for older groundwater. The dual-tracer approach reduces model uncertainty in 14 C correction and identifies mixing-affected samples. After screening, groundwater δ 18 O records closely match polar ice-core climate archives. High-precision 81 Kr dating, combined with 14 C, offers a robust age framework for reconstructing Late Pleistocene hydroclimate.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Development of millikelvin scintillation photodetectors with CUPID
abstract: CUPID is a next-generation tonne-scale cryogenic experiment that will search for the neutrinoless double beta decay $(0\nu\beta\beta)$ of $^{100}$Mo. It will be located at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory (Italy) and will employ the cryogenic calorimetric technique to reconstruct the energy deposited in Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ crystals, in which the isotope of interest is embedded. Preliminary measurements have been performed with the CUPID VSTT (Vertical Slice Test Tower), a prototype tower designed to test the detectors' response and the apparatus' mechanical and thermal stability. In addition, a key objective was to demonstrate the improved performance of germanium-based cryogenic light detectors. In CUPID, light detection is used for both particle identification and pile-up rejection. Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ is a scintillating crystal, enabling particle identification by exploiting the dependence of light yield on particle type. This requires collecting the Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ scintillation light, peaking at $\sim$600 nm, with a $\sim$300 $\mu$m-thick high-purity germanium wafer placed next to the crystal. The wafer is also equipped with concentric Al electrodes biased at a few tens of volts. This bias improves the signal-to-noise ratio by an order of magnitude thanks to the Neganov-Trofimov-Luke effect. This work presents preliminary results on the performance of the VSTT light detectors and of its Optical Injection System.

title: Bent-tailed radio galaxies as tracers of the intrafilament medium
abstract: Bent-tailed radio galaxies have traditionally been associated with, and used as tracers of, the dense intracluster medium. In recent years, however, such sources have also been identified outside of clusters, with only a few discovered in low-density environments of cosmic filaments. Their occurrence in low-density environments remains rare and is still poorly understood. We announce the discovery of bent-tailed radio galaxies in galaxy cluster filaments. We have identified two bent-tailed radio galaxies, J0020-25 and J0019-26, within a filament at the redshift of z ∼ 0.1273, and another bent-tailed radio galaxy, J0019-25, in a separate filament at z ∼ 0.1126. We used MeerKAT observations of these bent-tailed radio galaxies to place constraints on their intrafilament medium (IFM). The effects of the filaments could be seen in the radio morphologies of these galaxies. Using faint regions in each galaxy, we estimate the intrafilament pressure, density, magnetic field strength, and total energy density. We found an IFM density of ̊ho_ ≈ 3.8 g cm IFM 10^ -29 -3 $ for the surrounding medium of J0020-25 and J0019-26, and ̊ho_ ≈ (0.2 - 1.1) g cm^-3 around J0019-25. We found that our estimates for the intrafilament environment around J0020-25 and J0019-26 lie within the $̊ho_ literature estimates, while the density estimate found using J0019-25 is higher than the literature density estimates for the IFM and in agreement with the density of group environments. J0019-25 likely resides in a galaxy group embedded within a filament. These discoveries show the capabilities of using bent-tailed radio galaxies as probes to locate the otherwise invisible large-scale filaments. IFM 10^ -26 IFM

title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

title: Viscoelastic and thermal response on nuclear pasta states at finite baryon density
abstract: We compute the viscoelastic and thermal response of non-homogeneous hadronic condensates at finite baryon density representing crystals of baryonic tubes and layers. We describe them using analytic solutions of the Skyrme model in $3+1$ dimensions as ground states for a perturbative approach. At low enough temperatures, the lowest-energy excitations are described by a free massless scalar field theory in $1+1$ dimensions. We apply the Green-Kubo formulas to such excitations to obtain the elasticity tensor and other response coefficients. The analytic results of our computations are compared with available results on the nuclear pasta phase.

title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
abstract: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.

title: Proton Spin Fluctuation Decomposition
abstract: We formulate a fluctuation decomposition of proton spin in terms of the variances and covariances of the spin and orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons. We derive their representations in terms of single- and double-parton distributions. The definite proton spin imposes sum rules requiring the variances of its spin and orbital contributions to be compensated by their covariances. This framework reveals correlations and fluctuations that are invisible to the conventional proton spin decomposition.

Deep learning models for ADITYA-U MHD equilibrium
abstract: Abstract This work presents an integrated deep learning framework for rapid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium estimation in the ADITYA-U tokamak. A free-boundary equilibrium database containing 100,760 cases was generated using the pyIPREQ Grad–Shafranov solver from experimentally derived operating conditions spanning 766 ADITYA-U plasma discharges, with constraints representative of circular limiter plasmas near the flat-top phase. The database was used to develop a cascaded framework for predicting scalar equilibrium quantities, 1d safety factor profiles, and 2d poloidal flux profiles. Dense neural networks, principal component analysis (PCA), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) were investigated within this framework. The error propagation, cross-models consistency and ablation study of Grad–Shafranov residual were performed for the proposed framework. Across the test dataset, the models achieve median mean absolute errors of 1 × 10 − 2 for the safety factor profile and 2 × 10 − 3 for the normalized poloidal flux profile. The largest model requires approximately 1ms per equilibrium inference on a multi-core CPU. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a fast surrogate for equilibrium analysis, experiment planning and real-time plasma control applications for ADITYA-U experiments.

title: Track fitting at the full LHC collision rate
abstract: The LHCb experiment at the Large Hadron Collider underwent a major upgrade before the LHC Run 3 data-taking period, employing an all-software approach in its trigger system. Here we present a fast implementation of a Kalman filter, used in the first trigger stage since the 2025 data-taking period, allowing to determine parameter estimates of charged-particle trajectories at the full LHCb collision frequency of 30 MHz. This approach replaces computationally expensive magnetic field map lookups and numerical integration methods with fast analytical parameterisations while maintaining the mathematical framework of Kalman filtering. Implemented on approximately 500 GPUs within the first-level trigger, the algorithm has replaced the previous partial track fitting algorithm in the real-time trigger environment at the cost of a 2% increase in processing time. Compared to the previous fitter this parameterised Kalman filter shows a significantly improved momentum resolution, resulting in a factor of two improvement in the invariant mass resolutions for reconstructed D0 and J/{\psi} hadrons. It additionally demonstrates greater robustness against detector misalignment effects and substantially sharpens the discrimination between genuine particle trajectories and accidental background, more than doubling the rejection of the latter at no cost to genuine-track efficiency, for a standard selection working point.

title: Joint Bayesian Inference of Dense Matter and f(Q) Gravity with Nuclear and Neutron Star Constraints
abstract: We investigate neutron star (NS) properties in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity while consistently accounting for uncertainties in the dense matter equation of state (EOS). We focus on the linear $f(Q)$ model and perform a joint Bayesian inference of the nuclear matter and modified gravity parameters using a Taylor expansion EOS around nuclear saturation density. The analysis incorporates complementary constraints from nuclear saturation properties, chiral effective field theory calculations of pure neutron matter, heavy-ion collision, and empirical nuclear data, the GW170817 tidal deformability posterior, and NICER mass--radius measurements. The resulting posterior distributions simultaneously constrain the dense matter and gravity sectors and quantify their correlations within a common framework. For a canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NS, we obtain $R_{1.4}=11.28^{+0.35}_{-0.31}\,\mathrm{km}$ and $\Lambda_{1.4}=151.4^{+44.9}_{-31.2}$, while the maximum mass is constrained to $M_{\rm max}=2.22^{+0.29}_{-0.16}\,M_\odot$. The modified gravity parameters exhibit only weak direct correlations with most stellar observables, while a pronounced degeneracy remains within the gravity sector. Our results show that accounting for EOS uncertainties is essential for quantifying the interplay between dense matter physics and modified gravity and provide a systematic framework for confronting symmetric teleparallel gravity with nuclear and multimessenger NS observations.

title: The physical design of the superfluid helium-4 UCN source at CSNS
abstract: Ultracold neutrons (UCN) play a crucial role in fundamental physics research, enabling investigations into new sources of CP violation, neutron lifetime measurements, and the exploration of non-Newtonian forces. However, these experiments are often limited by the intensity of UCN sources. The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is developing a UCN source utilizing superfluid helium-4 at Beamline 12. This paper focuses on enhancing UCN density and total UCN number by analyzing various parameters that impact the UCN system, including the influence of different wavelengths of cold neutrons, incident beam size, converter length, wall and reflector materials, extraction method, extraction guide radius, and guide material composition. A preliminary design of the UCN source at CSNS is presented based on this analysis. For a Be-coated converter, the predicted saturated UCN density is 315 UCN/cm^3, with a UCN production rate of 12,055 UCN/s and an extraction efficiency of 84%, yielding approximately 1.3 x 10^6 extracted UCNs per cycle in accumulation mode. The UCN source design presented in this study forms part of the overall physical design of the Neutron Physics and Application Spectrometer at CSNS, which successfully passed its physical design review on March 25, 2025.

title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A multiwavelength study of its 2026 giant X-ray outburst
abstract: Context. GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. Aims. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented with archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. Results.NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of ( − 5.1 ± 0.1)×10 −8 s s −1 during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3–79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K α emission line, with no evidence of a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirmed the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H α and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart was detected, with a 3 σ upper limit of 36 μJy beam −1 at 1.28 GHz. Conclusions. The observed pulse profile evolution, spectral variability, and reversal of the pulsed-fraction energy dependence suggest substantial changes in the accretion-column geometry during the outburst. Weaker H α emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit. Together, these results reveal a complex interplay between Be-disk evolution, outflows, and neutron-star accretion geometry in GS 1843+00.

title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
abstract: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $\gamma$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $\gamma$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $\gamma$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

title: Metaheuristic physics-informed extreme-learning machine for initial orbit determination of near-Earth asteroids from too-short arcs
abstract: Context . Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. Aims . We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. Methods . We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. Results . The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach. Conclusions . MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.

title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low-recycling scrape-off layer: a one dimensional gyrokinetic study
abstract: Abstract A liquid lithium boundary offers a possible route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless such that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length ( λ n ) estimates presented here, can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but more complete models are needed. We present a gyrokinetic simulations, with one configuration-space dimension and two velocity-space dimensions, of low and higher-recycling LTX- β SOL conditions using Gkeyll , an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line from the low-field-side midplane to the high-field-side limiter. Gkeyll is used to evolve kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, the electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses with experimentally constrained density and temperature at the low field side mid-plane. The low-recycling case develops a hotter SOL, a larger electrostatic potential variation along the field line, and a density response that is not recovered with an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure of the field equations. This indicates that kinetic-electron dynamics and the associated ambipolar potential are important for maintaining quasi-neutrality and reducing electron end loss from the field line in the low-recycling regime. Collisionality scans show that, as the ion neoclassical collisionality is reduced below unity, the ion distribution develops a stronger non-Maxwellian structure. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, especially for the low-recycling case, because ions become mirror trapped, and electron transport is suppressed by the ambipolar electrostatic potential to maintain quasi-neutrality. These results suggest that low-recycling lithium-wall operation in LTX- β accesses a SOL regime in which mirror trapping and electrostatic modification of electron transport alter the field-line residence time relative to conventional high-recycling fluid expectations. These SOL modifications are expected to become more pronounced in larger devices.

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract: Abstract Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.

title: Physics at the Edge: Benchmarking Quantisation Techniques and the Edge TPU for Neutrino Interaction Recognition
abstract: This work presents a benchmark of quantisation techniques for convolutional neural networks applied to neutrino interaction recognition, motivated by the need for low-power inference close to the detector in future liquid argon time-projection chamber (LArTPC) experiments. Using simulation of a generic LArTPC, four Keras models are trained to classify neutral-current, muon-neutrino charged-current and electron-neutrino charged-current interactions, quantised using post-training integer quantisation and quantisation-aware training, and deployed on the Google Coral Edge TPU. Latency and energy per event are compared with those of an Intel Core i7-13650HX CPU, a consumer NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU and a data-centre NVIDIA A100 GPU, using measured energy at different batch sizes and thread counts; the energy of the Edge TPU is estimated from its nominal power. The accuracy degradation is strongly model-dependent: InceptionV3 shows no significant loss along either pipeline, whereas the other models are substantially degraded. At batch size 1, the Edge TPU is comparable to or faster than the CPU and 1.3-6.5 times slower than the A100, while requiring 5--70 times less energy per event than the other devices; with batching, the GPUs reduce this gap to a factor of 2.6-7.2. The Edge TPU is also approximately four times cheaper than the consumer GPU and more than two orders of magnitude cheaper than the A100. Its low power per device eases deployment where power and cooling are constrained, with an additional benefit in terms of environmental impact. This paper explores possible future integrations of edge AI technologies with neutrino physics.

title: PeV Diffuse Neutrinos from Magnetically Arrested Disks in Low-luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei
abstract: Abstract Radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGNs) are promising candidates for the PeV astrophysical diffuse neutrino background (DNB), but how the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state affects their neutrino output and what fraction of LLAGNs are in this state remain unclear. We present a comprehensive study of diffuse neutrino emission from the inner accretion flows of LLAGNs in the MAD state, including all three flavors and both hadronuclear ( pp ) and photohadronic ( pγ ) production channels. Assuming that ∼5% of the accretion power is transferred to nonthermal protons, current IceCube data allow at most 2.3 × 10 −3 of LLAGNs to have their inner accretion flows in an MAD state that can produce high-energy neutrinos. A lower fraction of the accretion power transferred to nonthermal protons would allow a proportionally larger fraction of such LLAGNs. Assuming that the comoving number density of low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) approximately matches that of LLAGNs in the MAD state, we also estimate an MAD fraction of ≃1.6 × 10 −3 . The corresponding diffuse intensity is compatible with current IceCube data and testable by IceCube-Gen2. For this MAD fraction, the all-flavor diffuse intensity peaks at E ν ≃ 1.5 PeV, with E ν 2 Φ ν ≃ 2.6 × 1 0 − 9 GeV cm − 2 s − 1 sr − 1 . Current IceCube data are beginning to challenge several predictions from previous LLAGN RIAF models, and the MAD component can become the dominant contribution from LLAGN accretion flows beyond the cutoffs of most earlier RIAF spectra considered here.

title: Operation and performance of ProtoDUNE Dual Phase liquid argon time projection chamber
abstract: ProtoDUNE-DP, with a total mass of the active volume of 300 t, is the largest Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC) built to operate in a Dual-Phase (DP) mode where the ionisation charge produced in the liquid bulk by charged particles traversing the detector is transferred for the readout in the gaseous phase above. Intended as a prototype of a far detector module for the DUNE neutrino oscillation experiment, ProtoDUNE-DP was operated at the CERN Neutrino Platform from 2019 to 2022. This paper describes various ProtoDUNE-DP detector components, discusses the commissioning and operation experiences, and presents the results on the detector performance from an analysis of collected cosmic ray data. Some key deliverables of the detector were achieved, including stable delivery of 300 kV to the TPC cathode, operation of the charge readout with an effective gain exceeding 5 before charging-up, stable functioning of the photon detection system with a relative time accuracy among PMTs below 16 ns. The long term operation of the charge readout system in dual-phase, however, was limited by the liquid surface and electrical instabilities. The ProtoDUNE-DP experience contributed to the final design of the DUNE Vertical Drift LArTPC.

title: Machine learning methods for subpixel trajectory reconstruction in discretized position detectors
abstract: We evaluate machine-learning methods for sub-pixel position and trajectory-angle reconstruction in scintillator detectors. Geant4 simulations use two $50 \times 50$ cm plastic-scintillator planes separated by 30 cm, each represented by an $8 \times 8$ grid of 64 touching computational cells of pitch 6.25 cm. The plates are optically continuous. Photons reaching any outer face are absorbed and scored once in the pre-step cell. We sum the collected photon energies in each cell and normalize the signals to the plane total. Photodetectors and electronics are not simulated. We compare a transformer, a convolutional neural network (CNN), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), and an energy-weighted centroid. We compute directions from the two reconstructed positions. On a common 19,053-event test set, transformer and CNN median position errors (per-event means of the two planes' radial errors) are 0.18 and 0.23 cm, or 2.9% and 3.6% of the cell width. Their median space-angle errors are $0.35^\circ$ and $0.52^\circ$, compared with 1.03 cm and $1.90^\circ$ for the centroid and $4.21^\circ$ for an idealized Monte Carlo reference retaining only the traversed cell. The transformer has the lowest median errors, whereas the CNN has the lowest position- and angular-RMSE point estimates. Large-error tails limit the RMSE gains. Learned methods recover sub-pixel information in this idealized response. Establishing gains for muon tomography requires realistic optical coupling, photodetector response, and electronics.

title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
abstract: AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.

title: Development of a Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence System Based on Scintillating Crystals Read Out with Kinetic Inductance Detectors for BULLKID-DM
abstract: The BULLKID-DM experiment has been proposed to search for WIMP-like dark matter particles with a mass of 1 GeV or lower and with a WIMP-nucleon interaction cross section down to $10^{-43}$ cm$^2$. To achieve this goal, the experiment utilizes a detector consisting of a stack of 16 silicon wafers instrumented with phonon-mediated superconducting Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs), to be operated at the underground facility of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), Italy. To reduce the residual background arising from $\gamma$-rays, neutrons, and muons, a cryogenic active anti-coincidence system (veto) operating at mK temperature, surrounding the main detector, is under development. The veto detector consists of segmented scintillating crystals read out by phonon-mediated KID light detectors. Current status and future developments of the veto system are presented. In particular, we focus on cryogenic tests of both bismuth germanate (BGO) and gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) crystals, which had been previously chosen as veto candidate crystals according to our preliminary studies on the dependence of their optical properties (i.e. light yield and scintillation decay time) on temperature. We finally present the operation and preliminary tests of a two-module veto prototype with multiplexed readout.

title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
abstract: We develop a scattering-order-resolved Stokes-vector recursion for axisymmetric polarized transport in a finite plane-parallel Thomson slab. The post-scattering radiation field closes exactly within two depth-dependent coefficients, yielding escape probabilities, angular distributions and linear polarization while conserving photon number. At high scattering orders, the principal eigenmode of the weighted self-adjoint transport operator controls the escape statistics, and the normalized angular distribution and polarization become independent of the seed source. The subdominant spectrum quantifies convergence, with the characteristic scattering order scaling as the square of the optical depth in thick slabs. We derive logarithmic corrections to the thin-slab complete-polarization limit away from the slab normal, together with a finite-optical-depth Galerkin approximation. In optically thick slabs, matching bulk diffusion to a polarized Milne surface layer yields finite-thickness corrections to the Chandrasekhar solution. We provide compact formulae for the principal and leading subdominant eigenvalues and the asymptotic angular and polarization distributions across both regimes. Combining the recursion with an angle-averaged thermal-Compton redistribution kernel gives approximate energy-resolved Stokes spectra. Comparisons with full polarized Compton calculations show that this separable reconstruction is most reliable for cool, optically thick media. Applied to the non-dipping observations of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary system 4U 1624-49, the model provides acceptable joint fits to the broadband intensity and IXPE Stokes spectra, showing that an extended corona overlying the accretion disc can account for the observed X-ray polarization.

title: Bayesian neural network with autoencoder for model-based description of α -particle preformation factor
The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
abstract: We report on a readout upgrade of Gator, a low-background high-purity germanium spectrometer operated at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso for material radioassay. The upgraded data acquisition records digitised waveforms, enabling noise rejection on an event-level basis, and offline energy reconstruction. Measurements before and after the upgrade show an improved energy resolution of 17% at the 2614.5 keV line of 208-Tl, with (2.14 +- 0.22) keV at FWHM, and suppression of electronic noise in the low-energy region. We assess the resulting sensitivity for a specified sample geometry, and present a new background measurement. The background rate in the (100-2700) keV range is (86.6 +- 0.5) counts/(kg day). We also show the radioassay results of sixteen Hamamatsu R17317 3-inch photomultiplier tubes with an improved stem design, which reduces the activities from the primordial 238-U and 232-Th chains by a factor of three, making them suitable candidate photosensors for the XLZD experiment.

title: Subpicosecond Optical Time Transfer under Simulated Motion with Electro-Optic Frequency Combs
abstract: Extension of high performance optical frequency comb-based time transfer to real-world systems is challenged by platform motion, particularly for large relative velocities. Here, we utilize agile electro-optic frequency combs to construct a laboratory-based simulator of a two-way optical time transfer system under motion. Through direct control of the electro-optic frequency comb parameters, we can artificially induce the effects of relative motion. We performed tests of the time transfer performance across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles that linearly increase from rest up to 400 m/s. Through a post-processed data analysis, we demonstrate continuous tracking of the clock offset between sites with subpicosecond precision throughout the velocity sweep. These results illustrate the versatility of using electro-optic frequency combs for optical time transfer in deployed systems.

title: SimpleClock: a satellite-disciplined oscillator for astronomical instrumentation
abstract: SimpleClock is a low-cost, high-stability timing reference designed for astronomical experiments that combines a global navigation satellite system (GNSS) timing receiver, a digitally tunable 10 MHz microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) oven-controlled oscillator, external thermal regulation and autonomous control. It provides 10 MHz and pulse-per-second references at an estimated prototype hardware cost of US\$500. Independently enabled frequency and phase feedback support precise point positioning (PPP) with Galileo's High Accuracy Service (HAS), satellite-based augmentation system (SBAS) solutions and standalone operation. Three-unit phase comparisons separate component noise and characterize disciplined-output stability over 200\,000 s recordings. Across five configurations, each analysed over 200\,000 s, equivalent single-unit differential Allan deviation and time deviation at 1000 s span $3.5\times10^{-13}$--$1.0\times10^{-12}$ and 115--447 ps, respectively. The maximum equivalent time deviation over averaging times from 1 to 50\,000 s spans 143--1090 ps. These results support applications in astronomical timing, including low-frequency very long baseline interferometry (VLBI).

title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. This parameterization serves as input to a parametric pixel simulation, which has been developed for chip design optimization and system-level studies. The simulation results are validated with test beam data.

title: Primordial quark stars made of a long-lived false vacuum
Multi-Angle Beam Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy for Diffraction-Contrast-Free Magnetic Imaging
abstract: Recent development of the differential phase contrast (DPC) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) technique has significantly advanced materials science supported by high-sensitivity detectors and powerful data processing. Especially the 4D-STEM technique, employing a pixelated camera as a STEM detector, enables extensive information acquisition through post-processing of large datasets. However, magnetic or electric field imaging using DPC is often disturbed by diffraction contrasts intrinsic to the crystalline material. In this paper, we demonstrate elimination of the diffraction contrasts for magnetic field imaging by using angularly distributed multiple electron beams generated by a multi-hole aperture within the 4D-STEM framework. This multi-angle beam configuration suppresses irrelevant crystalline contrast and yields direct magnetic information with high sensitivity from the specimen. The resulting 4D-STEM datasets also enable additional analysis of sub-beam size magnetic domain structures, domain walls, and diffraction-related information.

title: Imaging performance of a Single-Plane Readout Compton Camera
abstract: This work presents the design, development, and characterization of a compact Compton camera employing a novel single-plane readout architecture. The proposed concept simplifies conventional multilayer Compton cameras by optically coupling the scatterer and absorber into a single compact detector element using a light guide, enabling readout exclusively from one side with silicon photomultipliers. The system was validated through Monte Carlo simulations, prototype construction, and experimental characterization using standard gamma-ray sources. Detector performance for 511~keV and 662~keV photons was optimized using simulations based on the Geant4 framework, by guiding event selection strategy. Event reconstruction relied on coincidence detection consistent with Compton scattering kinematics, while image reconstruction was performed using maximum likelihood expectation maximization algorithm. The prototype comprises 64 detector elements arranged in an $8\times8$ matrix, read out by an $8\times8$ silicon photomultiplier array. Each element consists of two GAGG:Ce scintillators coupled by a 20 mm long light guide. Measured energy resolutions were $8.9\%\pm1.9\%$ and $10.8\%\pm1.6\%$ for the front and back layers, respectively. Successful gamma-ray imaging was demonstrated for Na-22 and Cs-137 sources, achieving angular resolutions of $12.4^\circ$--$14.3^\circ$ at 511~keV and $14.3^\circ$--$16.8^\circ$ at 662~keV, confirming the feasibility of the proposed single-plane architecture for compact and cost-effective gamma-ray imaging applications.
