title: Establishing Standards for Assessment and Reporting of SNSPD Performance
abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) can be made sensitive to single photons with near-unity detection efficiency, ultra-low dark-count rates, and sub-nanosecond timing jitter over a broad wavelength range. However, many studies report data inconsistently, often emphasizing a single performance metric without considering overall device performance. This inconsistent data reporting limits the field, as it makes it difficult to determine which device characteristics are most important. Different applications require functionalities that may conflict with one another; for example, longer-wavelength operation may require lower operating temperatures. Moreover, there is no universally accepted metric for defining the figures of merit of an SNSPD. In this work, we amass a dataset representing the state of the art of SNSPD fabrication, including operating temperature, operating wavelength, photon count rates (PCR), and dark count rates (DCR). We fit the PCR curves and suggest using the saturation plateau length to gauge the SNSPD's sensitivity. We then fit the DCR and compare the PCR and DCR. Using this approach, we establish a quantitative framework to determine the optimal biasing condition for a given device and to determine the device's sensitivity at that optimal biasing condition, enabling meaningful comparisons across disparate devices. Additionally, we offer concrete benchmarks for measuring device performance.

title: Development and characterization of monolithic sensors with internal gain in a 110 nm CMOS process
abstract: This paper presents the optimization and characterization of a Monolithic Active Pixel Sensor with internal gain implemented in the 110 nm CMOS process from LFoundry. This work, carried out within the framework of the latest ARCADIA production run, reports on the characterization of sensors with an optimized gain layer. Improvements over earlier prototypes, including substrate current reduction via guard-ring connection, are briefly discussed. Both laboratory and in-beam measurements are presented. Using soft X-rays from a 55Fe source, both the pixel response and the noise performance are analyzed. In addition, laser measurements demonstrate an electronic jitter ranging from 20 to 40 ps for a signal amplitude corresponding to one minimum ionizing particle (MIP). Finally, the results from several test beam campaigns are described, showing the signal amplitude, gain and time resolution of sensors with different doping profiles of the gain layer evaluated with MIPs. A time resolution of about 78 ps was measured in the optimal condition of bias voltage and electronics configuration. The results demonstrate that monolithic CMOS sensors with internal gain can achieve promising timing performance at ambient temperature, highlighting their strong potential for next-generation precision timing applications.

title: Development and Experimental Characterization of a Compact $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O Photoneutron Source for Low-Energy Nuclear Recoil Calibration
abstract: Calibrating the few-keV nuclear-recoil response of liquid xenon detectors calls for a low-energy neutron source. We have developed and characterized a $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O photoneutron source that converts the 2.615~MeV $\gamma$ rays from $^{208}$Tl into sub-MeV neutrons through the D($\gamma$,n)p reaction. After optimizing the D$_2$O geometry to balance neutron production against escape efficiency, we validated the chosen configuration experimentally. The forward emission rate is $1734 \pm 76~(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 65~(\mathrm{sys.})~\mathrm{h}^{-1}$, and the spectrum unfolded from Bonner sphere data is concentrated at $0.17$--$0.22~\mathrm{MeV}$. In a 220~h exposure of PandaX-20T, the same configuration should provide about 1000 selected nuclear-recoil events. These results support the use of a long-lived $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O source for low-energy neutron calibration of large liquid xenon detectors.

title: Crest factor optimization of multi-tone signals generated for low-temperature sensor readout
abstract: Microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID) are a growing technology of cryogenic detectors and have a great potential in radio-astronomy and cosmic microwave background (CMB) characterization. A review of the general readout performance requirements for experiments requiring the multiplexing of large arrays (~10.000 pixels) of such cryogenic detectors is presented. The focus is on the crest factor optimization process for proper excitation and readout of these large arrays of detectors. It is shown an algorithm to optimize the phase generation of the carriers to obtain a low crest factor, favoring the dynamic range usage of the electronic chain.

title: Characterization of a Large-Area HRPPD MCP-PMT Coupled to LYSO for TOF-PET
abstract: Large-area microchannel-plate photomultipliers (MCP-PMTs) such as the High-Rate Picosecond Photon Detector (HRPPD) are attractive for time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET). They offer excellent single-photon time resolution, low dark count rate, and large monolithic active areas. However, the coincidence time resolution (CTR) reported so far with PET scintillators falls short of expectations based upon their single-photon time resolution. We characterized a 104x104 mm$^2$ HRPPD coupled to LYSO crystals and read out through a custom high-frequency amplifier. With a 2x2x3 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal we measured a CTR of 107 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) against a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM)-based reference detector. After subtracting the calibrated reference detector's contribution of 42 ps, the single HRPPD detector was found to contribute 98 ps, corresponding to 139 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors in coincidence. With clinical 3x3x20 mm$^3$ crystals the CTR against the reference SiPM detector was 160 ps, corresponding to 218 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors. Timing and gain were uniform across output pads within measurement precision. Summing the four pads under a 3x3x10 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal, the energy resolution for 511 keV gamma ray was 14.6% FWHM, and the 1275 keV line of the $^{22}$Na source was within 1% of its proportional position relative to the 511 keV peak. Flood maps resolved the individual 3 mm elements of a 4x4 array despite the 25 mm pad pitch. To the best of our knowledge the observed timing resolution improves substantially on what has been reported for large-area MCP-PMTs coupled to PET scintillators, and the crystal array identification has not been demonstrated before on such a device. These results indicate that this device class deserves renewed consideration as a photodetector technology for high-performance TOF-PET systems.

title: Adaptive carrier signal synthesis for frequency-division multiplexed cryogenic detector readout
abstract: Frequency-domain multiplexing is a fundamental technology for readout of cryogenic detector arrays on a single transmission line. Synthesizing a large number of static carrier tones for resonator stimulation eventually drives the cryogenic low-noise amplifier beyond its P1dB, introducing detector signal distortion. Scaling array sizes to O(10^6) detector pixels therefore demands minimizing the total power on the transmission line by continuous tracking of the resonances, which requires the readout electronics to be capable of updating the carrier tones dynamically. This work presents an scalable FPGA-based implementation for carrier signal synthesis based on a numerically controlled oscillator and a polyphase filter bank, enabling real-time frequency adaptivity as well as frequency resolution of 4 mHz to precisely tune the operating point, while simultaneously reducing resource usage compared to the current memory-based implementation.

title: $N\Omega$ Dibaryon near Unitarity from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
abstract: The $N\Omega$ system is a promising dibaryon candidate because its constituents share no valence quarks and therefore avoid valence-quark Pauli repulsion. We determine the $^{5}S_{2}$ $N\Omega$ interaction in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD at physical quark masses ($m_\pi\simeq137~\text{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method. The interaction is attractive over the resolved range and supports a shallow state near unitarity. A direct $T$-matrix pole analysis gives $B_{n\Omega} = 0.61\,(^{+0.41}_{-0.30})\,(^{+0.60}_{-0.18})~\text{MeV}$; including finite-charge-size Coulomb attraction yields $B_{p\Omega} = 1.25\,(^{+0.46}_{-0.39})\,(^{+0.69}_{-0.25})~\text{MeV}$. These results provide a first-principles benchmark for future $N\Omega$ femtoscopy and dibaryon searches.

title: Analytical spectral framework for efficient and accurate space-charge field calculations in particle beams with arbitrary charge and energy distributions
A JWST redshift for the host galaxy of EP250207b of z = 3.2: a collapsar origin is viable
abstract: Abstract We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations of the field of the fast X-ray transient (FXT) detected by Einstein Probe, EP250207b, to resolve any ambiguity about the host galaxy and redshift of the FXT. EP250207b was originally associated with a nearby galaxy at z = 0.082, based on its low chance alignment probability, and a binary neutron star merger origin was proposed. However, we report the detection of a background galaxy at z = 3.2 at the location of EP250207b. Assuming this galaxy is the actual host galaxy, the rest-frame energetics and timescales of the event change. Furthermore, the available data are not able to rule out the presence of a supernova associated with EP250207b if at this redshift. We model the X-ray, optical, near-infrared and radio light curves using a tophat jet model implemented in Redback and find that they are consistent with an on-axis gamma ray burst afterglow. The energetics and host galaxy properties do not allow us to distinguish between a collapsar and a merger driven event.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
abstract: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.

title: $^{56}$Ni production in long-lived binary neutron star merger remnants
abstract: We investigate the nucleosynthesis and kilonova emission based on numerical-relativity binary neutron star merger simulations that incorporate a two-moment neutrino-transport scheme. Unlike in previous works with simpler neutrino treatments, a massive, fast (up to $v=0.3c$), proton-rich neutrino-driven wind develops in the postmerger phase of the simulations as long as the merger remnant does not collapse to a black hole. We evolve the ejecta for 100 days after the merger using 2D ray-by-ray radiation-hydrodynamics simulations coupled in situ to a complete nuclear network. The most abundant nucleosynthesis products are He, $^{56}$Ni, and $^{56}$Co. We find a total yield of $\sim 10^{-3} M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni for all mergers that produce massive neutron star remnants, independently of the mass ratio and equations of state. After a few days, the decay of $^{56}$Ni and later $^{56}$Co becomes the primary source of heating in the matter expanding above the remnant. As a result, the kilonova light curve flattens on timescales of days for polar observation angles. This is an important effect that should be included in future models of kilonova light curves. Furthermore, the observation of a $^{56}$Ni-$^{56}$Co feature could serve as a clear indicator for the presence of a long-lived neutron star remnant in future kilonova observations.

title: Probing gluon saturation with forward heavy-flavor correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
abstract: We investigate heavy-flavor azimuthal correlations as probes of gluon saturation in high-energy $p$+$p$ and $p$+Pb collisions within the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. Heavy flavor has several advantages: heavy-quark production is especially sensitive to the small-$x$ gluon distribution of the target, while the quark mass suppresses collinear radiation. Further, the heavy meson carries a large fraction of the momentum of its parent quark, so that the meson pair follows the partonic kinematics more closely than for light hadrons. We present the first calculation of heavy-meson pair correlations over the full azimuthal range that combines small-$x$ evolution from an initial condition constrained by HERA data with Sudakov resummation near the back-to-back limit. It provides a good description of the $D$-$\bar D$ and $b$-hadron pair correlations measured by LHCb. In contrast to the light-flavor case, we predict, in addition to a suppression of the away-side yield in $p$+Pb relative to $p$+$p$ collisions by about $15\%$, a broadening of the peak by approximately $10\%$ to $25\%$ for Gaussian fits near $\Delta\Phi=\pi$, which makes heavy-flavor correlations a promising observable in the search for gluon saturation.

title: Multi-approach Standard Model Effective Field Theory analyses of top-quark associated production in leptonic final states at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
abstract: Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) interpretations of measurements of top-quark associated production processes in leptonic final states are presented using the full Run 2 proton-proton collision dataset recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. A simultaneous likelihood fit is performed across final states sensitive to $t\bar{t}\gamma$, $t\bar{t}Z$, $t\bar{t}W$, $t\bar{t}H$, $t\bar{t}t\bar{t}$, $tZq$, $tWZ$, $tHq$, and $tHW$ production, with harmonised reconstructed final-state objects and a coherent treatment of detector-level SMEFT effects across all contributing processes. Two complementary analysis strategies are investigated: an approach employing a more generic event categorisation based on counting reconstructed objects, and a more complex approach combining orthogonal regions optimised to specifically identify individual processes, as employed by previous dedicated measurements. Constraints are obtained on the Wilson coefficients of dimension-six SMEFT operators affecting top-quark interactions, including top-boson, four-quark and top-lepton operators, together with complex operator contributions. The results do not show a significant deviation from the Standard Model expectation and 95% confidence interval limits are placed in a simultaneous fit to 33 SMEFT Wilson coefficients. The comparison of the two analysis strategies provides new insight into the design of increasingly complex SMEFT interpretations. The second, more complex, approach targeting individual processes results in the best sensitivity to the majority of Wilson coefficients.

title: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
abstract: It is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. We show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. Using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

title: Single-spike superradiant free-electron lasers
abstract: Free-electron lasers (FELs) deliver high-brilliance radiation from the infrared to X-rays, enabling atomic-scale studies on femtosecond-to-attosecond timescales. Yet conventional facilities rely on large, costly radio-frequency accelerators. Laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs), combining high accelerating gradients with ultra-high peak currents, offer a compact alternative and open up new prospects for advanced FEL operation. Here, we demonstrate a tabletop superradiant FEL driven by single-spike, pre-bunched electron beams from a LWFA. By manipulating the energy chirp during acceleration and compressing the bunch to sub-wavelength duration, we obtain coherent radiation extending into the vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) regime within a remarkably compact 3-metre beamline--from gas target to radiator. Under optimized conditions, the measured photon yield reaches 2.8x10^10 per pulse after transmission through a 500-um slit, with a reproducibility of approximately 70%. This approach uniquely exploits the energy chirp and high-current characteristics inherent to LWFA beams without recourse to exponential gain, substantially minimizing device length while obviating the need for external synchronization and offering enhanced tolerance to jitter--thereby establishing a practical route toward efficient, compact FELs suitable for applications in academic, industrial, and clinical settings.

title: Particle species dependence of femtoscopic source parameters in high-energy nuclear collisions
abstract: High-energy nuclear physics explores the properties of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic collisions of nuclei. Femtoscopy, a subfield of high-energy physics, utilizes quantum-statistical correlations of particles to characterize the space-time geometry of the particle-emitting source. Recent measurements and phenomenological investigations indicated that the shape of the source for identical pions can be well-described by L\'evy-stable distributions. The significant power-law tail of the pion source observed both in experiment and in simulations has been shown to originate from the process of L\'evy walk during the hadronic scattering phase of the collisions. To better understand the physical processes behind the formation of such power laws, an important next step is to investigate particle species dependence, especially the source shape of identical kaon and proton pairs. As a direct continuation of our previous studies, in this Letter, we present a detailed three-dimensional investigation of the two-particle source shape in simulations of Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV per nucleon pair collision energy using the EPOS3 model. We show the dependence of the extracted femtoscopic source parameters on particle species, centrality and average transverse mass. We find that the scale parameters do not show a clear transverse mass scaling between particle species, as there are systematic differences in the overlapping regions. The power-law exponents of pion and kaon pairs are compatible, while for protons it is higher, closer to the Gaussian limit. When new experimental measurements of kaon and proton correlations become available, these results will provide the basis of a data-model comparison.

title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
abstract: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted. We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained. We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0. Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

title: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
abstract: Short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs) are believed to originate from compact binary mergers, particularly binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, providing a probe of jet energetics and merger remnants. We compile broadband afterglow observations of 40 sGRBs and perform forward-shock modeling with off-axis Gaussian jets, excluding data potentially affected by additional energy injection. We derive distributions of beaming-corrected jet kinetic energy $E_k$ and radiative efficiency $\eta_\gamma$, and combine these with binary population synthesis and numerical simulations to infer remnant black hole (BH) magnetic fields assuming the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) jet-launching mechanism. For the 15 strictly constrained bursts, we find a median $E_k\simeq3.8\times10^{49}$ erg and $\eta_\gamma\simeq0.35$, with respective 68% intervals of $[5.1\times10^{48},1.9\times10^{50}]$ erg and [0.09, 0.79]. The inferred magnetic field supplied by the accretion disk and threading the BH horizon is approximately $7\times10^{15}$ G, with a 68% credible interval of $[2.3\times10^{15},2.4\times10^{16}]$ G, depending slightly on the neutron star equation of state. The full sample yields a higher median field of approximately $2\times10^{16}$ G, with the high-energy and high-field tails predominantly contributed by less well-constrained bursts. These results provide statistical constraints on sGRB jet energetics and suggest characteristic BH magnetic fields of order $10^{16}$ G. Comparison with pre-merger neutron star magnetic fields indicates a characteristic amplification factor of $\eta_B\sim10^3$, providing an observational constraint on magnetic field amplification during BNS mergers and subsequent BH formation.

title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

title: Evidence for MeV Radiation from a Large-Amplitude Crystalline Undulator
abstract: We report evidence for MeV radiation from a large-amplitude crystalline undulator in which 35 GeV/c positrons channel along periodically bent Si(110) planes. Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors produce ten periods with $\lambda_u = 334~\mu$m and midplane amplitude $A_u \simeq 1.85$ nm (XRD-validated modeling). Under planar alignment, the energy-loss spectrum shows an excess over the misaligned case peaking at $6.8 \pm 0.3$ MeV ($4.05\sigma$), in agreement with simulations and the 7.2 MeV analytical estimate. Simulations for 20 GeV FCC-ee injector positrons predict a peak brilliance of $1.8\times10^{21}$ photons/(s mm$^2$ mrad$^2$ 0.1% BW).

title: Comparison of the Neutron Star Birth Function from Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations with Observations
abstract: Using the mapping between progenitor core structure and the gravitational mass of neutron stars derived from sophisticated 3D supernova simulations, we construct the theoretical mass distribution of neutron stars at birth and investigate how it might comport with neutron star mass function measurements. In the process, we explore the effects of islands of black hole formation and subsequent mass accretion. We show that supernova theory can explain the observed neutron star mass function from its lower-mass peak near $\sim$1.35 $M_{\odot}$ to its higher-mass tail. Moreover, we suggest, but do not prove, that the lower predicted kick speeds expected during the birth of lower-mass neutron stars and the higher expected kick speeds expected on average for higher mass neutron stars may together sculpt the observed mass function in desired directions. The upshot of all these influences is to imprint upon the measured neutron star mass function features that reflect the varied physics of both neutron star origins and the neutron-star/black-hole dichotomy. Very approximately, we derive a black hole birth fraction of $\sim$19.6\%. In summary, we suggest that supernova theory can now be used to explain, however provisionally, various measured attributes of the population of compact objects and that an era of productive engagement between supernova theory and observation is at hand.

title: Benchmarking the expected performance of Bayesian parameter inference on Kilonovae
abstract: In the study of optical transients, parameter inference is a part of the process of extracting physical information, i.e. constraints on the source's characteristics, by comparing the observed lightcurves to the predictions of different astrophysical models and finding the model and parameter combination that make the closest match. In the developing field of the study of kilonovae (KNe), systematic uncertainties in modeling are still very large. Current-day models still struggle to fit adequately the whole multi-wavelength dataset of the AT2017gfo kilonova, associated to the Binary Neutron Star (BNS) merger GW170817, and thus obtain wide posterior distributions on the inferred source parameters. After reviewing the many sources of uncertainty embedded in KN analyses and the process of Bayesian parameter inference, we discuss how to quantify the performance of parameter inference analyses using metrics on information gain from prior to posterior. We highlight the systematic error margin hyperparameter $\sigma_{\rm sys}$, which correlates to a model's goodness-of-fit, and exhibit its major influence on Bayesian inference performance metrics. Using the example of two KN models from the literature with the Nuclear Multi-Messenger Astronomy (NMMA) Bayesian inference framework, we simulate the expected information gains that dedicated KN follow-ups with telescope networks could reasonably reach, for various observational cadences and error margins: we show that the wind ejecta's mass and electron fraction are the easiest KN parameters to constrain. We finally apply our KN analysis to the dataset of AT2017gfo to show that our information gain predictions match results on real data and discuss the complementarity of multi-messenger approaches.

title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
abstract: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $\tau-\tau_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $\tau-\tau_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.

title: Disentangling the Effects of Phase-Specific Transport Properties on Elliptic Flow Centrality Dependence in the AMPT Model
abstract: The centrality dependence of charged hadron elliptic flow $v_{2}$ in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200~\rm{GeV}$ is studied using the AMPT model with phase-specific control of partonic and hadronic transport properties. By separately varying the shear viscosity $\eta/s$, phase transition temperature $T_{tr}$, and hadronic scattering cross sections, we isolate their distinct effects on anisotropic flow. Hadronic rescattering is found to contribute increasingly to $v_{2}$ with centrality, with the contribution becoming dominant in peripheral collisions. Scaling up hadronic cross sections by a factor of four substantially amplifies $v_{2}$ in peripheral collisions and improves agreement with STAR data, suggesting that the flattening of $v_{2}$ at high centrality may reflect a larger effective hadronic cross section and highlighting the significant role of the hadronic phase in small systems.

title: Accelerating exact solutions of relativistic hydrodynamics and Levy-shaped freeze-out sources
abstract: Femtoscopic measurements in heavy-ion collisions indicate that the pion source is L\'evy-stable rather than Gaussian, while the source radii still follow the hydrodynamic scaling $R^2\propto 1/m_T$. We call this coexistence the L\'evy hydro puzzle. For a perfect fluid with $\varepsilon=\kappa p$ and $p=nT$, flow and pressure form a closed system, and density and temperature can be ``dressed'' by an arbitrary comoving function, generalising a freedom known from Hubble-type solutions to arbitrary flows. We show that, at nonzero pair momentum, the source is bounded by the pressure on the freeze-out hypersurface, so its tail can never be heavier than the pressure tail. This yields a criterion for power-law source tails with two routes: either the outer flow is ultra-relativistic and the temperature grows at least linearly (Hubble-type solutions), or the flow is slow, the temperature uniform, and the proper acceleration falls off as $1/r$. We present a new family of relativistic, accelerating, self-similar potential flows ($\lambda$-PF) and a new dressing of Gubser's flow. The acceleration of $\lambda$-PF generates no power-law tail, but with a Hubble-type dressing its source tail is L\'evy-stable in a range of parameters, generalising the Hubble-type L\'evy source to accelerating cores. The isothermally dressed Gubser flow realises the $1/r$ route: its tail exponent lies outside the L\'evy-stable range, but over the measured range it gives L\'evy-like sources with $1/R^2$ linear in $m_T$. Thus L\'evy-like sources and the hydrodynamic $m_T$ scaling are compatible in perfect-fluid hydrodynamics, but hydrodynamics does not create the power-law tail: it is either inherited from a power-law pressure, requiring a $1/r$ acceleration, or put in through the dressing. We outline extensions towards non-spherical geometries and elliptic flow.

title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

title: What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors
abstract: We discuss constraints that the X-ray emission from supernovae can place on their progenitor stars. Since almost all X-ray supernovae arise from massive stars, we concentrate on implications for massive stars. These stars lose mass throughout their lifetime in the form of stellar winds. X-ray emission can be used to gauge the wind properties, especially the mass-loss rates, via various techniques. The abundance of various elements formed by nucleosynthesis within the stars, and released in the stellar explosion, can be estimated from X-ray spectra. In many cases, a combination of X-ray light curves and spectra can allow us to extricate the structure and morphology of the surrounding medium formed by pre-supernova mass loss into which the SN shock is expanding.

title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

title: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
abstract: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $\omega$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(\rho)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $\Theta = dI/d\omega = \widetilde{\Theta}/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tilde{\Theta}$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $\Theta$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation. The adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.

title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
abstract: Natal kicks - kinematic impulses to neutron stars and black holes at birth - play a decisive role in the end-stage evolution of binaries hosting massive stars, in determining the global phase-space properties of compact objects, and in setting expected merger-rates detectable through gravitational-wave observations. Inferring the kick ($v_{\rm NK}$) for individual systems requires well constrained binary system properties and centre-of-mass kinematics, which must then be modelled to constrain likely system characteristics at supernova. As a result, population-wide studies of kicks remain few and far between. Here, we model plausible evolutionary histories for 68 accreting binaries, encompassing almost all black-hole and neutron-star X-ray binaries with 3D kinematics measurements, constraining allowed $v_{\rm NK}$ distributions for each source using a simulation framework presented in our previous paper. The resultant $v_{\rm NK}$ distribution for the sample can be simply represented by a broad Gamma distribution with mean $v_{\rm NK}$ = $128^{+17}_{-15}$ km s$^{-1}$ and scatter $\sigma$ = 117 km s$^{-1}$. Intriguingly, the distributions for black-hole vs. neutron-star systems are found to be formally indistinguishable. Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s$^{-1}$). There is a hint, but no statistically significant evidence at present, for $v_{\rm NK}$ scaling inversely with black-hole mass. Our work suggests either that similar physics drives kicks and shows evidence for effects beyond simplistic fallback-moderated scaling for black holes, or that selection effects conspire to erase differences between remnant types in current accreting-binary samples. Larger samples are needed to provide robust discriminatory tests between these possibilities.

title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
abstract: In a neutron star low-mass X-ray binary, heavy elements (with mass number ~100) are believed to be synthesized through the rapid-proton (rp) capture process, as indirectly indicated by the long tail of X-ray burst light curves. Although direct evidence for the rp-process was lacking so far, we reported in our previous study that an unidentified hump is present at ~30 keV of the Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 in its hard state. The feature was tentatively identified with a recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized ions of cadmium or indium, which are possibly produced by the rp process during X-ray bursts and lifted up into the neutron-star atmosphere. To reinforce this scenario, we quantitatively evaluated the physical conditions of the assumed emitting region in the atmosphere, and confirmed that the scenario is possible when the putative rp-process ashes in the atmosphere has ~10^7 times higher abundances than their solar values. The results are compared with theoretical model calculations for the nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts. We suggest that the observed spectral hump is a radiative recombination feature from the stable isotope 106Cd, produced in X-ray bursts via the rp-process. Further issues about the detectability are briefly discussed.

title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
abstract: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX~J1808.4--3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst \citep{2023ApJ...948..117C}, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5\% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14\% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25\% to 41\% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

title: Interaction between geodesic acoustic modes andresonantmagnetic perturbations in fusion plasmas
Tau polarization, new physics and CP violation in $\nu_\tau$-nucleus hyperon production
abstract:
Charged-current interactions of the $	au$ neutrino are the least constrained sector of the Standard Model (SM) flavour structure, and the polarisation of the produced $	au$ lepton probes new-physics (NP) couplings, including CP-violating ones. Hyperon and charmed-baryon production gives access to the $u	o s$ and $d	o c$ transitions, but any measurement would be made on nuclei, which calls for a proper treatment of nuclear effects. We therefore study the sequential reactions $
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^-(	o\pi^-
u_	au)\,\Lambda_c^+ X$ and $ ar
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^+ (	o\pi^+ ar
u_	au)\,\Lambda X$ within the impulse approximation. The energy and angular distributions of the pion, which encode the $	au$ polarization, are derived for an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function. As for free nucleons, an azimuthal pion asymmetry with respect to the plane spanned by the neutrino and the outgoing baryon is shown to remain. This is a CP-odd observable that vanishes in the SM, so that a nonzero value would signal CP violation irrespective of the hadronic form factors. Local Fermi gas results for ${}^{16}$O show that nuclear effects lower the reaction thresholds but leave the pion distributions, and hence the polarization information, close to their free-nucleon form. For representative NP scenarios the predicted asymmetries are at the percent level or below, with a magnitude that, in the $\Lambda$ channel, depends strongly on the transition form factors.

title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
abstract: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_\mu$ and $L_e-L_\tau$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.

title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
abstract: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N$_2$H$^+$ and C$^{17}$O in this disk. The C$^{17}$O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N$_2$H$^+$, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of $\sim 3.4$ from $0.039^{+0.067}_{-0.018}$ M$_{\odot}$ to $0.011^{+0.011}_{-0.006}$ M$_{\odot}$ if the C$^{17}$O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of $(4.8^{+4.3}_{-2.7} - 17^{+8}_{-8}) \times 10^{-6}$ relative to H$_2$ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N$_2$H$^+$ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.

title: Magnetically Deformed Neutron Stars and Gravitational Waves
abstract: We study the geometric figures of neutron stars and magnetars with spin periods from milliseconds to seconds and magnetic fields from $10^{12}$-$10^{15}$ G to hypothetical values near the Chandrasekhar-Fermi virial scale, $10^{18}$ G. In Newtonian theory, we find the equilibrium figure of a rotating incompressible fluid with a current-free uniform interior magnetic field matched to an exterior dipole field by surface currents. For aligned axes, an oblate spheroid is obtained by minimizing the total gravitational, rotational and magnetic energy at fixed mass, volume, angular momentum and frozen magnetic flux. Its ellipticity is the sum of rotational and magnetic contributions, recovers the Ferraro limit for a weak magnetic field, and has a magnetic weight that depends on the eccentricity for large deformation. For misaligned magnetic and spin axes, we introduce a quadrupolar shape tensor and diagonalize it to find a triaxial ellipsoid whose principal axes are tilted by magnetic pressure. The tilt angle and eccentricities are computed analytically as functions of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities and the misalignment angle. The magnetic energy of the misaligned configuration is obtained in closed form in oblate spheroidal harmonics for arbitrary eccentricity and obliquity. Its weak-field deformation, up to $10^{15}$ G, is proportional to $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, which fixes the magnetic forcing tensor, and its finite-eccentricity form gives a generalized Ferraro-Maclaurin relation for rotation-dominated misaligned stars. In the weak-field regime, the triaxial eccentricity is determined by the Ferraro eccentricity and the harmonic mean of order 2 of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities. The deformation parameters give the quadrupole moments and hence the continuous gravitational-wave amplitudes, luminosity and spin-down torque of the triaxial configuration.

title: Magnetars magnetic field evolution with ambipolar diffusion
abstract: The magnetic field associated with neutron stars is generally believed to be threaded inside the star. In the presence of a magnetic field, plasma in the interior of the star undergoes a series of processes that result in magnetic field evolution. It is believed that magnetar activities like X-ray, gamma-ray bursts, and giant flares (which release more energy in a few sec than Sun in 10 years), are mainly due to field decay. The most important process of field decay inside the core of the star is the ambipolar diffusion of the charged particles present in the interior plasma. The decay rate due to ambipolar diffusion is directly connected to the ambipolar velocity of the charged particles under the influence of the present magnetic field. The ambipolar velocity of the charged particles depends on the internal dynamics of the particles. We outline a general method to solve the particle dynamics in the presence of a magnetic field to have a magnetohydrodynamics equation from ambipolar velocity. The equation is general and applicable to all possible surrounding conditions temperature, matter states like normal or superfluid, etc.

title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.

title: Erratum: New high-spin level scheme of neutron-rich Rh 112 [Phys. Rev. C 87, 057302 (2013)]
abstract: The neutron-rich nucleus 112Rh has been reinvestigated by examining the prompt γ rays emitted in the spontaneous fission of 252Cf with the Gammasphere detector array. A new side band was built in 112Rh. Total Routhian surface calculations have been performed and confirm the role of triaxiality in the negative-parity structure of 112Rh.

title: Analysis of quasielastic scattering and one-neutron transfer channel in the N 14 + Yb 176 reaction
abstract: The strong interplay between the nuclear structure and reaction dynamics near the Coulomb barrier makes the reaction observables a powerful tool for probing the structural properties. To disentangle the roles of nuclear deformation and positive $Q$-value neutron transfer channels, the angular distributions for quasielastic scattering and neutron transfer have been measured for $^{14}\mathrm{N}+^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ system and analyzed in the context of the midshell heavy nuclei $A=176$, where inelastic and transfer couplings compete each other. The measured angular distributions for quasielastic and one-neutron transfer have been interpreted in light of coupled reaction calculations using the $\mathrm{FRESCO}$ code. Analysis of the quasielastic angular distribution indicated a strong influence of inelastic excitations arising from the large nuclear deformation of $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The influence of $2n$-pickup channel was calculated in the single-step and sequential modes. The analysis suggests that the $2n$-pickup channel have a feeble impact on the angular distribution and the transfer of $2n$ in step mode more adequately explains the experimental data. Furthermore, the analysis of the angular distribution for one neutron pickup channel suggested a significant contribution from higher energy states compared to lower energy states, which might be due to the large deformation of $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The present study validates the reported values of deformation parameters and spectroscopic factors, respectively, for the $^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$ nucleus. The results show a significant impact of the collective nature on the spectroscopic behavior of the reaction partners $^{14}\mathrm{N} + ^{176}\mathrm{Yb}$, which is reflected in the experimental observables. These measurements provide important input for separating the contributions of positive $Q$-value transfer channels and nuclear deformation in governing the fusion dynamics.

title: Updating GEANIE Pu 239 prompt γ -ray experimental data using a modern Hauser-Feshbach fission fragment decay model
abstract: We calculate fission $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ rays for neutron-induced reactions on $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}$ with the Hauser-Feshbach fission fragment decay model. By applying the calculated fission $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ rays as a background contribution, the historical $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}(n\text{,}xn\ensuremath{\gamma})$ reaction cross section data measured by the GEANIE (GErmanium Array for Neutron Induced Excitations) spectrometer are corrected. The correction also includes other $(n\text{,}xn)$ reactions that have very similar energies to the $\ensuremath{\gamma}$ lines reported by GEANIE. In many cases, the original GEANIE data are strongly reduced and they become much closer to the statistical Hauser-Feshbach model predictions. The total inelastic scattering, $(n\text{,}2n)$, and $(n\text{,}3n)$ cross sections are inferred based on the corrected GEANIE data, and compared with available experimental data as well as the statistical model calculations. Expected $\ensuremath{\gamma}$-ray energy spectra for neutron-induced measurements on $^{239}\mathrm{Pu}$ are also discussed.

title: Production of the 4 ΛHe hypernucleus in Au+Au collisions at √s NN = 3 GeV with STAR
abstract: Abstract The STAR experiment reports the first measurement of the ⁴ΛHe hypernuclei yield as a function of rapidity and transverse momentum in 0–50% central Au+Au collisions at √s NN = 3 GeV. The ⁴ΛHe is reconstructed through its three-body decay channel, ⁴ΛHe → ³He + p + π⁻, with a statistical significance of about 9.5 standard deviations. We find that the yield of ⁴ΛHe as a function of rapidity is consistent with that of ⁴ΛH, and the rapidity-dependent yield ratio of ⁴ΛHe/⁴ΛH is consistent with that of ³He/t. All the measurements, as well as the transverse-momentum spectra, can be reasonably described by the JAM with a coalescence afterburner, suggesting a coalescence-based formation scenario for hyper-nuclei at this energy. The canonical thermal model reproduces the observed yield ratios but overpredicts the absolute hypernuclei yields.

title: First observation and interpretation of ion cyclotron emission from energetic ions accelerated by lower hybrid waves in a tokamak plasma
abstract: Abstract We report the first observation of ion cyclotron emission (ICE) from a tokamak plasma during lower hybrid wave (LHW) injection and electron cyclotron resonance heating. Using a novel approach derived from linear kinetic theory, we infer key parameter values for the LHW-accelerated fast-ion distribution which drives the observed ICE spectra, and for the bulk plasma. These ICE spectra from deuterium plasmas in the EAST tokamak exhibit peaks at successive deuterium cyclotron harmonics, consistent with the collective relaxation of energetic deuterons through the magnetosonic cyclotron instability (MCI). By carrying out a multi-dimensional parameter scan of MCI growth rates in high-resolution two-dimensional ( k ∥ , k _ b o t ) wavenumber space, we obtain best-fit values for: the magnetic field; plasma density; background electron and ion temperature; and the concentration of fast deuterons, together with their energy, pitch ( u ∥ / | u | ) and thermal spread. We find that the observed ICE spectrum is likely driven by 770 keV deuterons, plausibly accelerated through LHW–ion interactions, which then undergo the MCI. The assumptions of the linear analytically based model include an infinite homogeneous plasma, and a ring-beam distribution of fast deuterons. Our results demonstrate a new scenario in which ICE serves as a passive diagnostic of energetic ion populations, and invite further investigation of the ICE–LHW connection.

title: Equation of State for Warm Neutron Star Outer Crusts
abstract: Abstract We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using molecular dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the neutron star (NS) outer crust assumed in U. Murarka et al. with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation P ( n B , T ) is obtained as a function of baryonic number density n B ∈ [7.48 × 10 −10 , 2.09 × 10 −4 ] fm −3 and temperature k B T ∈ [1, 5] MeV in the NS outer crust conditions. In order to improve the usability of our results, we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parameterization available in the Zenodo repository; see DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15348712 . We find that even at moderate temperatures thermal effects of ions are key in the higher-density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parameterization based on the thermal adiabatic index Γ th . We compare our results with other EoSs in the literature and provide a critical discussion.

title: Long-Range and Short-Range Longitudinal Flow Decorrelations in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
abstract: The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) remains poorly constrained. Using a transport-model calculation of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ in relative pseudorapidity $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}$, we find two distinct initial-state components of flow decorrelation: a long-range component driven by the global geometry of participating nucleons and a short-range component reflecting local energy-deposition fluctuations. This short-range component extends to $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|\ensuremath{\sim}4$ and can be misidentified as final-state nonflow. For isobarlike nuclei with different shapes, the calculation predicts an experimentally testable fingerprint of this component: it dilutes the deformation contribution at small $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$, so that the ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ ratio between deformed and near-spherical systems, such as $\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{U}$-to-$\mathrm{Au}+\mathrm{Au}$, rises with $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$. Separating long- and short-range flow decorrelations from nonflow gives access to the longitudinal initial structure and dynamics of the QGP.

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto–neutron stars
abstract: We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp interface. The surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the TM1e model with a small symmetry energy slope of $L=40$ MeV predicts various pasta shapes at low temperatures, while the TM1 model with $L=110.8$ MeV yields only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust with a thickness of about $1.2$ km, playing an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.

title: Is the Large Uncertainty of δ C P Fundamentally Encoded in the Neutrino Quantum State?
abstract: The precise measurement of the leptonic -violating phase δ C P remains one of the major open challenges in neutrino physics, as current experiments achieve only very limited accuracy. We address this issue through the lens of quantum estimation theory. A distinctive feature of neutrino oscillation experiments is that they cannot freely optimize the probe or measurement, since both are constrained by the production and detection of flavor eigenstates. We therefore examine whether the large uncertainty in δ C P originates from intrinsic properties—either of the neutrino quantum state or of flavor measurements—or if it instead stems from experimental limitations. By comparing quantum and classical Fisher information, we demonstrate that the limited sensitivity to δ C P originates primarily from the information content of flavor measurements. Furthermore, we show that, while targeting the second oscillation maximum, as in the ESS ν SB proposal, typically enhances δ C P information, this feature in fact strongly depends on the actual values of δ C P .
