title: Neutrino mass predictions with metaheuristic optimization under $A_4$ modular symmetry
abstract: The current research aims to conduct an exhaustive investigation of the neutrino mass model based on $A_4$ discrete non-abelian modular symmetry, specifically in the context of the linear seesaw mechanism, where the conventional type I seesaw mechanism is extended, with particular attention given to the optimization of the parameters using incomprehensible but intelligible-in-time logics optimization algorithm (ILA), a metaheuristic optimization. Unlike other approaches to discrete flavor symmetry, the modular approach to flavor dynamics is found to significantly reduce the number and complexity of flavon fields required to give realistic textures to fermion masses. The key predictions include neutrino masses, $U_\text{PMNS}$ matrices, effective neutrino masses for neutrinoless double beta decay, beta decay, Dirac and Majorana CP violation phases for normal (NO) and inverted mass ordering (IO), offering testable implications. The working efficiency of the ILA optimization technique is also estimated. The optimized neutrino oscillation parameters are well consistent with recent experimental data. Our analysis also aligns with Planck cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses $0.06<\Sigma m<0.12\ \text{eV}$.

title: GLOW. II. A Census of Oxygen in Low-mass Galaxies*
abstract: Abstract Oxygen is forged by stars and redistributed through galaxies by feedback-driven outflows, leaving a record of star formation and the baryon cycle imprinted on its present-day abundance and distribution. The Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds project quantifies the production, distribution, and retention of oxygen in 37 low-mass, low–metallicity, gas-rich galaxies in the nearby Universe ( D < 6 Mpc) spanning a critical stellar mass range (10 6.5 < M * < 10 9.5 ) where feedback is expected to strongly shape galaxy evolution. We incorporate literature results to extend the analysis over 10 5 < M * < 10 11.5 . We couple star formation histories derived from resolved stars with measurements of interstellar medium metallicity and gas mass, and compare the oxygen budgets with empirical constraints in the circumgalactic medium (CGM). We find low-mass galaxies retain between 4% and 25% (mean 11%) of their oxygen produced by stellar nucleosynthesis, and nearly all retained oxygen resides in the gas. Galaxies exhibit increased scatter to higher oxygen retention fractions when residing in denser environments (Θ 5 > 0.5) and within 1 Mpc of a massive galaxy ( M * > 10 9 M ⊙ ), indicating the environment likely affects the amount of oxygen retained, recycled, or accreted to galaxies. Contrary to expectations, oxygen retention does not correlate with position on the mass–metallicity relation. Although ionized oxygen is detected in the CGM, it remains unclear whether most missing oxygen resides there or has been expelled entirely. Hydrodynamical simulations, despite successfully reproducing the mass–metallicity relation, predict much higher retention fractions than measured in low-mass galaxies. Simple modeling indicates that wind mass-loading and outflow metallicity govern oxygen retention, and that low-mass galaxies accrete less baryonic material relative to the cosmic baryon fraction.

title: First Measurement of the Hubble Constant from Gravitational Wave–Galaxy Cross Correlations
abstract: Abstract We measure for the first time the Hubble constant ( H 0 ) from the cross correlation of galaxies and gravitational waves (GWs), by applying the Peak Sirens method. This method consists of finding the peak of the 3D angular cross-spectrum C ℓ ( z , D L ) between the galaxy redshifts ( z ) and the GW luminosity distances ( D L ). Using two GW events from the GWTC-3.0 catalog and the GLADE + galaxy catalog, we make the first detection of the cross-correlation peak at 5.9 σ confidence. This signal comes mostly from the best localized event in the catalog, GW190814, which alone provides a 3.4 σ significance. Adding the multimessenger event GW170817, but without using its known redshift, we find H 0 = 6 7 − 15 + 18 km s −1 Mpc −1 and the first observational constraint on the GW bias, b gw < 4.3 at 95% confidence interval. These measurements set the stage for future novel cosmological constraints with this technique.

title: Bayesian Inferences on the Twin-star Scenario from NICER Pulsars
abstract: Abstract We investigate dense-matter equations of state (EOSs) within a Bayesian framework, focusing on the constraints from the latest NICER mass–radius measurements of PSR J0614−3329 and the massive pulsar PSR J0740+6620, together with PSR J0030+0451 and PSR J0437−4715. For the hadronic sector, we adopt a meta-modeling EOS constrained by these NICER measurements. The hadronic inference indicates that PSR J0614−3329 favors a somewhat softer EOS than the other two ∼1.4 M ⊙ pulsars, while the ∼2 M ⊙ constraint prevents the EOS from becoming too soft. We then introduce a strong first-order phase transition through a constant-speed-of-sound quark-matter segment. Constraining the transition parameters with PSR J0614−3329 as the primary source and XTE J1814−338 as a secondary constraint, we find a preferred transition density of n t ∼ 3.3 n 0 , a sizable energy-density jump of Δ ϵ − Δ ϵ cr ∼ 800 MeV, and a relatively large posttransition sound speed of c s 2 / c 2 ∼ 0.7 . Including the additional constraint from HESS J1731−347 shifts these values to n t ∼ 2.7–2.8 n 0 , Δ ϵ − Δ ϵ cr ∼ 600–700 MeV and c s 2 / c 2 ∼ 0.85 . Such a phase transition generates a disconnected hybrid branch with radii of about 6–7 km at masses around 1.2–1.4 M ⊙ , and strongly suppresses the dimensionless tidal deformability relative to the purely hadronic branch. This pronounced change in tidal deformability is a characteristic signature of the twin-star mechanism and may provide an important observational tool for identifying phase transitions in neutron star matter in future multimessenger measurements. Our results demonstrate that the NICER data, particularly the recently measured PSR J0614−3329, when supplemented by XTE J1814−338, already provide meaningful constraints on both the strength of a first-order phase transition and the stiffness of the posttransition phase in dense matter.

title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

title: The role of spin polarization in event-by-event fluctuations
abstract: The event-by-event initial state fluctuations constitute a critical physical quantity for understanding the dynamics of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Due to the extremely limited available experimental data of such fluctuations, it is difficult to constrain or direct the characterization of the underlying initial state properties. This work constrains the correlation function between the initial eccentricity and the asymmetry by employing a parton distribution function that incorporates spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity and thermal shear. Based on the kinetic theory calculations, we found that the asymmetry fluctuations considering spin polarization have a significant splitting effect compared to those without spin polarization. These splitting exhibit pronounced system size and energy dependence. Moreover, the ratios of correlation function display similar system size and energy dependence--particularly in the low-temperature regime ($T \lesssim$ 0.12 GeV). These results suggest that spin polarization may serve as a useful constraint method for the event-by-event initial state fluctuations of heavy-ion collisions.

title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
abstract: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $\phi^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, M\"uller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $\omega$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $\omega \tau_\pi \ll 1$, where $\tau_\pi$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $\omega\tau_\pi$, since $\tau_\pi\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.

title: Non-Efimovian two-neutron halos with an s − wave core-neutron resonance
Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor
abstract: Hybrid pixel detectors represent the state-of-the-art technology for hard X-ray experiments at synchrotron light sources and free-electron lasers, owing to their high frame rates, extended dynamic range, and scalable detection areas. However, their application in the soft X-ray regime remains bottlenecked by the challenge of developing a sensor that can achieve high quantum efficiency and an sufficient signal-to-noise ratio at low photon energies. Here, we present inverse low-gain avalanche diode (iLGAD) sensors integrated with a thin entrance window, demonstrating single-photon resolution down to 390 eV (below the Nitrogen K-edge) with a signal-to-noise ratio of 5. Two gain layer designs, standard gain layer and shallow gain layer, were systematically investigated to evaluate their spectral response as a function of photon energy and operating temperature. A double-peak feature is observed in the energy spectrum, arising from the dependence of charge multiplication on photon absorption depth. Furthermore, a phenomenological spectral fitting model was established, enabling the quantitative extraction of the effective $\mathrm{n}^+$ layer thickness and gain layer depth. Beyond providing a fundamental understanding of iLGAD charge multiplication mechanisms and characterization results in the soft X-ray regime, these findings lay the foundation for developing large-area, high-frame-rate hybrid pixel detectors for soft X-ray. This advancement directly benefits soft X-ray photon science applications, including high-resolution ptychography, spectroscopy, and resonant scattering at synchrotron and FEL beamlines.

title: Calorimetry as inference: the information content of particle showers and the limits of energy measurement
abstract: A calorimeter does not measure the energy of a particle, it infers it from the record the absorption process leaves behind. Energy conservation writes every event as an accounting ledger, E = E_dis + E_B + E_esc + E_nu, of which only the dissipated component contributes to signal, so resolution is limited by how well the record of the dissipation constrains the missing entries. We formalize this: records form a lattice on which information is monotone; thinning a Poisson record scales Fisher information exactly by the retention; clustered records read out as sums cost the 1/(1+cv^2); and the quadrature budget a/sqrt(E) (+) b is the floor of every summed readout. The "ultimate limits" of hadronic calorimetry are identified as the first rung of a ladder, the residual spread of the invisible energy around a single correlated observable. We measure the ladder above that rung on Geant4 truth records of hadronic showers in copper, from the dissipated-energy sum to time-, position- and multiplicity-resolved records, with estimators validated on exactly solvable toy models. The achieved full-record value, model-conditional, is about 5.5%/sqrt(E) (+) 0.3% over 20-100 GeV, a factor 1.7-1.9 below the canonical one-functional construction on the same events (1.29% vs. 2.14% at 20 GeV). Under retrained high-precision neutron transport it moves from 1.29% to 1.30%, the dissipated-energy sum by 7%, and the gain from time structure becomes 0.17% in place of 0.28%. Dual-readout supplies the largest share of the information. Shower shape is next, almost entirely longitudinal, saturating at about one interaction length. Time structure adds nearly as much with or without shower shape, and stopped-muon neutrino losses set an estimated floor of 0.99% at 20 GeV. Every readout dimension has a measured information exchange rate, separating what new hardware can buy from what better algorithms can recover.

title: Conceptual Design of a Compact Magnetic Spectrometer for Space Radiation Measurement
abstract: We present the design of COMIRA, a compact magnetic spectrometer for space radiation measurement. The spectrometer consists of four layers of scintillating fiber trackers, four layers of silicon strip trackers, one threshold Cherenkov counter, two anti-coincidence counters, and a permanent magnet. The detector has an overall dimension of approximately 12x12 cm3 and a geometrical acceptance of ~6.6 cm2sr. Based on combined measurements of charge, velocity, and rigidity (momentum/charge), it enables the simultaneous measurement of the energy spectrum, angular distribution and time evolution of individual radiation components, including electrons, positrons, protons and light nuclei over an energy range from tens of MeV to several GeV. The design can be further optimized depending on the available resources and constraints of the hosting space platform.

title: Precision tests of SM and new physics with the COHERENT Ge-mini and TEXONO data
abstract: A comprehensive numerical analysis of the latest germanium based coherent elastic neutrino nucleus scattering ( CE ν NS ) data from the COHERENT Ge-mini and TEXONO experiments has been conducted to test the Standard Model (SM) and search for new physics. By combining CE ν NS and E ν ES signals with a consistent treatment of detector effects and systematic uncertainties, we obtain a low energy determination of the weak mixing angle from COHERENT Ge-mini, in agreement with the SM prediction. We derive novel constraints on neutrino electromagnetic properties, including the magnetic moment, millicharge, charge radius, and anapole moment, with TEXONO providing particularly competitive bounds. Inclusion of E ν ES significantly improves the sensitivity to the neutrino millicharge by up to three orders of magnitude. We also investigated light scalar and vector mediators, finding striking complementarity between reactor and stopped pion sources across different mediator mass regimes. Finally, we put bounds on sterile neutral lepton production through transition dipole, scalar, and vector portals, probing masses from the sub-MeV to tens of MeV scale. Our results demonstrate that current germanium based CE ν NS experiments provide a powerful low energy laboratory for precision electroweak tests and complementary probes of a broad class of physics beyond the SM.

title: Magnetic scattering experiments with an ultrashort pulsed soft X-ray source using iLGADs
abstract: Inverse Low Gain Avalanche Diode (iLGAD) sensors developed at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in collaboration with the Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) have demonstrated an excellent Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Quantum Efficiency (QE) in the soft X-ray range. In the current batch, single-photon detection is achievable at 400 eV with an SNR > 5, while the QE surpasses 85 % at 250 eV. Combined with the high frame rates of CMOS readout ASIC, iLGAD sensors make the hybrid pixel detectors excellent candidates for time-resolved magnetic Small Angle X-ray Scattering (mSAXS) experiments in the soft X-ray energy range. In this contribution, we evaluated ILGAD sensors bump-bonded to 25 {\mu}m pitch charge-integrating M\"ONCH chips at a laser-driven soft X-ray source. During the experiments, we measured energy-dispersed radiation between 600 eV and 1500 eV. These measurements were performed for the iLGAD sensor, as well as for the standard silicon sensor. Using the high-precision electronic trigger of the X-ray source, we were able to synchronise the detector with the X-ray source delivering few-picosecond pulses and optimise the timing parameters for the acquisition. Finally, we successfully performed the mSAXS experiment probing the magnetic domain pattern of a FeGd heterostructure, demonstrating better performance than a M\"ONCH detector with a standard silicon sensor. ILGAD sensors achieved a significantly higher photon detection efficiency and, consequently, a higher sensitivity compared to standard silicon sensors under the same conditions, particularly for the lower-energy Fe L3 edge.

title: Machine Learning Sensor Fusion for Water Vapor Radiometry based Tropospheric Delay Calibration
abstract: The next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA) intends to use 22 GHz water vapor radiometry (WVR) to correct for tropospheric phase fluctuations in its high-frequency bands. However, current delay-retrieval methods do not reach the required accuracy and reliability. As a remedy, we propose a machine-learning based retrieval concept and a preliminary architecture, framed as heterogeneous, multi-rate sensor fusion. Atmospheric reanalysis profiles and surface weather set the context in which per-antenna WVR spectra are used to estimate excess path by a Kalman filter whose parameters are learned from high-cadence calibrator phases. The method is being developed, with planned first validation on the 183 GHz WVR system of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

title: High efficiency superconducting filterbank with impedance-defined resolution for millimeter-wave spectroscopy
abstract: We present a high efficiency, moderate resolution on-chip superconducting filterbank spectrometer designed for line intensity mapping and broadband wave-like dark matter searches. Existing implementations used by the millimeter-wave community rely on resistive feedline termination for standing wave mitigation which caps the per-channel efficiency $\eta_\mathrm{ch}$ at 50\% and utilize microstrip resonators which highly couple the resolving power $\mathcal{R}=\nu/\delta\nu$ and $\eta_\mathrm{ch}$ to thin-film dielectric loss. The architecture presented in this paper addresses these limitations by eliminating the termination resistor and employing niobium coplanar waveguide resonators patterned directly on single-crystal silicon, which fixes the resonator's internal quality factor by the silicon substrate property rather than by the loss tangent of a deposited film. The resolving power is set by the impedance ratio between the resonator and feedline. Electromagnetic and circuit simulations of a ten-channel filterbank near 90~GHz at unity oversampling show $\mathcal{R}=1170$ and $\eta_\mathrm{ch}> 78\%$, with no significant trend in efficiency across channels. A ten-channel prototype, designed for $\mathcal{R}=92\pm5$ and $\eta_\mathrm{ch}=(81\pm3)\%$ over 90--106~GHz with a 560~nm interlayer based on simulations, was fabricated and optically characterized, yielding $\mathcal{R}=208\pm74$ and $\eta_\mathrm{ch}=(77\pm6)\%$. Measured $\eta_\mathrm{ch}$ well above the 50\% termination limit, together with demonstrated impedance tuning of $\mathcal{R}$, validate the design principles of this filterbank spectrometer and establishes a route to high-efficiency, high-resolution on-chip spectrometer arrays.

title: Challenges in the verification of MOSAIX ASIC for ALICE ITS3
abstract: The MOSAIX is a wafer-scale, full-functionality prototype ASIC for the ALICE Inner Tracking System (ITS3) upgrade, implemented in $65\,\text{nm}$ stitching technology. It integrates 144 independently powered pixel matrices, eight $10\,\text{Gb/s}$ serializers, and on-chip data and power distribution, making full-chip verification highly resource-intensive (over $80\,\text{GB}$ of memory and 192,000 tests). Verification also targets a sophisticated power-up sequence and radiation conditions of $10^{6}$\ particles $s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and $4\,\text{kGy}$ TID. This work presents a UVM-based verification strategy that identified 260 design errors and summarizes key lessons from ASIC sign-off.

title: Bayesian constraints on bosonic dark matter in neutron stars within a covariant density-functional equation-of-state ensemble
abstract: We investigate neutron stars admixed with repulsively self-interacting bosonic dark matter (DM) using current multi-messenger observations. The dark component is modeled as a complex scalar field coupled to baryonic matter only through gravity, allowing dark-core and dark-halo configurations. To quantify baryonic equation-of-state (EOS) uncertainties, we combine a three-dimensional scan over $(m_\chi,\lambda,F_\chi)$ with 27 DDME2-based covariant density-functional EOSs spanning $L_{\rm sym}=30,50,70$ MeV and $-600\le Q_{\rm sat}\le 1000$ MeV. The models are confronted in a Bayesian framework with NICER mass--radius measurements from the Amsterdam and Maryland/Illinois analyses and the GW170817 tidal-deformability constraint. After Bayesian evidence weighting over the EOS ensemble, the EOS-relevant dark-sector scale $\mu_\chi\equiv m_\chi/\lambda^{1/4}$ is localized around 250 MeV for both NICER data sets. In the $(m_\chi,\lambda)$ parameterization, the marginalized boson-mass posterior peaks at $m_\chi\simeq300$--$330$ MeV, while $\lambda$ remains broadly distributed. Since the bosonic EOS depends on $m_\chi$ and $\lambda$ only through $\mu_\chi$, their separate marginals are conditional on the adopted independent priors. The inferred DM fraction is more data-set dependent, with posterior modes near 4% for Maryland/Illinois and 12% for Amsterdam. Bosonic DM also shifts the inferred $Q_{\rm sat}$ from negative toward intermediate and positive values, whereas the response of $L_{\rm sym}$ is weaker. This indicates a model-dependent trade-off between DM-induced compactification and the high-density stiffness of baryonic matter. These constraints remain conditional on the selected EOS family and the assumption of a common effective $F_\chi$ for all sources.

title: Experimental demonstration of beam-driven wakefield acceleration in laser-plasma filament
abstract: Self-guided femtosecond laser pulses propagating in low-pressure gas can generate plasma filaments, establishing a framework for plasma wakefield acceleration (PWFA). This method exploits the intrinsic nonlinear light-matter interaction, reducing the energy required to generate plasma while enabling the realization of plasma stages suitable for PWFA. Here we report a proof-of-principle experimental demonstration of beam-driven wakefield acceleration of electron bunches with an accelerating field exceeding 250 MV/m in a laser-generated plasma filament. The witness bunch is accelerated while preserving both its charge and relative energy spread. The robustness and reproducibility of both the plasma source and the acceleration process are demonstrated with successful witness acceleration observed in 95% of the events and an rms energy jitter below 0.5%. The experimental observations are in agreement with particle-in-cell simulations, providing a consistent description of the underlying physical processes. These results demonstrate that laser-generated plasma filaments can serve as reliable plasma stages, delivering beam quality and operational reproducibility comparable to those achieved with established plasma-generation techniques. The concept bridges laser filamentation physics and compact accelerator technologies, offering a promising route toward sustainable, high-repetition-rate plasma-based facilities.

title: Searching for Ultra-Light Axions with Twisted Cavity Resonators of Anyon Rotational Symmetry with Bulk Modes of Non-Zero Helicity
abstract: M\"obius-ring resonators stem from a well-studied geometrical structure with a one-sided topology, the M\"obius strip, and have been shown to exhibit fermion rotational symmetry with respect to an untwisted ring resonator, which exhibits boson rotational symmetry [1]. Here, we present twisted hollow resonators with equilateral triangular cross-sections, leading to cavities with anyon rotational symmetry. Unlike conventional cavity resonators, these structures permit bulk resonant modes with a non-zero complex electromagnetic overlap $\mathcal C_p=\int_V\mathbf{E}_p\cdot\mathbf{B}_p^*\,d\tau$. The real and imaginary parts of this overlap couple to different observable quadratures. Although the negative-frequency component of a real axion field is immaterial for haloscopes employing a static DC magnetic field, it must be retained for a pumped resonator because the complex forms of Maxwell's equations differ for positive and negative frequencies and produce distinct upper and lower mixing branches. Retaining both branches shows that the real overlap produces amplitude-modulated sidebands, whereas the imaginary helicity of the modes studied here produces phase-modulated sidebands through the axion-photon chiral anomaly. A sensitive ultra-light dark-matter experiment may therefore be realised with an ultra-stable oscillator and a phase-sensitive readout. The sensitivity curves calculated here require the assumed noise floor to be interpreted as phase-modulation noise rather than amplitude-modulation noise, and consequently require sufficiently low residual oscillator phase noise at the axion Fourier frequency. The scheme removes the usual requirement for an external magnetic field and permits superconducting resonators with reduced surface loss and enhanced axion sensitivity.

title: Photon Calibration Techniques for High Resolution Cryogenic Detectors
abstract: Monoenergetic photons from a pulsed laser diode or LED are commonly used to calibrate the detector response of high-resolution calorimetric detectors. However, when the detector's resolution is larger than the energy of a single photon, a calibration is normally derived using Poisson statistics. In this paper, we clarify the assumptions implicit in this calibration method, before considering how a more realistic model of a detector's performance will violate these assumptions, biasing the calibration. Finally, we judge the individual impact of specific detector parameters on our calibration, and conclude with discussion of both the limits of our calculations and the implications for state-of-the art detectors.

title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.

title: Non-contact temperature sensing and optical scatter in cryogenically-cooled crystalline silicon
abstract: Cryogenic crystalline silicon is a promising optical material for next generation gravitational-wave detectors due to its low mechanical loss (a driver of thermal noise), high thermal conductivity and zero coefficient of thermal expansion at 123 K. In this paper, we report on the design and results of an experiment to measure the temperature of a flat-flat uncoated crystalline silicon sample using a non-contact sensing method relying on interference (optical fringes) made from reflections between the front and back surfaces. We also propose a scheme for implementation of this technique for cryogenic test masses in future gravitational-wave detectors such as Einstein Telescope and LIGO Voyager. Additionally, we characterize the optical scattering of the sample in vacuum at cryogenic temperatures by using a high-sensitivity infrared camera. We measured relatively constant scatter with an average bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of $(4.43\pm0.2)\times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{sr^{-1}}$ at a scattering angle of $\theta_{s} = 7.5^\circ$ over the (cold-plate) temperature range of 123-294 K and saw no evidence for growth of cryogenic molecular layers (ice) on the sample in our current setup.

title: Magnetic Johnson noise from arbitrarily shaped conductors: experimental validation of the fluctuation-dissipation finite-element method
abstract: Magnetic Johnson noise--magnetic noise caused by thermal current fluctuations in conducting materials--can interfere with measurements and limit their sensitivity. As the sensitivity of experiments increases, it becomes increasingly important to accurately estimate the magnetic Johnson noise from experimental components with complex shapes during both the design and analysis phases. A particularly powerful approach is to combine the fluctuation-dissipation theorem with finite-element calculations. This versatile approach can be used to calculate the magnetic Johnson noise from conductors of arbitrary geometry for a wide range of frequencies and for magnetic field detectors with general geometries, such as a finite-sized loop or a gradiometer. Using a SQUID gradiometer array, we measured the magnetic Johnson noise from conductors with complex geometries and compared the results with calculations performed using this method. The calculations reproduce both the measured noise amplitude and its frequency dependence, providing an experimental validation of this method. We also performed a detailed analysis of how the geometry and material parameters affect the frequency dependence of magnetic Johnson noise.

title: Construction and Commissioning of a Compact Xenon Gas Recycling System for a High-Harmonic Generation VUV Frequency Comb
abstract: A compact, closed-loop xenon recycling system for application in a High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) Vacuum-UV (VUV) frequency comb laser systems is designed, constructed and commissioned. It consists of three main sections, a low-pressure section (LPS) pre-filtering the gas of particulates, water and hydrocarbons, then a compression station (CS), allowing for a variable pressure of up to 60 bar, and a high-pressure section (HPS) with more filtering, pressure control and monitoring. The system proves to meet all design criteria in gas quality (the sum off all hydrocarbon contaminations up to 120 amu and CO$_{2}$ being below 10$^{-8}$ mbar) and recovery efficiency (>99.8$\%$ for all expected operational cases, neglecting possible geometric gas catcher losses in the HHG laser itself). The operation and results are presented and discussed. Furthermore, the system is compared to the performance of a similar system from which it is derived.

title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
abstract: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.

title: An Assessment of Water Vapor Radiometry Landscape in ngVLA Context
abstract: The ngVLA intends to utilize Water Vapor Radiometry (WVR) as an approach to lower calibration overheads for tropospheric phase fluctuation correction in its high frequency bands (5 \& 6; 30.5-116 GHz) to levels below those feasible with fast switched reference gain calibration. As a stepping stone to an eventual ngVLA WVR system, the JVLA/ngVLA teams pursued an effort to develop and install a set of MMIC based compact water vapor radiometers (CWVR) and carry out on-sky testing. Most recent tests found that the CWVRs installed on the VLA antennas under this effort were non-functional in tracking visibility phases. As part of the program to develop a WVR system for the ngVLA, this memo summarizes the current landscape of water vapor radiometry experience, the situation with the CWVRs, how they relate to the ngVLA WVR requirements, and the work needed to operationalize the CWVRs as useful test systems and to make broader progress. We currently lack statistically relevant WVR correction data to understand their expected performance for the ngVLA sites. We also discuss parallel additional approaches alternative and/or complementary to the CWVRs. A path involving tests to establish the functionality, stability, sensitivity, and switched power cal/data synchronism of the CWVR system in the lab and on antenna, followed by on-sky tests, and a parallel effort to assess the utility of autocorrelation outputs of the VLA K-band receivers for delay estimation is recommended. Potential paths going beyond traditional excess path estimation methods which may be necessary to meet ngVLA requirements and goals are touched upon.

title: Playing CHESS with stars. II. Homogeneous analysis of high-resolution optical spectra for a sample of 135 giants in 14 bulge globular clusters
abstract: Bulge globular clusters are key tracers of the complex formation history of the Galactic bulge, as they retain information on its past star-formation episodes. Their chemical abundances serve as empirical “fossil records” of the early evolution of the bulge. We present a homogeneous analysis of archival high-resolution UVES spectra for 135 giants in 14 Galactic bulge globular clusters. We explore the results in the context of the phenomenon of multiple stellar populations and discuss what the abundances reveal about the chemical evolution of the bulge. We employed the CHEmical Survey analysis System (CHESS) pipeline to derive atmospheric parameters on an accurate scale defined by reference stars. Abundances for Li, O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Sc, Y, Zr, Ba, Ce, Nd, and Eu were derived by spectrum synthesis. Deviations from local thermodynamic equilibrium (i.e., non-LTE or NLTE) were taken into account for Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Y, Ba, and Eu. We serendipitously discovered a Li-rich giant with A(Li) = 1.68 (after 3D NLTE corrections) in NGC 6723, which was hidden in the archival data. Our sample includes both first- and second-generation stars, as indicated by the observed spread in Na abundances. Compared to halo clusters, the bulge clusters show a lower α/Fe plateau at low metallicity and a more gradual decline in α/Fe toward higher metallicities. The Sc abundances are below solar and lower than in disk stars of the same metallicity. This difference could be important for solving open questions about the nucleosynthesis of this element. None of the clusters exhibit any significant spreads in heavy elements. Most clusters exhibit Ba/Eu ∼ 0.0, indicating a contribution from both s- and r-processes. Clusters with Fe/H $<$ -0.5 show negative Ce/Nd ratios, supporting the idea that these elements were predominantly produced by the r-process in these clusters.

title: On global reconstruction in generalized Rastall gravity and the invertibility of the Ricci scalar.
abstract: Abstract For the static and spherically symmetric case, we study the global consistency of the inverse reconstruction of generalized Rastall theory, G αβ +λH(R)g αβ = κ T αβ , when the geometry is fixed before the generalized Rastall function H(R). The analysis addresses the existence of a global inverse r=r(R) and the compatibility among the different radial branches when several radii produce the same value of the Ricci scalar curvature R. To illustrate the relevance of the analysis, we consider the regular Fan--Wang family with vanishing independent Schwarzschild mass. It is shown that R(r) is globally invertible if and only if μ=3 and 0<ν ≦ 1. The case ν=1 admits the elementary inverse r(R)=(24M F q 2 /R) 1/5 -q, whereas for 0<ν<1 the inverse is unique even though, in general, it cannot be expressed explicitly. It is also shown that the Hayward geometry employed by Lin and Qian and identified by (μ,ν)=(3,3) possesses two physical inverses over R min < R<0; the functions reconstructed on the two branches differ for ω ≦ 1/3, so the reconstruction is multivalued. For ω ≠ -1,1/3, a global single-valued function H(R) exists throughout the regular Fan--Wang family if and only if μ=3 and 0<ν ≦ 1. In this sector, H ∈ C 1 \ C 2 for 0<ν<1 and H ∈ C 0 \ C 1 for ν=1.

title: Energetic heavy ions in Jupiter's nightside inner and middle magnetosphere: Juno/JEDI statistics
abstract: Jupiter's magnetosphere is dominated by heavy ions, mainly comprised of singly charged oxygen ions and doubly charged sulfur ions, rather than by protons as in the case of Earth's magnetosphere. We investigate the energy and spatial distributions of energetic heavy ions in Jupiter's nightside inner magnetosphere near the equatorial plane. We conducted a statistical survey of Juno/JEDI observations obtained during Juno's primary and extended mission phases, covering radial distances of approximately 5-30 Jupiter radii, local times of 18--24(00)--06 hours, and energies of about 0.1--10 MeV. The energy spectra can be approximately described by power laws. On average, the duskside observations show higher absolute fluxes and smaller spectral indices than the dawnside and midnightside observations, suggesting that heavy ions are generally more energetic in the dusk sector. At a fixed local time, the spectral indices decrease with decreasing M-shells inside about 20 Jupiter radii. Outside this radial range, however, the spectral indices exhibit a peak or plateau-like profile. The transition in heavy-ion dynamics is further reflected in the phase space density at fixed magnetic moment. It remains approximately constant outside 20 Jupiter radii, but decreases inside this distance, with the transition occurring at smaller M-shells for lower magnetic moments. The observations suggest a transition in the behavior of energetic heavy ions at ∼20 Jupiter radii. We find that non-adiabatic mechanisms are required to fully account for their spectral and spatial properties.

title: On-detector machine learning for beam-induced background rejection at a 10 TeV muon collider
abstract: Abstract A 10 TeV Muon Collider is a compelling candidate for a future energy-frontier facility, offering unprecedented opportunities to explore the fundamental laws of particle physics. Muon decays in the collider ring produce intense beam-induced background (BIB) that can overwhelm detector occupancy and exceed readout bandwidth constraints. We investigate the potential of on-detector Machine Learning for BIB rejection in the vertex detector, exploiting pixel cluster shapes to distinguish background from collision products. We study three classes of lightweight neural-network architectures, and evaluate their implementation feasibility using high-level synthesis. Selected architectures achieve 88-90% data reduction at 99% signal efficiency, while requiring hardware resources compatible with potential ASIC implementation. These results demonstrate the potential of performing substantial BIB rejection directly in the pixel readout, providing a strategy for meeting the tracker readout requirements at a future Muon Collider.

title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
abstract: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $\alpha$, the dipole-radiation parameter $\gamma$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $\mu$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(\alpha \lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong. Our results demonstrate that future decihertz GW observatories can serve as powerful laboratories for testing dark-sector physics and probing dark matter interactions in compact binaries through precision GW measurements.

title: Enhanced Detectability of Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays from Off-Axis Short Gamma-Ray Bursts: Impacts of Structured Jets and External Inverse-Compton Scattering
abstract: The binary neutron star merger GW170817 established a direct link between gravitational waves and short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs), whose afterglows are commonly interpreted as nonthermal emission from structured relativistic jets viewed off-axis. Some sGRBs exhibit extended or plateau X-ray emission, suggesting prolonged central-engine activity. These X-ray photons can serve as seed photons for external inverse-Compton (EIC) scattering by relativistic electrons in the jet, producing very-high-energy (VHE) gamma rays. However, how the angular structure of the jet affects the detectability of EIC emission remains insufficiently explored. Here, we investigate EIC emission from off-axis structured jets and assess its detectability with the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). We find that EIC emission powered by extended and/or plateau X-rays produces detectable VHE signals from nearby sGRBs, particularly during the early afterglow, significantly outshining synchrotron self-Compton emission. In our adopted models, Gaussian and power-law jets produce brighter off-axis EIC emission than a top-hat jet, extending the viewing-angle range over which VHE emission may be detectable. These results demonstrate that early VHE observations with CTAO can probe both prolonged central-engine activity and the angular structure of relativistic jets in sGRBs.

title: Transverse Confinement in Cascaded Inverse-Cherenkov Acceleration via Phase-Trajectory Control and Injection Matching
abstract: Sub-relativistic electrons in micron-scale dielectric laser accelerators face coupled challenges of longitudinal dephasing and transverse defocusing, often imposing stringent requirements on injector emittance. Here, we demonstrate a combined strategy of phase-trajectory control and injection matching for sustained, confined acceleration. By coordinating the refractive-index and section-length sequences with the injected beam's Twiss parameters, we control accumulated phase slippage while maintaining transverse confinement. In a seven-section inverse-Cherenkov accelerator simulation, a 100-keV electron bunch with an initial normalized transverse emittance of 1 nm-rad and a relative kinetic-energy spread of 0.1% reaches 1154.7 keV over 1.545 mm, with a transverse rms beam size below 1 $\mu$m throughout the accelerating channels. The exit normalized emittance is 1.92 nm-rad, and the relative RMS kinetic-energy spread is 0.6%, with no particle loss under the specified tracking-acceptance criterion. The results demonstrate that coordinated structural sequencing and injection matching can relax injector-emittance requirements by up to approximately two orders of magnitude, offering a route toward compact dielectric accelerators for ultrafast electron diffraction, microscopy, and chip-scale coherent radiation.

title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
abstract: Self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas proceeds by the thermally activated formation of vacancy-interstitial pairs and the migration of these defects through the lattice, commonly known as Frenkel pairs in the materials literature. Molecular dynamics has recently resolved an Eyring law for diffusion in unstrained crystals, which we generalize to deformed crystals in this work. We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained crystal: $D(\varepsilon)=D_0(\Gamma^{*})\exp[V^{*}\sigma/k_{\rm B}T]$, with $\sigma=\tfrac12\mu\varepsilon^{2}$ the elastic energy density stored by the shear strain $\varepsilon$ and $V^{*}$ the activation volume. We find a single activation volume $N_{\rm act} = n_iV^{*}\simeq31$ suffices for typical astrophysical screenings with a reduction at higher screening. This suggests Frenkel pair formation requires only a brief coordination of the nearest neighbors at a thermal maximum in oscillation. Stress-enhanced diffusion supplies a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.

title: Reprocessing of X-rays emission in Ultra-Luminous X-ray sources
abstract: Most of the Ultraluminous X-ray Sources (ULXs) harbor either a neutron star or a stellar-mass black hole as a compact object accreting at super-Eddington rates. In spite of having such a high accretion rate, the reprocessed emission in ULXs is quite meagre compared to that observed in Galactic X-ray binaries, except for some absorption lines in the winds. In this work, we use archival Chandra and \xmm\ observations to investigate the extent of reprocessed emission in ULXs through three diagnostics: (i) searches for Fe $\rm K\alpha$ lines in bright well-known ULXs and Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars (ULXPs), (ii) evolution of hardness ratio around the eclipse transitions in the eclipsing ULXs, and (iii) the flux ratio between eclipse and out-of-eclipse (OOE) phases in eclipsing ULXs. We constrain the equivalent width (EW) of the Fe K$\alpha$ line, with upper limits of $\sim$11-20 eV for a fixed line centroid (6.4 keV) and width (0.1 keV). Allowing the centroid and width to vary yields more conservative upper limits of up to $\sim$50 eV. Furthermore, we have not observed any significant changes in the hardness ratio in eclipsing ULXs during ingress or egress, whereas in Galactic eclipsing X-ray binaries the hardness ratio increases during the transitions. Finally, the reprocessing efficiency (eclipse-to-OOE flux ratio) is found to be larger in ULXs compared to Galactic eclipsing X-ray binaries. Based on these results, we discuss the possibility of a metal-poor or highly ionized environment surrounding the ULXs, which suppresses reprocessed emission features.

title: Missing Mergers: On the Unexpected Delay-Time Distribution of Binary Neutron Star Mergers
abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration has detected two binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, GW170817 and GW190425. While no clear electromagnetic counterpart was discovered for GW190425, a coincident counterpart to GW170817 (GRB170817A, AT 2017gfo) was discovered in an early-type galaxy, NGC 4993. Using broad-band photometry and an integrated optical spectrum, we measure a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}$ Gyr (90% credible) for NGC 4993, which is an estimate of the delay time between star formation and merger for the GW170817 progenitor. BNS systems are expected to have a power-law delay-time distribution (DTD) with a minimum delay time, $t_{\rm min}$, of ~10 Myr and index $\alpha \approx -1$. This canonical DTD, convolved with the cosmic star-formation history, predicts ~16 BNS mergers at delay times of ~100 Myr for every BNS merger at 10 Gyr; under it, the chance of detecting even one merger as old as GW170817 is ~1.8%. The long delay time of GW170817 therefore implies many "missing" shorter-delay mergers if the canonical DTD holds. A DTD with $t_{\rm min} = 12.6$ Gyr and $\alpha = -1$ is favored over the canonical DTD by a factor of 40-140, and over short gamma-ray burst and Galactic double-NS DTDs by factors of 80-280. These results are in tension with current population synthesis models, the Milky Way double NS population, and the SGRB population. Explaining the LVK population requires either a dramatically different separation distribution than commonly assumed, an additional channel with a long delay time and comparable rate to an isolated-binary formation scenario, or a large population of BNS mergers missed in the LVK analysis. This result has wide-ranging implications for binary-population synthesis, chemical enrichment models, connections between BNS mergers and SGRBs, and future gravitational wave observations.

title: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search
abstract: We present MAGIKS, a multimodal framework for gravitational-wave (GW)-triggered kilonova identification that formulates counterpart search as query-conditioned gallery retrieval. Following an align-before-fuse design, MAGIKS combines GW source parameters and sky-localization maps with irregularly sampled multiband optical light curves and sky coordinates. A time-aware supervised contrastive objective provides coarse cross-modal alignment, while dual cross-attention evaluates consistency between optical coordinates and GW localization, and between GW parameters and optical evolution. We train and evaluate MAGIKS on simulated binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole mergers, Rubin Observatory kilonova light curves from regular survey observations and target-of-opportunity follow-up, GW-detected mergers without Rubin-detectable kilonova counterparts, and realistic non-kilonova contaminants. In independent galleries with one true counterpart and time- and sky-compatible distractors, MAGIKS outperforms optical-only and sky-localization-only ranking, with increasing gains as galleries grow. At 5000 candidates, it ranks the counterpart first for 39.8% of queries, versus 4.8% and 0.2% for these baselines. In a GW170817 study, we generate counterfactual Rubin observations using released GW parameters and three-dimensional localization, the measured counterpart position, and host distance. At the same gallery size, MAGIKS achieves top-1 and top-10 retrieval rates of 87.3% and 95.7%. It correctly classifies 94.2% of associated and non-associated GW-optical pairs. In a separate crossed-pair experiment, its matching score responds significantly to controlled changes in all five tested GW parameters. These results support GW-conditioned kilonova candidate prioritisation for future multi-messenger follow-up.

title: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
abstract: Her X-1 is an eclipsing X-ray binary system consisting of an accreting neutron star and an optical component HZ Her. In addition to the 1.24-s X-ray pulsations and the 1.7-d orbital period, the system also shows a 35-day X-ray variability related to the precessional motion of a tilted and twisted accretion disk around the neutron star. The long-term persistence of the 35-day X-ray variability suggests the presence of a stable clock mechanism, most likely free precession of the magnetized neutron star. We have studied the long-term behavior of the 35-day cycle of Her X-1 using all available CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI data and archival turn-on moments of the 35-day cycle spanning more than 50 years. We have used a sliding-window averaged X-ray phase light curve and the classical O-C (observed minus calculated) diagram for individual 35-day turn-ons to inspect the long-term trends of the O-C diagram. The O-C diagram demonstrates two similar parabolic trends separated by an anomalous low state (ALS) of the source suggesting a secular decrease in the 35-d precession period with $\dot P_\text{35} =(-1.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ and $\dot P_\text{35} =(-4.7\pm0.1)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ before and after the ALS, respectively. We conclude that the decay of the 35-day period as inferred from the O-C analysis can be interpreted in terms of the direct relationship between the change of the precessional period of the accretion disk to the long-term decrease of the period of the free precessional neutron star - due to continued accumulation of accreted matter.

title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
abstract: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm \mu m}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm \mu m}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,\mu{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

title: An efficient approach to resistive GRMHD simulations of binary neutron star mergers
abstract: Astrophysical plasmas are often highly conducting, but finite resistivity can nevertheless influence the evolution of strongly magnetised systems. Capturing these effects in general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics is computationally challenging because high conductivity leads to stiff source terms in the evolution equations. Standard numerical approaches rely on implicit-explicit (IMEX) time integration to maintain stability, but this substantially increases the complexity and computational cost of the simulations. Building upon the previously developed Resistive Extension upGrade for Ideal MagnEtohydrodynamics (REGIME), we present a new fluid-frame formulation that simplifies the incorporation of leading-order resistive effects by avoiding matrix inversions required in previous approaches. The method is implemented in a general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics code and validated through one-dimensional current-sheet tests and simulations of isolated magnetised neutron stars and binary neutron star mergers. We find that the new formulation reproduces the expected resistive behaviour with accuracy comparable to IMEX-based methods, while substantially reducing the computational cost and complexity of the simulations. In binary neutron star mergers, finite resistivity leads to measurable differences in the post-merger gravitational-wave signal and remnant structure, showing that resistive effects can produce measurable changes in the post-merger dynamics even in the high-conductivity regime.

title: Verification of the NIMSTELL code via application to linear magnetohydrodynamic instabilities in stellarators
abstract: A new simulation tool for macroscale dynamics in stellarators, NIMSTELL [Sovinec et al., “Semi-implicit stellarator magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) with nodal spectral elements,” arXiv:2606.28613 (2026)], is verified through benchmarking with the time-dependent code JOREK [Nikulsin et al., Phys. Plasmas 29, 063901 (2022)] and the eigenvalue code CASTOR3D [E. Strumberger and S. Günter, Nucl. Fusion 57, 016032 (2016)]. The comparisons establish NIMSTELL's accuracy and reliability in representative configurations, where analytical results are not tractable. Results from all three codes are assessed for linear tearing and ballooning instabilities in W7-A and tearing in a quasi-axisymmetric (QA) configuration. NIMSTELL and CASTOR3D are also applied to global non-resonant interchange in a quasi-helically symmetric (QH) configuration. The computed NIMSTELL and CASTOR3D growth rates agree to the level of 1.5% and 3% for tearing modes in W7-A and QA configurations, respectively, to 5.8% for a W7-A ballooning mode, and to 1.6% for a global interchange mode in QH configurations. While NIMSTELL results also agree with JOREK for a majority of the benchmark cases, the numerical discrepancies are somewhat larger than those with respect to CASTOR3D in specific parameter regimes. The discrepancies are largely ascribed to the use of reduced-MHD modeling in the JOREK computations. In addition to benchmarking, the nonlinear capability of NIMSTELL is demonstrated by modeling the loss of pressure due to global interchange modes in the QH configuration. The successful verification presented in this work provides support for applying NIMSTELL to physically relevant stability analyses of current experiments and future designs.

title: Three-dimensional reconstruction of cold fuel shells using down-scattered neutron imaging at the National Ignition Facility
abstract: In inertial confinement fusion experiments at the National Ignition Facility, the cold fuel density distribution during peak neutron production indicates the symmetry of imploded laser-driven deuterium–tritium fusion capsules. Since implosion asymmetry can degrade performance, characterizing the three-dimensional structure of the compressed fuel is vital for diagnosing implosion performance. The nuclear imaging system provides two-dimensional imaging of 14 MeV fusion neutrons on three nearly orthogonal lines of sight and 6–12 MeV down-scattered neutrons along two equatorial lines of sight. The 14 MeV images provide the shape of the fusion burn region, and the down-scattered images contain information about the cold fuel distribution, convolved with the fusion burn region. Two approaches are used to infer the cold fuel distribution from these measurements. The first deconvolves the two-dimensional primary fluence from the down-scattered image to provide a two-dimensional fluence-compensated down-scattered image. The second infers a three-dimensional density distribution using the three-dimensional primary emission and the down-scattered images. We compare these methodologies using synthetic multi-mode implosion data and experimental data from igniting experiments, focusing on assumptions, strengths, and limitations. We demonstrate that fluence-compensated images, while computationally efficient and useful for low-mode shape and shell dimensions from a single view, cannot reliably represent complex three-dimensional density structures even with multiple views. The more computationally expensive three-dimensional density reconstructions capture major asymmetries quantitatively in physical units. However, limited viewing angles can create artifacts, indicating that additional lines of sight would improve reconstruction fidelity and enable comprehensive characterization of the fuel and implosion physics.

title: The role of electron–ion equilibration on the size scaling of laser direct-drive implosions
abstract: The impact of electron–ion equilibration on the target-size scaling of direct-drive laser-fusion implosions is investigated. It is found that, with increasing scale, enhanced equilibration degrades implosion performance by reducing laser-drive efficiency during the acceleration phase and suppressing ion temperatures during deceleration, thereby diminishing the ion-temperature enhancement associated with thermal conduction at larger scales. By extending a steady-state spherical ablation model to include finite ion-temperature effects, we show that both the ablation pressure and mass ablation rate scale as (1+Ti/ZTe)−1. One-dimensional simulations are used to validate the ablation-model predictions and to assess the effects of equilibration during the deceleration phase. Because larger implosions experience stronger electron–ion equilibration, these results suggest a corresponding reduction in laser-drive efficiency during acceleration and degraded implosion performance during deceleration with increasing target size.

title: Numerical study and modeling on the feedthrough mechanism of double-interface Rayleigh–Taylor instability growth
abstract: Multi-interface Rayleigh–Taylor (RT) instability is one of the critical factors limiting the performance of double-shell inertial confinement fusion (ICF) targets. This work presents a study on double-interface RT instability. The right interface is subject to RT instability, while the left interface is mainly driven by feedthrough. At the right interface, spike growth remains decoupled from the left interface. In contrast, bubble growth is strongly suppressed by feedback from the left side, especially for thinner shells. This result differs from the vacuum-bounded limit of Baker et al. [J. Fluid Mech. 178, 161 (1987)], which stems from the absence of drag in vacuum vs the strong drag present in our finite-density configuration. At the left interface, bubble growth converges to the evolution pattern of the right side, while the spike region exhibits concurrent in-phase growth and anti-spike formation. The anti-spike forms when the restoring effect locally overwhelms the feedthrough-driven growth. We then quantify the roles of shell thickness, wavelength, Atwood number, and acceleration. Bubble feedthrough increases with thinner shells and larger values of the other parameters. In contrast, effective spike feedthrough shifts negatively when the shell thickness and left Atwood number increase, but positively when the other parameters increase. Based on these insights, we extend the classical buoyancy-drag model by modeling the shell-thinning processes and effects, and introducing the transition mechanism between the thin-shell and thick-shell regimes. The extended model retains the accuracy of the original formulation under common conditions, while delivering clearly improved predictions when the drag becomes significant.

title: Inert-material effects on ignition criteria and hot-layer volume ignition in high-gain room-temperature solid-fuel ICF targets
abstract: This work investigates how inert constituents modify ignition conditions in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) and, using idealized one-dimensional simulations, the ignition dynamics of massive room-temperature solid-fuel targets. We consider an ADT mixture in which equimolar DT is diluted by an inert species of atomic number Za and ion-number fraction xa. Reduced analytical models show that the inert component narrows the self-sustaining temperature window by decreasing the DT reaction rate through the dilution factor (1−xa)2 while increasing bremsstrahlung losses through Z⋆3=Z¯,Z2¯. Consequently, the Post condition, generalized Lawson criterion, ICF hot-spot areal-density threshold, and minimum kinetic-energy requirement become more restrictive as xa and Za increase, apart from a limited low-concentration regime for high-Za species. The numerical study uses the radiation-hydrodynamics code MULTI-IFE to investigate massive Carbon-DT (CDT) implosions as idealized ignition cases. A Monte Carlo pulse search yields a one-dimensional CDT target with a thermonuclear gain of approximately 22 for a laser energy of 411 MJ and a fuel mass of 164 mg. Homothetic scaling identifies the combustion threshold and compares targets on either side. Above this threshold, simulations reveal ignition in a fuel layer between a cold, dense, weakly reactive gap above the hot spot and the shock wave. The layer is formed and compressed hydrodynamically, then undergoes local volumetric self-heating when its thermodynamic trajectory crosses a local ignition condition. A reduced hot-layer ignition model linking areal density and temperature is derived and compared with simulations. Igniting this hot layer can compress the hot spot and ignite the remaining fuel.

title: A probabilistic model of laser drive asymmetries applied to an inertial fusion energy reactor design
abstract: In the pursuit of the realization of an inertial fusion energy reactor, directly driving the fuel capsules with laser beams is a compelling design choice due to the more efficient energy coupling compared to indirect drive. However, the laser illumination symmetry necessary for achieving ignition and gain imposes stringent accuracy requirements on the laser system. We present a reactor beam port configuration in which multiple beams per port are used to dynamically shift power between different beam spot sizes as the capsule implodes, reducing the laser light blowby while maintaining uniform illumination. A probabilistic model has been developed to directly propagate the laser drive modes from stochastic system errors (target offset, beam pointing, and power imbalance) without the need for Monte Carlo simulations. This model constitutes a useful tool for the broad optimization of the laser beam geometrical configuration of future facilities.

title: Corrected detector-level reconstruction of inclined radio air showers from trigger-level ADC waveforms
abstract: Autonomous radio arrays record air-shower radio pulses as trigger-selected analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) voltage traces. We reconstruct the primary arrival direction and energy while accounting for noise, direction-dependent detector responses and atmospheric refraction in inclined showers. Waveform cross-correlation corrects relative trigger times; plane- and spherical-wavefront fits estimate the initial direction and effective emission point. A modified voltage-domain angular-distribution fit uses source-end tangents of refracted rays to refine the direction and distinguish the particle core from the radio-footprint centre, reducing the median opening-angle error by approximately 50% relative to straight source-to-station viewing angles. Antenna and radio-frequency-chain inversion recovers the electric field, and early-late corrections give its lateral peak-amplitude distribution. An event-to-reference peak-amplitude correction is calibrated on 2,500 simulated electric-field showers to account for 50-200 MHz coherence loss; a semi-analytic Fresnel parameterisation examines its finite-source interpretation. Proton and iron reference lateral-distribution fits give two energy estimates, averaged with fixed equal weights. Validation uses 6,000 independent showers. In the field-level test with simulation-input geometry, either correction reduces the relative energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 11.90% to 8.31%. Across three waveform treatments, 3,073 common detector-level events yield mean relative energy residuals of -2.30% to -1.86%, standard deviations of 8.46%-8.96%, and median opening-angle errors of 0.0315-0.0349 degrees. The method is intended for sparse radio arrays detecting highly inclined showers, such as the Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection (GRAND).

title: Two gluon fusion into a $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
abstract: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($\pi^0$, $\eta$, and $\eta'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $\eta$ and $\eta'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence (as compared to vacuum).

title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
abstract: The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron. Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.

title: Updated 78mBr 2−→1+ lifetime from isomeric decay cascade in active target
abstract: The half-life of the 2 − state at 32.3 keV in 78 Br has been measured only twice, yielding mutually inconsistent values of (14.2 ± 3) ns and (8.3 ± 0.3) ns; the currently adopted value of (11.3 ± 0.3) ns is their unweighted average. We report a new measurement of this half-life using a self-coincidence technique in which both the 148.6 keV 4 + → 2 − and 32.3 keV 2 − → 1 + transitions of the 78m Br isomeric cascade are captured within single digitized waveforms from a LaBr3(Ce) active-target detector, following production via 79 Br(n,2n) 78m Br with a pulsed deuterium–tritium neutron source. We obtain half-lives of (118.45 ± 0.72) µs and (19.8 ± 0.4) ns for the 4 + → 2 − and 2 − → 1 + transitions, respectively. The method is validated by applying it to the analogous 5 − → 2 − → 1 + cascade in 80m Br, for which all measured half-lives agree with adopted values within 1σ. The new 2 − → 1 + half-life in 78m Br exceeds the adopted value by 15.96σ, implying a 43% reduction in the reduced electric-quadrupole transition probability B(E2; 2 − → 1 + ) relative to currently evaluated data. This substantially increased hindrance of the 2 − → 1 + transition constrains the structure of low-lying negative-parity states in 78 Br and motivates renewed shell-model and beyond-mean-field calculations in the neutron-deficient A ≃ 78 mass region, where shape coexistence and proton–neutron residual interactions are expected to play important roles.

title: Superheavy nuclei with Z = 119, 120: α-decay or spontaneous fission?
abstract: We propose a local formula for calculating α -decay energies Q α in superheavy nuclei (SHN) with atomic numbers Z > 110, achieving a mean deviation of only 0.026 MeV and thus providing high-precision Q α predictions for the heaviest nuclei. Using these calculated Q α values, α -decay half-lives are computed where the barrier is derived from the self-consistent Skyrme energy density functional, which are in excellent agreement with available experimental data. For spontaneous fission, we adopt three independent approaches: a new formula with a good accuracy, a fission barrier penetration framework based on the Skyrme functional, and the generalized liquid-drop model with shell correction. The predicted dominant decay modes for synthesized SHN with Z > 110 are consistent with experimental observations. As an encouraging result, α -decay is predicted to be the dominant decay mode for the candidate nuclei of as-yet-unsynthesized elements Z = 119 and 120, with half-lives of 0.2–0.6 ms for Z = 119 and 0.02–0.06 ms for Z = 120 , which are many orders of magnitude shorter than their corresponding spontaneous fission half-lives. This greatly facilitates the identification of elements 119 and 120. These results along with our methods offer valuable guidance for future experiments on the synthesis of new elements.

title: Improved calibration algorithm and its validation for Guide Tube Calibration System in JUNO experiment
abstract: The Guide Tube Calibration System (GTCS) of the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is designed to calibrate the detector boundary non-uniformity, contributing to the stringent energy resolution requirement of JUNO. A 27Bq 241 Am- 9 Be neutron source is adopted for GTCS calibration, providing both point-like prompt signals from γ rays and spread-out delayed signals from neutron capture. This source is less affected by local optical shadowing and provides a prompt–delayed signature similar to inverse beta decay (IBD) and cosmogenic neutron events, enabling direct cross-checks. Additionally, realistic experimental conditions, including radioactive backgrounds and electronic noise are considered, so that a dedicated set of event selection criteria has been developed for GTCS. Comprehensive simulations and analyses under realistic background and noise conditions indicate that using 241 Am- 9 Be calibration source is feasible to meet the required 1% uncertainty for GTCS. Applying the improved GTCS calibration algorithm to experimental data collected on 23 August 2025, the energy responses at five calibration positions have been obtained, providing input to the detector non-uniformity correction function. The results have a good consistency with simulation, demonstrating the feasibility and robustness of the updated calibration approach.

title: Design of a high voltage delivery system for noble liquid time projection chambers
abstract: Noble liquid time projection chambers (TPCs) are a leading technology in the detection of ionizing radiation, particularly in applications such as accelerator neutrino physics, dark matter detection, and neutrinoless double beta decay. This paper addresses the design considerations for implementing stable high voltage (HV) systems within large noble liquid TPCs, with a focus on the nEXO experiment. Utilizing insights from prior HV research and experimental investigations, we outline factors influencing HV stability and discuss design choices to improve stability and prevent electrical discharges. A novel HV delivery system concept is presented, tailored for the nEXO TPC, which incorporates these design considerations while also meeting the stringent radiopurity requirements of the nEXO neutrinoless double beta decay search. These design considerations and their specific implementation towards a HV delivery system offer guidance to future experiments applying high voltage in noble liquid environments.

title: Characterization and applications of the LaBr3 array at HUN-REN ATOMKI
abstract: A high-efficiency γ -ray spectrometer at HUN-REN Institute for Nuclear Research (HUN-REN ATOMKI), the LAnthanum Bromide Detector Array (LABDA) has been designed and constructed to study low-probability phenomena in particle physics, nuclear spectroscopy, and nuclear astrophysics experiments. The array is comprised of 12 cylindrically shaped LaBr 3 (Ce) crystals, each measuring 3 ′ ′ × 3 ′ ′ , produced by Saint-Gobain. Key performance parameters of the array have been systematically characterized over a broad γ -ray energy range (344–10762 keV), including energy resolution, energy non-linearity, detection efficiency, time resolution and intrinsic background. Intrinsic background suppression, using pulse-shape discrimination methods has been also investigated. The prospects for applying the array to different nuclear physics measurements are discussed.
